in writing. i voted in favour of this new four-year protocol for a fisheries partnership agreement between the eu and the democratic republic of são tomé and príncipe. the main objective is to provide european union vessels with fishing opportunities in são toméan waters, while respecting the advice of scientific experts in the field. the second objective is to strengthen cooperation between the union and são tomé and príncipe to promote a sustainable fisheries policy and responsible exploitation of fisheries resources in the são toméan fishing zone, in the interest of both parties. the overall financial contribution of the protocol is eur 2 805 000 over the four years.
in writing. the union has negotiated with são tomé e príncipe a new fishing protocol for a period of four years to establish the terms and conditions under which eu-flagged vessels may fish in são tomé e príncipe's waters. the first fisheries agreement between the eec and the democratic republic of são tomé and príncipe was concluded in 1984. eight protocols have since been implemented, including two on the fisheries partnership agreement. however, the results achieved so far in the field of sectoral cooperation are very meagre. so there was an urgent need to remedy the situation. this agreement, in coordination with other development support instruments such as the european development fund, should, in my view, promote a genuine sustainable development of são tomé and príncipe's fishing sector and related industries and activities, by increasing the added value that remains in the country as a result of the exploitation of its natural resources. so i decided to vote in favour.
in writing. the protocol to the fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and são tomé and príncipe is part of the continuity of the various fisheries protocols signed since 1984. i therefore welcome this agreement which will allow eu vessels to continue fishing in the archipelago's waters while guaranteeing financial compensation. the latter will support the sustainable development of the fisheries sector and related industries and activities in são tomé and príncipe. however, i agree with the rapporteur that the reliability of information on catches and the conservation status of fishery resources should be improved and that the archipelago's monitoring capacity should be developed.
in writing. the european parliament has given its consent to the conclusion of the protocol to the new eu/são tomé and príncipe fisheries agreement. the previous protocol, which was in force from 13 may 2011 to 12 may 2014, allowed the activity of 40 eu tuna vessels: 28 purse seiners and 12 surface longliners. the financial contribution was eur 682 500 per year, of which more than 35% was earmarked for supporting são tomé and príncipe's sectoral policy. a new protocol was initialled on 19 december 2013 and entered into force on 23 may 2014 for a period of four years. the project will benefit 34 eu vessels (28 tuna seiners and 6 surface longliners). the annual financial contribution was set at eur 710 000 for the first three years and eur 675 000 for the fourth year, eur 325 000 of which was intended to support the sectoral policy of são tomé and príncipe.

in writing. this agreement allows vessels flying the flag of seychelles to continue their activities in the waters and marine biological resources of mayotte, despite the fact that mayotte became a french region that is part of europe as of 1 january 2014. it is important to emphasize that this is the first tuna agreement under which the european union allows non-eu vessels to fish in its waters on payment of taxes. the agreement allows eight tuna seiners to operate in mayotte waters under eu jurisdiction for the next six years in exchange for a licence and a fishing fee. i believe that this agreement will help to consolidate cooperation between the eu and seychelles by establishing high-quality fisheries in terms of sustainability, transparency, control and surveillance of the respective fleets. the agreement also benefits both parties, is beneficial to the economic development of mayotte and the seychelles and respects the rules of the common fisheries policy and the iotc on conservation of the resource.

in writing. the european parliament has approved the conclusion of an agreement between the eu and seychelles on access for fishing vessels flying the flag of seychelles to the marine biological resources of mayotte. it is a partnership agreement which governs relations between the eu and seychelles in the fisheries sector. the agreement entered into force on 10 may 2003 and has been renewed twice since then. the agreement approved by the ep (paralled on 3 april 2014) provides for access to the 24-mile to 100-mile zone for 8 sliding-net tuna vessels and 2 seychelles-flagged refuelling vessels for a renewable period of six years. the zone 0 to 24 miles shall remain reserved for local mahora fisheries. this agreement allows a limited number of seychelles vessels (which traditionally fish in mayotte's waters) to continue fishing in the mahora exclusive economic zone. it should be noted that the territory of mayotte became an outermost region of the eu on 1 january 2014. before the change in status of mayotte, a private agreement governed relations between european and seychelles fishing vessels and mayotte.

plant breeding is an ancient practice and is not only carried out by genetic engineering. the flemish interest is not against science but urges caution, because the dangers are known and real. it can lead to monoculture and dependence on agro-industries. the ries proposal is an apparent improvement. it does allow member states to restrict or prohibit its cultivation, but not its importation or trade in their territory. that's a double whammy. the farmers are not allowed to grow them, but the uninformed consumers are allowed to have the gmo products on their plates without being asked. because there , too , the shoe is twisting , of course: the ggo must be recognisable and identifiable, so as to guarantee freedom of choice for consumers and producers. that is why, to avoid any misunderstanding, i voted against this text, but with this explanation of vote.
in writing. i welcome the new regulation adopted by the eu parliament today, as it gives eu member states more and legally secured options to ban the cultivation of a genetically modified plant on their territory, even if it is legal throughout the eu. in the past, member states were required to submit new scientific evidence if they wished to ban the cultivation of genetically modified organisms (gmos). if a so-called safeguard clause was imposed and not supported by new scientific evidence, suppliers of genetically modified organisms such as monsanto could sue the member state. in future, member states may also refer to political reasons such as land use or the socioeconomic impact of a crop. the commission also announced that it would develop a new legal framework to make the procedures for gmos more democratic. the new rules do not solve the problem of the use of gmos in the eu, however, as the import of these organisms - for example as animal feed - is still allowed in countries that have banned their cultivation. here too, stricter rules should be applied in order to better inform consumers in particular about the use of genetically modified feed throughout the food chain.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because it now allows member states to decide whether or not to allow the cultivation of gmos on their soil. the grounds for prohibition may, for example, be related to environmental criteria, land-use planning obligations or economic impact. the obligation to take measures to ensure the coexistence of crops and the desire to guarantee the transparency of the procedures for restricting and prohibiting the cultivation of a gmo should also be noted.
genetically modified organisms (gmos) are approved at european level on the basis of a scientific assessment by the european food safety authority (efsa). however, the very different opinions of the member states block this approval process. currently, 1 gmo is commercially grown in 5 member states in the eu. several member states have prohibited the cultivation of the gmo on their territory by means of a safeguard clause. after more than four years of negotiations, a vote was taken today on an opt-out for member states for european approved gmos. the commission hopes that this will help to break the deadlock in the approval process. the n-va supported the agreement. flanders is a leader in research into gmos and there are also many companies active. the nva wants to give innovation the necessary opportunities and believes that this agreement can contribute to this. moreover, the agreement addresses some of our specific concerns: the two-step procedure thus increases legal certainty. it is also essential that the flexibility provided does not jeopardise the credibility of the efsa risk assessment. there are a number of points which call for our attention in the implementation of this legislation. the possible fragmentation of the internal market, the situation in border areas and the workability of the rules should be monitored.
in writing. after more than four years of discussion, agreement has finally been reached on the delicate issue of gmo cultivation in the eu member states. as regards the authorization of gmos, the system remains purely european: it is the commission which decides, on the basis of scientific advice, whether or not to authorise a particular gmo. as far as the cultivation of gmos is concerned, it is up to the member states to authorise or prohibit it. i supported this agreement, which confirms the european character of the system and at the same time allows us to respond to the wishes of our citizens in the states where they are clearly against the cultivation of gmos.
in writing. i congratulate frédérique ries on the adoption of this report, which aims to give member states a broader legal basis to refuse the cultivation of gmos on their territory despite the authorisation of seeds by the european food safety authority. in the face of the concerns of our citizens, some member states want to prohibit further the cultivation of gmos. however, they are faced with a legal deadlock which calls into question compliance with the european legislation in force. this report therefore provides a better framework for the rejection of this crop, while at the same time giving member states greater flexibility.
in writing. the european parliament confirmed the agreement in principle reached in the trilogue in december on this compromise text which will amend directive 2001/18/ec and give member states the possibility to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of gmos on their territory. although it significantly improves on the european commission's original proposal and allows the eu to move beyond a status quo that is considered untenable, this compromise is certainly not the panacea. i therefore corrected my original vote because this new legislation is supposed to give the states the means to prevent the cultivation of gmos on their territory, but in fact gives biotechnology companies the power to negotiate with elected governments and excludes the main legal argument for banning these crops: the evidence of environmental damage. states should be the sole risk managers, retain their right to prevent the spread of gmos on their territory and should not require approval of companies seeking to profit from gm crops. this compromise is formalising the role of industry, which i reject. finally, i regret that this new compromise is a form of de federalisation.
in writing. the new gmo legislation was on the agenda for the european parliament's votes this afternoon. i voted yes, of course. we have won the case. the member states of the european union are now free to decide whether or not to allow the cultivation of genetically modified organisms on their soil. a real victory, the culmination of four years of legislative struggle. the pro-gmo lobby, led by several multinational corporations and the uk, was ultimately unsuccessful. moreover, we have obtained a legal basis for the refusal of the implementation of gm crops, an extension of the list of grounds for prohibition. such grounds for prohibition could be, for example, land-use planning obligations, socioeconomic consequences, measures to avoid the accidental presence of gmos in other products or agricultural policy objectives. the prohibitions could also apply to groups of gmos determined by species or characteristic. we have also demanded binding coexistence measures. we have given the states the power to impose sanctions to prevent contamination of traditional crops by gm crops.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report because it supports the incorporation into eu law of measures to provide greater protection for certain underwater species, in particular going beyond the habitats directive.
in writing. the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean (gfcm), established in 1949, covers the mediterranean, the black sea and adjacent waters. the main tasks of the cgpm are to promote the development, conservation and rational management of living aquatic resources, to design and recommend conservation measures and to promote cooperation projects in the field of training. for example, the gfcm has adopted a number of measures to ensure that seabirds, sea turtles and cetaceans are caught less by accident during fishing activities, and to protect sharks and rays from fishing activities. such measures go beyond the protection of these species already ensured at union level by the habitats directive. i voted for this report today because it proposes to amend regulation (eu) no 1343/2011 of the european parliament and of the council laying down certain provisions on fishing in the area covered by the gfcm agreement in order to include the measures contained in the gfcm recommendations.
in writing. i voted for mr mato's proposal. the measures contained in it go beyond the protection of these species already ensured at union level by the habitats directive and other union acts, and provide for specific recording and reporting obligations for both operators and member states. in addition, the proposal implements into union law certain measures concerning the fishery for small pelagic stocks in the adriatic sea.

in writing. the european ombudsman (or european ombudsman) investigates complaints about maladministration in the institutions and bodies (except the european court of justice) of the european union. this includes, for example, irregularities in administration, discrimination, abuse of power or failure to reply to letters. any eu citizen, company, association or other body established in the eu can lodge a complaint. since 1 october 2013, the office of the eu ombudsman has been held by emily o'reilly. in 2013, 23 245 citizens used the ombudsman's services. it dealt with 2 354 complaints, carried out 350 investigations and closed 461 investigations. the majority of complaints and inquiries came from belgium, germany, italy, poland and spain, and concerned mainly the european commission. i welcome the 2013 annual report and the work of mrs o'reilly, and congratulate her not only on her achievements but also on her good cooperation with parliament. your efforts to make the ttip negotiations transparent are commendable.

on behalf of the alde group. – mr president, my message this afternoon in this debate is clear. we have to work together in this parliament and we cannot waste time. two weeks after the attacks on charlie hebdo we must take a leap forward, and we must conclude in the european union a broad and ambitious package to tackle terrorism. we have to do this as parliament together with the commission and together with the council because it is a common task and there is a common goal to be achieved. in fact, what we have to do is to repeat what happened after 9/11. after 9/11, in 2001, alongside other measures we decided on a package and created the european arrest warrant, which at that time represented a dramatic change in europe because previously it had taken years to secure the extradition of a suspect. sometimes it took 10 years to bring someone back from the uk to france whereas since we have had the european arrest warrant it takes just days to transfer a suspect or a criminal from one country to another. we need the same level of ambition now: not to do the same things, because the threats have changed, but to have a similar package to strengthen our security in europe – and two things are at stake here. first of all, we need a common capacity to analyse the information and the risk, because that is lacking in europe. in all major terrorist attacks over the past 10 years, mr kirkhope, the perpetrators have been known to the services of the different countries. the problem today is not so much that we do not collect the info; the problem is that we do not share the info between our services in europe. that is the main problem. we have to create what we are calling ‘euro-intel’ – a system for sharing information and for common analysis of risks. i have heard a number of people today saying that this is not possible under the terms of article 4 of the treaty. well, i can tell you that in the last parliamentary term we changed the treaty twice: once to have 18 more members of parliament and the second time to introduce the european stability mechanism to save the banks. if it is possible to change the treaty on the fast-track procedure to save the banks, it has to be possible to change the treaty to increase the security of european citizens here in this european union. secondly, we must not make the error of the nationalists and the populists, namely to say that the problem is schengen. the problem is not schengen. the problem is that we are not sufficiently solid among ourselves to strengthen the outside borders of the schengen area instead of reinstating internal borders. finally, on passenger name records (pnr) i want to say just one thing, since mr kirkhope has spoken about this. we are in favour of a european pnr system but it has to go together with guarantees and with the protection of data and privacy. it is clear that mr pittella is right: this is about safety and freedom at the same time. and one last sentence about the targets in this debate: you cannot abuse the death of charlie hebdo as some are doing here in this parliament, ms le pen, mr farage. this is not about a war between civilisations and religions: it is about a war against criminals and terrorists, and that makes all the difference.

in writing. the economic recovery in the union is still subject to very high uncertainty and the risk of deflation is very real. the efsi is thus a tool that can and must contribute to recovery in a context where private investors remain hidden and public investment is curbed by socially dramatic austerity in some countries and economically unprofitable for the union. the public guarantee which is the basis of the recovery plan must be, at the very least, a lever for improving the welfare of european citizens. the principle of flexibility, which is gradually gaining ground, would also require that public investment going through the efsi be excluded from the calculation of deficits for the states concerned. this is of course essential to revive social projects and promote employment. but the socioeconomic situation of the union requires going one step further. flexibility must also be applied to other strategic public investments that will create jobs and socioeconomic redeployment. this includes local and regional government investments, which are constrained by the new accounting standards, but which contribute to economic activity without having a significant impact on debt.
president-in-office of the council. - mr president, the paris climate change conference at the end of this year is expected to adopt a new global climate agreement for the post-2020 period. this new agreement should be universal and capable of keeping us on track to limit the average global temperature increase to below 2°c relative to pre-industrial levels. the intergovernmental panel on climate change has indicated in its latest synthesis report that the target of 2°c and global emissions reduction of 40-70% compared to 2010 are needed by 2015, and that emission levels should be near zero or below in 2100. we have less than 10 months and we need to use this time efficiently. the results of the lima climate change conference, and a sense of urgency expressed by world leaders at the un climate summit in september, provide a necessary impetus for the work this year. the lima call for climate action, adopted in december, contains two main outcomes. the first is guidance for the communication of proposed emission-reduction targets, the so-called ‘intended nationally determined contributions’, and the second is the preparation of elements for the draft negotiating text for the paris agreement. in the paris agreement, all parties should have legally binding mitigation commitments, but levels of ambition and commitment types will differ. intended nationally determined contributions should therefore allow each party to choose its contribution type and define its level of ambition, in accordance with its national circumstances and capabilities. in october last year, eu leaders endorsed a target to reduce the eu’s domestic emissions by at least 40% in 2030 compared to 1990, in line with its long-term objective of reducing emissions by 80-95% by 2050. the strategic framework is now to be translated into an eu intended contribution.the presidency of the council is determined to ensure that the eu intended contribution is submitted to the secretariat of the un framework climate change conference within the first quarter of 2015. we expect other major economies to come forward promptly with their contributions as well. the paris agreement should go well beyond mitigation targets capable of delivering on the below-2°c objective. it should also be dynamic, with inbuilt flexibility and capacity to respond to evolving circumstances, responsibilities and capabilities. it should provide a long-term vision of the need for transformation towards a lower-emission and climate-resilient economy and it should enable broad and effective participation. let me underscore that, despite the significant progress, there are still important issues on which a shared global vision has yet to emerge, in particular on differentiation between countries’ obligations on the legal form and force of the paris agreement. intensive negotiations will be needed in order to find common ground on these outstanding core issues. the presidency of the council will make all possible efforts to ensure effective european union participation at the international negotiation sessions. outreach activities planned to take place throughout 2015 will be a crucial element in this process. they will contribute to the ongoing discussions. we have to talk to our partners all around the world to try to find common ground. moreover, in order to ensure an appropriate background for negotiations, we need to make sure that the eu’s efforts on emissions reduction and support for developing countries are adequately recognised. the presidency of the council will also stimulate eu-internal political debate on climate change with a view to the paris conference. the environmental council in march will be the first opportunity to discuss the eu’s expectations and strategy.
member of the commission. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, it is a pleasure for me to have this opportunity to exchange views on the european union's plans and activities on climate action, in connection with the conclusion of a global climate agreement which we want to reach in just over ten months' time at the united nations summit in paris. first of all, i would like to share with you my assessment of the lima conference. i had the opportunity to do so with the representatives of this house during that conference, in the framework of the daily meetings we held during the last cop. so, as many of you know, i consider the lima cop to have been an important step in our efforts to reach a global agreement in paris. i would like to highlight three conclusions of the lima conference. firstly, the decision to reiterate the need for all countries to submit their respective national contributions to reduce emissions by the end of march, known in english as intended nationally determined contributions. secondly, agreement was reached on the reporting requirements, which should describe these contributions in a clear, transparent and understandable way. finally, the decision mandated the united nations to prepare a synthesis report once all the respective contributions had been submitted. this report should enable us to assess the progress we are collectively prepared to make to keep global warming below two degrees celsius. lima has also been a tangible demonstration of the unity of the european union. there was a great deal of cooperation between the ministers and with the european parliament. we were able to react to changing circumstances in a satisfactory way and i hope that collaboration will continue throughout this year. however, much remains to be done this year. the draft elements of the final text of the agreement are too long and contain excessive options. the legal form of the future agreement, climate finance and the differentiation of national contributions to emission reductions are also very important issues that remain to be resolved. in order to articulate clearly our vision of the objectives that the paris agreement must achieve, in the coming weeks i will be presenting to the college of commissioners a communication entitled 'the paris protocol, a blueprint for fighting climate change beyond 2020'. this communication has two main objectives: firstly, to describe how we intend the paris protocol to be dynamic, transparent and legally binding and as such capable of responding to economic and geopolitical realities; and secondly, to translate the objectives of the european union's 2030 climate and energy strategy into our contribution to emission reductions, in line with the information transparency requirements agreed in lima. the communication will reiterate that we must work hard to reach an agreement in paris that applies to all. the united states and china have committed to action, and together with the european union, we would account for almost half of the world's greenhouse gas emissions. but all countries that can must submit their national contributions to reduce emissions this year, as we agreed in warsaw. all the g20 countries and other major economies are certainly in a position to do so. but, in parallel, and throughout 2015, we must mobilize our energies in the area of climate diplomacy, we must continue to engage with our partners and friends about our vision for the new agreement and encourage them to submit their national emissions reduction targets. the commission is certainly committed to working to maintain the european union's leadership on climate action and, together with the vice-president of the commission, federica mogherini, we will work to raise awareness among all international actors during this year. next week i will be in washington to meet with my counterparts from the state department, the energy department and the white house and on 4 february we will hold a meeting with chinese minister xie zhenhua and the secretary general of the united nations framework convention on climate change. last week the vice-president and high representative and i presented a climate diplomacy plan to the foreign affairs council which was supported by the foreign ministers. the joint implementation of this plan will contribute very positively to raising awareness in a large number of countries, both at bilateral meetings and within the framework of the g7 and g20. finally, i would like to say a few words about climate finance, an issue which is essential not only for the paris agreement but also for the credibility of the european union as an international actor. in 2013, the european union and its member states contributed €9.5 billion in climate finance, but there is no doubt that the european union and its member states need to continue their efforts. together with the ministers of finance and development cooperation, we must be able to engage with our partners on this fundamental aspect, in order to complete an ambitious agreement in paris. in addition to the climate negotiations we are also negotiating the post-2015 sustainable development goals. on this issue, commissioners vella and mimica are leading the work within the commission, and we will work together to ensure that our action is consistent. at the same time, we will continue to work together with the private sector and other international institutions, such as the world bank, to mobilize more resources. the success of the european union depends on the ability of parliament, the commission and the member states to speak with one voice. i will therefore continue to work closely with this house and the council to reach an ambitious, legally binding agreement in paris that applies to all countries.

"small country, great food" says it all. and that quality is certainly due in part to a strict european policy on food safety, from farm to fork. quality is also achieved through the efforts of countless smes, every day again, small businesses, medium-sized companies that work in the craft sector, which are proud of the quality they deliver every day again. i am absolutely opposed to this resolution for the following four reasons: origin labelling has nothing to do with safety. it does not improve quality, traceability or prevent fraud; it is operational and practically unrealizable. the sector is rightly alarmed. it increases administrative burdens and costs and ultimately leads to a higher price for the consumer, who may seem to find origin labelling relatively important but is not willing to pay extra for it; finally, this is a form of protectionism, which is contrary to the principles of the european single market and is particularly detrimental to smaller export-oriented regions such as flanders. we do not need additional rules to restore consumer confidence, but more controls, stricter enforcement of existing agreements and tougher penalties. voluntary origin labelling for meat as an ingredient already exists and is applied cost-effectively where there is clear market demand and operational feasibility. this can be worked on. europe needs a greater sense of reality and not a policy of blind alley that achieves no goal but only creates an unnecessary additional obstacle for the many smes in the already precarious economic fabric.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the european union's food labelling system is properly and effectively monitored. as a young european consumer, i am naturally also against fraud and for greater food safety and transparency. i am surprised to find that people in this house think that a compulsory nationality declaration is by definition a guarantee of safe food. but let's be honest with each other. the country of origin of meat does not determine its safety, but the way in which the producer works. i am listening to the concerns of consumers who want more clarity about their food, but i would like to see it based on scientific facts. we know that 75 per cent of consumers are unwilling or, in some cases, unable to pay the additional costs of compulsory origin labelling. if we really want to build a more social europe, we cannot adopt a measure which makes the lives of the weakest even more expensive. and how sincere do measures to empower smes sound when we are chasing those same entrepreneurs through the back door at cost? how consistent is our agricultural policy if we are putting farmers' already small profit margins at risk by raising the cost of meat processing? finally, mr president, i would like to say this: i hear young people every day calling for a europe that recruits, a europe that is less intrusive. the question is whether this measure will meet that call. i think we all know the answer to that.
mr president, commissioner, 90% of the citizens think it is important that the origin of the meat used as an ingredient is mentioned and this has been said on several occasions. consumers must be informed. the commission uses the argument of a significant price increase in the event of an obligation to indicate the origin of meat. that is not the truth, of course, but the argument of the food industry, which does not want to change anything. in fact, for those undertakings which voluntarily mentioned the indication of origin, the additional cost was estimated at 0.67%, i.e. a few cents. the cost is the number of intermediaries, many of whom are useless. it would cost consumers much less if there were fewer intermediaries in the chain and a more decent price could be paid to producers. the commission must listen to the consumer organizations and the european parliament must listen to both ends of the chain: the producers, who suffer, and the consumers, who are in demand. commissioner, you're on the grill. we are waiting for your legislative acts. a little courage, please.
vice-president of the commission. - mr president, thank you for a very deep, fine and fruitful debate. we have taken note of your views and i will pass these on to my colleague vytenis andriukaitis, who will be in charge of this particular issue. i would also like to underline that the estimated increase of 15% - 20% and up to 50% referred to the additional operating costs for the industry and not to the final product price. it is very difficult to estimate what kind of impact this would have on the final product cost. this depends firstly on the animal species concerned, secondly on the specific product concerns, on the applicable modalities, and fourthly on the specific operational situation of the operation concerned. the french study cannot be compared to the commission report because it only concerns beef, and second only in france, and third only voluntary schemes. it focuses on price increases whereas the commission report focused on increases in operating costs. the commission report also examined the willingness of the consumer to pay for information on origin, and this was found to be very weak. this aspect has not been assessed in other consumer surveys. as i said, i will take all the speeches here today to my colleague vytenis andriukaitis.
in writing. mandatory labelling of products containing meat is not a good idea. it's not helping to fight fraud. the recent horse meat scandal involved horse meat instead of beef, which is outright fraud and which would not have been changed by origin labelling. moreover, food control is already very well regulated in europe. all meat is traceable from the feed supplier to the store. we need to focus more on anti-fraud, not on additional legislation. producers who voluntarily wish to indicate the origin of the meat on their products are of course free to do so, but we are not in favour of an obligation. for meat processing undertakings, this measure would be an additional administrative burden and would entail additional costs which will inevitably be passed on to the consumer.

member of the commission. - madam president, let me underline, in order to set the context, that the european union and the international labour organisation (ilo) have a long record of good cooperation. even more, the ilo is a key partner for our external policies. the european union promotes the ratification and implementation of ilo conventions and relies on ilo supervision of labour standards, in particular core labour standards, and in the monitoring of trade association enlargement and development agreements. therefore, having a well-functioning ilo standard supervisory system is important for us since its conclusions are crucial to assessing compliance with international labour standards. and here we have a problem, due to the fact that since 2012 the supervision of labour standards cannot be carried out properly. why not? because employers’ and workers’ representatives at the ilo disagree on whether or not the right to strike is protected under ilo fundamental convention no 87, the convention concerning freedom of association and protection of the right to organise convention. secondly, employers’ and workers’ representatives also disagree on the capacity of the ilo supervisory bodies to decide on the scope of the right to strike, its limits and the conditions for its legitimate exercise. beyond this there is, as well, a risk of endangering the tripartite relationships and weakening the ilo supervisory system. as the commissioner in charge of relations with the international labour organisation, i am deeply concerned about these developments know, the european union is only an observer at the ilo. the commission will therefore not intervene on the substance of the discussion. these matters fall within the competence of the member states. the recognition of the right to strike in ilo convention no 87 is a delicate matter. at the last session of the ilo governing body, also thanks to european union coordination in approximating their positions, the eu member states were ready to support the option of asking the international court of justice for a clarification of the matter so that we can move forward and resolve this pending disagreement between employers’ and workers’ representatives. a tripartite meeting will take place in the ilo between 23 february and 25 february, the last week of this month, to discuss the issue. the commission is ready to support all players and provide information to feed into the discussion, notably by retrieving information on the situation regarding the right to strike in the european blue-card answer. – mr etheridge, i think you have a point and indeed speaking about the greeks or the germans or the muslims or the jews is probably not the right way to speak. you have a point there. however, it is a fact that statistically some groups in our society suffer from discrimination as a whole. it does not mean that they are not equal and that they are all the same, but when you see massive statistical bias against some communities, well, that is what leads me then to speak about the muslim communities. but i would agree with you that, indeed, we should not just categorise all societies as groups of people just living next to one another. mr timmermans also mentioned that in his speech. he does not want to see, and nor do i, a european society which is just a juxtaposition of individual communities. on that point at least we may agree.
the main question at the forthcoming european summit, mr president, is whether we can continue with this union, and more specifically with this monetary union, after the greek elections. the next summit will therefore be a historic debate on whether the political decision to create a currency, which was based from the outset on errors of thought and design, was not a mistake that we must undo. there's no such thing as a free lunch. greece will never regain its competitiveness within the euro system. so either it is said, not only in practice but now also officially, that the eurozone is a transfer system and then we must, as obama ordered us the day before yesterday, implement a debt cancellation or a debt restructuring variant of it, or we must correct the mistakes of the past and give greece a new life, out of prison. either obama or grexit, there aren't many other options. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.

in writing. the accession of a number of countries to the hague convention is to be welcomed. the abduction of one or more children abroad is a traumatic and dramatic event which must be dealt with as soon as possible in the interests of the children. the question is, however, what the signatures or the words of some of the acceding countries will be worth. for example, a former belgian minister points to the manifest reluctance of the moroccan authorities in cases of parental abduction. the eu is now claiming exclusive external jurisdiction in this area. this means that member states risk being finger-tapped by the eu if they were to take the initiative themselves. whereas the ultimate goal, by any means necessary, should be: find a quick solution for the kids.
in writing. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is an important legal instrument for the protection of children. the aim of this convention is to prevent international child abduction by means of increased cooperation between the contracting states. it has been ratified by all eu member states. the accession of gabon to the agreement is to be welcomed. this extends this useful legal framework to other countries. this ensures that the child's best interests are paramount.
in writing. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 is a very important instrument which allows contracting parties to cooperate in finding a solution to cases of international child abduction. it sets up a system to expedite the return of a child who has been abducted to the country where he or she is habitually resident. by decision of the council, the member states accept, each for its territory, the accession of gabon to the convention and thus the effective entry into force of the convention in the cases involving the european union and that country.
in writing. the european parliament voted today to approve the council's decision to accept gabon's accession to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction. in the context of cross-border parental abduction, the convention allows states parties to overcome differences and incompatibilities between their legal frameworks in order to cooperate with each other in the best interests of the child. in this connection, i would like to commend the work of the european parliament's ombudsman for children who are victims of crossborder parental abduction. the aim of this role, now held by irish mep mairead mcguinness, is to help parents find solutions that are primarily aimed at safeguarding the welfare of the child. in view of the increase in cases of crossborder parental abduction within the union, the work of mairead mcguinness is of great importance and is a testament to the european parliament's commitment to serving citizens.
in writing. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction establishes a system for contracting states to cooperate in finding a solution in cases of international child abduction. this is often the case when a couple separates. for the husband or wife from another country, it may be tempting to take advantage of the lack of cooperation between the states to obtain custody of the children. the main problem is still the differences between the legal systems of the member states. in such cases, the courts of both states often declare that they have jurisdiction and each of them grants custody of the child to the parent who is a national of the state in which he or she is domiciled. the convention therefore seeks to remedy such situations at international level by establishing the jurisdiction of the courts and the law of the state in which the child resides. it also sets up a system to ensure the immediate return of the child who has been abducted. i welcome the fact that libreville is joining today.
in writing. i voted for the convention in question. the purpose of the convention is to remedy such situations at the international level by establishing the jurisdiction of the courts and the law of the state in which the child resides. it also sets up a system to ensure the immediate return of the child who has been abducted. the union now has exclusive external competence in this area under opinion 1/13 of the court of justice. the member states are therefore no longer acting on their own behalf. the problem is that the convention does not provide for the autonomous action of international organizations. this problem necessitates the council decision asking the member states to accept, each on its own territory, the accession of gabon to the convention and, therefore, the effective entry into force of the convention in cases involving the european union and that country. the accession of gabon to the convention is welcome news; i fully agree with that, especially in view of the fact that the european union has many citizens of gabonese origin on its soil. this will protect children linked to this community from illegal abductions. this is a protection for children and will be extended to the whole of the union.

in writing. in voting for accession to the 1980 hague convention, the sensitive and painful issue of parental abduction is particularly addressed. child abductions are rightly experienced as tragedies by the victim parent. in a pluralist world, several very different rights are potentially applicable and therefore a source of legal uncertainty, in disregard of the interests of families and especially of the child. it is often difficult to keep in touch with the child abroad, either because the child is too young to talk on the phone or because the 'kidnapper' parent prevents contact. parental alienation is a common practice. psychological support is not sufficient in most cases, either before, during or after the abduction. the joy of the reunion is sometimes tinged by a sense of panic in the face of the scale of the task. as foreign minister, i had many opportunities to meet with parents of child abductees. i felt the parents' distress. i hope very much that with the accession to the hague convention, parents and children will be able to regain their share of happiness.

in writing. road safety is one of the main priorities of european transport policy. an important part of this policy is the enforcement of penalties for road traffic offences by non-resident drivers. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the following areas: this in turn requires a cross-border exchange of information between national administrative authorities: the member state in which a road traffic offence is committed shall have access to the vehicle registration data of the member state in which the vehicle is registered. the commission presented a new proposal for a directive in june 2014 based on its 2011 directive, which was annulled by the ecj. i welcome the legal basis (transport) adapted in accordance with the treaties, which obliges the member states which have been excluded (the united kingdom, ireland and denmark) to implement the directive. this ensures that everyone in the eu is treated equally, regardless of where their vehicle is registered.
in writing. directive 2011/82/eu facilitating the cross-border exchange of information on road safety offences entered into force on 11 november 2013. it allows the exchange of information between states parties on traffic offences committed by non-residents which endanger the safety of the driver and other road users, such as speeding, driving under the influence of drugs, failure to wear a motorcycle helmet, use of a mobile phone and driving on an illegal road. however, the directive was annulled by the court of justice on 6 may 2014 because it was approved on the wrong legal basis namely police cooperation (instead of transport safety). the court, however, allowed a period of one year for the adoption of a new text. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' to cover all vehicles, including those with a maximum mass of less than 100 tonnes. the amendment of the legal basis will also allow the inclusion of the united kingdom, denmark and ireland in the scope.
in writing. with today's vote, parliament confirms the agreement reached in december 2014, which allows the current cooperation between police services of eu countries to exchange information on traffic offences to continue. the cooperation will also be extended to all 28 member states (including denmark, the uk and ireland). this is an important measure to reduce the number of road deaths. the eu has set itself the goal of halving the number of road fatalities by 2020. it is important that foreign speeding or driving under the influence do not go unpunished. a good exchange of information on traffic offences between eu countries is therefore essential.
in writing. i voted in favour of this directive because it guarantees equal treatment for non-resident and resident drivers. its objective is to facilitate the cross-border exchange of information on road safety offences committed in a member state other than the one in which the vehicle in question was registered. member states will have reciprocal access to vehicle registration data through an electronic data exchange network. these exchanges should make it possible to identify drivers who commit road traffic offences abroad. the offences covered are: speeding, failure to wear a seat belt, crossing a red light, driving drunk, driving under the influence of drugs, failure to wear a helmet, driving on a prohibited lane, unlawful use of a mobile phone or any other communication device while driving. the measures provided for in this directive are not new. this directive incorporates the provisions of a directive adopted on 25 october 2011, but the legal basis of which was contested by the commission and annulled by the court of justice in its judgment of 6 may 2014.
in writing. i welcome the vote on this proposal for a directive which aims to facilitate the exchange of information on road safety offences. a previous directive on the subject was annulled by the court of justice of the european union (cjeu) in may 2014 on the grounds that its legal basis was incorrect. the ecj had, however, maintained the effects of the directive for one year, to allow the european institutions to adopt a new text without creating a legal vacuum. the new directive therefore takes account of the remarks of the ecj, seeking its legal basis in transport safety rather than in police cooperation. the new directive also extends its territorial scope, since denmark, the united kingdom and ireland, which initially decided not to apply the first directive, have joined the new text. i therefore welcome today's vote as an important step towards more effective enforcement of road traffic rules across europe, avoiding european citizens from becoming victims of reckless drivers who do not respect the road code.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text. many actors (associations of road accident victims, traffic and road safety authorities and, more generally, associations for which road safety is a priority), who all applauded the adoption of the directive, would not understand that parliament is not doing everything possible to avoid the formation of a legal vacuum. in addition, citizens, most of whom are not happy to receive a notification of a traffic offence, welcome the prospect of making this experience available to as many people as possible, regardless of the country in which the vehicle is registered. this directive could also reverse the trend at a critical moment. although the union is once again on track to meet the target of halving the number of road fatalities by 2020, the number appears to be rising again, due to a number of factors: the ageing of the car fleet, drastic cuts in infrastructure maintenance expenditure as a result of the economic crisis, a lack of funding for infrastructure and innovations that could improve road safety, etc.
in writing. i wholeheartedly supported this tool to save lives on europe's roads.

in writing. the european union's counter-terrorism policy is always guided by respect for fundamental rights and the rule of law. i expect the same from the united states of america. i categorically reject torture and other inhuman or degrading treatment. i therefore welcome a resolution by parliament condemning in the strongest terms the cia's cruel interrogation methods and calling on the united states of america to investigate and punish the numerous human rights violations resulting from the cia's secret detention programmes.
in writing. i have of course supported this resolution which was not signed by the epp in which the signatories welcome the decision of the us senate to publish the summary of the report on the cia detention and interrogation programme. the european parliament, the council and the commission have adopted a joint resolution on the situation in the middle east. the resolution calls on the united states to prosecute those responsible for human rights violations in this context and calls on member states to investigate allegations that there were secret prisons on their territory where people were detained under the cia programme. the commission also called on the member states to ensure that the eu's external borders are not encroached upon by the countries of the region.
in writing. the revelations by the us senate concerning the use of torture and other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment by the cia against detainees after the terrorist attacks of 11 september, and the alleged complicity of certain eu member states, have had a wide public response. the alleged use of european countries by the cia for the transport and illegal detention of prisoners had already been investigated by a temporary committee of the european parliament set up in 2006. the 'extraordinary transfer' programme implemented involved, in the majority of cases, secret detention and torture (simulations of drowning, mock executions, prolonged sleep deprivation and painful poses). like parliament in its final report adopted on 14 february 2007, i can only deplore the passivity or blindness of some member states to the illegal operations of the cia on their territory. it is time for the european states concerned to begin investigating these facts and, if they are established, to take the appropriate sanctions.
in writing. i condemn in the strongest terms the unspeakable practices of the cia in violation of national and international law, as revealed in the us senate report. nothing, not even the fight against barbarism, can justify such practices. at the same time, we must commend the us senate for having the courage to shed light on the very dark passages of its modern history. this is a real example of a system of democratic counter-power. however, as members of the european parliament, we must focus primarily on the passive and consensual acts of some of our member states. by turning a blind eye, they have broken their most profound commitment: that of respect for the rule of law. i welcome the request for an inquiry from the libe committee. however, this democratic control could be extended to a wider committee also including national parliamentarians, judges and academics. in the face of such grave acts, we must find an ambitious and adequate formula; we must have a historical counterweight strong enough to prevent the same mistakes from being made again.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution. we have already condemned on several occasions the cia's secret detention and extraordinary rendition programme, which have resulted in multiple human rights violations, including the use of torture and other inhuman or degrading treatment, abductions, secret detention, detention without trial and violations of the principle of non-refoulement. these are totally unacceptable and go against my values, let us say our european values!
in writing. the cia's practices are contrary to the letter and spirit of international law. the european parliament has been condemning these practices for some time. the criminal or terrorist activity the suspects were alleged to have committed is no excuse for the government to torture. the united states senate has had the courage to bring this dark page to light and to sharpen it. as members of the european parliament we should focus on the (active or) passive cooperation of some european governments. i hope that the libe committee in the european parliament will do its job and show the same courage as the us senate.
in writing. as the recent attacks in paris and the glaring foiling of attacks in belgium have shown, terrorism knows no borders. only a pan-european response can deal with the problem. the european parliament's resolution to implement a concrete package of counter-terrorism measures at european level at short notice is highly commendable. it aims to take both preventive measures (combating radicalisation) and to improve existing counter-terrorism tools such as an eu-wide passenger name record (pnr) .
in writing. i supported the motion for a resolution because it develops a comprehensive approach to the fight against terrorism. it condemns in advance and categorically all acts of terrorism and underlines the serious damage to our democratic values and freedoms. it also stresses the need to tackle the roots of terrorism and radicalisation, in particular in terms of policies promoting social inclusion. it also calls for greater cooperation within the union, particularly in the field of intelligence, so that the effectiveness of existing tools (sis, apis, europol, eurojust, cepol, etc.) can be enhanced. in general, it stresses the importance of the exchange of information between the police and judicial authorities of the union, in compliance, of course, with european and national law. it also stressed the need to combat effectively the trafficking of arms and to apply adequately the anti-money laundering directives in order to eliminate a major source of funding for terrorist networks. it also stressed the need to develop an appropriate external policy to strengthen links with partners useful in the fight against terrorism, to put an end to the financing of terrorism and to prevent radicalisation.
in writing. it is essential that we quickly agree on a european pnr system. it is indeed an effective tool in the fight against terrorism and serious crime; we need it to increase the security of european citizens, of all of us. but of course we must also take action in other ways. address the growing radicalisation, in particular by making a much greater effort to prevent and dialogue. in many cities, including my own country, the last few years have seen a sharp reduction in the extremely valuable street corner projects. we shouldn't have done that. it is clear that in many cases we will only be able to restore trust and dialogue by this means and that we will have to do much more.
in writing. the terrorist attacks committed on the territory of the union over the last ten years have highlighted a number of shortcomings and weaknesses that need to be addressed in order to improve the prevention of future terrorist attacks. the european union must now, more than ever, ensure the security of all, while guaranteeing the rights and freedoms that are the founding principles of the european project. i therefore voted in favour of the resolution on measures to combat terrorism, which sets out a series of actions to improve the union's effectiveness in this area, while respecting this balance. i also supported the adoption of an amendment calling for every effort to be made to finalise the eu pnr directive by the end of the year. however, i remain convinced that other measures must also be implemented in the short term: the strengthening of controls at the external schengen borders, including for citizens of the union, increased resources allocated to europol to combat terrorism and in particular against islamist propaganda on the internet, and the mandatory exchange of information on jihadists between member states.
in writing. after intensive negotiations, the european parliament adopted a resolution listing priority areas for action in the fight against terrorism and radicalisation in europe. among the major measures proposed is the need to break the national information divide that already exists. refusing to share information limits our chances of actively fighting terrorists. the member states must now take a further step by giving the european union the means to combat this scourge which goes beyond our borders, our continent. we must not give in to fear. data collection is essential as long as it is necessary and within the limits of respect for privacy. i shall therefore be firmly opposed to the creation of a european big brother. however, we must not be naive, information is the raw material in the fight against terrorism. we must therefore establish a framework which ensures this balance. i welcome the european parliament's decision to tackle the pnr data issue while reaffirming its commitment to data protection.
in writing. i voted today in favour of the resolution on counter-terrorism measures. these include the adoption of a 'european pnr' (a centralised database containing detailed files on all passengers passing through a european airport, kept for five years) linked to progress on the reform of personal data protection and privacy. the resolution also stresses the need to improve, enhance and accelerate the sharing of law enforcement information at the global level and calls for faster and more effective sharing of relevant data and information. it also recalls the need again and again to invest in programmes that address the root causes of radicalisation, including educational programmes, the promotion of integration, social inclusion, dialogue, participation, equality and tolerance.
in writing. - the greens/efa group today voted against the joint motion for a resolution on anti-terrorism measures, as the resolution is sending the wrong message at the wrong time. the resolution agreed by the four bigger political groups provides a carte blanche for eu governments to scale-back personal freedoms with measures that will fail to properly respond to the terrorist threat. instead of pushing for effective measures, the usual suspects who have been continually pushing for mass surveillance and data retention are using the paris attacks as an excuse to bulldoze through these measures, despite any evidence that they will prove effective in countering the terrorist threat. a coherent counter-terrorism strategy would focus on targeted surveillance of real suspects and ensuring security authorities have the means and resources to focus on specific risks and concrete suspicions, to follow any leads immediately, and to efficiently exchange information about dangerous individuals. this is what we should be trying to achieve. there is also a need to tackle radicalisation in schools and prisons. finally we are missing a call for a legal definition of profiling. stepping up mass surveillance will undermine security and is instead a victory for fundamentalists, who are combating precisely such democratic freedoms
