in writing. the internet governance forum (igf) was established in 2005 at the initiative of the united nations to organise multi-stakeholder meetings for democratic and transparent political dialogue. these meetings discuss a wide range of issues related to internet governance, such as net neutrality, data security and improving global internet access. as the igf's mandate expires at the end of 2015, the european parliament calls on the un general assembly to extend its mandate and provide it with more resources. i very much welcome this resolution because we need a sustainable and future-oriented internet policy.
in writing. the role of the internet governance forum is to discuss issues related to internet governance and to make recommendations to the international community. the igf is making an effective contribution (in cooperation with ms and the commission) to the development of a coherent and comprehensive eu strategy and is helping to build a positive and concrete framework for shaping the future of the internet. the current mandate of the igf is coming to an end. the un general assembly will discuss a possible renewal in 2015. i support the renewal of this mandate. the internet is the cornerstone of the digital single market. it promotes innovation, growth, trade, democracy, cultural diversity and human rights. on the economic side, it accounts for almost 11% of union growth and its contribution to gdp is expected to reach 5,7% in 2016. this is therefore a key issue for europe. europe also has a lot of internet-related issues to deal with: regulatory aspects of electronic communications, data security, respect for privacy, net neutrality, protection of fundamental freedoms and human rights online, the fight against radicalism, etc.
in writing. the internet has undoubtedly emerged in recent years as an essential element of political, social and economic life worldwide. as a means of communication, a driver of economic recovery and competitiveness, and a guarantor of non-discriminatory access to knowledge, the internet has a considerable influence on society as a whole. i welcome the adoption of the motion for a resolution renewing the mandate of the internet governance forum. by voting to strengthen the capacity of this forum, we are giving ourselves the means to fight against the misuse of the internet and to anticipate possible deviations. a stable mandate for the forum will enable it to gather the necessary expertise and to act effectively in pursuit of its objectives. it is a step forward in addressing the important challenges posed by the development of the internet, such as the online protection of fundamental freedoms and human rights, the protection of copyright, the enhancement of the safety of children's internet exploration, the fight against cybercrime, the confidentiality of personal data, etc.
in writing. the objective of the internet governance forum (igf) is to implement the mandate of the world summit on the information society in terms of organising forums for political, transparent and multilateral dialogue. the resolution i voted on today on the igf just made it clear that it is the eu's responsibility to support the holding of this forum and to increase the impact of these exchanges in political debates, as this makes it possible to build a positive and concrete framework for shaping, based on a multi-stakeholder strategy, the future of the internet. and this is happening at a time when some are trying to reduce the global connectivity of their citizens through censorship and other restrictions.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution. although the igf does not adopt formal conclusions, it is incumbent on the european union to support the holding of this forum and to increase the influence that these exchanges can have on policy debates, as this allows to build a positive and concrete framework for shaping, based on a multi-stakeholder strategy, the future of the internet. it is important that the member states and the relevant union institutions ensure that the igf remains a key priority for them and that they continue to support the igf and its secretariat, and contribute to the development of an effective and independent organisation capable of fulfilling its mandate and of accompanying the constant evolution of the internet governance model.
in writing. the use of the internet is both de-protective and democratizing, and at the same time threatening. the internet provides information and communication, which unfortunately can also be misused. by adopting this resolution to renew the mandate of the internet governance forum and to increase its capacity, we ensure that it can bring in the necessary expertise and act appropriately. it should, inter alia, protect the confidentiality of personal data and address the fight against cybercrime.
in writing. as a result of the bse crisis, country of origin information has been mandatory for fresh beef and beef products since january 2002. from april 2015, the indication of origin will also be mandatory for fresh, chilled or frozen unprocessed meat of pigs, sheep, goats and poultry as provided for in regulation (eu) no 1169/2011 on food information to consumers. in the wake of recent food scandals, such as the horse meat scandal, the eu is being called upon to restore consumer confidence. providing information on the origin of meat used as an ingredient contributes to better traceability of the food chain and to greater care by food business operators in the selection of their suppliers. the resolution urges the commission to submit a legislative proposal to this effect, requiring the indication of the origin of meat in processed food, in order to increase transparency throughout the food supply chain and to better inform eu consumers. i can only support this view because i believe that consumers of processed food should be able to identify where the meat in the food comes from.
in writing. the indication of the origin of unprocessed beef and beef products has been compulsory since 1 january 2002, following the bse crisis. from april 2015, the indication of the country of origin will also become mandatory for unprocessed pigmeat, goatmeat and poultrymeat. the resolution calls on the committee to draw up legislative proposals to make it compulsory to indicate the origin of meat in processed products. i supported this resolution which aims to increase transparency throughout the food chain and to better inform european consumers.
in writing. the n-va delegation voted against the resolution on the labelling of the origin of meat in processed food. we are in favour of continuing the voluntary labelling of origin, which is already being applied in a cost-effective way. a mandatory labelling of the origin of meat in processed food is unfavourable for a number of reasons. origin labelling indicates the origin but does not improve quality, traceability or prevent fraud. it is also a form of protectionism, which is contrary to the principles of the single european market and is particularly disadvantageous for smaller export-oriented regions such as flanders. the operational and practical feasibility is an obstacle, as are additional administrative costs and burdens which ultimately lead to a higher price for the consumer (who may consider origin labelling to be relatively important but is not willing to pay extra for it). the n-va regrets the lack of realism in the adopted text and believes that a solution to the breach of consumer confidence will not come from additional rules, but from more controls, strict enforcement of existing agreements and heavier sanctions.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution which calls on the commission to come forward with a balanced proposal to make the indication of the country of origin of meat used in processed foods compulsory, on the basis of an impact study and taking into account costs and administrative burdens. the resolution aims to extend the existing system for fresh beef and veal to all fresh meat from april 2015. that's a good measure. labelling increases transparency throughout the food chain. consumers are demanding such transparency. in december 2013, the european commission submitted a report on the possible consequences of mandatory labelling of the country of origin or place of provenance of meat used as an ingredient. she estimated the cost of such labelling to be 15 to 50% more expensive! it did not propose any legislation but suggested, as a possible alternative, eu/non-eu labelling, which was advertised as being cheaper. this resolution follows up on the contents of that report and the figures provided. these figures seem questionable (according to the french ministry of agriculture and ufc que choisir). the resolution therefore calls on the commission to review them.
in writing. i support the european parliament resolution on the indication of the country of origin of meat used in processed foods. parliament called on the commission to submit a proposal to make such an indication compulsory. while consumer confidence has been undermined by the scandals of recent years, the aim is to meet the legitimate expectations of consumers who want to know the origin of the meat they buy. it also means treating fresh meat and processed meat equally. in addition to better information for consumers, this system should also meet the requirements of transparency and traceability throughout the food chain.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution which calls on the european commission to submit a legislative proposal to make the indication of the country of origin of meat used in processed foods compulsory. i believe that the country of origin of meat used as an ingredient in prepared dishes should be indicated on the labelling for several reasons. because such a label would help to ensure better traceability and transparency throughout the food supply chain and would encourage the agri-food industry to be more scrupulous in their choices. because stricter rules on traceability will also enable the authorities to investigate food fraud more effectively (everyone remembers the horse meat lasagna scandal). and finally, because legislation to make the indication of origin for meat in processed products compulsory will also make it possible to better inform european consumers, who are more than 90% of those who consider this new indication important. the european commission will also have to propose labelling, taking care not to create too much complexity for businesses and to ensure that labels are clearly legible for consumers.
the european parliament, on the initiative of the greens, wants the origin of meat to be indicated on the labelling of foodstuffs containing meat. despite strong opposition from the christian democrats and the food industry itself, a majority of the european parliament supports this proposal. a consumer has the right to know where the meat in his pea soup or frozen lasagna comes from. this gives consumers an idea of the length of the food chain from the plate to the plate and allows them to make their choices accordingly. this will encourage producers to choose local production. opponents of labeling meat in processed products as ready meals say that these rules will increase the price of products by more than 10 percent. i suspect these statistics are a bit of a stretch. it is absurd that under the guise of too much bureaucracy a producer does not need to know where his meat comes from. especially after last year's horse meat scandal, it would be good for the food industry to be more open about their production processes. the european parliament is now forwarding the proposal to the european commission. the commission must ultimately decide whether to take action and come forward with legislative proposals.
in writing. is the lack of information about the origin of the meats on your plate such as ravioli, hash, dumplings, ham pizzas or the mysterious frica (n) delles over? this is the demand of the european parliament, which was voted on by a majority this afternoon. the commission refuses to mention the origin of these meats, claiming that this would cause additional costs for consumers, when the truth is quite different, only 0.67% for the companies that carry out this labelling. we are demanding legislation on this matter and controls to avoid a further breakdown in consumer confidence, as happened after the horse lasagna crisis. 90% of citizens think it is important that the origin of meat is mentioned as a food ingredient. it is to be expected that the commission's officials are among the remaining 10%. the commission, acting as the spokesman for the companies, refuses to mention the origin of the meat because of the additional cost to the citizen. the commission's argument therefore seems to be more dictated by the agri-food sector than by the interests of citizens' rights! the labelling of origin is compulsory for fresh meat, but it is also the case for prepared dishes.
in writing. the single european market is threatened by the call for mandatory country-based origin labelling. europe sets the standards for food safety, quality and sustainable production. on the other hand, greater awareness through the mandatory mention of 'made in the eu' is desirable. i would have liked, however, to see the resolution remove the administrative and financial burden of mandatory labelling. the resolution as adopted will leave it to the commission to avoid our agricultural industry being subjected to further administrative burdens by compulsory labelling, taking into account the safety of the food chain.
in writing. the acp-eu joint parliamentary assembly (jpa) is made up of representatives of 77 african, caribbean and pacific (acp) states and 77 members of the european parliament (eu). it is the 'parliament' of the cotonou agreement concluded between these acp states and the member states of the european union. it outlines the intergovernmental relationship between the contracting parties in the fields of development aid, trade, investment and human rights. the ppv meets alternately in an acp state and a european country to promote the north-south relationship. as the only interparliamentary assembly set up under an international agreement, i congratulate the ppv on the work it has done. i also welcome the fact that it has become an important forum for open and honest debate on issues of vital importance to development cooperation.
in writing. the acp-eu joint parliamentary assembly plays an important role as the only multilateral interparliamentary assembly established under the cotonou agreements. this allows for an open dialogue with the acp countries on, inter alia, the implementation of development cooperation under the edf and the application of the epas. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work. the resolution also calls on the pa to strengthen the dialogue on human rights and calls for the replacement of the cotonou agreement to include an explicit reference to non-discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation or gender identity. it also stressed that the post-cotonou discussions should be an opportunity to analyse in depth the failures and successes of the current agreement in terms of sustainable socioeconomic development in the acp countries. in this respect, it insists that any epa should be included in the development objectives in order to reduce poverty and guarantee fundamental human rights.
in writing. the acp-eu joint parliamentary assembly is a unique body, firmly rooted in relations based on mutual respect and understanding. it is a forum for discussing all kinds of issues, from current issues such as gay rights, violence against women, governance issues, traceability of natural resources, etc. in view of all these debates, it can be said that this assembly has gained a good experience and can boast of good results. the acp-eu jpa normally meets in plenary session twice a year: in europe, in the country holding the eu presidency, and in an acp country. we are seeing that european countries are finding it increasingly difficult to honour this commitment. i take this opportunity to call on the authorities concerned in the member states to assume their responsibilities by agreeing to hold these meetings. this year we will have to debate the future of this unique institutional structure. we must define the continuation of what is in history an unprecedented model of political cooperation. political dialogue is the basis of our relations.
in writing. in my view, the acp-eu joint parliamentary assembly (one of the joint institutions of the cotonou agreement) is a forum for open and democratic dialogue between meps and acp parliamentarians on the implementation of the agreement, in particular the monitoring of development cooperation under the european development fund (edf) and the conclusion and application of economic partnership agreements. i am therefore pleased that the report emphasizes the crucial role of national parliaments, local authorities and non-state actors in the acp countries in the preparation and monitoring of national and regional strategy papers and in the implementation of the edf. i would add that i voted in favour of the amendment requesting that the european parliament be given the political responsibility to take account of the opinion of the acp parliaments on the outcome of the negotiations on the economic partnership agreements before giving its assent.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my distinguished colleague, mr charles goerens. the quality of its work has helped the assembly to establish itself as a key player in acp-eu relations and cooperation. it proactively continued to monitor political, economic and social developments in the acp countries with a view to promoting the development goals and respect for all human rights and fundamental freedoms, including respect for fundamental social rights, democracy based on the rule of law and transparent and accountable governance, which are integral to sustainable development. acp-eu cooperation is supported by a legally binding system and the existence of common institutions. it is important that the app continues to monitor developments very closely to ensure that its voice is heard when considering the different options and alternatives to be put in place after the expiry of the cotonou agreement in 2020. whatever the outcome of the acp-eu post-2020 negotiations, the parliamentary dimension of the acp-eu partnership agreement must not be diluted, but must continue to play a major role after 2020.
the acp-eu joint parliamentary assembly is a unique forum where europe and the atlantic, caribbean and pacific countries speak and listen to each other on an equal footing. the european parliament is the body which discusses all the major and topical issues. the general assembly meets twice a year, once in an acp country and once in the country holding the eu presidency. as the resolution shows, we must look to the future of this institution this year. i think we should preserve this unique form of debate.

vice-president of the commission. - mr president, first i would really like to thank you for today’s debate, but especially i would like to thank you for the previous consultations we had in the committee on industry, research and energy (itre), the committee on the environment, public health and food safety (envi), and in many of the bilaterals where you give us very valuable advice on how the energy union should be constructed. therefore, having listened to your comments, i can say that we very much have overlapping priorities when it comes to the energy union. i think that there was overwhelming support for our key priorities like guaranteeing the security of supply, working much more on the completion of the internal energy market, putting the energy-efficiency-first principle into real use, continuing our decarbonisation efforts and being very focused in what we do in research and innovation in the field of energy. some of you have been saying that, regarding the dimension of the security of supplies, we could do more. of course we could, but i think, as you have read in our strategy, that we are taking the energy security issue to a higher level. probably never before have you heard such ambitious language as regards the ex ante check of the compatibility of the intergovernmental agreements with the european acquis. never before has the commission dared to push for much more transparency when it comes to long-term gas contracts, and never before have we been so clear that we need to diversify not only the routes but also the sources of our energy. we have been trying to present it in the new holistic way, because we have linked it very much with other dimensions and we are very clear in stating that we do not have to import the energy we save. it means we are increasing our energy security. mr eickhout and mr turmes have been very strong in underlining the importance of the efficiency-first principle, and i agree with them. i think that if you read our strategy in greater detail, you will see that we are not only doing lip service to this principle, we are making this principle operational. we are clearly describing how we are going to use it when we are discussing energy infrastructure projects and how we are going to link it with the funding for infrastructure projects in the future, and i think that we will see that in real life, this principle will be applied, and the commission will be the first to support its full implementation. i would say 90% of the honourable members have been referring to the importance of infrastructure and infrastructure development, and i think they are right. we cannot have an internal energy market without proper infrastructure, without proper interconnections. i think that, also in the commission, we agreed that we need to improve the governance of how we manage, how we follow up on our infrastructure projects, how we can make greater coherence in funding from different sources. we have projects of common interest, we have structural funds in the new member states, we have the connecting europe facility, and now, thanks to our president, we have the new juncker investment plan, which of course would be key for this big investment, which must be channelled to cross-border infrastructure. we will ensure that we have a much better governance system making sure that the infrastructure interconnections are built on time, with the support of the citizens and the member states, and they will make the free flow of energies in the european union a reality. i very much appreciate all of you who highlighted the issue of the energy poverty of vulnerable citizens in europe, and again i think that for the first time we have devoted such an important part of the energy union strategy to this problem. we recognise that we have a problem with energy poverty, and we are also proposing how this should be tackled. we should increase the competition on the internal energy market, because it should drive the prices down. at the same time we have to have a special instrument which would help, via social means, the most vulnerable citizens to take care of the cost, because in the europe of the 21st century we should not have such a high percentage of citizens who cannot afford to pay their energy bills. i also would like to reassure mr liese and other honourable members of this parliament on governance. the commission will launch dynamic and robust governance for the energy union, for our climate action and, as i said, also for our infrastructural build-up, and of course parliament will be a key partner in this effort. if you study carefully our roadmap, our action plan and all the legislative proposals which are proposed there, it is very clear that they have to adopt it through the ordinary legislative procedure, where parliament is, of course, a key partner as co-legislator. if you will allow me to react also to some questions related to research and innovation. mr duncan was, apparently, reading one of the previous versions of the energy union communication, because in the final text i would say that this policy is very much focused: we are focusing on four very concrete areas of research and innovation. we want to remain the world leader in the next generation of renewable technologies, including storage – how to store the energy which is produced by the renewable sources. we want to remain leaders in this market. we want to help our cities to become smart, and we also want to focus our research on how to make our transport much more sustainable. if you will allow me, i should like to conclude with some information on what the new agency for the coordination of energy regulators (acer) should do. i think that when we are talking about completion of the internal energy market and about much more cross-border connection, it is very clear that this dimension of cross-border cooperation would be much more important than before. i think that it is very clear that we need to have the possibility to adopt many more decisions at european level. we want to do it within the framework of the current treaties; we believe proposed by mr kofod. to conclude, i would like to thank you for your support, and i would highlight the comment made by mr buzek that the proposal is here: the strategy was adopted. what we need now the rapporteur. mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, it is with great pride that i present to you this report on equality between women and men, or rather, the reduction of inequalities. this report is the result of a long and intensive work with the fictitious rapporteurs, whom i would like to congratulate: mrs gabriel for the ppe group, mrs bilbao barandica for the alde group, mrs vallina for the gue/ngl group, mrs lunacek and mr urtasun for the greens/efa group, mrs aiuto for the efdd group and mrs von storch for the ecr group. in fact, it is their work that makes this report effective, concise and structured. it starts with a very simple observation: while we are in the aftermath of international women's rights day, equality is still far away. indeed, at the rate we are going in europe, we would have to wait until 2038 to reach the target of a 75% employment rate for women, and 2084 for equal pay. but let us rejoice, parity in national parliaments, in the european institutions and in the boards of european companies should be possible in 20 years! it is time to go beyond good words to action. this report recommends a set of measures to be taken to achieve real equality much faster. we therefore urge the european institutions and the member states to include the gender dimension in policy-making, including in the context of the european semester, the budget and the allocation of funds. this is a prerequisite for achieving the europe 2020 objectives, which are still a long way off. the second point i would like to stress is that the member states and the european institutions must implement better inclusion strategies to address the gap between pension rates and reduce the risk of poverty which is much more common among women, and single mothers in particular. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the future of the european union. i would like to point out that equal participation of men and women in the labour market would lead to an increase in gross domestic product of more than 12% by 2030. this is an economic argument to consider as we are still struggling in times of crisis. employment is essential, but there is more to life than work. promoting work-life balance for men and women must be a priority, including by investing in childcare and care facilities, and by supporting the updating of the maternity leave directive and the creation of paternity leave. real equality between women and men requires respect and non-violence, and in particular non-violence in the home. i therefore urge the member states to ratify the istanbul convention as soon as possible. only eight eu member states have already done so. what are the others waiting for? it is also essential to create a european year dedicated solely to the fight against violence against women. i have, moreover, together with other colleagues, including many fictitious rapporteurs, launched a written initiative on this subject, which i invite all my colleagues present and those who have left the chamber to sign. we also need to fight gender stereotypes, because it is from childhood that inequality develops, becomes alive, and this is in all aspects of our society. the proliferation of laws will be of no use if they are not supported by a public opinion that is aware of the issue of gender. finally, the report recalls the right of women to control their own bodies. i know, ladies and gentlemen, that many of you have received messages from certain lobbies which are contrary to our values and to women's rights. but this report is not just about that. it is equality and reducing inequality that we really need to focus on. i therefore call on all members to support this report, which is a strong signal to the european institutions, to national governments but also and above all to the citizens, especially since the report was rejected last year. that was a bad signal from parliament. in conclusion, i would like to thank the collaborators who have been very valuable to me in this matter: marie ramot, my assistant, and emmanuelle le texier, from the s&d group, who have really made sure that this work is well supported. the rapporteur. mr president, first of all i would like to say to mr chauprade, who has already left, that i am not french like him, as he said. i don't mind being called french, but i'm a belgian elected official. i am one of the 40% of belgians whose mother tongue is french. but more seriously in relation to this debate: two particular points, often raised, and a general observation. first, the quotas. we have talked about this a lot, and the first person to say it was mrs atkinson who said: 'we don't need quotas. and in our own country, ukip, we are setting a good example". i notice she can't do the math, because ukip is 6 women out of 23 elected, that's 30%. this is less than the average for many political groups. in this respect, i would like to congratulate the five star movement in its political group, which includes 8 women out of 17. in other words, almost half of the elected officials are elected officials. on the subject of quotas, i would like to pay tribute to a man: he is a european conservative named ansgar gabrielsen, the norwegian minister for industry and the economy. in 2001, it found that in 1993 there were 3% of women on the boards of large companies in norway. when he became minister, he said, "this has to change". he introduced quotas to the great general criticism, especially from the conservatives, and what happened? in 2008, there were 43 per cent women on the boards of large companies in norway. that's the highest rate in the world. we had to have quotas. they are a necessary evil, but they can no longer be questioned, since society is not evolving as fast as it should. secondly, the principle of subsidiarity, which is often mentioned. we are not here to initiate it, we are talking about an own-initiative report. so we are not going to change the laws in the member states, we are not going to interfere in their internal politics, in their jurisdiction. however, it is normal that when we address women's rights, and therefore inequality, we can address all rights and take stock at european level. if we do not discuss this issue in this house, we will not discuss it anywhere. i would like to thank all those who have generally welcomed the report. i hope that it will be voted on tomorrow, because it is important to talk about and focus on equality between women and men, and especially on inequality, by trying to reduce it more quickly than is the case today.
president. - mr president, we all know that the health costs of endocrine disruptors are enormous. this has already been proved by studies by the world health organisation and unip, this has been proved by the study by professor kortekamp, which was requested by the commission's dg envi, and this has also been proved by the study which was made public last week and to which you and mr pargneaux referred. the scientists say very clearly that the cost is at least 157 billion, 1.23% of the gross national product. according to these scientists, hormone disruptors do indeed cause lower iq, more obesity in adults and at least 5% of all cases of autism. so the situation is very serious. the european parliament has always supported the recommendations of professor kortekamp. there is a need for clarity on the definition of endocrine disruptors. in 2009 and 2011, the council and the parliament already made provision for interim criteria, but in 2009 the commission was also given the task of coming up with permanent criteria by the end of december 2013. in the meantime, another five years have passed, five years of debate, five years of lobbying from industry to the highest levels of the european commission. when it comes to hormone-disrupting substances, incompetent scientists have been responsible for sowing doubt, a tactic we also know from the tobacco industry. murder and arson was the cry of industry. the secretary-general of the commission, mrs day, decided to initiate an impact study. but that 's incredible . an impact study on scientific facts! it's like going to the source of cancer and asking the industry that makes the cancer-causing products: how do they cause cancer? for the greens/efa group mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, europe is a rich continent, not only in its history and diversity but also in its financial wealth. and yet europe is failing to invest, to plan for the future. the european union is not only a political force, but also a political force. investing in the energy transition - there is a lot of talk these days about the energy union - investing in education, research, innovation, the conditions for european competitiveness, investing in the restoration of our natural resources, the restoration of our social cohesion, is a matter of survival for our european union. yet these investments do not materialise. why would you do that? because for the last 20 years, the dominant dogma has been dictatorship and the maximisation of short-term profit. twenty years of financial deregulation, of financialization of everything and everything in the sole logic of profit, of its maximization, of the immediate return for the investor. how dare we call investors banks, investment funds, insurance companies, individuals who "invest" in companies for a microsecond? how can you talk about investors when even the most conservative of the insurance companies tell you they don't want to hold a stock or a bond for more than five years? so that is the question we have to answer. what can i do? this text, mr lamassoure, is a step in the right direction but a step of complete modesty. the aim is to attract investors to investment funds which are designed to operate over the long term. but i am surprised, in any case, that the council has refused - and mrs vestager has stressed this - the quota for european investment. we were very modest, we said that in order to be labelled as european long-term investment funds, 60% of the investments of these investment funds had to be invested in europe. the council considered that this was a red line which could not be crossed. what does the council want? does he want to favour investors or to favour investment in europe? i think that by refusing the quota the council has shown which side it is on. we shall vote for this text, but we believe that if we really want to revive longterm investment in europe, other measures are essential. first, retail banks should be distinguished from deemed investment banks. when you force the banks that collect the savings to do only one thing, which is to lend money to the real economy, and you close the casino to them, the entire european savings will ipso facto go to the real economy. secondly, we must have the courage to tackle a series of financial products whose sole purpose is to squeeze the lime out of the planet and the lime out of our societies to extract the maximum short-term profit from them. finally, a genuine european investment plan must be drawn up. i would like to draw two figures together: 13 billion is the public money that the juncker plan promises to mobilise, and it is one hundredth of the fraud and tax evasion in europe. if we were serious about fighting tax fraud and tax evasion, that's a trillion euros that would be going into the public coffers. blue-card answer.– it is becoming a habit for us to dialogue in this room. yes, i agree. i do not believe that 100% of the economy should be driven by public investment. public investment is needed, and that was the last of my three points. the first point was about the separation of banks, and why is that? well, because we want private savings. here i am speaking about private savings; we want them to be funnelled to the real economy. we need private investment. but what i have witnessed in my 22 years’ career in the private sector is that the time horizon of private investors has become ever shorter, not even for a quarter, but for a month or a week or a microsecond. i do not call that investment. so yes, i want private money to be invested, and private profits are legitimate as long as they result from value creation for society.

in writing. ‒ i welcome the granting of a financial contribution from the european globalisation adjustment fund, which the polish authorities had requested from the eu in the wake of the redundancies in the company and in two of zachem's suppliers. the fund was set up to provide additional support for workers who are suffering from the consequences of major structural changes in world trade patterns. the fund finances personalised measures for the reintegration of jobseekers, encourages self-employment and business creation, provides mobility grants and grants for disadvantaged or elderly workers. the company could not have foreseen the huge rate of redundancies due to its main supplier of tdi (toluyl diisocyanate) to the market. however, the low-cost production and the low-cost transportation can be interpreted as the reason for the 615 redundancies. it is therefore welcome that the eu has accepted poland's request and is providing funds to support the displaced workers, in the hope that the measures taken will help them to secure permanent, long-term and thus stable employment.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament has just voted on four requests for financial contributions via the european globalisation adjustment fund to help 2 498 belgian workers who were subject to collective redundancies in 2013-14 by several large companies in belgium in the steel, glass and construction machinery sectors. among these were 1 285 former arcelormittal workers in liège. as a belgian and as the alde group coordinator for the european parliament's committee on budgets, the body responsible for this type of request, i have followed very closely the progress of these european financial contributions and i am glad to have been able to give my full support to them. of course, they will not replace the jobs that all these workers have lost, but i hope they can help them cope with the difficulties they are going through. the priority now is to help these workers get back into work through appropriate training and the recognition of skills and competences acquired during their working careers. this is what the globalisation adjustment fund is helping to achieve.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of the decision on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund. nearly €1.6 million was allocated to finance the conversion, training and upgrading of entrepreneurship. this appropriation is intended to cover the cost of the staff of the european parliament's committee on budgetary control and the cost of the staff of the committee on budgetary control.
in writing. ‒ a europe that is close to its citizens is also, and above all, a europe that acts when they are directly affected by economic redundancies. this is the case today with the activation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) mobilisation mechanism voted this afternoon by the european parliament: 1 285 workers made redundant by arcelor mittal will receive aid totalling eur 1 591 486. this fund is the european contribution of 60% of the needs to support former arcelor mittal employees in their job search and, more broadly, in their career reorientation. it cannot be used to keep firms in business, to help them modernise or restructure. as is the case in most economic redundancies, people are affected in a sector that is experiencing the full force of global competition. a necessary but not sufficient boost to preserve european industrial policy, one of the union's main economic health vectors from which every member state and every citizen can benefit.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of mobilising the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) following the redundancies at arcelormittal in liège, as these contributions are a valuable aid to enable the conversion and reclassification of workers, in particular through training adapted to the opportunities of the labour market. nevertheless, the loss of jobs in many sectors is a painful reminder that such aid is not a panacea and that a serious policy of preventing and anticipating restructuring is essential. more broadly, europe needs to put in place a real, coordinated industrial policy focused on creating sustainable jobs in sectors of the future. in addition, the procedures for granting the egf should be accelerated and simplified to enable workers made redundant to cope with difficulties as soon as they arise.

in writing. ‒ i welcome the compromise because it not only makes trucks safer, but also makes an important contribution to environmental protection thanks to aerodynamic features.
in writing. ‒ regulations should be introduced on the permissible dimensions and weights of road vehicles in order to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and improve road safety. this better regulation will also make it possible to adapt legislation to technological advances and to the needs of the market in general, but it will also strengthen european standards in order to facilitate intermodal transport operations.
in writing. ‒ the aim is to amend directive 96/53/ec to improve the aerodynamics of vehicles and their energy efficiency, while continuing to improve road safety. the proposal provides for derogations from the maximum vehicle dimensions, allows for an increase in the weight of electrically or hybrid driven vehicles by one tonne, aims to facilitate the development of intermodal transport, confirms that the cross-border use of longer vehicles is legal for journeys crossing only one border, if the two member states concerned already allow it, and finally adds new provisions to enable the supervisory authorities to better detect infringements and to harmonise the administrative penalties applicable to them. since this proposal does not affect the budget of the european union and since it was necessary to amend directive 96/53/ec because of a number of shortcomings, i decided to support this proposal and to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ more security, less greenhouse gas emissions this is the newsletter that european trucks should soon be presenting following the european parliament's vote this morning approving amendments to european provisions on the design of heavy goods vehicles. two things: trucks, buses and coaches produce about a quarter of the co2 emissions from road transport in the union and about 5% of the total greenhouse gas emissions and are often involved in serious traffic accidents, as today's news shows again. these vehicles must meet strict size and weight standards to protect infrastructure and ensure road safety. today, with the evolution of technology, these 1996 rules are obsolete. the new provisions will enable manufacturers to design trucks that are more environmentally and safely performing without reducing their load capacity. for example, better aerodynamics would reduce their greenhouse gas emissions by 7 to 10 percent and rounder cabs would reduce dangerous blind spots. european trucks will therefore soon be safer, cleaner and more efficient.
in writing. ‒ yesterday we adopted, at second reading, the revision of directive 96/53/ec on the maximum dimensions and weights of lorries (also known as 'mega lorries'). the text adopted aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and improve road safety. it allows, on the one hand, the addition of retractable aerodynamic devices to the rear of vehicles and the installation of rounded cabs, which will now offer the driver a better overall view (which i welcome because every year there are on average between 350 and 400 accidents between a truck and a weak user, of which about 30 are directly due to the blind spot). and secondly, the new rules are designed to make trucks more environmentally friendly. these new types of heavy duty trucks are expected to be in circulation from 2022. it is now up to the council to approve this text in april.
in writing. ‒ the n-va supports the new directive on vehicle dimensions and weights. the previous directive was adopted in 1996 and was therefore in urgent need of revision. the updated directive aims to improve the safety of all road users and to achieve environmental gains by focusing on the energy efficiency of vehicles. although the revision certainly includes steps in the right direction, the n-va regrets the continuing legal uncertainty for cross-border transport by ecocombines. these ecocombis were an important part of the original proposal of the european commission, but were unfortunately scrapped by a majority in the european parliament and the council. a missed opportunity. in flanders, the first ecocombi hit the road earlier this year. the n-va remains fully behind the pilot projects and remains committed to further cooperation with neighbouring countries such as the netherlands.
in writing. ‒ we insist on the objective of moving freight from road to rail and river transport and welcome the unanimous vote in the committee on transport. this is a "positive signal" for the fight against climate change. mega trucks are no longer relevant, except in very localized cases. the text is generally very concerned with the safety of road users and takes into account the preservation of the environment, with the promotion of alternative fuels and the aerodynamics of vehicles. the road is still too important for the transport of goods in europe, but parliament is sending a positive signal today for the fight against climate change!
in writing. ‒ the objective of this long-term investment fund (eltif) is to ensure smart, sustainable and inclusive growth in the european union. it finances long-term projects outside the banking sector, which are intended to contribute to infrastructure or research projects. the creation of this new regulatory framework is to be welcomed because it both protects retail and private investors and addresses the reluctance of banks. society and the real economy benefit from each other.
in writing. ‒ the long-term investment fund is a proposal for a new financing framework to enable private companies to invest in the real economy of the european union and thus create jobs through growth. at the moment, reinvestment in productive investment is essential to revive the economy and employment. it is therefore essential that europe takes up and promotes these projects, particularly in the context of the horizon/europe 2020 objectives.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of the provisions to address the reluctance of banks to lend to smes and to certain research projects. smes are the engine of our european economy. they represent 99% of enterprises and employ more than 100 million europeans. they need funding to remain competitive and innovative. the creation of european long-term investment funds (eltifs) will put funds of non-bank origin directly into the real economy, contributing to long-term projects, in particular for infrastructure, intellectual property or research.
in writing. ‒ desperate search for private capital: this is the most common activity in the european institutions today. in view of the bleak state of public finances, combined with the difficulty of the states in generating new revenue, a new path is emerging, the one chosen by the commission and confirmed in the lamassoure report: mobilizing private capital through the creation of this new financing instrument, the european long-term investment funds (eltif). a fund that would invest, for example, in unlisted companies or european infrastructure projects. the commission estimates that around €2 billion of private investment is needed to launch its policy of major works by 2020: the trans-european transport network by rail, road or canals, as well as projects on innovation and digitalisation. while potential investors for whom eltifs can provide a stable source of income have been identified, such as pension funds, insurance companies, foundations and municipalities, the keys to success have yet to be invented. it will take a lot of persuasion from the juncker commission to convince these investors to hold off on their investment in the european project for a while.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on european long-term investment funds and i followed the recommendation of my political group on this matter.
in writing. ‒ in light of the benefits that a reduction in transaction costs for card payments brings to the eu internal market and its consumers, this initiative is very welcome. i am also pleased that the competition rules are being applied consistently in the area of clearing charges.
in writing. ‒ the fees that banks charge retailers for processing customer payments will be capped by this measure. the ceiling will apply to national and cross-border payments and should result in reduced costs for consumers. this is good news for the transparency of payment charges and for the consumer who will see his costs reduced.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation limiting the fees charged by banks for credit and debit card transactions. currently, merchants must accept all cards under the conditions set by the banks. the calculation of the fees charged to traders varies from country to country and from bank to bank. the whole system lacked transparency. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of consumers in the event of a breach of the directive. for purchases by debit card, these charges will be limited to 0.2% in a cross-border transaction. for domestic debit card transactions, a transitional period of five years has been set. after this period, the fees will be limited to 0,2% or eur 0,05 per transaction. i have wholeheartedly supported the compromise proposed by the rapporteur because the regulation is in the interests of consumers and traders. it should mainly benefit buyers as a result of lower transaction costs. however, traders will be free to pass on or not to the selling price the reduction in payment costs resulting from these ceilings.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament voted today on the interinstitutional agreement on the regulation on the capping of multilateral interchange fees (mifs) for payments by immediate debit and credit cards. as a reminder, mifs are paid by a merchant's bank to the bank of the holder of the payment card used for the transaction. they are allowed in some member states at different maximum levels (up to 1.5%), but are prohibited elsewhere. consumer organisations point out how much these mifs provide excessive revenue to the mastercard and visa networks and how they are ultimately reflected in the price of goods purchased by the consumer. the vote on this report should therefore be a game changer and i welcome this because, under the new provisions, retailers who choose a card system will now only have to accept cards from that system which are subject to the cap provisions. by exercising this right, they could accept a reduced range of cards, but the capped fees should also reduce costs for both retailers and customers (for example, for all credit card payments, the cap will now be set at 0.3% of the transaction value).
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report with great conviction. the eu is putting limits on the excessive costs of accepting payment cards. the agreement between member states and parliament to set a legal ceiling on the fees that banks and credit card companies can charge is a good thing. retailers in europe are overpaying €6 billion a year for accepting payment cards because there is no healthy competition in the payment market. consumers are paying the price in the end. this legislation will put an end to that. at the moment, visa and mastercard have a duopoly on the european market. these companies and the banks that issue their cards make a lot of money from this lack of competition at the expense of retailers who end up passing on higher prices to consumers. the payment industry's fierce lobby has not been successful. parliament has defended the interests of consumers rather than the excessive profits of these credit card giants. the maximum rate of 0.3% of the purchase price for credit card transactions and 0.2% for payments directly debited from the account will apply. however, member states may also choose to fix a fixed amount of up to 5 cents per transaction.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the text, convinced that safe, efficient, competitive and innovative electronic payments are essential if consumers, traders and businesses are to enjoy the full benefits of the internal market, especially as global trade becomes electronic. the fragmentation of the internal market is detrimental to competitiveness, growth and job creation within the union. in order to ensure the proper functioning of the internal market, it is necessary to remove direct and indirect obstacles to the proper functioning and completion of an integrated electronic payments market, in which there is no distinction between national and cross-border payments.

in writing. ‒ more than 100 years after the first international women's day, we are still discussing the same unresolved issues: equal pay for equal work, maternity leave, workers' rights, violence against women. it is time to make way for a society where everyone has equal rights and equal opportunities. every week we are confronted with news about the inequality between men and women and the prevailing stereotypes. an oecd study shows that girls do better than boys in secondary education, but still underperform in subjects such as math, science or computer science because parents and teachers unconsciously perpetuate gender inequality. in india, authorities are trying to ban the documentary "india's daughter", which interviews one of the perpetrators of the gang rape on a bus in late 2012. this is a violation of freedom of expression and a denial of how deeply rooted violence against women is in society. the numbers speak for themselves: women earn 16.4% less than men for equal work in 2012. women's employment has increased but is mainly part-time with adverse effects on social rights and pension accumulation. that is why i support the tarabella report.

in writing. ‒ this report assesses the competition and competitiveness policy within the european union, which is extremely important in the current crisis. the report seeks to ensure fair competition and calls for action to combat dumping in the labour market. it also addresses fragmentation behaviours in the union's digital market.
in writing. ‒ i voted against paragraph 85, not because i am against fair competition, of course, but because such a general incentive in practice sometimes goes too far. in the case of port services, we must make a clear distinction between the economic activities of a port company and the public tasks it performs. the latter are not subject to the competition rules and we must therefore be able to expressly guard their public nature. such a general encouragement as that in paragraph 85 to the commission and the member states, which ignores the nuanced way in which we are supposed to apply competition rules, could not therefore count on my support.
in writing. competition policy is crucial in the current context in order to restore the european union's competitiveness on the world stage. i fully support the words of the commissioner responsible for competition, margrethe vestager, when she insists on the need to strictly enforce the competition rules, to fight cartels, to investigate abuses of dominant positions, to monitor the financial sector. it is vital to develop a competition policy in full respect of the treaties. it is about consumer welfare.
in writing. ‒ without a free and effective competition policy, the european union will not be able to impose its model on the global economy, namely fair rules for all economic actors and a significant share for smes, the main creators of innovation and jobs. that is to say, the importance of proper enforcement of the competition rules in the union as underlined in the messerschmidt report voted on this afternoon. competition policy must benefit consumers, businesses and society as a whole. it is also important to emphasise that certain sectors are strategic and require an appropriate union policy: the digital single market, the energy sector, industry and transport sectors. a logical focus on areas undergoing rapid change where, in the digital field, us companies have a near monopoly and, in the more traditional industries (automotive, shipyards, steel or robotics), asian companies occupy the pole position. if europe is to move up the gear, it must also know which direction to take. this is why the rapporteur's proposal to have current competition policy initiatives assessed to meet the challenges of globalisation is welcome.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament adopted yesterday by a large majority (526 votes in favour, 108 against and 59 abstentions) the report on the annual report on competition policy, which specifically targets the giant google. the resolution also calls for the eu to take action to combat the spread of the virus and to ensure that the virus is contained in the body of the person who is infected. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competition' in the context of the directive. to this end, the european commission was asked to take strong action against obstacles to competition, based on the principle of non-discrimination.
in writing. ‒ competition policy is an integral part of the union's genetic code. the three instruments of competition policy, established by the treaty of rome, are designed to maintain a level playing field and an open and dynamic market. this encourages companies to seek success on their own merits (price, quality and innovation) in order to meet the needs, preferences and wishes of intermediate and final consumers. the european social market economy would be unthinkable without competition. but i would like to make it clear that this cannot be possible without strict respect for consumers and workers, and that respect for labour and human rights must prevail!
in writing. ‒ the european political project is based on the free movement of goods, services, capital and people. this is only possible in a free and open competition. this competition policy is at the service of firms, consumers and society as a whole. only if it is efficient and free can it serve as a model for the rest of the world and thus contribute to a global free economy as a model of fairness, sustainability and with a focus on smes, employment and innovation. i fully support the rapporteur's proposal to have the current competition policy initiatives evaluated in order to meet the challenges of globalisation.

in writing. the policy of the european central bank plays a key role in the outcome of the financial crisis which has affected the whole of europe. it helps to maintain price stability in the euro area and thus stabilise inflation. it is responsible for the prudential supervision of credit institutions established in the euro area, thus contributing to the safety and soundness of the banking system and to the stability of the financial system in the european union and in each euro area member state. it is worth recalling that mario draghi's plan to counter the collapse of monetary union is to be welcomed. the aim is above all to try to get back to an inflation rate of around 2%. finally, it should be stressed that there is a genuine and transparent dialogue between parliament and the ecb. the president of the ecb presents the annual report of the institution in plenary and takes part in a regular monetary dialogue with the committee on economic affairs.
in writing. i voted in favour of the text. however, i remain deeply concerned about the continued sluggishness of economic activity, with euro area gdp in 2013 showing negative growth for the second year in a row, and weak growth in the first three quarters of 2014, accompanied in many euro area member states by high unemployment rates that threaten the stability of the euro area and undermine popular and political support for the european project. moreover, i can only note the steady decline in the inflation rate in the euro area since 2011, which is accompanied by differences in inflation rates between member states. the significant gap between the ecb's explicit objective of keeping inflation below, but close to, 2% over the medium term and the current interest rates close to zero or even negative in several euro area member states should be highlighted. the risk, acknowledged by the ecb president, that current deflationary trends will undermine the anchoring of medium to longterm inflation expectations is real.

in writing. ‒ this report formally endorses the amended agreement establishing the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean (gfcm). the gfcm is a regional fisheries management organisation whose role is to promote the development, conservation, sound management and enhancement of living marine resources, as well as the sustainable development of aquaculture in the mediterranean and black seas. the procedure to amend the text of the agreement establishing the gfcm was launched in 2013 following a performance review carried out in 2011. the main changes introduced are: a clearer explanation of the object of the agreement establishing the gfcm, in order to define what would be a sustainable use of marine biological resources from the biological, social, economic and environmental point of view; better definition of the functions of the gfcm, including the promotion of common fisheries management through multiannual management plans, the establishment of fishing zones with regulated access, and the collection and dissemination of data, as well as sanctions and dispute settlement mechanisms.

in writing. the 2016 budget set its guidelines: to foster growth by supporting job creation, business and entrepreneurship, to show solidarity both within the union and towards third countries, and to put european finances in order by tackling arrears and reforming the union's revenue system. the commission will have to present a plan to reduce the backlog of payments, which is constantly increasing. it is time for a thorough reform of the union's own resources. we give our full support to the efforts of the monti group.
in writing. ‒ growth, solidarity and paying the bills are the three priorities set out by the european parliament in its political guidelines for the 2016 budget. it is a response to the new european situation set in motion by the juncker commission, which wants to act in the areas essential for europe's future: investment, recovery and job creation. two points seem very important to me: - to focus on the 20 million smes, which represent 99% of enterprises in the european union, and to create the conditions for them to become the main job creators again; - to remedy the slow take-off of the european youth employment initiative. the release of €1 billion proposed by the belgian employment commissioner is therefore welcome. solidarity is the other strong point of the resolution adopted this afternoon: economic solidarity by maximising the use of the structural funds (33% of the european budget) and by reducing regional disparities. humanitarian solidarity also means that the burden of migration flows should be better distributed among the countries of the union. finally, it is essential to reduce arrears, which reached eur 24.7 billion at the end of 2014: paying your creditors is as important as cleaning up your public finances!
in writing. ‒ encouraging growth by supporting job creation, businesses and entrepreneurship, showing solidarity both within the union and towards third countries and... tackling payment arrears and reforming the union's own resources system: these are the priorities adopted by the european parliament yesterday by a large majority (484 votes in favour, 188 against and 36 abstentions) for the negotiations on the 2016 budget. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. we also reiterated our commitment to hold at least three interinstitutional meetings on payments this year. because... at the end of 2014, the amount of unpaid invoices had reached eur 24.7 billion for the cohesion programmes for the period 2007-2013 alone. finally, we have advocated - once again - a thorough reform of the european union's financing system. the ball is now in the commission's court, which is due to present its draft budget for 2016 by the end of may.

in writing. ‒ the report clearly shows that the commission has increased its efforts to combat fraud linked to its financial interests, but that the problem persists. in fact, fraud in the spending of money is on the rise. in terms of expenditure, regional development funds are primarily intended for job creation and social welfare for citizens. as mayor of a municipality benefiting from these aids, i can testify to their decisive impact in ensuring a better future for our people. we cannot tolerate the misuse of this aid for a major social purpose! in terms of revenue, fraud, in addition to the loss of resources it represents for the union, can only feed smuggling, international crime and money laundering. we cannot therefore tolerate it. i also think that the fight against corruption is essential. the latest barometer by the ngo transparency international points out that this scourge is raging in the eu. the commission's initiatives can only be encouraged. but also better cooperation between member states, rapid approval of the proposal for a pif directive and the implementation of a european public prosecutor's office, which are part of effective cooperation with olaf and eurojust.
in writing. ‒ the fight against fraud is central to the sound management of the union's financial interests. in 2013, the amount of fraud alleged or established directly related to the union budget amounted to eur 309,1 million according to the annual report. a declining total, but behind which there is in fact an increase in the number of cases. if all irregularities are taken into account, fraudulent or not, this amounts to 2.14 billion euros. this is unacceptable for the european parliament, which has chosen to take the bull by the horns by adopting a series of measures to combat fraud: strengthening cooperation between the commission and the member states, combating smuggling, creating a single database for all the irregularities registered, standardising administrative procedures, involving the european parliament in the negotiations on the creation of the european public prosecutor's office and improving the efficiency of the european anti-fraud office (olaf). at a time when everyone at all levels of government is being asked to tighten their belts, it is essential that the financial interests of the union are protected. that is the signal given by the members of the european parliament today.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the text. however, i would like to stress our concern at the threats still facing the union's budget, which are the result both of non-compliance with the rules (non-fraudulent irregularities) and of intentional infringements or criminal acts (fraud). there is a need for closer cooperation between the member states and the commission with a view to adopting appropriate and sufficient measures and means to prevent and rectify non-fraudulent irregularities and to combat fraud.

in writing. – the european semester – ags growth survey 2015 is extremely important for europe as a tool for economic policy coordination and governance. i voted in favour because i believe a good balance has been achieved. at macro level the report reflects my position on the need for structural reforms in the eu, the modernisation of economies and the continuation of fiscal consolidation. it also calls for the tax burden on labour to be reduced and for wages to be brought into line with productivity. another important position cautioning against protectionist tendencies and restriction of the four freedoms has been adopted as well. the report furthermore recognises that the investment gap can be bridged by targeting significantly higher levels of investments in private companies and in european business. it promotes a well-functioning financial system where increased stability and existing cross border institutions can facilitate liquidity and market making, especially for small and medium-sized enterprises. last but not least, it highlights the fact that the member states and the commission have not yet delivered on their commitment to complete the single market, especially the single market for services and the digital economy. this is what i believe our priority must be next.

in writing. - i work for the internal market commission. i would like to remind you that the single market is an essential component of the union's competitiveness and its greatest economic strength. this market of 500 million people gives the european union the opportunity to be the world's leading economic power. it offers businesses across the continent a 'home' market in which to sell their products and services, attracts investment from around the world and is the gateway for european trade with distant markets. the crisis has shown that the european union needs to act to improve its economic model and strengthen its competitiveness, which requires a combination of sound public finances, structural reforms and targeted investment. europe 2020 is the union's strategy to boost sustainable growth and job creation, and the single market has a crucial role to play in this regard. however, the potential of the single market is not being fully exploited at present. the european union must encourage member states to increase their crossborder trade in services and must take urgent measures to adapt to the evolution of digital technologies!

in writing. ‒ i am pleased that parliament has taken a concrete initiative to combat child pornography on the internet. i voted in favour of this text because it covers a large number of aspects of prime importance: rapid removal of illegal content, reporting to the law enforcement services of the member states, measures to combat online child-harassment, etc. i welcome the fact that the text strongly advocates a comprehensive approach to the phenomenon and wider collaboration, and that it does not forget to address the situation of victims of online sexual abuse. however, i believe that the resolution could also have included provisions against cyber predators. the manipulation of children on the internet for sexual purposes is not the only example of cyber predation. other forms of manipulation exist for the purpose of committing or having committed a criminal offence, kidnapping, incitement to hatred, suicide or anorexia, terrorist recruitment, misappropriation of personal data, etc. in addition, complementary initiatives could be considered with a view to codifying the status of a minor in cyberspace.
in writing. ‒ the fact is that in the last decade or so, the number of child pornography web sites has exploded, and so have the number of visitors! the latest europol report confirms this, active online pedophiles are increasing in number because they are becoming more difficult to track. new technological developments allow them to share their criminal acts easily and safely. it is in this context that the european parliament this afternoon urged the member states to combat child pornography on the internet effectively. starting with those more than half who have not yet fully transposed the directive on combating the sexual abuse and sexual exploitation of children. after the dutroux affair in particular, in belgium in particular but also in the four corners of europe, an arsenal of tools has emerged. today, we need to go even further, and new measures at european level are necessary: strengthening mechanisms for reporting and removing illegal content, improving children's education about the dangers of the internet, improving international cooperation (investigations and prosecutions)... because it is our duty to help our children protect themselves against this "deadly web" that the internet has become.
in writing. ‒ this resolution, which i voted in favour of, calls on member states to do more to investigate cases of sexual abuse of children on the internet, prosecute the perpetrators, protect child victims and remove illegal content online. more than 80 percent of the victims of child pornography on the internet are under the age of ten. the fight against the sexual exploitation of children and child pornography requires a comprehensive strategy covering the investigation of offences, the prosecution of offenders, the protection of children who are victims and the prevention of the phenomenon. to do this, the law enforcement agencies of the member states and europol must finally have the funds, the human resources, the investigative powers and the technical capacity to seriously and effectively investigate and prosecute offenders! new high-tech capabilities should also be developed to overcome the problems associated with the analysis of large quantities of child pornography images. the resolution also calls for the eu to take action to ensure that children's personal data are protected and that children are better informed about the risks and consequences of using their personal data online. the current reform of data protection contains specific articles for minors.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the text. sexual abuse and sexual exploitation of children, including child pornography, are serious violations of fundamental rights, in particular the right of the child to protection and care for his or her well-being, as enshrined in the 1989 united nations convention on the rights of the child and the charter of fundamental rights of the european union! the rights and protection of children on the internet must be safeguarded and measures must be taken to ensure that illegal content is promptly removed and reported to law enforcement agencies, and that there are sufficient legal instruments to investigate and prosecute offenders.

in writing. ‒ we adopted yesterday (by 336 votes to 145, with 64 abstentions) the annual report on the european union's common foreign and security policy (cfsp). in summary, the report suggests improving internal working methods and institutional structures, preserving and strengthening the european political and legal order, and strengthening the rules-based world order. in this text we expressed our concern at the lack of coordination and coherence between the union's policies and stressed how financial and budgetary constraints are further restricting europe's influence in the world and its role in the service of regional and global security. the question that was the subject of this report was, of course, how can a foreign policy be credible if it is not based on adequate defence capabilities of the member states and an effective common security and defence policy (csdp)? in view of the current situation, the question is now even more acute and i hope that the summit of heads of state and government on the subject scheduled for june will help to make progress in this area.
