in writing. ‒ what prompted meps to discuss and vote on the sustainable operation of the bar on thursday? a delicious fish, it is found in all corners of europe, from the north sea to the bay of biscay, and inland waters of the iberian peninsula and ireland. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. as we go up the stream that allowed the bar to make its way to the plenary, we recognize the excellent work of the fisheries commission and its members, who have alerted the public to the danger to this species. the bar is the new trend. so much so that the world's stock of this fish has declined by 32 percent in the last five years. this worrying decline has prompted the commission to ban pelagic trawl fisheries for cod until 30 april 2015 in most european seas. the alarm signal sounded by the european parliament this afternoon is a good one. because of the failure to do so in time, the wild cod is in danger of extinction in the coming years.
in writing. ‒ given the worrying state of the stock of blue ling in european waters (it has been declining sharply since 2012...), we adopted on thursday 12 march a resolution calling for the establishment of a management plan to manage blue ling fishing activities. the resolution endorses the proposal for a regulation published by the european commission on 26 january which prohibits, until the end of april 2015, vessels fishing with pelagic trawls from keeping, transferring, transhipping and landing rods. for the period after 2015, the measures to manage the bar stocks are still under discussion... the text adopted in plenary also stresses the importance of evaluating various management measures relating to commercial fisheries, in particular the establishment of a tac (total allowable catch) a measure already proposed by the european commission a few years ago. but since the member states have still not been able to agree on the allocation of quotas between them, discussions will shortly be resumed between the council and the commission.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the text. we believe that measures to manage the fishing activities of the barred-fish must be taken at european level if this species is to be saved. the commission should propose a multiannual management plan for bluefin tuna in order to increase the stock population above levels that can achieve maximum sustainable yield. it is important to involve professional and recreational fishermen and advisory councils in the development of such a plan.

member of the commission.– madam president, honourable members, thank you very much for your very straightforward comments. i have heard them and i will ensure that they are taken into account by the commission in its current assessment process, as well as its further work on enhancing the clarity and consistency of applicable social and market rules, in particular as part of the road package. by doing so, we will take a more comprehensive approach, which many of you have called for. i would like to underline that the establishment of national minimum pay rates is a positive development. but of course the national measures, while protecting workers, must respect eu law so as to preserve the proper functioning of the internal market with all the benefits it brings across europe. we shall also draw lessons from this experience. the commission will continue to monitor ongoing developments. it reserves the right to intervene against unilateral measures that unduly restrict fundamental freedoms such as the free movement of goods, workers and services. in the pursuit of constant improvement, we will also be looking into the most appropriate measures to create efficient, safe and socially responsible road transport services, with people at the heart of eu transport policy. finally, i would like to stress one more time that the commission will inform parliament of the outcome of its assessment of the compatibility of the german measures with eu law as soon as possible, but please understand that we need to follow eu procedures and that takes time. i assure you, however, that the commission will continue to act as a guardian of the eu treaty and eu law. i will see you again as soon as possible on this topic.

in writing. ‒ yesterday, i supported the european commission's proposal to raise €1.8 billion on the international bond market and lend it to ukraine, with no interest added to the rate that the european union itself must pay back to its external lenders. the economic crisis is raging in ukraine. the country is also beset by long-standing structural problems - such as corruption - exacerbated by the armed conflict in the east of the country, as well as by trade restrictions imposed by russia and the escalating conflict over natural gas supplies between the two countries. having lost access to international debt markets, ukraine can no longer borrow money on its own. the union has therefore done so for ukraine and i welcome the strong political message that the union is sending to ukraine on the same occasion: 'europe stands firmly by your side!' it should be noted that the disbursement will be linked to the implementation by ukraine of structural reforms such as better management of public finances, anti-corruption measures, changes in the tax administration, reforms in the energy and financial sectors and measures to improve the business environment.

in writing. ‒ ukraine will receive eur 1.8 billion in eu financial assistance. this is the largest amount of eu aid ever given to a non-eu member state. this assistance will take the form of loans, repayable over a maximum of 15 years and subject to ukraine respecting the country's democratization process, as well as the rule of law and human rights. this aid is intended to stabilise the country's economy and support substantial reform of the state. the european commission, together with the imf and the world bank, will follow up the reforms, where necessary in consultation with the european parliament and the european council. this is how we as the eu can help the country to recover and preserve its independence.
in writing. the adoption of the annual report on taxation by a large majority of meps in the european parliament underlines the importance of a european tax policy. ensuring fair taxation helps to revive the union's economy. the financial transaction tax is now a necessity. it could contribute directly to the budget of the european union by increasing its own resources. i believe that the oecd is already doing a remarkable job of ensuring that developing countries can participate on an equal footing with other countries in the formulation and reform of global tax policies.
in writing. ‒ in this report, which i supported yesterday, parliament calls for simplification of national tax systems in order to reduce the administrative tax burden on individuals and businesses; removing obstacles to cross-border activity; encourage more eu countries to join the 11 states that have introduced a financial transaction tax; to introduce a common consolidated corporate tax base (ccctb) for union companies; increase the transparency of tax returns (since they create opportunities for tax evasion and competition); to improve the access of national parliaments to tax-related content; to combat selective tax advantages granted to certain undertakings; to ensure that the european commission establishes a blacklist of tax havens and countries with tax practices that distort competition by july 2015; to suspend or revoke banking or advisory authorisations of accountants or other financial advisors if there is evidence that they have contributed to tax evasion; the commission has also proposed that the tax burden be shifted from labour to other forms of taxation and that vat be collected more effectively. the fight against tax evasion must be a top priority for the union. parliament is in that line and i welcome that. something to follow.
in writing. ‒ tax justice and european tax coherence are our objectives for a europe where citizens are on an equal footing with businesses and where the general interest takes precedence over the private interest. with regard to the text voted tonight, immediate, coordinated and comprehensive action is required in the field of tax policy both within the union and at international level in order to eradicate tax evasion, to combat tax fraud and tax evasion, and to combat aggressive tax planning and, of course, tax havens. this immediate action could replace the introduction of new levels or forms of taxation and would generate additional funds that member states badly need to boost public investment and promote growth and job creation.

we all know that the subject of the armenian genocide is still very sensitive and difficult to discuss, even now, 100 years after the events. but this resolution is not a resolution against anything or anyone, and certainly not against the turkish people or its leaders. this resolution is an important first step towards making room for the past. by recognizing and commemorating the armenian genocide, future generations will no longer be trapped in the past but can free themselves from it. for this reason, in 1998, the belgian federal parliament was one of the first national parliaments to recognize the terrible fate of the armenians and other populations as a genocide. the most important thing is probably to understand the historical and ideological context in which the genocide could have taken place. we can learn lessons from the fact that today too, ideologies are emerging from time to time which can result in aggressive regimes, where forced deportation and genocide are no longer to be excluded. i therefore regard this resolution first and foremost as an important lesson and warning for our generation and for the next.

"blue card" is the answer. i said that a quota is not really a solution. you see in many countries that there is a quota system, but still people with disabilities are not finding work. on paper, that's fine, but it doesn't always work in practice. the accompanying measures are lacking and we need them more than just a quota. so the government must provide support. for example, interpreters must be provided for deaf people, and workplace adaptations are needed for wheelchair users. the employer is not always willing to pay these costs. if the government offers to intervene, it may be better than a quota alone.
in writing. obligation to employ disabled workers in companies with at least 20 employees, principle of non-discrimination, obligation to negotiate measures relating to occupational integration, general accessibility, these are the legislative framework established for disabled workers. however, disabled people continue to have great difficulty in finding or keeping a job and their unemployment rate remains twice that of the general population. as early as 2009, the busnel report entitled 'employment, a right to live for all' highlighted the priority to be given to preventing occupational exclusion and maintaining employment. in 2014, the right to employment in the ordinary workplace for people with disabilities is still far from being effective. the european parliament has a role to play in ensuring that some citizens are not left behind and in helping to make europe a europe for all citizens.
"summer turtles and quails are the big losers in malta". i fully endorse this quote from the flanders bird protection agency. malta missed a historic opportunity to end spring-hunting of migratory birds in a referendum last saturday. the poor record of malta in implementing and enforcing the birds directive is well known. while this island should be a refuge for migratory birds because of its geographical location, in practice it is one of the main bottlenecks between africa and europe, and hunters kill large numbers of birds both in spring and in autumn. this is clearly contrary to european regulations. malta was condemned by the european court of justice in 2009. i now ask the european commission to send a clear signal to put an end to this hunt at the earliest opportunity. i also expect the commission, in the revision of the birds directive, to make these irresponsible practices structurally impossible, not only in malta but also in the rest of the european union.
in writing. ‒ many carriers have struggled to cope with the decline in volumes and the drop in freight rates following the economic and industrial crisis of 2008. this is particularly the case for the transport company mory-ducros, whose turnover has been falling in recent years. in bankruptcy, the company was taken over by a new entity mory global but 2,804 people will remain on the job. the egf will provide €6 052 200 to implement a major action and service plan to help redundant workers reintegrate into the labour market.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this request for a financial contribution of eur 6 052 200 for 2 513 workers made redundant by mory-ducros sas, the second largest french operator of freight transport services. as a result of the financial and economic crisis, this sector has been hit hard. a price war has broken out because of the decline in physical production in europe. in addition, costs (gasoline, wages, materials) have risen, leading to a deterioration in operating margins, large losses and numerous bankruptcies in the road freight transport sector. mory-ducros accumulated significant losses in 2012 and 2013. in november 2013, the company declared bankruptcy and was placed under judicial administration. in february 2014, a liquidator was appointed. as part of the liquidation, the newly created mory global took over 50 out of 84 branches and re-employed 2 107 workers (out of 4 911). of the remaining 2 804 workers, 2 513 will be able to receive, with the help of the egf, expert advice on individual career paths and training to develop their job search skills. the egf contribution is 60% of the cost of these personalised services.
in writing. by approving on wednesday afternoon european jobsearch aid for the 2,500 workers made redundant by the french road haulage company mory-ducros, meps showed that european social policy is not a mere word. financial support from the european globalisation adjustment fund, following on from the €5.2 million received in march by 2,498 workers made redundant in belgium: duferco, saint-gobain sekurit, caterpillar and arcelor mittal liège; europe does not fail to act in the interests of its citizens when they are directly affected by economic redundancies. the citizens of the european union obviously expect more from the european project than a passive social policy based on the 'safety net' alone. this is why it is essential to facilitate financing for smes and innovation on the one hand, and to revive investment in major infrastructure projects that create wealth, jobs and social cohesion on the other. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's transport policy is not disrupted by the introduction of new technologies.
in writing. ‒ the global financial and economic crisis has not spared the road freight transport sector of over 3.5 tonnes, whose activity decreased by 13.7% in the european union and by 21% in france between 2007 and 2012. this contraction in activity has led to a price war between the various companies in the sector, leading to numerous restructurings over the same period. this is particularly the case at mory-ducros, where 2 513 workers were made redundant as a result of the economic downturn. in order to help these many workers, i naturally voted in favour of the request made by the french authorities for a financial contribution from the egf of eur 6 052 200. i hope that this contribution will enable them to regain employment stability quickly.
in writing. ‒ on 15 april, meps voted in plenary in brussels to provide €6 million in aid to the dismissed mory-ducros employees under the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf). the aid application concerns 2 513 workers at more than 80 sites in metropolitan france. before its liquidation in february 2014, the mory-ducros group was the second largest operator in the courier and charter sector. the group has suffered the consequences of the decline in road freight transport in vehicles over 3.5 tonnes. this, due to the crisis and less activity, decreased by 13.7% in the european union between 2007 and 2012. this decline has led to a price war and increased competition between carriers, while their operating margins have been reduced by the concomitant rise in the cost of fuel, wages and materials. the fund was set up to facilitate the reintegration of workers made redundant as a result of globalisation.
in writing. ‒ globalisation is inevitable and goes hand in hand with the opening up of new markets, international competition, economic growth and job creation. the downside of this is job losses in less competitive sectors. the nva delegation in the european parliament understands the objectives of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf), but also has an eye on the taxpayer who pays the bill. moreover, social policy should be a competence of the member states in the first instance. a european transfer union is not a panacea for tackling unemployment. in particular, structural reforms are needed to get back on track with economic growth. the n-va meps therefore abstained on this dossier.

madam president, a few figures are sometimes better than a long speech: a plastic bag is five seconds of manufacture, five minutes of use and up to 500 years of decomposition. that is the significance of the compromise we are talking about here, which was reached between parliament and the council to discourage their use. in practice, therefore, member states will have a choice: reduce the number of lightweight plastic bags used per person per year to no more than 40 by 2025 or stop giving them away for free in shops by 2018. that's reasonable. unfortunately, given the disparities in europe - 4 plastic bags per consumer per year in finland, for example, compared to 400 in poland or portugal - this is probably reasonable but not sustainable, and i regret it. it will take ten years in total to do, in the end, less well than the best students in the class. frankly, europe can do better and must do better. when i say 'europe', i am speaking of the member states lagging behind, which could usefully draw inspiration from the good practices of the north. not only in the north, because, as we have heard, the good pupils are in ireland and the grand duchy of luxembourg, in particular.

i welcome the agreement reached as a good, balanced and feasible first step towards reducing co2 emissions from maritime transport. international maritime transport is the last of the mohicans, as it is the only mode of transport not yet included in the eu's commitment and objectives to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. the sector accounts for 4% of total eu greenhouse gas emissions. this share is increasing and will continue to increase in the coming years, not only in the eu but also globally. there is therefore an objective reason for making the necessary efforts in this mode of transport. reliable and comparable data must always form the basis of a well-thought-out policy. the proposed system of monitoring, reporting and verification is therefore a good and necessary starting point and has the potential to create a win-win situation in several areas. so there are reasons to support this agreement with conviction.

in writing. fishing is a dangerous occupation, with a higher rate of occupational mortality than other occupations. the number of deaths in the fishing sector is 24 000 a year. it was therefore urgent for parliament to send a strong message by encouraging the member states of the union to become parties, in the interest of the union, to the international maritime organisation's international convention on standards for the training, certification and watchkeeping of personnel on fishing vessels. at present, 22 of the 28 eu member states have already adopted the convention, which guarantees that fishing vessel personnel are qualified and fit for work, and four have already ratified it.
in writing. ‒ with 24 000 seafarers dying each year, fishing is the occupational activity officially recording the highest number of occupational accidents. the european parliament's vote is intended to push the member states to allow ratification of the 1995 international convention (stcw-f). twenty years later, only four member states have ratified the text. these countries are therefore the only ones where fishermen benefit from safe working conditions as provided for in the convention, safety training and certificates guaranteeing the quality of the staff on boats over 24 metres. the eu can only give its approval to ratification of the agreement, which must be done at national level, even if european legislation takes precedence in the event of a conflict. the international maritime organisation (imo) aims to enforce these safety standards and ensure a significant reduction in accidents in the maritime sector. it also encourages member states to adopt their own safety laws for seafarers working on vessels of less than 24 metres in length. unfortunately, they have not yet been taken into account in the international convention. #mrk
in writing. ‒ the purpose of the stcw-f convention is to ensure that personnel working on board fishing vessels are qualified (and hold an official certificate attesting to this) and fit for work (after medical examination) and, therefore, to minimise the risks to the safety of persons and/or property at sea, or to the marine environment, during operations on board vessels. the purpose of this decision is to authorise member states to ratify the stcw-f convention in accordance with the union's exclusive competence for the recognition of regulated professions exercised by union nationals on board fishing vessels.

in writing. ‒ our parliament today approves the introduction of the ecall automated emergency call system. the system, which is installed in cars, is designed to trigger a europe-wide emergency call to 112 in the event of an accident, thus saving valuable time in saving lives. according to the commission, around 25 700 people lost their lives in road accidents in 2014. the ecall is expected to reduce this figure by up to 10%. from 31 march 2018, all car manufacturers will have to provide such a device in their new cars. i welcome this step. in accidents with serious injuries in particular, rapid assistance is often vital. by committing to installing ecall in all vehicles from 2018, we can help to reduce the number of road deaths significantly.
in writing. ‒ the deployment of an ecall in-vehicle system is one of the european union's main road safety objectives. this system would make it compulsory for all new vehicles sold in the european union to have an emergency call service. it would guarantee the initiation of an emergency call to 112 in the event of a serious accident. the installation of this system would reduce the number of road deaths by between 1 and 10%, depending on the member state. i consider road safety to be a top priority, and the number of deaths on european roads must be reduced. that is why i voted in favour of this text, which will undoubtedly save lives.
in writing. ‒ with our vote today, the green light for the rollout of ecall is finally on. parliament has long called for this: every new vehicle will be equipped with an ecall system by 2018 at the latest. by automatically alerting emergency services in the event of an accident, they can be on the scene up to 50% faster. this could save 2,500 road traffic fatalities a year. ecall will therefore be crucial to delivering on our commitment to halve the number of road deaths by 2020. ecall is already on the market, but is currently an optional extra that is reserved for those who have extra cash in their wallet. from 2018, fortunately, there will be no additional costs, but it will be mandatory built into every new car. with this new legislation, we are ensuring that privacy is protected and that access to other ancillary services (such as repairs) is guaranteed in an open and transparent manner. of course, member states must also fulfil their obligations and prepare to process ecall data and ensure that ecall works everywhere.

in writing. ‒ the present proposal to amend directives 98/70/ec and 2009/28/ec aims at the switch to low greenhouse gas biofuels. conventional biofuels lead to indirect land-use change, which means that, although biofuel crops are grown sustainably, they displace food crops and lead to increased greenhouse gas emissions. the environmental benefits sought are thus negated. for this reason, i welcome the shift from conventional biofuels to those that take indirect land use change into account and hope that this will also create a long-term perspective for sustainable biofuels.
in writing. ‒ co2 emissions from transport play an important role in global warming. the renewable energy directive sets binding targets to be achieved by 2020 to achieve a 10% share of energy from renewable sources in transport. directive 98/70/ec provides for a 6% reduction in the greenhouse gas intensity of fuels used in road transport by 2020. to achieve these objectives, it is essential to increase the share of advanced biofuels and to limit the contribution of traditional biofuels in the composition of diesel and petrol in the european union. advanced biofuels can significantly reduce greenhouse gas emissions even when indirect land-use change emissions are taken into account. it is therefore to achieve these objectives and to preserve the environment that i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. – i voted in favour of the final compromise package on the fuel quality directive and renewable energy directive as i believe that the eu has shown a clear vision on its approach to biofuels and the related indirect land use change. although i voted in favour, i nevertheless believe that this compromise package fails to address some opportunities for a further use of industrial waste streams as renewable fuels. i firmly believe that firms that can reuse carbon, through the addition of bacteria to its industrial waste streams (co2 bio-fermentation of industrial waste streams), should be considered (at least) twice their energy content in annex ix. this should not be conditional upon being renewable according to article 2a, but should rather be based on respecting the sustainability criteria (60% ghg reduction vis-à-vis fossil fuels).
in writing. ‒ the reform of biofuels policy is necessary. biofuels were hailed as the solution to renewable energy in transport 10 years ago, but they have proved to be unsatisfactory and sometimes even problematic. for example, more land is being used to produce biofuels from agricultural crops, resulting in deforestation, increased co2 emissions and rising food prices, especially in developing countries. the n-va therefore supports the new rules on biofuel production, which are a policy shift in the right direction and restrict conventional biofuels based on agricultural crops. however, this is done in a workable, consistent and realistic manner so as not to jeopardise the security of investment. the n-va also supports the development of advanced biofuels but considers it too early for a binding target. we are therefore satisfied with the indicative target of 0.5% by 2020. the technology for these advanced biofuels is still in its infancy. we don't want to risk making the same mistakes as in the past. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's policy on biofuels and bioliquids, and will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's policy on biofuels and bioliquids.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of the directive amending the fuel quality and renewable energy directives, which limits the contribution of conventional biofuels, improves the greenhouse gas performance of biofuel production processes by raising the minimum greenhouse gas emission reduction levels for new installations and encourages greater market penetration of so-called 'advanced' biofuels. it is essential to promote sustainable biofuels, i.e. produced from waste or plant residues, so that their production does not harm the food needs of the population and livestock.
in writing. ‒ driving or eating, you'll have to choose, for a few years at least. the european agreement on biofuels adopted today by the european parliament's plenary is not a major reform. this is a compromise in the classic sense of the term, which, while providing a clear legislative framework for the production of biofuels, from the first to the third generation, while protecting the investments already made in agricultural crops, does not take a clear position. the new legislation states that first generation biofuels (mainly rapeseed or palm oil) should not account for more than 7% of final energy consumption in transport by 2020. these agrofuels were promising a decade ago, but they have the major disadvantage of putting food prices under pressure. the rest has been done by the timidity of the member states, which have not been able to unlock the investments in the biofuels of the future, produced from waste or innovative technologies based on micro-organisms. as the rapporteur, my liberal colleague nils torvalds, said: 'we have not been fully successful in opening up the market for more advanced biofuels'. that's a euphemism for "not at all".
in writing. ‒ yesterday, the european parliament formally endorsed the agreement reached in the trilogue on the draft legislation to promote more sustainable biofuels that protect the interests of developing countries and the climate. the draft directive aims to cap the use of agrofuels in transport by 2020, to accelerate the production of advanced biofuels such as algae and waste, which do not compete with food production, and to take into account the iluc factor (for 'indirect land-use change') in order to account for greenhouse gas emissions related to the production of these first generation agrofuels. the main thrust of the text adopted is to limit the use of first generation biofuels to 7% of final energy consumption in transport by 2020. fuel suppliers shall report to the member states and the commission on the estimated level of greenhouse gas emissions related to indirect land-use change. the commission will then publish the data on these iluc-related emissions. by the end of 2017, the commission should assess the possibility of including iluc factors in the sustainability criteria for biofuels.

in writing. ‒ this plan aims to develop a multi-species approach to cod, herring and sprat stocks in the baltic. this plan will take into account biological interactions, environmental conditions and will be subject to scientific monitoring. it also provides for a more flexible approach to resources through the establishment of annual fishing opportunities. this should allow for a balanced and sustainable exploitation of stocks.
in writing. ‒ since 2008, we have had a cod stock management plan in the baltic to keep the stock size within reasonable limits. in other words, maximum catches are set and a series of technical measures are adopted taking into account the characteristics of each stock, the fisheries in which it is found and the economic impact of the measures on the fisheries concerned. the 2008 plan did not cover herring and sprat. the new plan therefore replaces the previous provisions, which is justified as the stocks concerned are interdependent (the cod feeds on sprats and herring, while herring and sprats sometimes feed on cod eggs). this new plan is an important step in the implementation of the reform of the common fisheries policy. the multiannual management and the fact that these three interacting species will now be managed by a single plan should make the baltic sea fisheries more sustainable by increasing predictability, which i welcome.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament adopted an important report on fisheries management this afternoon. in this case, the baltic sea was chosen as the first example of application of the new common fisheries policy (cfp) adopted in 2013 in its multi-species management plan component. the plan should allow for the balanced and sustainable exploitation of these stocks, in particular cod, herring and sprat, which account for more than 94% of the catches made in the baltic sea, as well as fishing opportunities and thus resources for fishermen. the message from the plenary is the right one: not only does it strengthen the committee on fisheries in its determination to put an end to overfishing and promote management plans as key tools of the cfp, but it also enables parliament's delegation to negotiate in trilogue with a strong position and to free itself from the national interests that are expressed in the council. we hope that the final agreement will be ambitious, because it will be the basis for all future fish stocks management plans in the north sea, the mediterranean and the north-west and south-west atlantic.
in writing. ‒ the multiannual plan voted today aims to establish a framework for the multi-species management of cod, herring and sprat stocks, which account for more than 94% of the catches made in recent years in the baltic sea. this long-awaited plan should allow for the balanced and sustainable exploitation of stocks and provide fishermen with livelihoods. at the same time, it should ensure management based on the most up-to-date scientific advice on the state of the stocks concerned, the interactions between species and other aspects related to the ecosystem and fisheries.
in writing. ‒ i agree with the general idea in the commission proposal that a multi-species management plan in the baltic sea is necessary. the multispecies approach is much more effective than the one based on a single species. the plan should allow for the balanced and sustainable exploitation of these stocks and stable fishing opportunities and thus resources for fishermen. at the same time, it should ensure management based on the latest scientific advice as regards the state of the stocks concerned, the interactions between species and other aspects related to the ecosystem and fisheries.
in writing. ‒ the obligation to land unmarketable bycatches is one of the main lines of the reform of the common fisheries policy. it will be phased in between 2015 and 2019. since this obligation is in contradiction with several existing european regulations, the commission has proposed an 'omnibus' regulation which amends these texts in order to replace discharges to sea by landing.
in writing. i support this report for two reasons. firstly, the commission proposal for a regulation is in line with the objective of the reformed common fisheries policy of progressively eliminating discards in all fisheries in the european union by introducing an obligation to land unintended catches which are not marketable, either because of the absence of a quota or because they are smaller than the minimum conservation reference size. secondly, this initiative was welcome insofar as this landing obligation was in contradiction with several european regulations currently in force.
in writing. ‒ the text voted on today, already informally approved by parliament and the council, now obliges fishermen to land unwanted catches rather than discard them at sea. among the measures taken, the european commission will have to draw up an annual report on the implementation of this landing obligation. a two-year period was provided before penalties for failure to comply with this obligation. and a mechanism has been put in place to prevent the development of a parallel market for non-marketable catches.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the text. i share the view of my colleague, mr cadec, that the legal alignment for fisheries subject to the landing obligation after 2015 will have to be achieved at a later date, in connection with the new framework of technical measures which the commission will propose in a few months' time. the omnibus should therefore only concern the urgent problem of the implementation of the landing obligation for the fisheries concerned in 2015. i support the proposal to abolish the provisions on other fisheries. it stresses that 2015 will be a test year to assess the consequences of the implementation of the landing obligation.
in writing. ‒ on 1 july 2013, croatia joined the european union as its 28th member state. for this reason, croatia is now included as a contracting party to the partnership and cooperation agreement between the european commission, the member states of the eu and the russian federation and the protocol is additionally published in croatian. the agreement was concluded in 1997 for a period of 10 years and has been automatically renewed for a period of one year since 2007. this includes, among others, arrangements in areas such as trade, education, energy and political dialogue. i welcome this step, particularly as the agreement is of particular importance for european-russian relations because of its framework function.
in writing. ‒ through the protocol, croatia will be integrated into the eu-russia partnership agreement, which aims in particular to promote trade and investment and to establish economic, financial and technical cooperation.
in writing. ‒ this is a technical report on a draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union and its member states, of the protocol to the partnership and cooperation agreement establishing a partnership between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and the russian federation, of the other part, to take account of the accession of the republic of croatia to the european union. this afternoon parliament gave its approval to the conclusion of this agreement.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union and its member states, of the protocol to the partnership and cooperation agreement establishing a partnership between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and the russian federation, of the other part, to take account of the accession of the republic of croatia to the european union.
in writing. ‒ in 1999, 29 european countries undertook to establish a european higher education area in the framework of the bologna declaration. 16 years later, the process is being evaluated and then revised. particular success has been achieved in the area of harmonisation and recognition of studies, and the associated increase in the mobility of european students and transnational employability. in addition, europe-wide higher education systems are now more transparent and offer easy and fast access to information. the european higher education area now has 47 members. i welcome the evaluation of the implementation of the bologna process and its further development, in particular to ensure pan-european quality and to optimise the coordination of the different actions such as horizon 2020 and erasmus+.
in writing. ‒ the bologna declaration, signed in june 1999, aimed to create a european higher education area by 2010. today 47 countries are part of the bologna process. the aim of the project was to improve student mobility, the quality of education and the employability of young graduates in education. although bologna is a success on the whole, it needs to be given a new lease of life to overcome the challenges ahead, particularly in the field of youth employment. to achieve the goal of coherent, transparent and high quality higher education, it is crucial to focus on implementing all the tools at our disposal and to put the student back at the centre of the educational paradigm. it is therefore to improve the quality of higher education in europe that i have decided to support this report.
in writing. ‒ in june 1999, 29 european countries signed the bologna declaration, which aimed to create a european higher education area by 2010, to expand the choice of educational opportunities and to ensure the compatibility of higher education systems in europe. i voted for the report on the follow-up to the implementation of the bologna process because it urges the countries of the european higher education area to implement the agreed reforms and stresses the importance of ensuring the mutual recognition of university degrees. education is one of the pillars of our society. it is also a privileged instrument for combating social inequalities and youth unemployment. therefore, member states should be encouraged to increase scholarships and continue to intensify partnerships in order to achieve the european higher education area.
in writing. the bologna declaration, drawn up in june 1999, had as its main objective the creation of a european higher education area by 2010. the aim of this new european area was to offer students a wider choice of quality courses and a simplified procedure for the recognition of both internal and external qualifications. after more than ten years, it is appropriate to carry out an evaluation and follow-up of the implementation of the bologna process. quality higher education is essential for the cultural, economic and social development of the european union.
in writing. ‒ the bologna process is essential for the development of societies. the european parliament intends today, by its ambitious vote, to give new colour and energy to a process which is running out of breath. while the main priority for many countries is to ensure the quality of higher education, there is also an urgent need to put the student at the centre of learning, by ensuring financial support, international mobility and improving social inclusion. twenty-nine countries signed the bologna declaration in 1999. today, more than 47 countries are committed to creating a genuine european higher education area (ehea), building growth and a knowledge-based economy. there are successes, fortunately the recognition of university degrees or the three-cycle structure (bachelor-master-doctorate) , but we are still far from the initial objectives. other interesting avenues to be explored are those of new technologies, such as online courses accessible to all, the very popular moocs (massive open online course). it is also crucial to focus on synchronising financial measures taken in support of the bologna process, such as horizon 2020 and erasmus+, to address new european challenges.
in writing. ‒ in june 1999, 29 european countries signed the bologna declaration, which aimed to create a european higher education area by 2010. one of the first objectives of the bologna process is that a student enrolled in a european university has the right to obtain a degree in any member state and to have it recognised throughout the european union. progress has already been made in the areas of higher education structures, harmonisation and quality, mobility and employability. the report adopted focuses in particular on the importance of making the best use of available funds and finding new funding models, and on the need to reinforce the bologna process in the important role it can play in the revision of the europe 2020 strategy and, above all, in the investment plan for europe presented by jean-claude juncker.
in writing. ‒ how can you vote against such a report? it is also an opportunity to recall that our desire for a coherent, transparent and high-quality higher education sector is essential for cultural, economic and social development. the bologna objectives provide the essential tools for higher education in europe to meet the challenges of our time. however, there is still a long way to go before these objectives can be fully achieved. while the process has many successes, including strong structural convergence, new challenges have replaced the old ones. to address these and to give a new impetus to the process, it is essential to focus on the proper implementation of the current structure and tools, to correct their shortcomings and to move towards an educational paradigm that places the student and the acquired skills at the centre of learning.
in writing. ‒ european cinema is an important medium for promoting and disseminating cultural diversity across europe. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the matter. therefore, specific investments are needed to improve the cross-border availability of works. this is ensured in particular by the promotion of subtitling and dubbing. it is also essential to ensure the widespread digitisation of films to prevent the loss of works, as has unfortunately happened to many silent films. i welcome measures in the field of european cinema and in particular events such as the brussels short film festival, which is currently taking place, to enable the distribution of cinematographic works throughout europe.
in writing. ‒ the world of cinema plays a key role in the constitution of a european cultural heritage. in 2014, european cinema set a new record: 1,500 european films were screened in the union. that's twice the number of american movies. however, the number of viewers is still far below that of the films from across the atlantic. to address this problem, it is necessary to extend the distribution of european films to new distribution channels such as video-on-demand services and streaming. more money must also be invested in promoting films and in their international distribution. the creative europe programme, which has a budget of €1.5 billion for the period 2014-2020, aims to improve the distribution, visibility and accessibility of european films. i therefore voted in favour of this report in order to support european culture and the film industry.
in writing. ‒ the european film industry has a major impact on the european cultural landscape as well as on employment and economic growth. however, most films produced in europe are only released in their country of origin (only 8% are distributed outside the eu). in the face of american films which are much more widely distributed in europe, securing a wider audience for european productions is a challenge for european cinema. the distribution of public subsidies is one explanation for the distribution problem: almost 70% of these subsidies are devoted to production, leaving little money for marketing/distribution. the report i supported contains several suggestions to stimulate the distribution of european cinema: encouraging subtitling of films (rather than their translation), supporting small cinemas and enabling them to equip themselves with digital projection, financing the digitisation, preservation and online availability of european film heritage and supporting european co-productions to lead to a wider distribution of films.
in writing. unlike the american film industry, european cinema is currently characterised by a heterogeneous structure in terms of both funding mechanisms and types of productions. as a result, distribution is largely limited to the country of origin, but, above all, this complicates promotion outside the european union. the cinema sector has a direct impact on the european cultural landscape, as well as on employment and economic growth. i therefore welcome this report which stresses the importance of stimulating the distribution of european cinema and of exploiting its full cultural and economic potential.
‒ "culture shapes the soul of europe. a film induces a sense of identity like no other medium, it is the very reflection of our society, its values, its hopes and fears". perhaps inspired by wim wenders, the european parliament this afternoon encouraged the european film industry to continue developing new business models to improve the distribution of its films. in 2014, europe produced and distributed nearly 1,500 works in its own market, whereas the united states did half as well in its own market. poor promotion and fierce international competition mean that european productions still have difficulty crossing national borders. quick and easy to access, video on demand and online files could be an innovative way to facilitate access to european films for viewers. it is essential to continue to develop film education in school curricula, festivals, and awards such as the lux prize. in 2014, the european parliament awarded "ida". this film has allowed thousands of citizens to share the extraordinary fate of this young polish nun in search of identity.
in writing. ‒ the report voted on today aims to broaden the audience for european films. it emphasises the need to improve the overall effectiveness of the financing instruments already in place to promote the competitiveness and diversity of the european film sector. given the cultural and economic potential of the audiovisual sector, the european film industry should develop within a stable and adaptable legal framework that encourages investment and diversity and allows for the development of new online services. the text adopted thus focuses on several points, such as the development of the sector, crossborder promotion and distribution, financing and programmes supporting the audiovisual sector, film and media education, instruments for the production and distribution of european films, etc.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text. the report on european cinema in the digital age aims to support european cinema and encourage its promotion, distribution and visibility in order to enable all europeans to benefit from their cultural heritage. the european parliament's lux prize is a perfect example of how european cinema should be promoted. each year, the prize focuses on films that address issues affecting european public opinion. the ability of cinema to convey cultural values across cultures makes it the ideal tool for a debate on europe and its future. in the context of the current economic, political and social crises, which also threaten art, culture and cinema, the lux prize offers a solid springboard for european creativity.
in writing. ‒ sustainable forest management and a functioning and balanced ecosystem guarantee quality of life, sustainability, jobs and sustainable value for ourselves and future generations. i therefore welcome the measures taken under the new eu forestry strategy, in particular to strengthen cooperation between the individual member states without having to interfere too much with national sovereignty.
in writing. ‒ the forestry sector is crucial to the well-being of the european economy. with 3.5 million jobs, the forestry sector is the third largest employer in the european union, just behind metallurgy and the food industry. in a context where an increasing number of policies (energy, environment, climate, etc.) influence the management of our forests, it is essential to adopt a new european forestry strategy to ensure coherence and coordination between the different actions. this strategy will provide a global overview of actions in the field of european forestry. it is therefore for reasons of consistency and protection of our natural heritage that i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ we need a new common forestry strategy (the current one has been in place since 1998) focused on sustainable management, promoting the use of raw forest products and increasing the competitiveness of the forestry industry. forests cover about 40% of the eu. 60% are private. the forestry sector employs over 3 million people. a new strategy is needed to address cross-border challenges such as forest fires, climate change, natural disasters, but also to strengthen forest industries and improve the efficient use of raw materials such as wood and wood products. a new strategy will boost the competitiveness of eu forestry, improve its self-sufficiency in timber, reduce its trade deficit and boost employment in the sector. in addition, as energy demand increases, forests are expected to play a greater role in the eu's future energy mix. the review of the effectiveness of the timber regulation to combat illegal logging and the placing of illegal timber on the eu market must also be finalised. finally, an action plan should be developed to prevent deforestation and forest degradation.
in writing. the importance of forests and their benefits to our society are no longer to be demonstrated. wood, as a sustainable raw material, is an important resource in europe, and 40% of the european territory is covered by forests. in this context, it was important to strengthen the eu's forestry strategy to meet new cross-border challenges. this will include promoting the sustainable use of wood and other forest materials to create jobs and stimulate growth, as well as improving forest management and exploitation, all while reducing red tape.

in writing. ‒ forests and other wooded areas cover more than 40% of the territory of the european union. the forest area has increased by 0.4% per year in recent decades. the text voted today establishes a framework for action to promote forestry coordination and the creation of synergies with other sectors that have an impact on forest management. the text focuses in particular on the sustainable management of forests and ecosystem services, on how to meet the growing demand for renewable energy and raw materials used in products, on the challenges facing the forest industry and on managing transnational threats to forests, such as forest fires and forest pests. the report also stresses the need to ensure that forest resources and forestry materials are used and reused efficiently, but opposes legally binding rules that favour the use of wood.

answer is "blue cardboard". madam president, the question is whether i am suspicious of the member states. yes, i am suspicious of certain member states, clearly. a whole series of fraud cases are still pending in the member states. these too often play the card of their interests, of their view of sovereignty, to escape or to allow some to escape from judgment and, therefore, to establish impunity. that is why i am in favour of centralisation, so that we have an increasingly single system of jurisprudence.

the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, as regards the estimate of parliament's revenue and expenditure for 2016, the committee on budgets wanted to stress from the outset the need to take account of the general context of budgetary restraint prevailing in all our countries and therefore to propose a draft budget for 2016, which is realistic, but very tight in terms of the increase in appropriations. we have therefore agreed from the outset, firstly, that the european parliament's budget for 2016 should be below 20% of the total administrative expenditure of the union and, secondly, that the increase in current operating appropriations, compared with 2015, should not exceed 1.6%. it should be added, however, that the deadly terrorist attacks of recent months and, more generally, the persistence, if not the aggravation, of these threats have led us to give a very special place to the problem of security. so, in addition to the 1.6% increase in the current budget, we decided to create an exceptional allocation of eur 15 million to strengthen the security of the european parliament buildings, particularly in brussels, and to allocate a significant part of the appropriations to strengthening cyber security, which all experts agree is both necessary and urgent in the european parliament. once this general framework was set, we focused on the operational priorities to be implemented for 2016 and, in fact, we agreed on the need to strengthen a single priority, namely the strengthening of the financial means to enable us to better perform our work as parliamentarians. since the treaty of lisbon - as you all know - we have considerably increased our powers in the area of legislation. a considerable effort has already been made to strengthen the staff of parliamentary committees in this area, but we remain too ill equipped to exercise real control over the delegated and implementing acts which directly result from our legislative activity. we have therefore proposed a number of measures, on which we have agreed with the council. the first measure is to increase the number of secretaries of parliamentary committees, which have to scrutinise a large number of delegated acts, implementing acts or multi-decision programmes, by 20 new posts. secondly, a request to the bureau which accepted it to develop and implement new regulations to ensure a better balance between accredited and local assistants. it is clear to all people of good faith that accredited assistants are essential to enable a member of the european parliament to carry out his work as a co-legislator and a supervisor of the executive effectively. thirdly, in addition to the measure i have just mentioned, it was also decided, at the request of certain political groups and, later, of the bureau, to increase what is commonly known as the secretarial allowance. this measure, unlike the previous one, was not widely accepted. some political groups and individual colleagues have not considered it appropriate or necessary. the commission notes that the commission has not yet adopted a decision on the application of the principle of equal treatment for men and women in the field of employment. the agreement which finally was reached between the bureau and the committee on budgets on this subject is explicitly based on a very clear premise: the appropriations needed to finance this implementation will only be released after the bureau has drawn up satisfactory new regulations to increase the number of accredited assistants and to better control local assistants by limiting their number. fourthly, the evaluation of a member's performance is not only, and not primarily, a question of quantity but of quality, that is to say, of content. the current systems of classification of parliamentarians unfortunately lead to certain deviations which must be put to an end. the bureau and the committee on budgets have therefore agreed to ask the conference of presidents to ensure that new rules on written questions are put in place to put an end to their incredible inflation, which in too many cases is of little or no interest. in view of the general framework and the priorities i have just mentioned, the bureau and the committee on budgets finally agreed to reduce the bureau's initial estimates by eur 11 822 000. we have postponed the review of the kad's housing policy and financing arrangements until autumn. i thank my colleagues, in particular the fictitious rapporteurs from the other political groups, the staff of the committee secretariat, who have done a remarkable job, and the staff of the political groups for their help. i thank you, mr president.

in writing. ‒ with some 4.8 million young people aged 15-24 currently unemployed, youth employment is one of the european union's top priorities. it has therefore developed a number of instruments for member states to combat this serious problem. the youth employment initiative is one such instrument and contributes to the political objectives of the youth guarantee (providing unemployed young people with a quality job, training or traineeship within 4 months) in regions where the unemployment rate is above 25%. however, the original pre-financing rules, particularly as regards co-financing, meant that this instrument could not be used by the member states. in order to provide the necessary impetus for youth employment projects, the commission has proposed to increase the pre-financing rate from the current 1% to 30%, which de facto results in a eur 1 billion advance being released. in view of the urgency of the situation, i am pleased that parliament has approved this proposal by a large majority.
in writing. ‒ to tackle youth unemployment, the eu has launched the youth employment initiative to help particularly the most affected areas. unfortunately, because of the lack of sufficient public resources, member states have not made sufficient use of this tool for launching projects to offer young people a job, a traineeship or training. the commission therefore proposes to release €1 billion to allow a shift from 1% to 30% of project pre-financing from 2015. i can of course only support this initiative as youth employment must be the first priority.
in writing. ‒ the youth employment initiative's funding for the period 2014-2020 is €3.2 billion, with an additional €3 billion coming from member states' allocations from the european social fund. in february the commission adopted 28 (out of 34) operational programmes implementing this youth employment initiative. all could receive one third of the allowances in advance as soon as the amended rules come into force. this is of paramount importance. the number of unemployed people aged 15-25 who are neither in education nor in training is increasing alarmingly every year. i supported the adoption of the financing plan because i hope that these european funds will be able to help the member states to implement effective programmes and initiatives with a long-term effect, which some estimate will involve the employment of 650,000 young people.
in writing. i support the commission's proposal to insert in the european social fund regulation a provision providing for additional initial pre-financing for operational programmes supported under the youth employment initiative. the prefinancing rate would be increased from 1 to 1.5% to a maximum of 30%. the european union has already set up the youth employment initiative for the period 2014-2020 with a budget of €3.2 billion. economic recovery depends largely on active, creative, committed, dynamic and courageous youth.

in writing. ‒ meps undertook the annual ritual of the european discharge this afternoon. in practice, the european parliament's plenary, which generally follows the recommendations of the committee on budgetary control, is in fact checking whether the union's accounts have been managed in accordance with the rules. in a sort of audit role, the european parliament has for example given discharge to the european chemicals agency (echa). with a budget of €107 270 800, echa, based in helsinki, is one of the three major achievements of the reach regulation, which is a major turning point in the regulation of industrial chemicals. reach is also a new procedure: registration and authorisation, a new risk management tool. the agency's task is still enormous, since between 2007 and 2018, almost 30 000 substances (out of 100 000 existing on the community market), representing the vast majority of the tonnages produced and placed on the market, will have to be notified to the agency and registered by industrialists. reach is based on the principle: no data, no market .

in writing. ‒ meps undertook the annual ritual of the european discharge this afternoon. in practice, the european parliament's plenary session, which generally follows the recommendations of the committee on budgetary control, is responsible for checking whether the union's appropriations have been spent in accordance with the rules. in a sense, the european parliament is the accounting officer and the only authority that can grant, postpone or refuse discharge, which is a requirement for the formal closure of the accounts of all european organisations. the four political institutions are concerned: the european parliament, the commission, the council and the european council, but also the european court of justice and the european court of auditors and nearly 50 executive agencies and european institutes. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover the whole of the eu. they acknowledge the efforts made by the agency to seek synergies with other agencies, for example through the service level agreement on the performance of controls in collaboration with other agencies located in southern europe, such as the european maritime safety agency.

in writing. ‒ the eu's objective is to create a european capital markets union. i therefore welcome the commission's proposal to create money market funds, particularly to fill in gaps in investment and financing. as short-term financial instruments, money market funds can help the economy grow and provide a high level of liquidity in the short term. however, a strict regulatory framework is necessary to counter the risks of the funds.
in writing. ‒ i abstained in this vote because we did not have enough guarantees for a sound reform of the monetary funds at european level. monetary funds are a key component of the shadow banking system. there are two main families of money funds. the variable value mmfs and the constant value mmfs. the constant value monetary funds were at the heart of the concerns in this dossier. these constant value monetary funds operate outside the traditional banking regulation even though they act like banks. the promise of a constant value repayment is an accounting mirage. the price of the assets in which the fund invests fluctuates as in any financial market. this opacity creates an advantage for the first to escape the bottom, leaving the remaining investors to wipe out the entire losses in the absence of external support. the risk of panic and contagion is real in the event of market instability. it is therefore extremely important to legislate on this subject, providing all the guarantees of transparency and risk reduction.
in writing. – the money market fund regulation is very important as it represents a €1 billion market. such a large market is strategically important, especially in a period where we want to build capital markets as an alternative to bank financing. the regulation will be putting in place a new lvnav product which will be crucial to the financing of the real economy. however i am concerned about the 'sunset clause' whereby the lvnav will end after 5 years. the first argument is that the impact assessment estimated that €250 billion will flow away, and we really cannot afford this. the second argument is that it suggests a negative speculation that the product does not work and that consequently investors will not take up this new lvnav product if there is a cut-off date after 5 years. while i can support a review of the lvnav after 4 years this review should determine whether the lvnav should continue or not rather than the parliament predetermining the outcome with a sunset clause. the lvnav already has in place sufficient safeguards to address systemic risk for example daily and weekly liquidity thresholds, liquidity fees and redemption gates for times of market stress, strict diversification requirements etc. despite these reservations i have voted in favour of the mmf report, fully trusting that the outcome of the trilogue will deliver a more balanced text, especially around the sunset clause.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft regulation on monetary funds on the grounds that the aim of the proposal is to ensure that all types of monetary funds are transparent, liquid and stable, so as to enable them to play their role as short-term financing. monetary funds are an important part of the shadow banking system, which is viewed with justified concern because it is poorly regulated. i am glad that we have finally been able to adopt the common position after months of intensive discussions in the econ committee. i am particularly pleased with the change in the constant-net-worth monetary funds, a large part of which is now set to disappear within five years. the way is now open for negotiations with the council in the form of a trilogue. i hope that a compromise can be found with the member states.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament approved yesterday a common position on the proposal for a regulation establishing a european framework for money market funds. the text provides for the creation of three new types of constant value monetary funds ('cnav'): public debt cnavs, cnavs that would invest a majority (99,5%) of their assets in public debt, retail cnavs for charitable organisations, public authorities or foundations, and finally, under the leadership of the adle group, low volatility net asset value monetary funds ('lvnav'). for the latter category of funds, a clause is provided for a mandatory conversion of these lvnav to vnav (variable liquidity value funds) after 5 years (the 'sunset clause'). the commission will assess whether the lvnav funds address the issue of financial stability and systemic risk one year before the expiry of this authorisation. the commission will be required to submit a legislative proposal based on its findings, including the possibility of indefinite authorisation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the text. as an internal market specialist, i would stress that in order to preserve the integrity and stability of the internal market, it is necessary to establish rules on the functioning of monetary funds, and in particular on the composition of their portfolios. the aim is to make monetary funds more resilient and to limit the risks of contagion. uniform rules applicable throughout the union are necessary to enable mmfs to respond to investor redemption requests, in particular in stressed market situations. in addition, uniform rules should be established for the portfolio of such funds to ensure that they can cope with substantial and sudden redemption requests from a large group of investors.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament gave its green light this afternoon to the revision of the common import regime for certain textile products. the regulation, which was established in 1994, aims to promote the orderly and equitable development of trade in textiles between the european community and the supplying countries. the text is important for the sector, with a turnover of €166 billion in 2013, the european union is the 2nd largest exporter in the world, just behind china. technical shortcomings identified in the commission's work will therefore be corrected. in reality, it is much more than adapting the old procedure to the harmonisation imposed by the lisbon treaty. the overhaul decided yesterday implies real changes in substance. the textile sector employs nearly 1.7 billion people in the european union, so clarifying and simplifying these rules was crucial to ensure legal certainty, but also to allow the clothing and textile sector in europe to survive. #mrk
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the codification of council regulation (ec) no 517/94 of 7 march 1994 on the common rules for imports of textile products from certain third countries not covered by bilateral agreements, protocols or other arrangements, or by other specific community import rules. i am motivated by a concern for the clarity and transparency of the law. the proposed new regulation will replace the various acts incorporated in it, whilst fully preserving their substance. at present, the only countries exporting textiles to the union that are not covered by agreements, protocols or other bilateral arrangements are belarus and north korea. the regulation then sets quantitative limits on imports of several textiles originating in those two countries and allows surveillance measures to be imposed on other third countries where imports of textile products originating in those countries cause or threaten to cause serious injury to community production of similar or directly competing products.
in writing. ‒ we can sell clothes, we cannot sell human rights!!! i am sure i shall vote for this text and insist on the traceability of the origin of the garments and on the strict observance of working conditions in accordance with the human rights convention!
in writing. ‒ i welcome this proposal for the 2016 budget, in essence, because it recommends, among other things, to increase the transparency of the funds available to a member of the european parliament for the exercise of his mandate. i have, however, opposed an increase in the social assistance allowance, because it sends the wrong signal in times of shortage of public funds. this is the view shared by the belgian and dutch delegations within the epp group.
in writing. ‒ in this report i supported in particular the amendments which stressed the need for greater transparency in the allowance for meps' overheads and which also called on the bureau of the parliament to define more precise rules on responsibility for expenditure authorised under this allowance, without this entailing additional costs for parliament. i also supported the amendment which considered that an increase in the allowances for secretarial expenses of members was not appropriate in the current context of persistent crisis.
the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' in the context of the directive. i voted against it. the monthly allowance paid to 751 meps to run their offices and pay staff will rise from eur 21 379 to eur 22 879 in 2016 if these recommendations are implemented. this increase in the secretarial remuneration of members is not appropriate in the current context of the ongoing crisis. despite a dramatic socioeconomic crisis that is shaking the eu to its foundations, many of my colleagues unfortunately seem to be living in an ivory tower. liberals, christian democrats and social democrats say that we must work harder through the lisbon treaty. the epp even asked for more money than has been approved today. this is simply not necessary. in times of austerity, asking for extra money is not a good idea. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover the whole of the european union.

in writing. ‒ the eu loses a large amount of funding each year through financial fraud. however, only a minority of cases result in prosecution. for these reasons, it is now appropriate to establish a european public prosecutor's office (eppo) in accordance with article 86 (1) tfeu. the esta is now to prosecute financial crime at the expense of the eu centrally in cooperation with national law enforcement authorities. the national parliaments have been critical, particularly in relation to the respect of the principle of subsidiarity. i welcome the establishment of a central prosecutor's office and hope that it will live up to its role as an independent authority, with a clear division of responsibilities and the highest level of transparency.
in writing. ‒ an independent european public prosecutor's office should make it possible to combat fraud against the financial interests of the european union more effectively. to maximise its effectiveness, it must of course be coordinated with olaf and eurojust.
in writing. ‒ i supported the european commission's initiative to create a european public prosecutor's office because every year several hundred million euros from the eu budget are exposed to fraud, corruption and other criminal offences. these crimes undermine citizens' trust in the european institutions and deprive economic and social development of part of its funding. at present, the eu does not have the ability to prosecute criminal offences against its budget. criminal investigations/prosecutions are the exclusive responsibility of the member states and the efforts of national authorities to combat financial crime affecting the eu budget vary from one member state to another. there are also practical obstacles as law enforcement authorities rarely have the resources to carry out cross-border investigations. we therefore need a common response, namely a european public prosecutor's office with the power to conduct investigations (in collaboration with national authorities), to prosecute and to bring cases before the competent courts. in short, an independent european public prosecutor's office that brings real added value.
in writing. the european parliament sends a clear message: we say 'yes' to the european public prosecutor's office but 'no' to a bureaucratic, costly, inefficient structure which is dependent on the member states. the fight against fraud is above all an ethical issue, aimed at strengthening the rule of law and putting an end to situations of impunity. the effectiveness of the fight against fraud now depends on the goodwill and the arbitrariness of the member states. it is the european union's responsibility to defend its financial interests. i denounce the double-talk of some member states which publicly praise the added value of establishing a european public prosecutor's office but which in the backyard empty its substance by ensuring that they will maintain almost total control over its exercise. the european public prosecutor's office should be able to provide a genuine added value only if it is independent and transparent. the european parliament proposes in a report, to which i have actively contributed, a series of concrete measures to this end. the independence is mainly reflected in the process of appointing future prosecutors, in the distribution of competences (giving priority to the european public prosecutor's office), and in the structure of the european public prosecutor's office (where chambers composed of several prosecutors hold the real power).
