in writing. ‒ last week we adopted the report on the draft european public prosecutor's office. in this report we have stressed that this office, which is intended to combat fraud against the european budget, must be fully independent of national governments and european institutions and under democratic control. it is crucial that this office be free from political pressure. we also asked for the rules governing the division of jurisdiction between the public prosecutor's office and the national prosecutor's offices to be clearly defined and considered that national authorities who would conduct investigations falling within the competence of the european public prosecutor's office should be obliged to inform the latter. the selection procedures for the european public prosecutor's office should be open, objective and transparent. finally, i welcome this vote, which should make it possible to combat more effectively offences affecting the financial interests of the union. the commission estimates that this would mean a loss of more than eur 500 million per year. other agencies even estimate the loss to be $1.3 billion a year!
in writing. ‒ the european parliament today adopted by a large majority an interim report on the commission's proposal to set up a european public prosecutor's office. i fully support the proposal. this interim report sends a strong signal to european governments about the importance of a european public prosecutor's office. the european public prosecutor may not act unilaterally: any decision on, for example, the choice of jurisdiction, the indictment or the closure of a case must first be examined by a court. the report also stresses the importance of clear and consistent rights of defence, so that legal rules cannot be circumvented by cherry-picking and selecting the most favourable legal framework for a particular case. the creation of such a european public prosecutor's office will also strengthen the fight against tax fraud. the european commission estimates that €500 million of eu taxpayers' money earmarked for subsidies is being misused each year. that's disastrous in times of crisis. an effective european public prosecutor's office is needed to tackle this gigantic problem, all the more so as the existing european anti-fraud office (olaf) is only allowed to carry out administrative investigations and therefore has little real power.
in writing. ‒ the n-va delegation did not support the interim report as a whole. n-va is in favour of effective fraud prevention and efficient use of public funds. more needs to be done to tackle organised crime and fraud. fraudulent spending of public funds should be taken very seriously and investigated immediately with the full cooperation of all member states concerned. however, we do not think that the creation of the eppo as a new eu agency the third of its kind, alongside eurojust and olaf is the right solution. we are particularly concerned that the eppo would be an unnecessary duplication of anti-fraud instruments and thus a waste of taxpayers' money. the eppo is to be established by the european parliament and the council. in addition, it can only be stated that the pif directive, which contains the crimes that would fall within the competence of the eppo, is still stuck in trialogue negotiations. the commission's proposal is wrong in its approach and timing. we therefore see no reason to make a number of recommendations to the council in the margin as a condition for our agreement.
in writing. ‒ i agree with the rapporteur's considerations. the added value of the eppo should be to entrust a single and independent body at european level with the task of investigating and prosecuting criminal offences affecting the financial interests of the union, to increase the number of prosecutions, to improve the efficiency of recovery operations and to strengthen taxpayers' trust in the european institutions. the current system, while functioning well in some member states, has proven rather ineffective in prosecuting and recovering funds at union level.

in writing. ‒ on 19 april, 800 migrants fleeing conflict and persecution lost their lives when their boat of opportunity, which was taking them to a better world, sank. in the face of this terrible humanitarian tragedy, the european parliament reaffirmed its determination to fight ferociously against smugglers, the real criminals who exploit human despair as a commodity. this tragic event is unfortunately only the most important of a growing phenomenon. since 1 january this year, 24 000 people have reached the italian coast at the risk of their lives, thousands have been rescued at sea and the less fortunate, more than 1 500, have never made it to a safe port and have drowned in the mediterranean. today's emergency is a humanitarian one, and the response must be swift and effective. the budget for operation triton (border surveillance) will be tripled from 2.9 million to 9 million euros per month, but to tackle this scourge europe will have to propose more concrete measures, such as making frontex a genuine border protection agency, developing a humanitarian visa system that would not force migrants to rely on criminal networks, or implementing a genuine community asylum policy.
in writing. ‒ less than a week after the european summit on the migration crisis in the mediterranean following the tragedies at sea, the european parliament adopted a resolution calling for the mandate of operation triton, led by the frontex agency, to be clarified in order to increase its area of operation and be extended to eu-wide search and rescue operations. the text of the resolution also stresses that operation triton should resemble a permanent and robust european humanitarian rescue operation on the high seas, to which all member states would contribute financially. member states should continue to demonstrate solidarity and commitment by increasing their contributions to the budgets and operations of frontex and the european asylum support office. on this point, i welcome jean-claude juncker's decision to release €120 million for 2015 to enable the triton budget to be tripled and i share his disappointment at the council's refusal to tackle the problem of illegal immigration. the resolution also calls for greater efforts by the 28 on the issue of humanitarian visas and the strengthening of the fight against smugglers and traffickers and criminal sanctions.

in writing. ‒ on 19 april this year, some 800 people lost their lives fleeing persecution and conflict in their home countries. they died in the mediterranean, seeking a more humane existence that they hoped to find in europe. that hope is exploited by people smugglers who use criminal practices to make money off the backs of these people in their misery. the european union has already taken action to help the victims of the war in afghanistan. the european parliament has voted in favour of declaring war on these smugglers. we agree to a tripling of triton's resources but i fear that is by no means enough to deal with this influx of refugees. we need to focus on the causes of migration rather than just migration itself.

in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. the directive will also be extended to cover the use of energy from renewable sources, such as wind, solar, wind energy, wind turbines, and wind turbines.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this draft report which urges bosnia and herzegovina to adopt the interim agreement on preferential trade with croatia and at the same time calls on both parties to take account of mutual interests in order to conclude an agreement satisfactory both for the eu member states and for the members of the alliance.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament has given its approval to this report on exceptional trade measures for the benefit of the countries and territories participating in or linked to the eu's stabilisation and association process, and the suspension of their application with regard to bosnia and herzegovina.
in writing. ‒ on 2 april 2015, 148 students of the christian faith were killed by the somali terrorist group al-shabaab in a massacre at a kenyan university. the commission has also been asked to provide information on the situation in the country, and to provide information on the situation in the country. however, other regions are also experiencing a massive increase in religiously motivated violence, such as syria and iraq (is/da'ish). i condemn in the strongest terms the acts of violence motivated by religion and welcome the motion for a resolution tabled by parliament on the 'persecution of christians in the world in connection with the murder of students in kenya by the islamist terrorist group al-shabaab'.
in writing. ‒ on april 2, 2015, al-shabaab militants entered the campus of garissa university in kenya and killed 148 students, targeting mostly non-muslim students. the european parliament wishes to express its solidarity with the victims and their families. parliament also called on the kenyan authorities to avoid any polarization by opposing muslims and christians. parliament called on the eu to adopt a comprehensive and coordinated response to combat radicalisation and the financing of terrorism. indeed, the root of the problem of terrorism must be tackled if this global threat is to be eradicated.
in writing. ‒ the massacre of 147 students at kenya's garissa university is part of a series of atrocities by the terrorist group al-shabaab, which has already claimed responsibility for several large-scale attacks in kenya over the past 20 months, including the westgate shopping centre attack in nairobi, in which 67 people were killed, and two attacks in mandera county in late 2014, in which 64 people were killed. i supported the resolution because it condemns these savage murders and, more generally, the violence to which christian minorities are now subject, particularly in many countries of the african continent. i hope that my political group will be more active and more determined in denouncing the persecution of religious and ethnic minorities.
in writing. ‒ on april 2nd, in garissa, kenya, 147 students were murdered in cold blood, 79 others were injured, by members of the terrorist group al-shabaab. what was the motive for the murder ? religion, beliefs, where you came from. the number of attacks on religious minorities around the world has increased dramatically in recent months. christians were the target. that is why i have this afternoon wholeheartedly supported all the amendments tabled by the epp, which recall the harsh treatment of the christian community throughout the world. every day, hundreds of christians are being slaughtered, beaten and arrested by islamic terrorists. over 150,000 of them are murdered every year, just because they are christians. the murder of these christian students once again reveals the horror of jihadist groups. a reality that shows how these armies are engaged, in the name of islam, in a planned strategy not only of territorial expansion, but of extermination. #mrk
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution which condemns the recent attacks in various countries against christian communities and reaffirms its solidarity with all persecuted christians in various parts of africa, particularly following the atrocities in kenya, libya, nigeria and sudan. the number of attacks on religious minorities around the world, especially christians, has increased exponentially in recent months. the number of christians murdered each year now exceeds 150,000...
in writing. ‒ we cannot accept that people are killed for the sake of their faith, regardless of their religion. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution. i would like to express my deep concern at the misuse of religion by the perpetrators of terrorist acts in various parts of the world. the use of religion in various conflicts is not without its critics. the increasing number of terrorist attacks on churches around the world, including the one that killed 14 in pakistan on march 15, 2015, is a cause for concern.
in writing. ‒ in view of the recent destruction and looting of cultural monuments and sites, particularly in syria and iraq, i welcome this joint motion for a resolution. the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the european union's cultural heritage is protected. in addition, proceeds from the illegal sale of works of art are channelled directly to terrorist groups, in particular is/da'esh, thus becoming a means of financing terrorism.
in writing. ‒ recently, there have been many destructions of archaeological monuments in iraq, syria and tunisia. the vast majority of this destruction was perpetrated by groups linked to the islamic state. parliament condemned and deplored the cultural cleansing of syria and iraq by the islamic state. parliament also called on the eu high representative to take action to protect the cultural and archaeological heritage in these countries. parliament called on the commission to support all the initiatives promoted by unesco to safeguard and protect the cultural heritage of iraq and syria.
in writing. ‒ many archaeological, religious and cultural sites in syria, iraq and tunisia are now being targeted for destruction by extremist groups linked to the islamic state group. according to unesco, these attacks on cultural heritage are a real "cultural cleansing". they are also crimes against humanity and crimes of persecution. the illicit trade in cultural goods is the third largest illicit market after narcotics and arms. this trade is dominated by organized criminal networks. it is essential to put an end to this through a european strategy and the help of the member states. security measures must be implemented at eu borders to prevent cultural goods from syria or iraq from being smuggled across eu borders. we must do everything possible to prevent further looting and destruction and to protect civilian lives.
in writing. ‒ nearly 300 sites of syrian cultural heritage have been destroyed, damaged or looted in more than three years of war. adding to the civil war is the threat posed by the islamic state (is) group, which is accused in iraq of destroying historic sites and, at the same time, selling antiquities to finance itself. isis considers statues to be idolatry, and has dynamited many churches and other monuments, shrines of christian, jewish or muslim heritage. let's not forget that isil has complete control of the communications channels. it is likely that some of the works that are supposedly destroyed are in fact only copies, the originals, priceless and loaded with history, being sold to the highest bidders in order to continue financing their barbaric terrorism. finally, i would like to denounce this cultural extermination, not to mention the human extermination that marks the daily lives of syrians and all the inhabitants living, or rather surviving, in the entire area of influence of the group "islamic state". all dictatorships have always been based on fear and blackmail. it's the same here. europe cannot just sit by and watch the united states negotiate with the bloodthirsty bashar al-assad, nor can it watch this part of the world burn to the ground!
in writing. ‒ in view of the recent escalation of tension in the maldives, parliament expressed its concern at the political crisis in which the country is sinking and called on the eu high representative to monitor the situation closely.
in writing. ‒ the maldives is among the worst countries in the world in terms of torture and intimidation of the opposition, media and civil society. many authoritarian deviations are deplorable, such as the reintroduction of the death penalty. currently, in the maldives, minors can be sentenced as young as seven years old and executed as young as eighteen. in the meantime, they're in jail. this is an intolerable situation, contrary to international human rights obligations and the convention on the rights of the child. i support the motion to reinstate the moratorium on the death penalty. i also regret the serious irregularities in the trial of the former president, two former ministers and the former vice-president of the house. i support the demand that they be released and their rights respected. i support the call for an immediate end to political interference and the depoliticization of the maldivian judicial system. i call for a credible and open political process involving all democratic forces, with a view to restoring and preserving stability in the maldives and putting the country back on the path of democratic transition.
in writing. ‒ in this resolution, which i co-signed, the european parliament calls on all parties in the maldives to avoid any action that could aggravate the increasingly marked authoritarian drift and to respect democracy and the rule of law. the text calls for a credible and open political process involving all democratic forces and an immediate end to the intimidation of political opponents and political interference. the text also calls for an immediate end to all forms of violence against peaceful protesters, critical media and civil society. parliament also called for the depoliticization of the maldivian judicial system and for urgent reforms to guarantee the independence and impartiality of the judiciary. deploring the 'serious irregularities' in the trial of former president mohamed nasheed, we demanded his immediate release and full respect for his rights, should his conviction be overturned on appeal.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution which seeks to clarify the situation in the maldives. the conviction of former president mohamed nasheed for breaching anti-terrorism legislation raises very serious questions about the rule of law in the maldives. respect for the rule of law, the right to a fair trial, due process and the independence of the judiciary, as provided for in the iccpr, are essential elements of the democratic process. the citizens of the maldives, including former president nasheed, must be treated with respect for these important principles in a pluralistic society! the european union must follow the situation in the maldives more closely, the issue of respect for the rule of law must be raised at the un human rights council's universal periodic review of the maldives.
in writing. ‒ this is the annual follow-up report on albania's application for membership. the european parliament welcomes in particular the fact that the country was granted candidate country status in june 2014. parliament also welcomed the establishment of joint working groups to strengthen cooperation in the fields of justice, the fight against crime and the fight against corruption, among others. parliament also expressed concern at the continuing political division in the country and called for a climate of confidence to be established.
in writing. ‒ in july 2014, the president-designate of the european commission, jean-claude juncker, declared in the house that 'there will be no further enlargement in the next five years'. a sensible proposal which was one of the priorities of the mr programme in the last european elections. the need to consolidate europe before enlarging it does not mean that the negotiations with the neighbouring countries such as albania must stop. this country, which was granted candidate status in june 2014, certainly needs a european perspective, but it does not meet european standards today. the difficult economic and social situation in the eu requires increased vigilance. european decision-makers want to pay much more attention to chapters 23 ('judiciary and fundamental rights') and 24 ('justice, freedom, security'). in this respect, the 2014 follow-up report on albania indicates significant progress to be made in five priority areas, namely public service reform, strengthening the judiciary, fighting corruption and organised crime, and improving the protection of human rights. these are all areas which are at the heart of the rule of law.
in writing. ‒ in this follow-up resolution, meps called on the ruling coalition and the opposition in albania to cooperate in a responsible and constructive manner. parliament also noted that the fight against organised crime remains a major challenge in the country. the resolution also calls on albania to do more to ensure the independence, efficiency and accountability of the judiciary and to guarantee the independence of the public broadcaster.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the text. we can welcome the fact that albania has been granted the status of candidate country. this step should be seen as an incentive to continue reform efforts. concrete measures and long-term political commitment are needed to consolidate the democratic transition and to successfully pursue the reforms inherent in the process of accession to the european union. we must be vigilant to ensure that these reforms produce convincing results.
in writing. ‒ this is the annual follow-up report on bosnia and herzegovina's application for membership. parliament welcomed the council's response to its call for a review of the union's approach to bosnia and herzegovina. parliament also called on the country's political leaders to avoid any nationalist rhetoric which would increase divisions in bosnian society. parliament also expressed concern at the inefficiency of the judicial system and the extent of corruption in the country.
in writing. ‒ we do not vote in favour of this resolution because we do not share the underlying denial of the constituent peoples as the main constituent of the state system of a multi-ethnic state. on the one hand, we too believe that the action of every level of government should be geared to efficiency gains. on the other hand, we believe that the negation of the different policy preferences of the peoples who make up the community does not contribute to the further peaceful development of a multi-ethnic state in which the memories of violent conflict have yet to be healed.
in writing. ‒ in july 2014, the president-designate of the european commission, jean-claude juncker, declared in the house that 'there will be no further enlargement in the next five years'. a sensible proposal which was one of the priorities of the mr programme in the last european elections. the need to consolidate europe before enlarging it does not mean that the negotiations with the neighbouring countries such as bosnia-herzegovina must stop. this country, which has been a potential candidate for membership of the european union since 2003, certainly needs a european perspective, but today it is still far from european standards. the difficult economic and social situation in the eu requires increased vigilance. european decision-makers want to pay much more attention to chapters 23 ('judiciary and fundamental rights') and 24 ('justice, freedom, security'). the 2014 monitoring report on bosnia and herzegovina thus highlights the country's continuous efforts to integrate into the eu. progress still needs to be made in political and economic matters, but also in taking account of the interests of the citizen. concrete measures must be taken without delay at several national levels.
in writing. ‒ in this resolution on the 2014 follow-up report on bosnia and herzegovina that we adopted, we called on the new leaders of bosnia and herzegovina to agree with the european union on a well-defined roadmap to establish a broad and open reform timetable. and encouraged these leaders to fully commit to achieving the necessary institutional, economic and social reforms. as such, reform of the judiciary and of the fragmented, politicized and dysfunctional public administration is paramount. moreover, the political impasse, the overly complex and inefficient institutional architecture, and the lack of cooperation between political leaders are currently seriously hampering the country's stabilisation and development.
in writing. - i voted for the resolution. i encourage the new political leaders to avoid any divisive nationalist and separatist rhetoric that polarizes society, to seriously undertake reforms to improve the lives of the citizens of bosnia and herzegovina, to create a functioning, pluralistic and democratic state and to bring the country closer to the european union. otherwise, nothing will be possible.
in writing. ‒ the key issue for the eib at the moment is the creation of the structural and investment funds (esif). the fund is intended to transfer funds to weak regions, especially those with high unemployment and low economic growth. the commission will therefore be required to increase the number of workers. the report also stresses that the eib is not a bank with commercial interests but a catalyst for the financing of sound public and long-term private investment. i welcome the annual report of the european investment bank for 2013.
in writing. ‒ in this dossier, we have been thinking about how to develop the eib, since in the coming months the place that this institution will occupy in the european economy will be even more important. it will be responsible for managing the billions of euros in the juncker plan: over 300 billion euros that will be invested in the european economy to boost activity and create jobs. as the socialist group's representative on this issue, i have insisted that the eib should make sustainable investments; i think about buildings that use little energy. i also stressed one very damaging element for the european economy. in its investments, the eib does not invest directly in projects, but relies on financial intermediaries. and unfortunately, sometimes these intermediaries are based in tax havens, in luxembourg, in the cayman islands or in mauritius. this is clearly unacceptable and the eib will have to avoid these intermediaries in the future. i hope that these recommendations will make it possible to invest sustainably in the future and to revive the european economy.
in writing. – the 2013 european investment bank (eib) annual report is very important as it considers the activities of the eib as the largest public investor in the european economy and a catalyst for long-term private and public investment. i voted in favour of the report because it had the right focus in the current environment: the focus on smes, investments and governance is crucial for sustainable economic growth. the report also includes a strong section on transparency and financial intermediation and it correctly reflects the situation around climate and energy. a less positive element was the excess detail included on some areas that do not belong in the report – for instance, the detailed information around the european fund for strategic investment belongs in the efsi regulation, which is still being negotiated in trilogues. going forward, the report should increasingly consider the eib’s evolving role in an evolving landscape. the eib must strengthen its competitive position in the global market and must adapt itself to meet the needs of the market. we shall follow the eib closely to see if it is executing its role in a less bureaucratic way and more in line with market practice.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which considers that all possible resources of the member states and the european union, including those of the eib, must be effectively mobilised without delay to support public and private investment, boost competitiveness, restore sustainable and inclusive economic growth and promote the creation of quality jobs and infrastructure, in line with the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy and taking into account that the eib has a mission to support social cohesion and is able to provide meaningful support to member states facing difficulties in the current difficult socio-economic context.
in writing. ‒ i very much welcome the report by mr urtasun. although the eib has already made efforts to improve its operations, i remain concerned about the bank's operations, including the lack of transparency and accountability. in view of the important role that the eib will play in the development of the juncker plan, these shortcomings need to be addressed as a matter of urgency. the report we have adopted today rightly expresses concern about some of the projects supported by the eib, both in terms of their added value for the economy and in terms of environmental sustainability. instead of investing in controversial fossil fuel projects (such as the castor gas storage facility in catalonia) or road construction (such as the 'passante di mestre' motorway in italy, where there was a suspicion of mafia interference), the eib should go all in to supporting small-scale sustainable and energy-efficient projects, and stop financing non-renewable forms of energy. we also ask that the european fund for strategic investments (efsi), in which the eib will play a major role, invest in those areas where the benefits for employment are greatest, taking into account strict social and environmental standards.
in writing. ‒ on the advice of the experts in my political group, i voted in favour of the text. however, the improvement of the eib's financial instruments does not replace the economic and structural policy reforms implemented at national level to foster sustainable growth and job creation.
in writing. ‒ recognising that the theme of the 2015 world expo in milan - feeding the planet, energy for life - provides an opportunity to address global food challenges and imbalances, including food waste, undernutrition, obesity and global warming, parliament calls on the commission and the member states to take action to ensure the right to adequate, healthy, sustainable and reliable food.
in writing. ‒ tomorrow is the opening of the 34th world's fair. the expo not only offers numerous economic opportunities but, through its chosen themes, can also be a catalyst for addressing various global challenges, in particular the demand for healthy, sustainable and quality food. flanders, the region i represent, will be prominently present at the world expo to put its innovation, creativity and entrepreneurship firmly on the map. i attended the press conference recently where the flemish actions were proposed and was particularly impressed. the whole food chain is characterised by flemish expertise: the commission has also proposed a number of measures to improve the quality of foodstuffs, from production, land use and food safety to food surpluses and packaging to waste treatment. thanks to the commitment of many partners, flemish craftsmanship, which offers creative solutions to the challenges of tomorrow, is being presented in an excellent way. it also links up with a theme we are currently discussing in the eu, namely the transition to a circular economy that is more efficient in the use of raw materials and treats waste as a material. i am therefore pleased to announce that in september i will be able to provide a forum to bring some of these flemish best practices to the attention of the european parliament.
in writing. ‒ five years after shanghai, the world food fair, on the theme of how well the world eats, opens in milan tomorrow and will run until 31 october. under the slogan 'feeding the planet, energy for life', the 2015 world expo focuses on one of the most important global issues to avoid growing imbalances on the planet. indeed, the beginning of the 21st century is marked by two disturbing phenomena: on the one hand, nearly 900 million people worldwide suffer from malnutrition; on the other, about 1 billion people, mainly in the richest countries, are overweight or obese. this is why, during the six months of this international event, which brings together 145 countries and 53 national pavilions, the aim is to inform and raise awareness among industrial players, citizens and the media on the problems of sustainable consumption, nutritional diversity and food waste. we hope that the milan exhibition, beyond the beauty of the pavilions, the meeting between tradition and modern agriculture, will provide a starting point for answering the question: how can we feed two billion more people by 2030?
in writing. ‒ solving the problem of food security requires strong and viable agricultural and fisheries sectors throughout the european union, a prosperous and diversified rural economy, a clean environment, and family farms supported by a dynamic, fairer, internationally sustainable and properly funded common agricultural policy. this is, in essence, what the european parliament called for in its resolution on the 2015 world expo in milan, which opened on friday 1 may. parliament stressed the need to implement a sustainable and adequately funded cfp (common fisheries policy), to ensure consistency between the union's trade and fisheries policies and to step up the fight against illegal fishing.
in writing. ‒ the biggest challenge of world hunger is to ensure that everyone can feed themselves and, most importantly, feed themselves with healthy food. in europe, more than 22 million children are overweight, while adolescents on average consume only 30 to 50 per cent of the recommended daily allowance of fruit and vegetables. in the light of these figures, i believe it is essential to promote a healthy and balanced diet from an early age, while re-educating young citizens to know about food and its origin and to become familiar with its taste and texture. it is only through education that we will promote responsible and healthy lifestyles. this is the approach taken in my report which was recently adopted by the agri committee on the distribution of fruit, vegetables and milk in schools. the new programme must be understood as both a fresh food distribution programme in schools and a food education programme and must be accompanied by a clearly defined health objective: to reduce childhood obesity and to encourage the consumption of fruit, vegetables and milk.
in writing. ‒ the increasingly violent actions of boko haram and the increase in the geographical areas controlled by the group raise fears of the worst for nigeria, the most populous and ethnically and religiously diverse country on the african continent. parliament condemned the violence and deplored the massacres of innocents in the country. parliament also called on the international community to support the new nigerian president in his fight against the islamic group. however, parliament noted that the fight against terrorism must be conducted with respect for human rights and the rule of law.
in writing. ‒ nigeriathe violence perpetrated by the terrorist group boko haram in nigeria has already killed more than 22,000 people since 2009. the united nations estimates that 1.5 million people, including 800,000 children, have been displaced. i supported the resolution condemning the atrocities committed by boko haram. the new president of nigeria must do everything possible to restore stability and security throughout the country. this includes taking firm action against internal corruption, mismanagement and inefficiency in public institutions and the military. the fight against terrorism is never an isolated fight. the whole economic community of west african states and the african union must therefore step up their response to boko haram terrorism and coordinate the fight against terrorist groups in the sahel region. without large-scale cooperation, the violence will continue. the international community must help nigerians who have taken refuge in neighbouring countries. we must also do everything possible to free the 2,276 women and girls kidnapped by boko haram since last year.
in writing. ‒ this afternoon, the ep gave its support to the new president of nigeria in his fight against boko haram. his challenge is to end the violence of the rebel group and to restore security and calm to his country. nigeria is the largest economy in africa. despite its immense resources, it is one of the most unequal countries in the world: more than 70% of its population lives on less than $1.25 a day, while 10% controls more than 90% of the wealth. since 2009, the country has been in a bloodbath, teased by the madness of the boko haram terrorist movement. anyone who did not adhere to their extreme dogmatic beliefs was executed, beaten, raped, or kidnapped. in april 2014, the world was shocked by the abduction of more than 270 girls from a public school in chibok city. we remember, it was followed by the poignant #bringbackourgirls awareness campaign. but how many others since then? nigeria needs help. the international community must redouble its efforts to combat the root causes of this form of terrorism: corruption, trafficking, embezzlement, etc. the recent rescue of nearly 300 girls and women in sambisa forest gives hope...#mrk

for the ecr group the execution of eight death row inmates earlier this week caused a global uproar. the ecr group shares this indignation and condemns the execution of this barbaric punishment, both in principle and by virtue of article 2 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union. to remind us all, and especially the european leader who seems to have lost sight of the eu's view on the death penalty, of article 2, i repeat it here: "right to life: everyone has the right to live. no one shall be sentenced to death or executed". we respect indonesia's sovereignty and its authority to establish its own criminal laws. we all understand the fight against the global drug trade. it is a modern country with impressive economic development, but the moral aspect must not be lost sight of. it's manifested in many areas: from freedom of the press to freedom of expression to respect for fundamental human rights. the execution of the death penalty violates those human rights and is not a weapon to exercise authority. an appropriate response would have been to convert the death sentence into a life sentence or a long prison term. the people involved should be in prison, but they don't deserve to be killed. on behalf of the ecr group, my colleague charles tannock and i have written a letter to the indonesian government, asking for mercy. it couldn't have worked. i hope indonesia hears our signal today. stop the executions, please!

the situation of refugees in the yarmouk camp has been humanly unbearable for more than three years. this resolution is certainly intended to alert the international public to this tragic situation, which is too little known. it also has an interest in the context of a conflict that is far from being resolved in syria. it is a sign of the role of the european union, which, together with other powers, must be able to act in the syrian conflict, which is itself at the root of many problems, such as the refugee crisis and the catastrophic humanitarian situation, but also forced migration, which is synonymous with human tragedies that should be alleviated. that is why this resolution is so relevant, and i hope that it will be supported by all members.
mr president, the right to demonstrate is a fundamental right: the possibility of peacefully expressing one's discontent, whether with the government in power, in support of an international cause or in recognition of its specific features. this right is one of the best means of communication and action for civil society and the political world. it was on the pretext of unarmed gatherings that the algerian judiciary decided to imprison nine workers' rights activists. they were sentenced to terms of imprisonment of six to eighteen months in a permanent prison, solely because they were publicly and peacefully demonstrating their support for the workers and the unemployed. we must demand the unconditional release of these activists who are defending their legitimate rights. law 91-19, which prohibits the right to peaceful assembly, and article 97 of the algerian penal code, which criminalizes it, must also be repealed. these laws are used as a pretext to cover up algerian judicial abuses and violate algeria's commitments under the international covenant on civil and political rights and the african charter on human and peoples' rights.
for the greens/efa group mr president, what is striking about the history of benchmarks is that breaches of the law have continued massively, well beyond the financial crisis. you'd think the financial crisis would have brought the industry back to a little bit of reason. but some of the mega financial institutions - we've mentioned deutsche bank, but there are many others - have had fun manipulating these indicators for their own benefit, for years, until today perhaps. some will say, "well, today they have been fined by the banks, not by the individuals". i would remind you that in some countries these fines are even tax deductible, so they are paid by the taxpayer. so it was obviously time for a new regulation to be introduced, and i thank cora van nieuwenhuizen for her work. we had a compromise practically until the end. in the end, however, some last-minute amendments have in fact removed from this regulation a number of indicators which would otherwise have been considered critical. as you have seen, we have a hard regime for critical indicators and a soft regime for indicators that are considered non-critical. a number of indicators are therefore excluded from this legislation. the only thing i can say is that i am glad that the member state which controls these indicators the most, the united kingdom, did not wait for the european parliament to adopt a much stricter regulation than the one we are approving today. however, i wonder, a bit like sylvie goulard, why, when it comes to financial regulation - we know we have a single market - we are ultimately leaving it to the discretion of the member states, with little control for esma, moreover, to enforce this regulation. we cannot therefore accept that the definition of a critical indicator should be left to the member states. if we can still amend the text tomorrow at the last minute with the amendments we are going to table, we will be in the majority.

in writing. ‒ the waiver of parliamentary immunity is anything but a simple act and follows a very rigorous procedure. in the case of a member of the european parliament, immunity may, as a general rule, be waived where the offence is not connected in any way with the performance of the duties of a member of the european parliament and therefore falls within article 9 of the protocol on the privileges and immunities of the european union. the same article also provides that immunity may not be invoked in the case of flagrant misconduct and may not impede the right of the european parliament to waive the immunity of one of its members. this derogation is logical and is usually justified either by the seriousness of the facts alleged or by the possibility of reaching a judicial decision quickly. that is not the case with the adoption of the ferrara report this afternoon. the european parliament is simply following the advice of the committee on legal affairs, which had recommended that the european parliament should lift the parliamentary immunity of viktor uspaskich, as requested by the prosecutor general of the republic of lithuania. the commission has also proposed that the council should be able to take a decision on the matter.

in writing. ‒ following the london interbank offered rate (libor), commodities and exchange rate benchmark scandals that resulted in multi-million fine imposed on several banks in europe and the us, the commission published in september 2013 a draft regulation on a wide range of benchmarks, seeking to address possible gaps at every stage of benchmark production and use. the price of many financial instruments and contracts depends on the accuracy of the benchmarks. doubts about the integrity of indices used as benchmarks can undermine market confidence, cause losses for consumers and investors and distort the real economy. it was therefore time to regulate this system, in particular by defining the indices used as benchmarks in financial instruments and contracts. the socialist group, of which i am a member, has succeeded in extending the scope of the performance criteria, including the role of national supervisors in defining the key benchmarks, qualitative and quantitative criteria and the inclusion of all entities, not just those that are supervised.
in writing. – the benchmarks regulation is very important because the manipulation of benchmarks affects us all. the law came about following the scandal over the manipulation of the libor interest rate benchmark, which is frequently used to determine interest rates for mortgages and bank loans. i have voted in favour of the report as it is aimed to prevent the manipulation of financial benchmarks such as the london interbank offered rate (libor) and euribor. the new european legislation is a well-balanced as it lays down rules on how an index must be calculated and how possible conflicts of interest must be avoided. the new draft law will introduce eu-wide rules to improve the reliability, representativeness and fitness for purpose of benchmarks. producers of major indices are placed under the direct supervision of financial supervisors and the law will also provide more information to users of benchmarks.
in writing. ‒ today, the european parliament voted overwhelmingly in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the parliament and of the council to make the benchmarks used to price mortgages, loans and bonds of eu citizens more reliable. it is in response to the scandals concerning the manipulation of some of these financial indices. for example, between 2005 and 2009, large banks operating in the union manipulated the libor and euribor indices, the rates at which banks lend to each other, set daily by... the banks themselves. by manipulating these indices, banks have, among other things, influenced the prices of our financial products to their own advantage. they have thus amassed large sums of money at the expense of european consumers, businesses and investors. the main objective of this regulation is to streamline the process of calculating benchmarks by reducing conflicts of interest in the panel of european banks that determine the value of benchmarks. and it is to avoid further scandals of this kind and to restore public confidence in the financial sector that a new, stricter regulation was voted on this morning.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament approved by 517 votes to 146, with 27 abstentions, a common position on the proposal for a regulation to strengthen governance in the formation of financial benchmarks, paving the way for interinstitutional negotiations, the council being already ready. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'customs' in the definition of the concept of 'commercial property'. qualitative criteria have been added to determine which indices can be considered critical. the final decision on whether an index is critical would be taken by the european securities and markets authority (esma) and national authorities. however, a national authority could also consider an index administered on its own territory to be critical if it has a significant impact on the national market. the calculation of critical benchmarks that relate to at least two countries will be monitored by a college of supervisors, including esma and other competent authorities.
in writing. ‒ the manipulation of libor and exchange rate indices, as well as the alleged manipulation of other indices, have highlighted the importance of the indices as well as their weaknesses. in the wake of these revelations, the european union has revised its market abuse legislation to clarify the illegality of index manipulation and to include this type of behaviour in the criminal law. a large majority of european citizens are affected, directly or indirectly, by the indices. all financial instruments are affected by the use of indices: derivatives, equities and bonds, as well as physical and commodity markets, the latter having seen a considerable increase in the volume of commodity index funds over the last ten years.
in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of the report as it is aimed to prevent the manipulation of financial benchmarks. the new european legislation is well-balanced as it lays down rules on how an index must be calculated and how possible conflicts of interest must be avoided. the new draft law will introduce eu-wide rules to improve the reliability, representativeness and fitness for purpose of benchmarks.
in writing. ‒ this report prepares the international conference on financing for development to be held in addis ababa from 13 to 16 july 2015. the european union is the world's largest contributor to development aid financing. it is essential that the eu continues to devote 0.7% of its gni to development aid, as it is our responsibility to support developing countries. the report goes in that direction and that is why i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. ‒ official development assistance (oda) is a key instrument for financing development. in 2005, eu member states committed to spending 0.7% of their gross national income (gni) on oda by 2015. this objective was not achieved. i therefore support the political message which parliament is sending to the commission, the council and the european states through this report. by 2020, member states must meet their target and effectively devote 0.7% of their gni to oda, with 50% of oda and a minimum of 0.2% of gni for the least developed countries. however, domestic resource mobilization is more predictable and more sustainable than foreign aid, which cannot cover all investment needs in developing countries. i therefore support the call for the eu to develop a regulatory framework with developing countries that stimulates transparent and responsible investment and contributes to the development of a vibrant private sector in developing countries.
in writing. this report is timely; it prepares the eu's position for the international conference on financing for development to be held in addis ababa in july 2015. i welcome the adoption of this report which encourages the eu and its member states to honour their contribution of 0.7% of gdp. this commitment must be respected without delay. it is also necessary to develop innovative sources and strengthen the capacity of developing countries to overcome aid dependence through the promotion of good governance and the development of effective tax systems. sustainable development will only be possible if it is adequately funded and if it is based on the ability of developing countries to finance themselves access to basic public services such as improved health care. the promotion of good taxation, budgetary support, the development of banking, resilience to epidemics such as ebola and the sharing of health risks, the development of the autonomous capacity of african countries for peacekeeping are all themes that deserve special attention at the addis ababa conference.
in writing. ‒ 0.7% of gross national income, a symbolic figure, a reasonable figure to help the countries of the south to develop and, yet, a figure still unattainable for 24 of the 28 member states. in the face of north/south imbalances, unprecedented regional conflicts and the massive influx of refugees that is the direct consequence, the 28 capitals would have every interest in respecting their commitment signed in 2005. a goal set 45 years ago that has the full support of european citizens, at 85%, according to a eurobarometer published in january 2015. this is another reason for the eu to devote 0.7% of national income to official development assistance, especially as 1.5 billion people still live in extreme poverty. that is the message that the european parliament has sent today by its vote. of course, other sources of funding, including private ones, will also be needed to achieve the new sustainable development goals. however, public and private funding do not have the same roles and impact. and that is the major challenge we have to face: to ensure the best possible synergy between these different sources of funding.
in writing. ‒ 2015 is a pivotal year for global development aid action with the adoption of the sustainable development goals and an agreement on global climate action. i voted in favour of this report, which recalls that the european union is the world's leading donor of development aid and that this aid represents almost 60% of official development aid worldwide. the report also calls, and i welcome this, for the european union and its member states to reformulate without delay their commitment to allocate 0.7% of gnp to official development assistance, with 50% of development assistance and at least 0.2% of gnp reserved for the least developed countries.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the text. it urges the european union to assert its leading political role throughout the preparations for a sustainable development framework, a renewed agreement on financing for development and other implementing arrangements, in accordance with the commitments and values enshrined in its founding treaties. we believe that the conditions for the delivery of eu development aid should not be dictated by other partner donors.
in writing. ‒ a functioning, safe and effective healthcare system is essential. unfortunately, many preventable incidents still occur throughout the eu, especially in the field of patient care. the commission's progress report shows that the member states are on the right track, but in some countries the savings in health care resulting from the economic crisis are being sacrificed. this needs to be avoided and investment, in particular in research on resistance in human and veterinary medicine, needs to be maintained despite the economic stresses. i fully support this report because of the importance of improving patient safety and of containing antimicrobial resistance.
in writing. access to effective healthcare is a basic right in the eu. while there has been clear progress since 2012, the battle is not yet over. the exchange of good practice and efficient solutions between member states will only allow us to make the necessary progress. i therefore supported this report.
in writing. ‒ the debate on healthcare in europe is about a major issue: improving patient safety and antimicrobial resistance. the figures show that 8 to 12% of patients admitted to hospital in the union (more than 3 million people) suffer adverse events, including care-associated infections (cais). in fact, more than 25 000 people in europe die each year from ibs caused by multidrug-resistant bacteria. this sad record is due in part to cuts in health care, but mainly to a series of aggravating factors, such as the lack of appropriate national programmes, the difficulty of reporting 'adverse events' and collecting data, the lack of warning and monitoring systems, the inappropriate use of medicines, the packaging of antibiotics, etc. so much of this infection could be prevented. while public health is a matter for the member states, the eu has a certain amount of leeway. i voted for this report because i support the call for the governments of the 28 to invest in continuing training, monitoring of medical services, early warning systems and research into new effective products.
in writing. access to effective health care systems is an essential element of our european societies. this efficiency cannot be achieved without increased patient safety. while much progress has been made since 2012 in this area, this path should be continued, including through the exchange of good practices and effective solutions between all member states. that is why i am very much in favour of this proposal.
in writing. ‒ 37 000 people in europe, 3 000 in belgium, these are the worrying figures for the number of deaths each year as a result of hospital-acquired infections or antibiotic resistance. across the eu-28, more than 3 million people are infected in care facilities each year. the most common are urinary tract infections, pneumonia, infections in the area of the body that has been operated on and generalized infections, such as sepsis and bacteremia. the adoption by this afternoon's plenary of the pedicini report on safer health care in europe is important and provides an opportunity to take stock of the spread of microbes, particularly in hospital settings. i would like to draw attention to two key proposals to combat this phenomenon: investing in the search for new antibiotics that are effective, particularly against diseases that are particularly likely to be resistant to antimicrobials, such as k. pneumoniae, e. coli, hiv, staphylococcus aureus or tuberculosis; strengthen intensive hygiene and control programmes, in particular early detection of resistant strains and isolation of patients with severe bacterial infections. it is clear that the issue of hospital-acquired infections must become a public health priority.
in writing. ‒ yesterday, in plenary, we adopted a resolution on safer healthcare by 637 votes to 32, with 10 abstentions. the resolution deplores the negative impact of the economic crisis on national health budgets and calls on the member states to ensure that patient safety is not affected. we also proposed measures to ensure that antibiotics are used more responsibly, such as prescription-only use, microbiological diagnosis before prescription, marketing practices to prevent conflicts of interest between producers and prescribers, better information and increased surveillance. we also called on pharmaceutical companies to invest in new antimicrobials and asked the commission to put in place a legislative framework to encourage the development of new antibiotics. finally, we have advocated limited use of antibiotics in veterinary medicine, which should be limited to therapeutic purposes.
in writing. ‒ patient safety and the fight against drug resistance, in particular antimicrobial resistance, are certainly not unknown topics to those who manage health systems, or to those who have frequented the chambers of the european parliament's committee on the environment, public health and food safety in recent years. in this context, this own-initiative report is a step in the right direction.
in writing. ‒ improving patient safety and tackling antimicrobial resistance is of paramount importance. access to effective healthcare is a basic right in the eu. while there has been clear progress since 2012, the battle is not yet over. the exchange of good practice and efficient solutions between member states will only allow us to make the necessary progress. i therefore supported this report.
in writing. ‒ it was important that parliament could take a stand on this issue of the future of smes in europe. i am pleased to see that we have been able to instill concrete measures on green growth in smes. green growth sectors have economic and environmental benefits for smes in the eu and are set to grow significantly in the coming years. the starting idea is that economic growth and environmental sustainability can go hand in hand. smes are the backbone of the european economy and an important driver of economic growth and job creation. the vast potential of the green economy can only be fully exploited if there is a suitable framework for research, development and innovation.
in writing. as rapporteur for this report, i have looked at where the growth opportunities lie for our european smes active in the green growth sector. at the same time, i thought it was important to also make clear where the bottlenecks are: the commission has already taken a number of measures to improve the quality of the information provided by smes. i am glad that, with the support of a large majority in this house, i can put these elements on the agenda.
in writing. making the european economy more sustainable is essential. an effective strategy cannot be achieved without unconditional support for smes, the lungs of our european economy. the action plan proposed in this document aims to promote the greening of european businesses while supporting the development of green entrepreneurship. it will also allow for better exploitation of resources, thus ensuring a certain gain in competitiveness in the long term. at a time when the european economy is in need of a revival, it is more vital than ever that it move without delay towards a more profitable and sustainable model.
in writing. ‒ this report, which i voted for, is based on the green action plan for smes launched by the european commission, a genuine initiative to encourage smes to take greater advantage of green growth. among the 183 amendments put to the vote, many focused on support for the green and circular economy and the growth opportunities in these areas. i voted in particular in favour of the provisions which stressed the importance of using resources more efficiently and those which aimed to facilitate the start-up of young and start-up companies by working with research institutes, universities and vocational training centres.
in writing. ‒ green growth sectors have tremendous economic and environmental benefits for smes in the european union and are set to grow significantly in the coming years. the starting idea is that economic growth and environmental sustainability can go hand in hand. smes are the backbone of the european economy and an important driver of economic growth and job creation. it is important that policy-makers fully grasp the potential of the green economy, while being aware of the challenges faced by smes, in particular with regard to greening their products, production processes, business practices and services. the commission's green sme action plan is a positive initiative, which will encourage smes to further enhance the benefits of green growth.
in writing. ‒ i wholeheartedly supported the report by mr philippe de backer, member of the open house. european smes active in the green growth sector have a variety of growth opportunities but also bottlenecks such as knowledge, lack of investors willing to take risks, etc. it is important that these elements are put on the agenda and that europe can think about how it can respond to the various needs of these smes.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the new directive to step up the fight against tax evasion, money laundering and terrorist financing. i also supported the new money transfer regulation which aims to improve the traceability of payers and recipients and their assets. financial crime is a cross-border phenomenon. to combat this, the eu needs to have harmonised rules. i am therefore glad that members have wanted to go further than the commission's proposal. the requirement for member states to maintain central registers containing information on the beneficial owners of companies and trusts is a major step towards greater transparency. these new rules are an important step in the fight against money laundering, corruption and terrorist financing. they ensure consistency with the approach taken at international level. it is now time for member states to implement these new rules swiftly.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament has completed a new strategic legislation to combat money laundering and terrorist financing. the tools introduced by this directive, in particular the register of beneficial owners, will strengthen the capacity of national authorities to detect and identify billions of euros of criminal activity. the new rules are more flexible, focusing on high-risk activities and providing for simplified measures for low-risk activities. this new legislation will make the european market work better, while strengthening the stability of our economies. we will also be better equipped to detect the financial flows that support terrorist groups and thus better able to combat this scourge. it is therefore crucial that these rules are operational as soon as possible. by adopting this text, we have not only brought our rules into line with the most recent international recommendations on this matter, including those of the financial action task force, but we are also setting an example for the rest of the world. in order to make our efforts more effective, we will need to strengthen our cooperation with third countries which are moving in the same direction.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which provides for stricter rules on money laundering to combat tax evasion and the financing of terrorism. from now on, company owners will have to be registered in the central registers of eu countries, which are open to both the authorities and to persons with a 'legitimate interest', such as journalists. i also welcome the adoption of new rules to facilitate the tracing of transfers of funds.
in writing. ‒ i welcome this vote, which marks a major step forward in the fight against money laundering, corruption and tax evasion. the european parliament agreed to a register of ultimate stakeholders so that public authorities, citizens and organisations can see which natural person is behind a jumble of corporate structures. transparency is the biggest enemy of money launderers and tax evaders. thanks to this legislation, anyone with a valid application will soon be able to see the shadowy structures behind companies. criminals try to launder money they have earned through corruption, fraud and drug trafficking, among other things, through a network of companies with opaque structures. they use it to try to fool the government and the citizens. every year, two to five percent of our economy is laundered worldwide. you figure out what that's gonna cost the taxpayer. the register of ultimate stakeholders also clarifies the structures through which multinationals evade tax. tax evasion is legally legal, but morally unacceptable. with this register in hand, researchers can pinpoint which multinationals are not interested. the european union countries now have two years to transpose the directive into national law and to establish a register of final stakeholders.
in writing. ‒ the beneficial owners of companies will have to be registered in the central registers of eu countries, open to both authorities and persons with a 'legitimate interest', such as investigative journalists, under the new rules agreed with the council and adopted by the plenary on wednesday. the new directive aims to step up the fight against tax fraud and the financing of terrorism. that's a good thing!
in writing. ‒ the proposal aims to revise the regulation on information on the payer accompanying transfers of funds in order to increase the traceability of payments and to ensure that the eu framework remains in line with international standards. the regulation on transfers lays down rules requiring payment service providers to transmit information on the payer throughout the payment chain for the purposes of preventing, detecting and investigating money laundering and terrorist financing. the aim of the proposal is to increase transparency by including the following changes: information on the principal; to bring credit cards, debit cards and telephones within the scope of the regulation if they are used for money transfers; obligation to establish a risk-based procedure to determine when a payment is to be blocked, suspended, executed, etc.; align with the fatf traceability rules; to strengthen the sanctioning power of the competent authorities; make the publication of penalties compulsory.
in writing. ‒ the adoption of this new regulation is part of the european parliament's efforts to establish a legislative framework that provides the necessary tools for the prevention and detection of money laundering and terrorist financing. more specifically, the rules adopted today improve the traceability of money transfers, in line with the recent revision of international standards on the subject. we have today chosen greater transparency in a financial system which is becoming increasingly complex and therefore more prone to fraud. action to increase transparency is therefore in the interest of citizens by combating money laundering. this is a huge sum of money every year and internationally, between 2% and 5% of gdp , money that does not benefit our economies. and the toll is even higher because the terrorism financed by these laundered funds affects the lives of millions of people around the world. this new regulation is important because it increases transparency while ensuring that the storage and exchange of information complies with the criteria of personal data protection and privacy.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament rejects the commission's proposal for a delegated act because it considers that the exemption granted for the use of cadmium in screen lighting is based on an outdated situation as cadmium can already be replaced by quantum boxes. in view of the danger of cadmium to human health and the damage it causes to the environment and in the light of technological developments, the use of cadmium for screen lighting should be banned as soon as possible.
in writing. ‒ since 1993, cadmium has been classified by the international agency for research on cancer (iarc) as a human carcinogen, i.e. as dangerous. this heavy metal is found in products as varied as batteries, solders, paint pigments, fertilizers, and pesticides, as well as in general lighting and screen lighting applications. the commission is also proposing to extend the derogation for this substance provided for in the rohs (restriction of hazardous substances) directive. i agree with the objections raised by the european parliament for at least two reasons: the first is linked to the very principle of this legislation, which has banned the use of dangerous substances such as lead, mercury, cadmium, hexavalent chromium and polybrominated diphenyl ethers (pbde) since july 2006. the second reason concerns the exemption for cadmium on lighting applications, such as led lamps, which normally expired on 1 july 2014. there is therefore no justification for extending the derogation as the european commission wants, which must not compromise the health of european consumers.
in writing. ‒ yesterday, by a very large majority (618 votes in favour, 33 against and 28 abstentions), the european parliament vetoed the commission's proposal to authorise, by way of derogation and by delegated act, the prolonged use of cadmium in lighting applications for television screens using quantum dot technology. the carcinogenic heavy metal cadmium is one of the substances restricted for use in the european union under the directive on the restriction of the use of hazardous substances in electrical and electronic equipment (directive 2011/65/eu). although the commission has invoked the need to adapt this legislation to technical progress and has argued that cadmium-free quantum dots were not yet technically available to justify its proposal to exempt cadmium from the provisions of the directive until july 2017, its argument has not convinced us. other solutions exist and a range of tvs using cadmium-free quantum dot technology are widely available on the european market. in other words, the draft legislation was not justified.
in writing. ‒ following a ban on f-gases, the european parliament is now taking the fight against cadmium to the next level. cadmium is harmful to health, while there are equivalent alternatives available. the european parliament therefore objects to a commission proposal to allow the use of cadmium in televisions and lamps. naturally occurring cadmium is present in very low concentrations in the earth's crust. as a result, our bodies cannot cope well with prolonged, heightened exposure. that leads to adverse effects, from high blood pressure to bone formation disorders. the commission therefore prohibited the use of cadmium, with one exception: television sets. by placing so-called cadmium quantum dots in tvs, they become more energy efficient. the commission considers that this advantage outweighs the adverse health effects of its use. the commission intends to extend this derogation. this is despite the fact that cadmium-free quantum dots are available on the market. the commission also succumbed to an intensive lobbying by lamp manufacturers, which is extending the use of cadmium to lamps. the commission has also carried out a study to evaluate this extension. it is therefore a good thing that the european parliament as a whole is now opposing it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the commission delegated directive amending, for the purpose of adapting it to technical progress, annex iii to directive 2011/65/eu of the european parliament and of the council as regards an exemption for cadmium in general lighting and screen lighting applications. this is a readjustment text.

in writing. ‒ the bacterium xyllella fastidiosa is currently decimating olive trees in southern italy. it is estimated that 10% of the trees in the lecce area , or several thousand hectares , are already infected. it is therefore urgent that the european commission take all necessary measures to prevent the spread of the bacterium to other regions of italy and to other member states. finally, the commission must also take measures to provide financial support to farmers affected by the outbreak.
in writing. the pathogen xylella fastidiosa, also known as olive tree plague, has taken on serious proportions. this plant disease causes a very heavy economic loss to the entire production chain of the olive industry in italy. since the first detection of this pathogen in italy in 2013, more than 1 million trees have already been affected. it is feared that this bacterial infection, carried by insects, is now threatening more than 11 million olive trees and that if it spreads, it could infect several southern crops. for the time being, xylella fastidiosa cannot be controlled on its own and efforts should focus on preventing further spread within the eu. to this end, it is recommended that drastic phytosanitary measures be taken. for example, specific controls on the import of plants which may be carriers of that disease should be streamlined and increased, and it is recommended that only plants from production zones free of the bacteria be transported. it is also necessary to monitor carefully the use of pesticides in the fight against crickets, the main vector. in any case, the commission should intensify scientific research into efficient and sustainable pesticides and the commission and the member states should choose the best approach for a rapid economic and landscape recovery of the affected regions.
‒ xylella fastidiosa, a barbaric name for a bacterium recently discovered in southern italy, in the province of lecce to be more precise, and which has already caused considerable damage to olive groves in this region. the european parliament has taken this threat very seriously by adopting this afternoon a resolution on this pathogen which is causing concern to the authorities and the agricultural world. the latter follows the decision taken on 28 april by experts from the 28 countries of the european union to strengthen prevention measures and in particular to ban the import of coffee plants from honduras and costa rica, since three coffee plants were tested for xylella contamination on 15 april. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. efsa has already expressed in a communication the importance of targeting the import of host plants in order to avoid 2015 being the year of the spread of this bacterium in europe.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament adopted a resolution calling for additional measures to prevent the spread of the xylella fastidiosa bacterium that is infecting olive trees in puglia, italy. it should be noted that xylella fastidiosa poses an immediate and very dangerous threat to the production of certain crops in southern europe, in particular olive trees, almond trees and peaches, as well as vines and citrus fruits. the bacterium could also cause unprecedented losses and severe economic, environmental and social consequences. parliament therefore called on the commission to take targeted measures to prevent the spread of xylella fastidiosa in the union. it was asked to compensate producers for the eradication measures and loss of income and to use all possible funds and instruments to contribute to the economic recovery of the affected areas. parliament also called for greater resources to be made available to ensure the detection of harmful organisms at points of entry into the union. finally, parliament called for the creation of a public database to enable the exchange of information and the development of detailed guidelines for the application of disease prevention and control measures.
