in writing. ‒ i supported this report which underlines that a transition to sustainable societies and economies, including sustainable consumption and production patterns, can offer the opportunity to create new quality jobs while converting existing jobs into green jobs in almost all sectors and throughout the value chain. the report also calls for the introduction of social and environmental criteria in public procurement policies and for the reduction of employment burdens in favour of environmental taxation (without impact on the financing of social protection).
europe can achieve a new period of economic growth if it resolutely chooses to shift to a low-carbon and sustainable economy. a green economy offers solutions for the climate and the environment, but also for society. through structural change to a green growth economy, we can transform the existing traditional employment and create new job opportunities. a green transition will have a positive impact on employment. however, a number of processes need to be put in place to support and accelerate the transition to a green growth economy. without new skills, there are also no opportunities for high-quality new jobs. education is best prepared for this by closing the gap between the training it provides and the skills needed for the jobs of the future. for industry, high-quality innovation should prepare the economy for a low-carbon and energy-efficient future. particular attention should also be paid to smes, which are the main drivers of employment creation in europe. sme-oriented measures should aim to further stimulate innovative green entrepreneurship.
in writing. ‒ in july 2014, the commission published its 'green jobs initiative: harnessing the job creation potential of the green economy', showing its unwavering interest in the eu's transition to a low-carbon economy. the european parliament responded this afternoon by adopting the jean lambert report which highlights the potential of the green economy in terms of job creation. in an internal working document from 2012, the commission had indeed gone a little too far when it boasted that "up to 20 million jobs could be created by 2020 in the green economy", but the ongoing economic and social crisis in europe no longer allows us to set such ambitious targets, but the trend is there. investing in the circular economy and renewable energy is seen as a matter of course, if not a necessity, for europe to get back on the path to sustainable growth and quality jobs quickly. the report also calls for a meeting of eu leaders at the end of 2016 to take advantage of the mid-term review of the multiannual financial framework (mff) to support the greener transition of our post-industrial economies.
in writing. ‒ through its europe 2020 strategy, the european union aims to develop a smart, sustainable and inclusive economy. to do this, the eu has set itself five ambitious targets to be achieved by 2020. these include the target of 75 per cent of the population aged 20-64 having a job by 2020. to achieve this, europe is focusing on promoting sustainable and inclusive growth. between 2002 and 2011, an estimated 3 to 4.2 million green jobs were created. to continue along this path and to achieve the objectives set out in the europe 2020 strategy, the report in question proposes concrete ways of making the most of the potential for green job creation. given the importance of promoting sustainable and inclusive growth in order to create jobs, but also not to jeopardise the living conditions of future generations, i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mrs lambert's text. while it is clear that the world of work is already being affected by major international trends, the eu's response has so far been limited. in order to ensure that we can maintain and develop employment opportunities and job creation, we need a comprehensive and joint response, from the political level down to basic training. time is running out, because we are now missing opportunities that are being seized in other parts of the world, and we are not fully preparing our workforce to deal with the challenges that we are already facing.
in writing. ‒ many developing countries lack the resources to provide sufficient public goods (education, infrastructure, etc.). the lack of public funding is due in no small part to the massive tax evasion and avoidance practices in the countries concerned. i support the proposed action plan to combat tax evasion and tax evasion in developing countries, so that european development aid can be stepped up in this area too.
in writing. ‒ this report provides an opportunity to address the issue of taxation in developing countries. tax evasion is a scourge that affects all countries of the world. these means of avoiding taxation by moving all or part of the assets or activities to another state, in an illegal, fraudulent or unfair manner, represent a significant lack of revenue for the state budget, revenue that could be allocated to vital needs for the entire population: social security, health care or education. tax revenues should contribute to strengthening public investment capacity in developing countries. it is important for these countries to raise fair and effective taxes to finance infrastructure, public services, health care and education. it is also an essential tool in the fight against poverty. this is why we must support the transfer of knowledge and skills to help develop their tax administrations. the oecd provides us with an effective example of good practice through its 'tax inspectors without frontiers' initiative.
in writing. national revenues are and will continue to be the main tool for financing sustainable development. the mobilisation of national revenues is a prerequisite for ending aid dependence and promoting universal access to public services. developing countries (ldcs) are rich in natural resources, but these resources generate only a small share of national income. although the share of national income in the gdp of the developing countries has increased in recent decades, it is still very low. in most countries, it is below the threshold below which governments have difficulty in financing basic public services (15%). it is essential to strengthen tax systems and to combat tax evasion and tax fraud in the developing countries. i welcome the adoption of the report on tax evasion and tax evasion. this is a strong message to the negotiators at the international conference on financing for development, because optimal taxation not only increases the resources available for development, but also strengthens good governance and consolidates the state by promoting the stability of governments' budgets and allowing them to take ownership of their policy choices.
in writing. ‒ ahead of the conference on financing for development in addis ababa, ethiopia, from 13 to 16 july 2015, the european parliament adopted this afternoon an important and detailed report to support developing countries in the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion. it is true that the lack of fair, efficient and transparent tax systems is often glaring in the developing countries. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover the whole of the eu. another benefit of good governance in the area of taxation is that it would enable many developing countries to move beyond their long-term dependence on foreign aid and to move in the opposite direction, where tax revenues would be reinvested in the consolidation of the state and public infrastructure. a new approach which will obviously require good european cooperation with the beneficiary countries, in terms of training sessions, expert missions or other forms of supporting activities.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which calls on the european commission to present without delay an ambitious action plan on supporting developing countries in the fight against tax evasion and the establishment of fair, balanced, efficient and transparent tax systems and urges that beneficial ownership information on companies, trusts and other institutions be made public in open formats. the text also calls on the european union and the member states to enforce the principle that multinational companies in all countries and sectors, whether listed or not, should make the publication of country-by-country information a standard and welcomes the adoption of an automatic exchange of information mechanism. the report also calls for a global definition of tax havens, the introduction of sanctions for operators who use them and the drawing up of a blacklist of countries.
in writing. ‒ given the importance of better mobilisation of domestic resources and the problems faced by developing countries in the fight against tax evasion and tax fraud, there is a need for a list of recommendations that parliament should support, in view of the international conference on financing for development to be held in addis ababa and given the range of existing international initiatives to reform the global tax system. this includes: strengthening financial and technical assistance to developing countries and regional tax administrations; adopt solutions to improve transparency and cooperation in the fight against tax evasion, such as an automatic information exchange mechanism and the publication of country-by-country information, taking into account the needs and constraints of developing countries; conduct a study at eu and member state level on the impact of tax policies on developing countries. the tax rights of source countries should be preserved in the negotiation of tax conventions and a genuinely intergovernmental body should be created in which developing countries can participate in an equal footing in the overall reform of existing international tax rules.
in writing. ‒ the global economy uses one and a half times the value of the planet's resources to produce and absorb waste worldwide. it is estimated that by the 1930's this amount will have reached the resources of two planets. europe is more dependent on imported resources than any other region in the world, and many resources would be depleted in a relatively short time. i welcome this report because it addresses this problem, among other things, and also because it points out that improving the use of resources could bring substantial net savings to businesses, public authorities and consumers in the union, estimated at eur 600 billion or 8% of annual turnover, while reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 2·4%. in addition, increasing resource productivity by 30% by 2030 could generate almost 1% gdp growth and 2 million additional permanent jobs. resource efficiency therefore remains one of the most important components of sustainable living.
in writing. ‒ i supported this report in favour of the transition to a circular economy. this approach is obviously based on a model that favours sustainable investments. the commission should rapidly present ambitious proposals on the circular economy to limit the environmental impact of the extraction, processing, production, use and disposal of raw materials. sustainable waste management, including recycling, is also essential. i am also of course in full support of the provision to ask the commission to set quantified targets for the reduction of food waste. the donation of foodstuffs must increase substantially within the union and the commission must create a favourable environment in this respect. i will continue to take initiatives in this area in my work as a member of parliament for wallonia.
in writing. – i voted in favour of the resource efficiency report because i believe we have to make a change in the way we use our resources. as i also wrote in my report on green growth opportunities for smes, making the transition to a more efficient economy can lead to advantages for our businesses, in addition to the large environmental benefits that it will bring.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the circular economy and recycling of waste. the european commission has withdrawn a legislative proposal on the circular economy from its 2015 work programme, but it is expected to come back with a proposal in the coming months. i am glad that parliament is seizing this momentum to adopt a text supporting ambitious measures such as a 30% increase in resource productivity and a gradual and binding reduction in landfilling. this is a good initiative and i hope that the commission will follow suit. belgium is the world champion in recycling, but other member states have a lot of room for improvement. i personally support in particular the call for the creation of conventions in the member states which would require large supermarkets to redistribute their sales to food associations. this provision seems obvious to me when you consider that in europe some 90 million tonnes of food are thrown away every year, while millions of people are dependent on food aid. i am sorry to say, however, that in some european countries food waste is not even a topic.
in writing. today, only 40 percent of solid waste is reused or recycled. the rest of the waste is still going to landfill or incineration. the circular economy offers a sustainable solution to the waste problem. unlike in the linear system, where raw materials are converted into products that are destroyed after a short lifetime, the circular economy aims to maximise products and raw materials and minimise value destruction. not only does this reduce the waste mountain, opting for a circular economy also means developing new opportunities for growth and jobs in europe. the european commission is talking about a 'boost' that will create up to 2 million new jobs by 2030. european companies and smes will also be less dependent on imports of raw materials in this economic system and thus strengthen their global competitiveness. the european commitment to a better environment and a sustainable economy is not without obligation. to achieve the economic and environmental objectives, investment is needed to modernise production processes and to produce better recyclable and sustainable products. a policy framework is required to support the businesses that are driving this transition to a circular economy.
in writing. ‒ the pietikäinen report is an important text in the work of the european parliament. it suggests a paradigm shift, that of moving from an economy designed for at least two centuries in a linear way, that is to say closely dependent on a line of production, consumption and exchange consisting of producing goods to consume them, then throwing them away, infinitely, to a circular economy. based on better exploitation of human or natural resources used and an expansion of capital invested, the circular economy is the appropriate response to the scarcity of resources in europe and the fact that 40% of the materials used in the european union are imported. to take the example of an irreplaceable everyday object, the smartphone: at the end of 2013, its life expectancy was estimated to be less than two years in europe, compared to eight years in india. however, the world is still not recycling enough of its highly polluting electronic waste: 80% of it ends up in landfills. it's not sustainable! it is therefore much more than the technology that needs to be changed, based in particular on the planned obsolescence of products, it is the whole economic model that needs to be revised in order to achieve a modular mobile telephone in the coming years!
in writing. ‒ the transition from a society of waste and resource waste - whether food, energy or raw materials - to a society of repair, reuse, recycling and resource efficiency is a necessity and a great opportunity for europe. a strong commitment to a circular economy will enable the union to reduce its dependence on imported resources, protect the environment, boost innovation and the competitiveness of its industry and create jobs. the text adopted urges the commission to submit new legislation based on binding targets for waste reduction and the progressive elimination of landfilling and a policy that promotes the decoupling of economic growth from resource use. the text also calls on the eu to achieve a sustainable production model by 2050 and to set binding targets for the reduction of waste generated by 2025. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european union. the european parliament called for the creation of conventions in the member states under which the retail food sector would distribute unsold products to charitable associations.
in writing. ‒ each european citizen produces 5 tonnes of waste a year and consumes up to 14 tonnes of raw materials. we are consuming and producing more and more while the planet's resources are dwindling by the day. this must stop, or it will seriously handicap the lives of our children and grandchildren. the european parliament has voted in favour of the commission's proposal to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' to cover the transport of dangerous goods. more efficient waste management and improved product durability must once again become european priorities. reuse, repair or transform: these are the three key words of the circular economy. without this, our society has no future.
in writing. ‒ the 2010 fukushima nuclear disaster has once again shown that, despite the latest technology and safety measures, a nuclear accident can never be ruled out. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's energy policy is not undermined by the failure of the member states to implement the directive. we need pan-european strategies to be better prepared for such incidents. this includes clear provisions on maximum levels of radioactivity in food and feed. they can help to ensure that consumers are protected from contaminated food more quickly in the event of a nuclear emergency. for these reasons i support the report by mrs esther herranz garcía.
in writing. ‒ the n-va delegation supports the original proposal of the european commission and therefore votes against the parliament's position. in its opinion of 31 march 2015, the european parliament's committee on legal affairs clearly advocates the preservation of the euratom legal basis as proposed by the european commission. this is also consistent with other relevant legislation. the european parliament also wanted to change the legal basis for the rules on the protection of public health against radioactive substances in water intended for human consumption. but the court of justice disagrees and has made it clear that the procedure laid down in articles 31 and 32 of the euratom treaty takes precedence over more general provisions of the tfeu when it comes to union measures for the protection of public health against radiation and radioactive contamination. the committee on legal affairs considers that, even under the legislation in question, a change in the legal basis would most likely result in the act being annulled if challenged before the court.
in writing. the chernobyl and fukushima disasters are well present in our memories. the chernobyl tragedy is not yet over. in ukraine, 29 years later, more than 6 to 7 million people in the contaminated areas are still affected by radiation. the radioactive threat in fukushima is still everywhere. however, due to governmental bans and controls, contamination of most agricultural and livestock products is below 10 to 20 becquerels. it was essential to revise existing european regulations on the permissible levels of radioactive contamination of foodstuffs in order to protect human health as much as possible.
in writing. ‒ the world has not been spared from nuclear disasters in recent decades, and everyone remembers the terrible images of the chernobyl and fukushima accidents. if life is slowly returning to the contaminated areas, it is of course essential that the public authorities provide "safety nets" to protect the local population in the first place. preventive measures include the establishment of maximum permitted levels of radioactive contamination of food and feed following a nuclear accident. this is precisely the subject of the herranz garcia report voted on this afternoon by the members of the european parliament. i have of course voted in favour of this text which sets european permissible levels for foodstuffs for both marketing and export and import, as i have supported amendment no 56 tabled by the green group calling for a reduction by 10 of the permissible levels tolerated in animal feed in the event of radioactive contamination or, more seriously, of any type of nuclear accident in europe. if there is no zero risk, lowering the permissible thresholds for radioactive presence to the maximum is a public health imperative.
in writing. ‒ in general, the issue in this report was not so much the frequency of a particular food taken in isolation for a particular diet as the accumulation of doses from various sources, whether dietary or not. i have therefore been vigilant and demanding in ensuring a high level of protection of public health.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the text, but i also voted in favour of the rivasi (greens/efa) amendment, which was controversial.
in writing. ‒ the creation of a european capital markets union is intended to increase investment in the real economy, as a capital markets union will facilitate access to capital for smes and help to increase the diversification of sources of finance. i therefore support this motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ the capital markets union is a european commission project to deepen and further integrate capital markets in the 28 eu member states. the european parliament has therefore decided to draw up a resolution to set out its priorities on the subject. its priorities are set out in seven action points: a new legal framework for economic policy coordination, a simplified and more targeted six-monthly process, an increase in the eu's investment capacity, the establishment of a fiscal capacity within the euro area, a single market, a new social pact and, finally, a more democratic institutional framework.
in writing. – i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on building a capital markets union, which represents the democratic view from the european parliament on the cmu initiative. the cmu initiative is very important as its objective is to create much-needed growth and jobs in europe. the report recognises that we need to improve access to capital markets through new sources of funding and fill the funding gap especially for smes, while providing for an appropriate regulatory and supervisory framework geared to the needs of the real economy. at the same time it states that europe will have to play to its own strengths but that compatibility with international markets has to be guaranteed so that investment can also be attracted from abroad. the role of savers and investors in cmu was correctly identified as one of the priorities, as without them there will be no deeper or broader capital markets.
in writing. too often misled at the expense of multinationals, smes currently have very little access to credit. the proposal to consider the creation of a capital markets union (cmu) to improve access to capital markets, in particular through various sources of finance, therefore seems to me very interesting. i therefore fully support this measure, because i am convinced that it will lead to the development of smes, which will also contribute to job creation. i would like to draw your attention to the fact that we must remain vigilant in the control of those capital markets which, as a reminder, were at the origin of the financial crisis. in addition, we must also ensure the control of the rating agencies, which, without wanting to throw a stone in the water, have their share of responsibility in the crisis of 2008.
in writing. ‒ on 26 february 2014, the european parliament stressed 'the need to improve access to capital markets through new sources of financing' in its resolution on the long-term financing of the european economy. the galtieri-balz text adopted this afternoon goes into more detail and sets out the priorities of meps on the construction of a capital markets union. the decade-long steady decline in investment in the real economy in europe needs to be addressed. the latter remains highly dependent on banks, which makes the economy vulnerable in the event of a tightening of bank credit, as is the case in the post-financial crisis period, with a perverse effect: the difficulty of access to credit for smes, even the most innovative, and therefore a direct consequence on job creation. in belgium, in 2014, almost 30% of small businesses did not obtain the bank financing they requested. this is why two types of reforms are needed: one to simplify the rules on equity financing, which are too burdensome for private companies, and the other to remove the barriers to access to finance for smes, the heart of european economic activity.
in writing. ‒ by voting in favour of this report, i supported the european commission's pragmatic and proportionate approach to achieving a capital markets union (cmu) by 2019. the umc plan includes immediate initiatives including the revitalisation of a simple and transparent securitisation market which would help to alleviate bank balance sheets, the revision of the directive requiring companies wishing to raise capital to publish a standard prospectus and the amendment of the prudential rules on insurance ('solvency ii') to stimulate investment in infrastructure.
in writing. - i voted for the text. i am surprised, however, that the american example is mentioned so often. we call on the commission to develop a european approach to enhance the diversification of sources of financing and investment for european businesses, through a cmu based on the characteristics and interdependence of the european banking system and the capital markets landscape, while taking into account the specificities of the european business financing model and the need to develop non-bank sources of financing for growth, and to complement them with procedures allowing market operators to raise debt, equity and risk capital directly from the market. the commission should not necessarily rely on peer reviews with other courts. cultural differences should not be ignored. it will be necessary to formulate adequate responses to overcome them.
in writing. ‒ security threats have changed considerably in recent years. terrorism has taken many forms and now often plays a threatening role in cyberspace. many threats to european security are also due to other factors such as poverty, racism, homophobia, etc. in a globalised world, it is no longer possible for a single state to guarantee the security of its own country. the european countries must therefore work together, and for these reasons i welcome the resolutions adopted.
in writing. ‒ i have approved this motion for a resolution in which parliament welcomes the commission's european security agenda for 2015-2020. it highlights measures to combat terrorism, terrorist financing, radicalisation, crime and cybercrime in order to ensure the security of citizens. it also stressed the need to tackle the causes of crime (poverty, inequality, etc.) and called for a proper balance to be struck between prevention policy and repressive measures in order to preserve freedom, security and justice. it welcomed the special attention given by the programme to fundamental rights and, in particular, the commission's commitment to carry out a rigorous verification of any proposed security measure, not only with regard to the objectives to be achieved but also with regard to compliance with fundamental rights.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the european security agenda. i think it is important that the european parliament expresses a strong and courageous position in favour of the safety of citizens. the european union is more necessary than ever, as member states are no longer able to deal with crossborder threats on their own. this resolution welcomes the creation of the europol counter-terrorism centre, which i hope will be effectively operational by 1 january 2016. it stressed the need to provide europol with the financial means necessary to carry out its additional tasks and called for the mandatory registration of persons suspected of terrorism in the sis (schengen information system) and the harmonisation of reporting criteria. i would have very much liked to see a call for a real european governance of the union's security. i believe that just as we have a person responsible for the external security of the union, we should also have someone responsible for internal security. unfortunately, this conviction was not included in the final text, although it was in the text voted in committee.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament wanted to send a strong signal by adopting this afternoon the new european security agenda for 2015-2020, proposed by the commission last april. this programme responds to the major security challenges facing the european union. terrorism, radicalisation, organised crime and cybercrime are a growing threat to the european citizen. the recent attacks in france, denmark and also beyond our borders in tunisia and kuwait remind us of this. these attacks on the population, but also on our democratic values, have been coordinated on a scale that transcends national borders and should therefore encourage us to cooperate more closely. while the primary responsibility of any state is to ensure the safety of its citizens, the cross-border nature of this crime makes isolated efforts unsuccessful and clearly requires action at the level of the european union to build trust and facilitate cooperation, exchange of information and joint action. parliament will not compromise on fundamental rights.
in writing. ‒ the text of this resolution condemns the measures of mass surveillance and the recording of innocent individuals and underlines the need for democratic control of security measures at national and european level. the text also regrets the absence of a community definition of national security, a flaw which allows the proposed or used legislative instruments to remain vague. the resolution also calls for a legislative initiative to amend the second generation schengen information system to create an alert for suspected terrorists. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of personal data. the resolution also condemns any conflation of terrorism, immigration and islam, as well as the serious violations of human rights, illustrated in particular by the secret prisons of the cia in europe.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution. it is important to recall the crucial importance of locating and stopping financial flows in the fight against terrorist networks and organised crime groups, in particular financial flows outside the swift network. i welcome the efforts to ensure fair and balanced participation in the us-led terrorist financing monitoring programme and reaffirm my commitment to this programme. the war must be fought at the financial level to deplete the terrorist resources.
in writing. ‒ the situation in yemen is alarming. given the geostrategic importance of the country, the situation could also have serious consequences for the security of the eu and the stability of the middle east as a whole. the eu, as a champion of democracy and human rights, has a moral obligation in this crisis. thousands of people are on the run. we are on the verge of a catastrophic humanitarian crisis. i therefore support the position of the motion for a resolution and hope for a political solution soon, which should be achieved in cooperation with the un.
in writing. ‒ the resolution, which i have endorsed, urges all parties to put an immediate end to the use of violence and stresses that the european union has reaffirmed its commitment to continue supporting yemen and its people. parliament reiterated its full support for the unity, sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity of yemen and expressed its solidarity with its people. it stresses that there can be only a political, inclusive and negotiated solution to the conflict and therefore urges all yemeni parties to work towards resolving their differences through dialogue, compromise and power-sharing, culminating in the formation of a government of national unity in order to restore peace, avoid economic and financial collapse and address the humanitarian crisis.
in writing. ‒ i supported the joint resolution on yemen because the rapid deterioration of the political, security and humanitarian situation in that country is extremely worrying. i join in condemning the destabilising and violent unilateral actions by the houthis and military units loyal to former president saleh. i also deplore the fact that the air strikes by the saudi-led coalition and the naval blockade it has imposed on yemen have caused the deaths of thousands of people, created favourable conditions for the expansion of terrorist and extremist organisations and exacerbated an already critical humanitarian situation. i am convinced that there can be only a negotiated political solution to the conflict in yemen. that is why i support the request to invite all parties to resolve their differences through dialogue, compromise and power-sharing, leading to the formation of a government of national unity, the only one capable of restoring peace, avoiding economic and financial collapse, and dealing with the humanitarian crisis.
in writing. the current crisis in yemen is a major global concern. already subject to geographical, sectarian and tribal divisions, yemen has become a battleground for rivalry between aqap (al-qaeda in the arabian peninsula) and isis/daesh terrorist groups. the conflict in yemen has already left more than 3,000 dead, 10,000 wounded, 250,000 refugees and 335,000 internally displaced persons. it is taking on a regional dimension and poses serious risks to regional stability and peace in the world, in particular in the horn of africa, the red sea and the wider middle east. the european union and the international community must act decisively to end this conflict, which benefits terrorist groups such as aqap and is/daesh, whose terrorist acts are a threat to world peace.
in writing. ‒ meps are concerned about the rapidly deteriorating political, security and humanitarian situation in yemen and stress the urgency of ending the country's divisive conflict between government forces and the houthi shia rebellion. a climate of general insecurity and economic paralysis has set in, causing an unprecedented humanitarian crisis. 20 million people are currently in need of humanitarian assistance, including nearly 9.4 million children. this situation also poses serious risks to the stability of the region, in particular with regard to the horn of africa, the red sea and the wider middle east. with a health system on the brink of collapse and the impending announcement of a fuel shortage, which is already severely limiting the delivery of humanitarian aid and will soon lead to water shortages, yemen is on the brink of collapse. parliament strongly condemned all the violence perpetrated in particular by the houthis but also by the saudi-led coalition and the terrorist attacks by daesh. the urgent need now is for a political dialogue and coordinated humanitarian action under the auspices of the un.
in writing. ‒ in this resolution, which i voted for, the european parliament called for a truce to last until the end of ramadan, while at the same time calling on the eu and its member states to work within the united nations to ensure the country's supply of drinking water. this would be essential to pave the way for a potential peace process and offer the people a perspective by allowing them to improve agriculture, feed themselves and rebuild their country, the text stresses. indeed, according to reuters, fighting and aerial bombardment continued last week, despite the truce. the houthi shia rebels bombed residential areas of aden and continued to advance into the hadramaut desert. the arab coalition, led by saudi arabia, has carried out airstrikes on the capital, sanaa.
in writing. - i have of course spoken in favour of this resolution, of which i am a co-signer. i condemn all violence and attacks and threats of violence aimed at intimidating participants in the consultations organised with the good offices of the united nations. stress that the un-mediated inclusive political dialogue must be led by yemen in order to reach a consensus-based political solution that ends the crisis in yemen, in line with the gcc initiative and its implementation mechanism, the final report of the national dialogue conference, the peace and national partnership agreement and relevant un security council resolutions.
in writing. ‒ the middle east and north africa have been rocked by numerous crises for years. the increasing presence of terrorist organisations such as boko haram, al-shabaab, is and al-qaeda is compounding the problem. the situation in these regions is also crucial to the security situation in the eu and should not be underestimated or disregarded. the peaceful resolution of crises, the fight against radicalisation and the displacement of terrorist militias should therefore be given high priority in the eu.
in writing. ‒ the middle east and north africa face major security challenges, with the fight against isil currently the priority for these regions. in this regard, the report underlines the need for the eu to encourage support for a transition policy in tunisia, to support the development of civil societies and an inclusive security environment. the report also addresses the issue of women's rights in these regions. it stressed the importance of involving women's organisations and organisations working for gender equality in the consultation of civil society carried out within the framework of the european neighbourhood policy. i supported that report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution which sets out a series of recommendations on what european action should be in several countries: tunisia, libya, iraq, syria, yemen. i am not able to give a precise list of the measures i support, as i am limited to 200 words. however, i would like to express my strong support for the calls for greater international support for the democratic transition and for the strengthening of the political and administrative capacities of the countries concerned, in order to be able to respond to the challenges posed by the social and economic crisis and the inadequate protection of human rights. another key element is the stabilisation of areas liberated from terrorist groups, in order to guarantee lasting security. as regards the israeli-palestinian conflict, i support the point of recalling the need to create the conditions for the resumption of peace negotiations between israel and the palestinian authority with a view to a final settlement of the conflict, based on the solution of two states living side by side in peace and security, within the 1967 borders and with jerusalem as the capital of both states.
in writing. the growing tensions in the middle east and north africa (mena) are having a devastating impact on the stability of the entire region. these developments pose serious risks to the security of union citizens and call for a concerted response by all member states. this response must be structured around three axes. firstly, it seems to me essential that the union should have a genuine common european defence, capable of responding quickly and effectively to the various crises at its borders. secondly, democratic consolidation, respect for fundamental rights and support for civil society in the nafo countries are key factors for the long-term stabilisation of the region. finally, deepening economic cooperation is an important means of reducing inequalities and would reduce the risk of radicalisation and withdrawal, particularly among young people, by promoting social progress. i support the coordinated implementation of these three aspects of our foreign policy, which will ultimately make the region safer and more sustainable in the future.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament calls on the european union to develop a clear and long-term strategic line for its security action in the middle east and north africa (mena) region. the conflicts in syria, iraq, yemen and libya, as well as the escalation of tensions in the middle east and north africa, are a major source of destabilisation for the region. the consequences of the arab uprisings in the countries concerned, together with the complexity of the new situation and the imperative need to combat the 'islamic state' group and other terrorist organisations, require a review of the union's action. the european union must now speak with one voice in order to exist diplomatically and become a major political actor in this region. the middle east and north africa are experiencing geopolitical upheavals that could profoundly and unpredictably alter regional balances. the stability and security of the north-east asia region are fundamental to security, but also to the defence of the political and democratic values of the european union. the european parliament has set itself ambitious goals and proposed a new paradigm: that of genuine political cooperation which goes beyond economic issues.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which calls on the european union and its member states to address the root causes of the rapid deterioration of the situation in the moan region in a comprehensive and ambitious manner, supports the international campaign against the islamic state group and welcomes the commitment of the coalition partners to work together on a common strategy. the text of the report also welcomes the allocation of €1 billion under the eu strategy 'elements for an eu regional strategy for syria and iraq and the threat posed by daesh', of which €400 million is directly allocated to humanitarian aid.

in writing. ‒ the neighbourhood policy aims to deepen relations and strengthen partnerships between the european union and its neighbouring countries. the resolution calls for a review of this policy in order to provide a rapid, flexible and adequate response to the situations on the ground, while proposing a strategic vision for the development of relations with neighbouring countries. this resolution, which i approved, also stresses support for democracy, judicial reform, good governance and institution building.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution calling for the eu to pursue a strategic, ambitious, forward-looking, coherent and targeted neighbourhood policy (npp) with the objectives of creating an area of prosperity, stability and security. i believe that the enp must above all be more political. support for democracy, the rule of law, good governance, state building, human rights and fundamental freedoms must be at the heart of the enp. moreover, as the security environment in the eu's neighbourhood is deteriorating, we need to be able to broaden the range of crisis management interventions, to help our neighbours build appropriate security structures and to promote joint security initiatives by neighbouring countries. finally, the enp must be seen in the context of an overall foreign policy. i am convinced that in the future the union should provide for sufficient funding in line with its enhanced commitment to its neighbourhood, in particular through the review of its external financing instruments.
in writing. since the events of 2011 (arab spring) and developments in the eastern neighbourhood, we have seen that the eu is not responding sufficiently to the rapidly changing circumstances in its neighbourhood. the maintenance of sustainable economic and political relations requires an urgent and thorough rethinking of the european neighbourhood policy. the eu must be able to anticipate new developments quickly and adequately. the enp must be diversified and tailor-made. the recent developments in the neighbouring countries have taught us that each neighbour has its own challenges and expectations. the enp must therefore be targeted and coherent. increased conditionality is also appropriate. cooperation with countries where real progress is being made in the areas of democratisation, strengthening the rule of law and respect for human rights can be financially stimulated. at the same time, the eu must safeguard its own strategic interests in its relations with its neighbours, such as in the area of energy security. an effective neighbourhood policy also involves enhanced cooperation on trafficking in human beings and crossborder crime. the objective of the enp remains to achieve an area of prosperity, security and stability in the neighbourhood and to guarantee these objectives for the citizens of the eu.
in writing. ‒ meps stressed the importance and need to revise the european neighbourhood policy (enp), which is clearly no longer appropriate in view of the security problems at the eu's borders. events in the middle east and north africa in recent years have shown that the enp does not allow for a prompt and adequate response to difficult situations and rapidly evolving armed conflicts. these neighbouring countries face different problems and require specific responses. the enp should become a stronger, more effective, more targeted policy with a greater political and strategic dimension. its initial objectives of creating an area of prosperity, stability, security and good neighbourliness based on the common values and principles of the european union must remain the guarantors of this policy. the european parliament regrets the modest resources allocated by the european union for its action as a 'global partner' until 2020, which represents only 6% of the total budget. it also recalled that the enp is an essential component of the union's foreign policy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which recalls that the initial objective of the european neighbourhood policy (enp) is to create an area of prosperity, stability, security and good neighbourliness based on the union's common values and principles, by providing support and incentives for in-depth structural reforms in neighbouring countries. that said, i am convinced that strengthening the partner countries' own development potential requires going far beyond the political dialogue that currently predominates in the enp and extending it to a social, economic and cultural dialogue that takes into account all political, social, ethnic and cultural differences.
in writing. ‒ a review of the european neighbourhood policy is important and necessary. the new enp should be able to provide a rapid, flexible and adequate response to situations on the ground, while offering an ambitious strategic vision for the development of relations with neighbouring countries in a bilateral and multilateral framework, in line with the commitment to promote the core values on which the enp is based.
in writing. ‒ i supported the non-binding resolution adopted by the european parliament on the modernisation of copyright law, as it points out, among other things, that future proposals for reform of eu copyright law in the digital age must ensure an appropriate balance of rights and interests between authors and consumers. on the other hand, it calls for better cross-border access to online content, without ignoring the importance of territorial licensing, especially for tv and film productions. as regards the right to produce and publish images and photographs of works (e.g. buildings or works of art) in public spaces, the current eu copyright law leaves it to the member states to introduce a 'freedom of panorama' clause into their national legislation. i have, however, rejected the proposal in the draft resolution that the commercial use of such images should always be subject to the prior consent of the authors or other authorised persons and i hope that the commission will put forward a proposal which will convince as many member states as possible to incorporate this 'freedom' into their own rules.
in writing. ‒ the report calls for copyright reform that includes fair remuneration for creators and increased protection for consumers, who must have access to culture and information. we have a very rich tradition of music, art and literature in the union, and the proposals for exceptions for education and libraries must allow the widest possible public to have access to them.
philippe de backer (alde),in writing. – the increasingly digital way in which we work nowadays demands current copyright to be updated. there must be a fair balance between the rights of the creator on the one hand and the rights of the consumer on the other. this report should guide the commission in its work when drafting the copyright reform, which is to be published in the autumn.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on copyright and related rights. as the commission will be presenting a proposal for copyright reform next december, it seemed to me very useful for the european parliament to be able to give its priorities and to call for a review of ad hoc legislation to better adapt it to the digital environment. several areas need to be explored: geoblocking and cross-border accessibility of copyright-protected services and content, portability of online services within the eu, ensuring fair remuneration for all categories of rights holders, especially with regard to the digital distribution of their works, etc. i also supported the amendment to strengthen the rights of journalists. as regards the panorama exception, i voted against paragraph 46. i believe that in the absence of a consensus solution it is better to preserve the present situation and to confirm that the member states have the possibility of introducing or not a so-called freedom of panorama clause in their legislation.
in writing. in europe, culture is the third largest source of employment in the european union, with just over 7 million jobs and a turnover of over eur 540 billion per year. creators, authors, publishers, and so on, are calling for vigilance. copyright is by no means a limit to innovation. on the contrary, it allows the authors, artists, etc. to live. it allows the creation and protection of the works of the spirit. the future of europe is knowledge, innovation and culture. by finally including culture in the europe 2020 strategy, we will be highlighting our most valuable assets. by promoting copyright, we will be able to secure europe's place in the global knowledge economy. as paul ricoeur said: "no culture is universal, but each one represents a gateway to the universal, a singular experience of humanity which, like language, exists only in the plural".
in writing. ‒ this afternoon, the european parliament adopted the reda report on copyright by a large majority. a welcome initiative around controversial topics such as geo-blocking or the portability of rights in the digital age. the committee on legal affairs and citizens' rights has also voted in favour of the proposal to restrict the freedom of panorama, the exception to copyright which allows anyone to draw, photograph or film buildings or works of art in public space and to disseminate the result without having to obtain the prior authorisation of the right holders. today, each country legislates as it sees fit. belgium is one of the few countries to restrict this freedom. meps voted in favour of the proposal, but voted against the proposal. social network users will in principle be able to continue posting selfies in front of public buildings or artworks without being restricted by copyright. other amateur photographers will have to continue to rely on the tolerance of rights holders while awaiting european harmonization, which i wish to see in order to achieve freedom of panorama.

in writing. ‒ the european democracy fund (edf) is an independent institution supported by member states and eu institutions that supports actors of democratic change in the european neighbourhood. the report, which i have approved, highlights the role and the positive results achieved by the emff since its recent creation, in particular by combating corruption, promoting non-violence, encouraging social and political participation and protecting the people and journalists who are working on the ground to ensure and accelerate the establishment of a democratic process.
the events of spring 2011 and the revolts in eastern europe have shown that requests for urgent assistance to political actors and civil society activists in the eu's neighbourhood have often been met with a lack of response. in response to this criticism, the european endowment for democracy was established in 2013. the efd aims to support new political actors and civil movements in critical and urgent circumstances, including repression by authorities. the edf has been strong in providing emergency assistance in crisis situations. for example, during the protests on euromaidan square, the equipment of kyiv post was destroyed. since efd was acting as a quick lender at that time, kyiv post was able to return to the air within three days. parliament called for continued attention to be paid to freedom of expression and freedom of the media. it also called on the edf to tackle the effects of social exclusion, to promote women's political participation and to develop new actors to support democracy. in order to support the proper functioning of the edf, it would be welcome if those member states which have not yet contributed also did so quickly.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on burundi because, in the critical political and security context that this country is experiencing, the maintenance of the electoral calendar by the burundian government, despite widespread international condemnation and the opposition's boycott, is extremely worrying. it is clear that the electoral process was severely compromised by restrictions on media independence, excessive use of force against protesters, a climate of intimidation against opposition parties and civil society, and a lack of confidence in the electoral authorities. i condemn in the strongest terms the violence that continues in burundi. the essential elements of the cotonou agreement, including respect for fundamental rights and democratic principles, continue to be violated. it is inconceivable that these crimes go unpunished and that the perpetrators are not arrested. i therefore support the request to the commission to freeze funding to the burundian government and to redirect eu aid by increasing financial support to civil society and focusing on humanitarian aid.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament strongly condemned the decision of the burundian government to hold the presidential elections until 15 july. the issue, of course, is pierre nkurunziza's willingness to seek a third term, which is strictly excluded by the constitution. the outgoing president uses a legal twist to justify his guilty stubbornness, his first term would be the result of parliament and not elections. since then, the country has been in turmoil and protests have been widespread. shortly after a coup attempt by a former army general on 13 may, the burundian vice-president, several magistrates and members of the independent national electoral commission fled the country, seventeen officers were arrested and more than 70 people died in the violence. in this context, the electoral process is highly compromised: media muzzled, protests severely repressed, opposition suppressed, etc. the resolution calls on the commission to take all necessary steps to ensure that the elections are held in a peaceful, credible, free and fair manner.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution which condemns the decision of the burundian authorities to hold the presidential elections in july, which should have been postponed in view of the deteriorating political climate and the worsening humanitarian crisis. the text of the resolution calls for an immediate end to the violence, urges the burundian authorities to postpone the presidential elections and calls on all parties involved in the electoral process to honour their commitments under the arusha agreement, which restored peace to the country after years of civil war. the text also calls on all parties to resume dialogue and on the burundian authorities to involve all actors in the efforts required to create an enabling environment for the holding of peaceful, credible, free and fair elections. only through dialogue and consensus between the government, the opposition and civil society can a lasting solution be found. finally, the european parliament also called for the immediate lifting of restrictions on media and internet access, as legitimate elections cannot take place unless the media are able to exercise their rights and journalists are able to do their job without intimidation.
in writing. ‒ as the guarantor of the arusha agreements, the european union has a duty to act against the crimes committed in burundi. the resolution calls on the high representative for foreign affairs to punish those responsible for these acts of violence by banning their visas to the eu and freezing their assets in the member states. we also call for a reorientation of european aid by suspending all cooperation with the authorities and by strengthening our support for burundian civil society. i voted for this text, of course.

the president. - the next item is the report (a4-0179/97) by mr de gucht, on behalf of the committee on foreign affairs, security and defence policy, on the situation in the democratic republic of the congo (drc). large groups of young congolese are eager to take up civic citizenship and play a role in improving life in the country. three months ago, a simple citizen initiative to raise awareness among young people was shut down by security services and 30 people disappeared behind bars. the foreigners have since been released, but the organizers yves makwambala and fred bauma are still in custody today on suspicion of treason. the congolese government continues to struggle with a huge identity problem. on the one hand, the country has a very talented young generation, but on the other hand, their initiatives are clashing with a rigid and corrupt government. the panzi hospital of dr mukwege, last year's winner of the european parliament's sakharov prize, faces a debt of over half a million euros in back taxes. an unpaid bill, totally surreal. the congolese generation of today symbolizes the hope for change and peace. unfortunately, grassroots initiatives to educate young people about their civil rights in the "democratic" republic of congo can quickly cost them their freedom. oh, the irony.

the european ban on commercial seal products has a chequered history. my own party, the nva, was with former mep frieda brepoels in the cradle of the ban in 2009. the ban was a long-awaited response to the demand of millions of citizens to ban products from the cruel hunt from our market. the law did not fail to have its effect. in canada alone, that meant saving over 2 million seals. the ban has been challenged several times, but it stands. and it is crucial that the wto also gives the green light. with some targeted amendments to ensure wto compatibility, the ban is now firmly entrenched. parliament and the council have reached a defensible agreement which meets wto requirements in a timely manner, puts animal welfare at the centre and does not undermine the original legislation. our delegation will therefore support the agreement tomorrow.

in writing. the ilo and the eu share a common commitment to social and economic progress, better living and working conditions and employment promotion. it is essential that member states ratify the 2014 protocol to the ilo forced labour convention. the conventions on freedom of association and collective bargaining, the elimination of forced and compulsory labour, the elimination of discrimination in employment and occupation, the abolition of child labour are terms of reference which must become indispensable. but the real debate here is about the role of the state as an impartial public authority, a guarantor of equal opportunities and social justice. it is about access for all to education, justice, administration, health care, and culture. this debate will lead to policy solutions such as, for example, greater fiscal convergence, which too often, like unregulated globalisation, encourages the risk of social dumping. i repeat that it is up to the public authorities to play their role as protectors and regulators, enabling them to carry out the great royal functions which naturally fall to them.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on the ilo labour force convention and thus gave my consent to the proposal for a council decision. once adopted, this council decision will authorise member states to ratify the 2014 protocol to the international labour organisation's forced labour convention as regards social policy issues. despite the 1930 convention no 29 on forced labour, we must recognize that this phenomenon is still relevant in our societies. according to the ilo, at least 20.9 million people are victims of forced labour worldwide. this is a problem we cannot ignore. the 2014 protocol referred to here should address implementation gaps, strengthen measures to prevent trafficking in human beings for the purpose of labour exploitation and improve protection and compensation for victims of forced labour. in view of all this, i felt it was inevitable that i should vote in favour of this report.
