in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this regulation, which aims to improve customs risk management and to strengthen the detection and prevention of customs fraud, so that the internal market is equipped with safe products, accompanied by certificates of authenticity.
in writing. ‒ with the development of international trade, customs fraud has increased in recent years. fraud linked to false declarations of origin of products alone represents an annual loss of eur 100 million. this scourge has a considerable negative economic impact on european businesses and the community budget, and it also poses health risks for our consumers. to be effective, the fight against this grey economy must be based on the rapid exchange of information. the delays in the european anti-fraud office's investigations into customs debts subject to limitation periods, which resulted in significant losses, show that the current working method is not fast enough. the new rules, adopted by a large majority in the european parliament, are designed to give national and european authorities effective and reliable tools to access and contribute to a secure flow of information in real time. this modernisation of cooperation between member states will improve the fight against customs fraud and will also speed up the implementation of electronic customs, with positive effects on the competitiveness of european businesses.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this recommendation on mutual assistance between the administrative authorities of the member states, which aims to improve cooperation between them to ensure the proper application of customs and agricultural regulations in the member states.
in writing. ‒ olaf, the union's anti-fraud agency, regularly finds that both the member states and the european commission lose a lot of revenue through alcohol and cigarette smuggling. for example, they are exported to third countries and then reimported, which allows tax evasion. in the negotiations with the council, the epp was the main opposition to the inclusion of export data under the guise of 'trade secrets'. also, customs agents currently have few tools to determine whether the origin of the goods as declared actually corresponds to the actual route of containers. the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the information provided by the member states is not misused. this report at second reading provides a solid basis for taking stronger action against customs fraud, in the interests of privacy. the establishment of a system of registration of excise goods in the form of a european database and the improvement of border surveillance systems will help to minimise the loss of tax revenue. this new legislation will help to improve cooperation between customs services without increasing the administrative burden. at the same time, consumers are better protected, as fewer counterfeits can enter europe. that is why i voted in favour of this regulation.
in writing. ‒ trade in seal products is generally prohibited due to moral concerns about animal welfare. the only exception is the traditional hunting of indigenous communities like the inuit. i welcome these strengthened rules for the eu ban on trade in seal products as they promote animal welfare and take into account the right of indigenous communities to self-determination.
in writing. i welcome the adoption by the european parliament of the report to amend the regulation on trade in seal products to ensure that it is in line with the decision of the wto dispute settlement body. the commission had considered that the two derogations from the ban on the import of seal products on the european market provided for in the european regulation were not justified. these two derogations concerned traditional subsistence hunting and hunting for the sustainable management of marine resources. the union thus sets very strict limits on the possibilities for placing seal products on the european market. only products from traditional hunting, which is carried out for subsistence purposes and with due regard for animal welfare, should be allowed to be placed on the european market. the amended regulation was adopted in 2009 in response to public demands strongly opposed to the conditions for the killing of seals. the union had thus put into practice the principle of animal welfare which is dear to its citizens and had thus responded to their ethical concerns.
in writing. ‒ meps in plenary today gave a very strong backing to the busoi report on the sensitive issue of trade in seal products. it is the meat, oil or fur of seals used mainly in the clothing and cosmetics industry, in traditional cooking and in the manufacture of furniture. in practice, this means the introduction of a new regulation to bring existing legislation into line with wto decisions and recommendations. since 2010, the european union has imposed an embargo on seal products, citing the immoral nature of the seal hunt, and at the same time provides for two derogations: - products from hunts by the inuit or other indigenous communities ('ci derogation') - products from small-scale, non-profit-making hunts aimed at the sustainable management of marine resources ('grm derogation'). the wto concluded in 2014 that the latter derogation was not justified. it was therefore important to adapt the legislation, to put the cursor in the right place, taking into account animal welfare standards in the 21st century while incorporating the millennia-old hunting traditions of the inuit.
in writing. ‒ i voted yesterday in favour of this report which calls for a ban on the sale of seal products in the eu by ending a derogation for products from hunting to protect fish stocks. since 2009, the eu has banned trade in all seal products, both clothing and food, in an apparent effort to protect the welfare of these animals. however, europe has so far granted two derogations, accepting that the inuit community can continue to sell these products and allowing trade in products from hunting when it is aimed at protecting fish stocks. the second exception was put to the vote yesterday. the eu's ban on trade in seal products was challenged in the world trade organisation by norway and canada, leading the wto in 2014 to ask europe to clarify its exemptions. the text adopted on tuesday therefore confirmed the derogation granted to the inuit community, specifying its conditions. these new stricter rules will apply from mid-october 2015.
in writing. ‒ although some nordic member states have tried to get an exception to the ban on trade in seal products, i am pleased that parliament has today, by an overwhelming majority, made the legislation watertight. the changes that have been made were made at the instigation of the world trade organization. it was clear that the distinction between commercial catches and catches for the purpose of marine resource management was too vague. in addition, mrm catches could still be marketed. by removing the marine resource management aspect from the legislation, that is the problem of the job. however, an exception remains for the inuit community, which is still allowed to hunt seals on a limited basis but cannot bring the derived products to the european market. i voted in favour of the report, which has already received very wide support among the european people in the past.
in writing. ‒ as regards trade in seal products, i voted in favour of the report because, firstly, it is not desirable to allow these products to be traded on european markets. this should ensure that fewer and fewer seals die a horrible and useless death. in this way we are also bringing european legislation into line with wto rules. it is to the credit of the european parliament that it has taken care of the inuit and allowed the thousands of skins still in stock to be sold. there must be a balance between the economic and traditional necessity of seal products for the inuit on the one hand and a ban on the cruel slaughter of these seals for global consumption on the other.
in writing. ‒ the cloning of animals is strictly prohibited for ethical reasons and because of the impact on animal health and the possible consequences for human health. i therefore voted in favour of a comprehensive ban on cloning, i.e. a ban on the cloning of animals, the breeding material of cloned animals, their offspring and products, and the importation of reproductive material, and i supported the text put to the vote.
in writing. – science develops at a fast rate. not so long ago an ivf procedure was a risky issue and the success rate was very low. due to continually deepening and improving our scientific knowledge, we have managed to significantly improve this technique, helping many parents that have fertility problems. i voted against this report because i believe we need to be able to develop our science. in addition, the evidence that we have at the moment does not show a significant adversely impact on health. low efficiency rates are exactly a reason to develop our science, rather than to tie its hands.
in writing. ‒ i voted for a ban on the cloning of animals bred and bred for agricultural purposes in the european union. this prohibition concerns possible imports of milk and meat from cloned animals, since the european union does not market such products on its territory. on the other hand, it imports 300,000 tonnes of beef a year and in the absence of a traceability system in the countries where the cloning technique is authorised, it is impossible to know the share of cloning in the imported products. the commission wants to limit the marketing ban to the cloned animal itself. i believe that we should go further and extend the ban to the descendants of cloned animals, to germ products (embryos and sperm) and to products derived from them such as meat or milk. by voting for this ban by a large majority, parliament is sending the signal that consumer protection must take precedence over the financial interests of certain producers.
in writing. i welcome the adoption by the european parliament of the report on the cloning of animals bred and bred for agricultural purposes. parliament has just voted in favour of a much stronger line than the one originally proposed by the commission. parliament called for a comprehensive and total ban not only on the cloning technique and the placing on the market of cloned animals and products derived from cloned animals but also on the importation of the offspring of cloned animals, products derived from their offspring and germinal products of cloned animals. parliament also called for a traceability system to enable these bans to be effectively implemented. parliament has thus adopted a position without appeal categorically rejecting cloning, a position which is broadly in line with public concern in this respect. it is public health and ethical concerns about animal welfare that have led the majority of meps to vote in favour of this ambitious report.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament has said a categorical 'no' to animal cloning, to the placing on the market of cloned animals or live cloned embryos, to the marketing of products such as milk or meat from cloned animals, and to the importation into the eu of products derived from the offspring of cloned animals and food products derived from the offspring of these clones. i am glad that parliament has voted for a general ban on cloning for human or animal consumption, in the interests of human health, animal health and welfare and the environment. in this way, we are respecting the 80% of european citizens who do not want to hear about food from cloned animals on their plates. the report voted yesterday calls on the eu to legislate by regulation and impose a certification system on exporters of products derived from cloned animals to the eu to ensure the traceability of these foods and thus ensure the application of the regulation.
in writing. ‒ i have decided to vote against the cloning of animals for agricultural purposes for a number of reasons. first, many of the cloned animals die after a few weeks of excruciating pain. secondly, cloning is not yet ready in the european union and the european market is threatened with being flooded by asian cloned products. this resolution will correct this imbalance. thirdly, the majority of the population is not (yet) ready to accept cloning in its food chain.
in writing. ‒ the charter of fundamental rights guarantees all citizens of the european union and its residents the same personal, civil, political, economic and social rights. i therefore welcome the european commission's proposal to create a mechanism for regularly monitoring the situation of fundamental rights in each member state, so that possible violations of these fundamental rights can be prevented.
in writing. ‒ the report adopted by parliament on the situation of fundamental rights in the european union highlights key elements related to respect for democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights. it addresses, in a progressive way, such essential areas as equality and non-discrimination, the rights of children, migrants, lgbti people, people with disabilities, violence against women, the protection of minorities, etc. i would like to emphasize a particular point in the report. the need to establish a permanent mechanism to monitor the respect of fundamental rights and the rule of law by each member state. this is of course fundamental to the protection of all european citizens. i can only welcome the fact that a majority of parliament has supported this report which recalls the importance of member states' respect for human dignity, freedom, non-discrimination, diversity and the fundamental principles of democracy. these are the values on which the european construction is based and which must therefore be respected at all times by each member state.
in writing. – i voted in favour of this report because i believe it is very important that we keep a close watch to the state of our union, and its fundamental values. we have to keep a mirror to ourselves and to the member states when it comes to our rights and freedoms. rights of the lgbti community, asylum seekers, immigrants and other vulnerable groups have to be respected. i fully support the call for effective action against violence against women, hate crime and hate speech. this report is a good reflection document on the state of our fundamental rights.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this ambitious report which aims to assess how member states have respected fundamental rights in 2013-14. this type of report is indispensable as it is clear that even within the eu, fundamental rights are applied according to different interpretations. the text addresses the rights of women and children, lgbti people, religious and ethnic minorities, the homeless, etc. it looks at topics such as freedom of expression, freedom of the media, counter-terrorism measures, privacy violations, surveillance and hate speech. it does not shy away from the dramatically current issue of the situation of migrants and asylum seekers and urges that solidarity and respect for the fundamental rights of migrants and asylum seekers be placed at the heart of european migration policies. a request to which i can only join with conviction.
in writing. the union is quick to denounce human rights violations in the world but is reluctant to do so at home. women, children, lgbti people, people with disabilities, the elderly, migrants, roma - all are victims of violations of their most fundamental rights, again and again, in all member states. the report sheds light on all these violations and provides concrete solutions. today we still lack the union of our rights. today more than ever we need objective and continuous monitoring of the situation in each member state, based on common indicators. we must also institutionalize dialogue and make it systematic in the event of a member state's breach of the commitments it made when it joined the european union.
in writing. ‒ the text adopted yesterday, which i supported, expresses its concern about the hot-deportation procedures, the reception of migrants and their detention in closed centres, as well as negative stereotypes and misinformation against them. the resolution also condemns the security measures at the eu's borders, including the construction of walls and barbed wire, and calls for border controls to be carried out in compliance with fundamental rights. the resolution also calls on the commission to develop a scoreboard using 'common and objective' indicators to assess the situation of democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights. this scoreboard should serve as a basis for continuous monitoring and an annual national evaluation system, which i welcome.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the epp alternative resolution because i think it is shameful that, for the sake of political leaders in its midst such as mr orban and mr berlusconi, it has tried to water down the resolution before us. it is not because a member state is part of the european union that it can abandon the efforts it made to join. eu membership is a continuing effort based on the protection of citizens' fundamental rights, especially when it comes to sexual and reproductive health rights. i therefore voted in favour of the resolution.

in writing. ‒ the public hearings of commissioner candidates provide the european parliament and citizens with an opportunity to learn about each candidate's priorities and assess their competence. when problems are revealed in the debate, it is for the european parliament to oppose the nomination of a candidate and to ask for his replacement. once again, the european parliament is leading the way and at the forefront of transparency. the report aims to draw conclusions from the latest process of commissioner hearings and to put forward some ideas which could lead to a change in procedures. the text adopted requires, for example, that each member state nominate at least two candidates for the post of european commissioner: one man and one woman. the text also states that the current scope of commissioners' declarations of interests is too limited and that the commission should be asked to revise its regulation on this matter as soon as possible.

the internet and social media are powerful weapons in the fight to protect human rights and ensure freedom of expression. these communication systems have the advantage of instantaneous global dissemination of distressing news about human rights violations and restrictions on freedom of expression, and the ability to provide rapid help and support. but this technology can also be used to block news sites, to imprison citizens, bloggers and journalists, or to physically abuse them, through large-scale surveillance, censorship, interception and so on. access to and use of the internet is a fundamental human right. the commission should also be able to provide information on the impact of the measures taken by the member states on the environment and on the environment in the union, in particular by providing information on the impact of the measures taken by the member states on the environment and on the environment.
in writing. ‒ open internet access and technological advances are playing an increasingly important role in enabling and ensuring the full and unhindered enjoyment of human rights and fundamental freedoms. unfortunately, these technological systems are sometimes hijacked by government and oppressive regimes or criminal organizations to breach them through censorship, surveillance, tracking of information, and so on. in its report on the impact of intrusion and surveillance on human rights in third countries (2014/2232(ini) parliament called on the commission to ensure consistency between the union's external actions and its internal ict policies. parliament also called for the adoption of a directive on the protection of the environment against the adverse effects of ionizing radiation. finally, the report also draws attention to the critical situation of whistleblowers who, when they report abusive surveillance practices in third countries, should be considered as human rights defenders and thus be entitled to eu protection.
in writing. ‒ i support, like the whole s&d group, the approach of quality controls in the cap rather than an increase in controls. this report, which i have approved, calls on the commission to simplify the arrangements for the expenditure of the common agricultural policy, taking account of the diversity of european agriculture and avoiding the dismantling of the instruments already in place. believing that the simplification and rationalisation of the cap is crucial for the future prosperity of the union's agricultural sector, the motion for a resolution in the report suggests in particular: - reducing the administrative burden on the cap in order to reduce the error rate; - introducing tools to differentiate between error and fraud; - clarifying the guidelines for national authorities and farmers; - improving the quality and content of inspections rather than the quantity of controls.

in writing. ‒ this report, which i voted for, underlines the importance of innovation in all sectors of the blue economy in order to create new jobs and promote growth. the sea and the coast are indeed important drivers of the economy. the concept of the blue economy covers a wide range of sectors of economic activities related to the seas and oceans, ranging from traditional sectors to emerging sectors, such as fisheries, aquaculture, maritime and river transport, ports and logistics, tourism, pleasure boating, cruises, shipbuilding and repair, maritime and coastal defence works, exploration and exploitation of mineral and energy resources at sea and biotechnology. the text of the report as adopted is centred on several proposals, including a call for concrete targets and timelines to improve the accessibility of marine data, in line with the commission communication 'innovation in the blue economy: realising the job and growth potential of our seas and oceans'.
in writing. ‒ with nearly 5 million young europeans unemployed, all the relevant levers must be used to reduce this human tragedy. one of these, as emphasized in this report, which i have approved, is to awaken the entrepreneurial spirit and sense of initiative among young people and to prepare them as well as possible for the knowledge economy and the ways in which society operates today. the rapporteur stresses in this connection the need to promote entrepreneurship among young people through education and training. in concrete terms, the parliament's resolution calls on the commission:- to adopt a systematic approach;- to use the instruments available;- to develop skills at all levels of education.
in writing. – i have voted in favour of the initiative report on ‘promoting youth entrepreneurship through education and training’ because i strongly believe europe needs to support and encourage its young entrepreneurs to have their own business. i am convinced that entrepreneurial skills and competences, such as in ict, as well as transversal competences should be promoted in order to increase the rates of youth self-employment and to provide the young generation with a real opportunity to start their own businesses. with the adoption of this report the european parliament has asked the european commission to develop frameworks and support member states with the use of european funds (erasmus and esif). we have also asked for member states cooperation and sharing best practises. this report is important not only for the future of our youth but also for our european economy. we need to invest wisely in our future!
new zealand is the easiest and fastest country to start a business. the member states of europe are lagging behind. however, it is smes that form the backbone of the european economy. they actively contribute to innovative and sustainable growth. that is why entrepreneurship must be promoted. in addition to removing obstacles to entrepreneurship, greater efforts should be made within education to promote an entrepreneurial culture among young people. a positive image of entrepreneurship will motivate young people to turn their own creative ideas into concrete business plans. teaching entrepreneurship-oriented skills should be part of school curricula. the business community can also play a crucial role in entrepreneurship education. by offering targeted traineeships, including abroad, and by organising exchange projects between schools and industry, the theoretical teaching at school is enriched by the economic reality of industry.
in writing. ‒ on tuesday, the european parliament voted a resolution containing a series of measures aimed at achieving a coherent and effective education policy for young people. this is reflected in concrete initiatives taken by the european institutions and the coordination of member states' actions as well as follow-up measures. this is a valuable coordination when it comes to promoting the entrepreneurial spirit among young people, in particular by using innovative teaching methods. in seven years, the unemployment rate for 15-24 year olds in the union has risen from 15.5% to 22.2%, an intolerable increase, while belgium has seen an increase of more than 4% over the same period. this new legislative tool comes at a timely time in a europe which had 4.85 million young people out of work at the beginning of this year. the initiative is based on the wider europe 2020 strategy, which proposes five objectives in the fields of employment, research and development, climate change and sustainable energy, education, the fight against poverty and social exclusion.
in writing. ‒ in february 2015, 4.85 million young people were unemployed in the eu-28. although the number of unemployed youths has decreased by 494,000 compared to february 2014, this rate remains unacceptable. the jobs of young people are often sacrificed on the altar of fiscal consolidation in the member states. once unemployed, young people face poverty and social exclusion. in this context, the european parliament's motion for a resolution on promoting entrepreneurship among young people through education and training (2015/2006 (ini)) makes perfect sense and is a way of supporting employment. through this proposal, the european union is committed to strengthening and encouraging the close link between vocational training and school training as a model of success. by acquiring entrepreneurial skills, young people are encouraged to set up their own businesses, to succeed in this way, and thus to actively support job creation within the european union. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ as a liberal, i think it's of the utmost importance that the government creates opportunities for young people. this crisis is hitting young people very hard in their search for work. if the european union can facilitate the search for entrepreneurship by young people, we should embrace this opportunity with both hands. i therefore voted in favour of this agenda with conviction.
in writing. ‒ following the european commission's communication on an integrated approach to european cultural heritage, the parliamentary committee on culture and education issued several recommendations. the report highlights the real economic and strategic potential of cultural heritage. it contributes to job creation and the development of innovative products, services and processes. cultural tourism, to name just one example, is a key sector for the recovery of growth and employment. in the same way, cultural heritage represents a valuable contribution to several flagship initiatives of the europe 2020 strategy. i endorsed this report which highlights the role of europe's cultural heritage as a strategic resource for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which calls for an integrated approach to european cultural heritage. this heritage is a rich and diverse mosaic of cultural and creative expressions, including natural, built and archaeological sites, museums, monuments and works of art, historic cities, literary, musical and audiovisual works, as well as the knowledge, practices and traditions of european citizens. we have inherited it from previous generations and it is our duty to pass it on to future generations. this is far from the case in the world today, where terrorists are savagely demolishing with explosives and bulldozers heritage pieces representing other cultures but belonging to a universal heritage that we all share. in such a troubled time, it seemed to me essential to promote the inclusion of cultural heritage on the political agenda and to encourage member states to preserve our heritage, but also that of other cultures and civilizations through international cooperation.
in writing. building a culture of mutual respect, establishing relations between men on equal terms in rights and duties, creating a more harmonious society, is a fundamental need for humanity. while globalisation has unquestionably promoted the multiplication of trade and progress, it is our duty to combat the danger of the uniformity of our cultures. culture is a vector of openness and a motor for democracies, acting against any nationalist withdrawal, racist temptation and exclusion that are fuelled by the current economic and financial, climate and food crises. i believe that each people has its own message to deliver to the world. each people, each human being, has, by virtue of its culture, its own positive identity, the means to bring to humanity the genius of its imagination and creativity. as the rapporteur has rightly said, 'our cultural heritage is the silent witness of our long history, our creativity and our struggle'. cultural creation often draws or expresses a vision, a commitment, a bias. whether it is a relevant or impertinent bias, what matters is that it is the exercise of a right, including the right to denounce.
in writing. ‒ culture, a victim of the barbarism of those who wish to see the end of a people, as evidenced by the recent attacks by isil on the ancient city of palmyra, is a strong witness to our past, but also to our history, our roots, our identities and our common future in the european project. this is why parliament voted this afternoon a resolution to unlock the full potential of europe's cultural heritage, which deserves to be valued and preserved. in practice, cultural matters currently fall under several directorates-general within the european commission and are financed through several complementary programmes. the aim is to simplify this fragmented operation by proposing a number of solutions to the main obstacles that prevent it from reaching its full potential. these new legal, financial and technical perspectives should make its operation more efficient. it is also becoming urgent to give due consideration to the economic potential and political importance of cultural heritage. it is about giving culture the place it deserves in our political agenda so that it can make a real contribution to growth and job creation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which advocates an integrated approach to european cultural heritage. the text adopted yesterday stresses in particular the importance of european subsidies and the contributions made by the european institutions to help member states preserve and promote cultural heritage in order to achieve its full social, economic and political potential.
in writing. ‒ the european citizens' initiative on the right to water was the first successful example of such a democratic instrument. citizens can thus call on the european commission to propose legislation. however, as the previous proposal did not sufficiently take account of the demands of the citizens' initiative, i support the resolution on the revision of the legislative proposals and the eu water framework directive (wfd). the water supply is to be excluded from trade agreements.
in writing. ‒ the report by the committee on the environment, public health and food safety, which denounces the european commission's lack of ambition in the european citizens' initiative 'right2water', regrets the lack of new elements and formal political commitments despite the deep concerns of citizens. it should be remembered that water is not a mere commodity, but a public good essential to life and human dignity. the report therefore highlights the following key points: - water cuts are a violation of human rights; - water distribution companies cannot be privatised; - water quality is a priority; - member states and regional authorities should embark on a genuine social agreement to guarantee the availability, stability and safe management of this resource; - the water framework directives and the drinking water framework directives must be implemented; - much larger financial resources are also needed in the developing countries; - the commission is called upon to make the renewal of ageing drinking water networks a priority of the investment plan for europe. i supported that report.
in writing. ‒ the n-va believes that water is a public good and that the public sector should play a crucial regional role in water policy and management. developing a long-term vision is crucial in this respect. this does not mean, however, that the private sector cannot play a role in this. in flanders, too, water management and policy in the broad sense of the word are based on a mix of public and private actors. the n-va also stresses that, in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity, member states have the right to decide for themselves to use different management systems for water supply. the resolution adopted by the european parliament today does not agree with our position on several fundamental points. the nva delegation therefore voted against the resolution.
in writing. ‒ the citizens' initiative is a mechanism that allows one million citizens from at least one quarter of the member states to ask the commission to propose legislation in areas falling within its competence. the aim of the water as a human right initiative was to ensure that eu governments provide all citizens with safe drinking water and adequate sanitation. i share the aim of this citizens' initiative and i particularly support the call to make the right to water and sanitation as recognized by the united nations a separate human right. i also support the inclusion of these rights in the charter of fundamental rights. however, other provisions in this report led me to abstain on the final vote. i believe that the provisions on drinking water supply are a matter for the member states and not for the eu. other policy provisions on austerity and the troika seemed to me to be out of place. i also had difficulties with certain provisions which were against trade agreements and in favour of a complete ban on all private water management initiatives.
in writing. access to water is a human right. in view of the scarcity of water resources, the problem of access to water will become more and more pressing and will undoubtedly require a responsible response from the political side. i am glad that this issue has been debated in the european parliament following the right2water citizens' initiative. citizens have sent a clear message that water policies must be a priority for europe. this issue will therefore undoubtedly remain on the european agenda and will have to be part of a broader and more comprehensive approach to the optimal and responsible management of our natural resources in general.
in writing. ‒ the boylan report is a striking example of the political diversion of a good citizen idea, in this case access to water. this is in the wake of the first successful european citizens' initiative: "water and sanitation are a human right!" ( right2water ), with over 1.9 million verified signatures in thirteen member states, the european parliament has rightly wanted to support this tool set up to enable european citizens to take part in the european debate. there is nothing to say about the form or support for the call for the right to water by its inclusion in the charter of fundamental rights. on the other hand, many of the reservations i have about certain proposals in the boylan report explain my abstention in the final vote. clearly, politically oriented passages on austerity policies or the outright ban on all private initiatives in water supply and management are contrary not only to the values i defend but also to the european treaty which authorizes delegations of public service missions. take belgium, for example, where inter-municipal water management systems abound, often not in the best interests of the citizens. surely that is not an example for us to follow!
in writing. ‒ i am very pleased that the european parliament has just voted on a citizens' initiative entitled 'water, a human right'. this initiative was one for which i had been an ambassador in my previous capacity as secretary-general of the confederation of christian trade unions in belgium. by then we had collected almost two million signatures. two million europeans who want water to be accessible to all, who want water not to be a commodity. water is like air, we all need it to live. there is therefore no question of privatising it. on the contrary, water must be available in quality and quantity to all. we must ensure that prices for the first consumers are much lower than those for the large consumers. in any case, the citizens' initiative which was supported yesterday by the european parliament is something important. important for humanity, but also important in terms of democratic credibility. it is now up to the european commission to implement what is contained in this citizens' initiative.
in writing. ‒ two million europeans are calling on the european commission to treat water as a public rather than a private good through the right2water citizens' initiative. the environment committee of the european parliament adopted a resolution endorsing the citizens' initiative and calling on the commission to oppose the privatisation of drinking water supplies. drinking water is not a commodity, it's a human right. it is important that the european parliament makes this very clear. the european commission too often pushes for privatization through competition rules, trade agreements such as ttip or in the demands for financial aid to greece. i am very glad that we voted against the centre-right resolution and supported the resolution of the committee on the environment. the conservative resolution of the christian democrats, liberals and ecr removed criticism of plans to privatise water supplies as part of aid programmes for countries in financial need. it removed the call to exclude water supply from the competition rules for the internal market and the call to exclude water supply explicitly from liberalisation provisions in trade agreements such as ttip, tisa and ceta. she also removed the call to enshrine water as a human right in the european water directive and advocates public-private partnership.
the rapporteur. madam president, you said four minutes, sorry for the joke. madam president, mr president-in-office, madam commissioner, mr president-in-office, i share your relief, at any rate for 2015 and 2016 as regards payment appropriations. last year we spent almost all of the budgetary authority's negotiations with the commission trying to find a solution to the dramatic problem of payments. now, the situation is not good for 2015. she's bad, but she's stable. it's going to get better in 2016, but it's not going to last. i would like to ask the commissioner whether he is aware that the commission has not yet taken the necessary steps to ensure that the budgetary authority is able to meet the requirements of the budget. with regard to the 2016 budget, mr president-in-office, we have three main priorities which i believe are shared by almost all political leaders: the need to stimulate growth, the need to deal with the unprecedented wave of refugees seeking protection in our territory with humanism and efficiency and, you have forgotten this today but i imagine it is not voluntary, the need to remain alert to the terrorist threats that continue and will continue to weigh on us. i shall not talk much today about this third challenge, except to remind you of the need to strengthen the human and technical resources available to the union's bodies, such as europol, eurojust, the eu-lisa agency, which play a very important role in the exchange of strategic information to combat terrorism and prevent new attacks. we believe that the resources you have provided at council level and even at commission level are not sufficient to ensure that these bodies are as efficient as possible. that said, the major and most urgent problem we face today is the unprecedented influx - as you said - of refugees seeking protection in the territory of the union. we have been pleased to hear statements by mr juncker and a number of other politicians whose views we share - i am not talking about mr orbán - but, mr president, we must follow the budgetary means. the commission's draft budget for 2016 provides for an increase of eur 169 million compared to 2015, but this will not be enough. this will not be enough, especially as the cost of distributing or relocating refugees will skyrocket. if mr juncker announces tomorrow his proposal to add 120 000 beneficiaries to the 40 000 already planned, it will be close to 960 million euro that will have to be mobilised to comply with the provisions of article 18 of the regulation establishing the asylum, migration and integration fund. so don't think we're going to get away with this. one last word, madam president, and i'll be done with this. i regret, as does my colleague josé manuel fernandes, the rapporteur, that the council has again felt the need to reduce certain budget lines for the horizon 2020 programme and the connecting europe facility, whereas, according to all the information in our possession, these lines are the subject of proposals 36 000 for horizon 2020 alone for the period 2014-2015 which unfortunately cannot be accepted because of the conditions you have created. i think that's a profound mistake.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the asylum seekers are not forced to return to their country of origin. and those conditions are equally important to all of us. first of all, measures must be taken to better guard our external borders. i am thinking here of the establishment of hotspots and the associated effective return of economic migrants. secondly, the european commission should amend the qualifications directive to allow eu member states to have a strong activation policy. thirdly, the distribution of asylum seekers should be fair and thus take into account, inter alia, already processed asylum applications and historical migration flows. the current redistribution parameters do not meet this requirement. they place the responsibility again on the western european countries which have so far made the greatest effort. again, i ask myself: is this what we mean by european solidarity?
the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the following areas: madam president, i congratulate the commission and our rapporteur on the quality of the work that has been done. like many of my colleagues and, i hope, almost everyone in this house, i support a plan for the solidarity and fair distribution of refugees according to the contributive capacity of the various states. i have three comments. firstly - and this has already been said - there is an urgent need to reform the dublin mechanism, which is the institutionalisation of selfishness to the detriment of the most exposed states on the borders. secondly, on relocation and distribution, there is an amendment which was adopted on the initiative of our rapporteur, and which provides that the preferences of candidates for relocation must be taken into account as far as possible. i think this is important because refugees are not packages that can be dispatched mechanically. thirdly, rather than leaving it to the member states, especially greece and italy, to decide on the distribution of applicants among the different states, i believe that this task should be left to the european asylum support office (easo), because this is the only way to guarantee an impartial and consistent mechanism throughout the union.
the european union's cohesion policy aims to overcome regional disparities within the european union, so that these regions will grow closer together economically, socially and territorially. at least that's the theory. now the practice. the european central bank released a study in the quiet summer months showing that the euro design has caused the countries, and thus the regions in the euro area, to grow much further apart in recent years. whether it's education levels, technological development, labour force participation or productivity. looking at the european commission's regional competitive index, one sees time and again how much more divided this continent is becoming. billions and billions are being thrown at it through regional investment policy to bring together what cannot be brought together. i myself come from the belgian member state where years of financial injections in the wallonia region have not brought the flemish and the walloon regions closer together. - no, it's the opposite. you are now going to try to do the same between regions in 28 member states. you may be able to go on with your ever closer union ideology, but i know better from experience. we, like our group, are voting for sovereignty and independence.

in writing. ‒ since palestine was granted observer status at the united nations in 2013, the european commission, and together with the eeas, switched to using the name palestine. it is only natural that the european parliament should use the same name.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the partnership agreement with guinea-bissau because of the importance of its trade relations with the fishermen of the european union, but also because fishing ensures the survival of thousands of inhabitants of guinea-bissau. the agreement also welcomes the improvement in the health situation in the country and the positive developments since the presidential elections in may 2014.
in writing. ‒ the first fisheries agreement between the eec and guinea-bissau was concluded in 1980. following several implementation protocols, it was implemented as part of the european union's proposed strategies for the countries of the south, which provide financial and technical assistance to local fishermen in exchange for fishing rights for the european fleet. the european parliament again approved this type of initiative on tuesday. this small island off the west coast of africa has almost 1.4 million people, most of whom live below the poverty line, with one of the lowest gdps in the world, and the coup d'état on 12 april 2012 has only exacerbated political instability. its economy is largely dependent on agriculture and cashew nut cultivation, hence the need for this diversification brought by europe. in concrete terms, the planned european aid is eur 9.2 million. in return, it authorises many european vessels, such as freezer trawlers and shrimp trawlers, as well as 28 freezer tuna vessels and longliners and 12 tuna seiners, to fish in guinea-bissau's waters.
in writing. ‒ we recognise the value of the eu fisheries partnership agreement with the republic of guinea-bissau as an important instrument for the country's fishing sector, the eu fleets operating there and the export opportunities it could create with europe. however, we abstain on the present report with recommendations and the draft resolution on the implementation protocol, as it is too much a copy of the 2012 implementation protocol which was suspended following the military coup in april 2012. the commission has also been asked to provide information on the implementation of the new rules on the conservation of fishery resources. the current protocol does not reflect the new political challenges facing the nva delegation following the upheavals in the country and the difficulties facing the local fishing industry.

in writing. guinea-bissau is one of the least developed countries in the world and one of the most indebted. this poverty has been exacerbated by a period of political instability following the military coup of 12 april 2012. since may 2014, the country has been experiencing positive developments thanks to the holding of democratic presidential elections. the fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and guinea-bissau comes at a good time; the conclusion of the agreement should enable the european union and guinea-bissau to strengthen political dialogue, consolidate the reconstruction of the country and revitalise one of the key sectors of its economy. the eu's financial contribution of eur 9 200 000 will support guinea's fisheries policy and strengthen its budget. it should enable the development of the local fishing industry and improve working conditions in small-scale fishing. i welcome the approval given by parliament to the council to conclude this agreement, which is an indispensable tool for reducing guinea-bissau's dependence on the agricultural sector and international aid.

in writing. the cape verdean archipelago remains economically vulnerable despite its enormous potential in the fisheries sector. the conclusion of a fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and cape verde will strengthen policies for sustainable fisheries and good governance. in addition to the payment of a total amount of eur 1 050 000 for access to fishery resources and eur 1 200 000 for fees due by shipowners, this agreement and its protocol provide for the payment of eur 275 000 annually for the first two years and eur 250 000 for the last two years to support the cape verdean fisheries sector. this financial contribution will help to revive economic growth in cape verde. it is an opportunity for both partners to strengthen political dialogue and cooperation in the fight against illegal fishing, the management of fisheries resources with a focus on improving the health quality of fishery products and promoting the development of small-scale fishing.
in writing. ‒ this afternoon, the european parliament gave its consent to the conclusion of a new protocol under the fisheries partnership agreement with cape verde. the agreement, signed in july 1990, provides for fishing opportunities for european vessels in the territorial waters of the republic of cape verde in return for financial aid. this seventh protocol covers a four-year period for this island state, which since 2008 is no longer one of the least developed countries (ldcs) benefiting from a special tariff preference system. despite this change in status, the archipelago, comprising ten islands and five islets, has a poorly diversified economy, increasingly based on tourism. the financial aid, amounting to eur 3 300 000, will enable the country to revive its economy while allowing sustainable exploitation of resources, with particular attention being paid to the capture of sharks, which are very common in this part of the atlantic ocean. in practice, this protocol provides for increased fishing opportunities for large european vessels: 28 purse seiners, 30 surface longliners and 13 tuna seiners.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this new protocol, which promotes sustainable fishing and a more responsible exploitation of fisheries resources, and which establishes a mechanism for sustainable resource management.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this new protocol to the fisheries partnership agreement with madagascar which provides, among other things, for the financing of a fisheries observation programme in madagascar because of the importance of this sector for the malagasy economy but also for european fishermen.
in writing. the development of fisheries, which is one of the key economic sectors of madagascar, is an essential instrument for its sustainable economic growth. the partnership under this agreement will promote the fight against the waste of stocks, the creation of new opportunities for growth and employment in madagascar's coastal regions, the transfer of autonomy and the decentralisation of decision-making in this sector. i welcome the approval given by parliament to the council to conclude this agreement, which is an opportunity for the european union to encourage madagascar to make efforts to comply with the acp-eu partnership agreement, in particular article 9 thereof on human rights, democratic principles, the rule of law and good governance. this agreement will help to employ local fishermen and promote fishing opportunities that promote the processing of catches in madagascar. the agreement is an indispensable tool for enabling the malagasy citizens and the population of neighbouring countries to benefit from the benefits of the gradual opening of markets and the tremendous added value of globalisation in terms of development.
in writing. ‒ in recent years, the eu has concluded some 20 fisheries partnership agreements with countries of the south. they all have a common objective: financial and technical assistance to local fishermen in exchange for fishing rights for the european fleet. a concrete example is given this afternoon by the positive vote of the european parliament on the fisheries agreement between the republic of madagascar and the european community. because although the island of madagascar is a huge territory, the fourth largest island in the world, its economy is underdeveloped and diversified and is based primarily on agriculture, livestock and fishing. european aid is therefore essential, amounting to over eur 6 million for the four years of the partnership agreement. in practice, the latter authorises 94 vessels, including 40 sen­dars and 54 longliners, to fish up to 15 750 tonnes of fish in the waters of the exclusive economic zone of the republic of madagascar. it is also important that this fisheries agreement includes a biodiversity component through monitoring of fisheries activity and mention of vulnerable and protected species.
in writing. ‒ by adopting this report, the european parliament approved the conclusion of the new eu-madagascar partnership agreement. the agreement includes fishing opportunities for 94 eu vessels (from spain, france, italy and portugal): 40 sen­dors and 54 longliners of various sizes. it is planned to catch 15 750 tonnes of fish in the waters of the exclusive economic zone of the republic of madagascar. in total, the agreement provides for a counterpart of eur 6.1 million from the european union to the republic of madagascar during the four years of validity of the partnership agreement.
in writing. ‒ the trade facilitation agreement (tfa) is of great importance to european trade, which accounts for 22% of world trade. i therefore voted in favour of this recommendation to amend the marrakesh agreement to simplify and harmonize procedures in international trade. this will facilitate the implementation of the tfa for developing countries through special and differential treatment, and will also allow for technical assistance from developed countries in certain areas.
in writing. ‒ the trade facilitation agreement (tfa) is of great importance to european trade, which accounts for 22% of world trade. i therefore voted in favour of this recommendation to amend the marrakesh agreement to simplify and harmonize procedures in international trade. this will facilitate the implementation of the tfa for developing countries through special and differential treatment, and will also allow for technical assistance from developed countries in certain areas.
in writing. the marrakesh agreement establishing the world trade organisation (wto) in 1994 had to be amended in view of the profound changes in the world landscape, the new economic and geopolitical realities. the conclusion of this protocol will thus allow the trade facilitation agreement (tfa), adopted by the wto general council in november 2014, to be incorporated into the wto legal framework. the tfa is expected to reduce the total cost of trade by more than 14% for low-income countries and by more than 13% for upper-middle-income countries by simplifying the movement of goods across borders. the tfa will also help to drive forward the process of 'active integration' through a series of provisions aimed at speeding up the movement, release and clearance of goods, the use of electronic payment, the easing of formalities and documentation requirements, the standardisation of border procedures, etc.

in writing. my vote is intended to contribute to the objective of harmonising contractual and inland navigation standards in europe and to the proper functioning of the internal market. belgium had already ratified this in 2008 but was still in an illegal situation which now requires europe to give authorisation to belgium as well.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this draft resolution which authorises belgium and poland to ratify the budapest convention on the contract for the carriage of goods by inland waterway and the republic of austria to accede to it. the budapest convention entered into force in 2005 and contributes to the internal market in transport by harmonising contracts and standards for inland navigation in europe.
in writing. ‒ despite the continuing flows of refugees, some member states still refuse to allow european coordination and a fair distribution of these people seeking protection within europe. greece, italy and hungary are overwhelmed with asylum applications. other member states do not want to take in refugees at all and are thus denying their solidarity with their european neighbours. such an attitude is unacceptable and a common european response to this situation is urgently needed.
in writing. ‒ i have endorsed this report which underlines the need for solidarity between member states to respond to the challenges of migration. the rapporteur stresses that the proposal to relocate 40 000 refugees from italy and greece to other member states is a first step but will obviously be insufficient in view of the number of migrants arriving daily in certain countries of the union. it therefore calls for a deepening of this intra-european solidarity. the resolution also stresses the need and urgency of offering dignified reception conditions to migrants and of taking into account certain elements in the country of relocation (family, language, etc.). the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment-related aspects of the transport of dangerous goods.
in writing. only an ambitious european solution to the migration crisis will ensure a solidary and sustainable management of the phenomenon. states like greece and italy cannot manage the entire flow on their own. this is a collective responsibility. i am therefore pleased that the european parliament has given its consent to the establishment of a relocation mechanism for 40 000 migrants currently in greece and italy. i regret, however, that the member states have not succeeded in establishing a mandatory allocation mechanism. this mechanism will soon be consolidated by a new commission proposal which aims to distribute an additional 120 000 asylum seekers across europe, not only from greece and italy but also from hungary. these mechanisms are now partly responding to the emergency but can only be the first step towards a permanent european mechanism.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which proposes temporary emergency measures to relocate an initial number of 40 000 asylum seekers from italy and greece to other eu countries over a period of two years. i also supported the provisions for increased solidarity and the establishment of a fair and equitable relocation mechanism. i also had the opportunity to deplore the fact that the regulation was not suspended and that the reference to the first country of entry into the union was not deleted.

in writing. ‒ europe continues to face a number of challenges related to the economy, climate, environment and society at large. the report stresses that most of these challenges have a strong urban dimension. they are mainly manifested in and around cities (e.g. poverty, social and spatial segregation, environmental degradation) or are solved there (efficient resource management and carbon neutral economy, economic development and innovation, social innovation and integration, etc.). the rapporteur notes that, although the role of cities in economic, social and cultural development is recognised, the policy response at european and national levels has been slow and fragmented, with many sectoral initiatives but little integration. it stresses that more and more people feel it is important that cities are sufficiently involved in the design and implementation of eu policies and that these are better adapted to urban realities. this change in mindset has resulted in calls for an eu urban agenda from a wide range of stakeholders at local, national and european level, which are echoed in this report which i have approved.

in writing. land use planning is purely political in nature. urbanization is transforming the very structure of states and creating a new economic and political institutional framework. cities attract. by 2025, about 75% of the world's population will live in urban areas and 95% of the growth in urban population will be driven by economically weak social groups. the city is not just a territory. it is a political, social, economic and cultural entity that is in perpetual change. it's a living body. it is a place of contrasts where tradition, modernity, wealth and poverty meet. as the congolese writer sony labou tansi writes: "every city has its soul. every city has its own body, its own skin, its own intelligence, its own stupidity, its own monstrous side, its own mystery... in writing. ‒ 359 million people (72% of the total eu population) live in cities and their suburbs. although the pace of urbanisation has slowed in recent years, it is estimated that 80% of the eu's population will be urban by 2050. in view of these figures, and also of the importance of cities in economic, social, cultural and environmental development, the european commission has wanted to launch a debate on the urban dimension of european policies and on the main features of a possible future urban programme of the european union. the debate will focus on the need to set up an eu urban agenda. in response to this request, i voted today in favour of a report which calls in particular on the commission to present a communication setting out the features of the future european urban programme. this communication must be done in close cooperation with various stakeholders, including the social partners. like parliament, i invite the commission to identify major urban challenges in collaboration with stakeholders, to appoint a policy officer to set the strategic direction and to appoint a special eu urban policy coordinator.

the inclusion of disabled people in the labour market is absolutely necessary from a purely economic point of view. it's not just about our social or ethical responsibility. no, i'm not going. it's the economy, stupid. in fact, the number of people with disabilities seeking work is twice as high as that of other jobseekers. this is despite the fact that their specific skills and talents could contribute to greater diversity in teams and companies. employers need to realise that if they fully exploit this untapped potential, their companies can build up a competitive advantage. as long as vulnerable groups such as people with disabilities are excluded, there can be no question of a truly competitive and inclusive labour market. after all, so much talent is being lost. considering the aging tide that's coming down on us, it's a real shame.

mr president, the precariousness of employment is a growing concern. it has multiple origins. firstly, there are the effects of the crisis we are going through, but it is also the consequence of the changes in our economies and the evolution of management methods, especially in the largest companies. the lack of economic predictability and the flexibilization of work are important components of this. this precarious situation takes various forms, such as the development of parttime work, fixed-term contracts and the use of temporary jobs. it also takes an illegal form, illegal through undeclared work or the proliferation of fake self-employed. these fraudulent practices must be firmly combated, in particular by the effective establishment of the platform to combat undeclared work, by strengthening and coordinating social inspectorates, and by setting up and implementing a social europol, a european social inspectorate. in the case of atypical contracts, it is essential to provide for measures to secure career paths. the training throughout life is, from this point of view, a decisive factor. finally, the fight against job insecurity, the fight against fraud and measures to safeguard careers must be an integral part of the social foundation mentioned this morning by the president of the commission. if the european union wants to achieve triple a, and it must, it must rise to the challenge.

that our healthcare systems were developed in a previous century when people mainly died from malnutrition and infections. but now we see people suffering from chronic diseases, requiring years of innovative treatment. healthcare spending in the eu has grown by nearly 50% since 2000, to almost 12% of european gdp, and it will continue to rise. nor is it only drug pricing which is to blame. this means that we have to look fundamentally at how we run our healthcare systems if we want to keep them open, qualitative and affordable for everybody. i have heard many good proposals coming from the need. therefore, i would like to make three concrete proposals. first of all, there are major differences in healthcare spending between member states. the european semester could serve as a tool to monitor healthcare quality, organisation and spending. recommendations per member state and follow-up of implementation of best practice by the commission would then be key. secondly, the world health organisation (who) has estimated that 20% to 40% of healthcare budgets are wasted due to inefficiencies. so we have to keep a competitive edge when it comes to innovation. this means creating a simplified, stable and favourable environment for investing in healthcare, ranging from drug development to e-health applications to prevention strategies, bringing down the cost for the whole system. rare disease fund which would harmonise the health technology assessment procedure, making it easier for companies to enter all european markets and obtain reimbursement. the combined member states would have a stronger negotiating position over the price and the fund would guarantee access for all patients suffering from a rare disease to the most novel and innovative treatments. the rare disease regulation is a decade old so let us finish this work. we have to change our thinking about healthcare and the way that we look at european healthcare systems, so i count on the commission to lead the way. i think that we will support you in many aspects.
