in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on 'investing for jobs and growth: promoting the economic, social and territorial cohesion of the union'. the european parliament has voted to approve a new budget for the european union for the period 2007-13 which will cover the period from 1 january 2007 to 31 december 2008. one criticism i would like to make of this policy is the delay in payment by the commission. implementing a large-scale policy with a large budget only makes sense if the aid arrives on time. i therefore strongly urge the commission to do everything possible to honour these outstanding invoices. the new governance principle means that funding can now be suspended if a member state does not comply with the recommendations made in the economic governance process. in this respect, i am of the opinion that this means of pressure should be considered only as a last resort.
in writing. ‒ in view of the major challenges posed by the active ageing of the european population, strong political commitments followed by concrete actions are needed to ensure social inclusion, active participation and well-being for all generations. the sustainability of public pension schemes, unemployment among people over 50 and discrimination against the elderly are all aspects of the phenomenon of active ageing which must be the focus of our concern. sharing the view that the european commission must make more concrete progress towards the objectives set after the 2012 european year for active ageing and solidarity between generations, i support this report and the initiatives to establish new networks for sharing resources, projects and ideas between the private sector, the public sector and civil society.
in writing. by 2060, one active worker will be replaced by one retired worker. under the same policy, i understand. therefore, 'active ageing and solidarity between generations' was chosen as the central theme for the european year in 2012, with the aim of raising awareness among policy-makers and opinion-makers of the opportunities of, and mobilising them for, active ageing policies. people stay fit and healthy longer. this means that these social advances should no longer be seen as a burden but as an enrichment for our society. older people are a full-fledged population and their continued participation in public life should be encouraged. therefore, policies should be put in place to address the worrying phenomenon of older people's unemployment and to keep this vulnerable but experienced group of workers in the labour market, for example by developing programmes such as 'generation mentorship', but also for maintaining a good quality of life and standard of living. many citizens are committed to socially valuable causes alongside or after their professional careers. the voluntary work and the social value of this citizen participation should therefore be more appreciated. finally, active ageing also means ensuring that people have good access to lifelong learning, healthcare and social services.
in writing. ‒ active ageing tends to enable older people to remain healthy for longer and to optimise their participation in society. improving access to healthcare, long-term care and social services is key to achieving this, despite the willingness of some to cut back in these services in order to cope with the crisis. to raise public awareness of the importance of active ageing, the european union decided to make 2012 the european year of active ageing and solidarity between generations. a report on the implementation, results and overall evaluation of the 2012 european year for active ageing was discussed in parliament today. on the positive side, the report highlights the mobilisation of stakeholders around this issue and the increase in the number of initiatives promoting active ageing. however, the establishment of new networks for sharing resources, projects and ideas between the public sector, the private sector and civil society has rarely been achieved, according to the report. i share these views and have therefore decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted with the greens for the report on the european year for active ageing and intergenerational solidarity (2012) because it examined both the shortcomings and the successes, which is important to do better in the future. this has enabled the mobilisation of relevant actors, but has failed to build new networks between the public, private and civil society sectors to share resources, projects and ideas. the involvement of the social partners varied and was nil in private enterprises. the project was approved late and had a very small budget. it is important that older people should not be seen as a burden on the economy and society, but should have added value through experience, achievements and knowledge. the policy of viewing active ageing as an economic instrument (employment of older workers) is rejected. member states should take into account the whole life cycle and guarantee individual and adequate pensions and the right to age in dignity. the european commission is invited to explore a new eu financial instrument to provide a minimum income for all eu citizens living below the poverty line.
in writing. ‒ the 2011 transport white paper sets out a future strategy for a competitive transport system, with the aim of increasing mobility, removing significant barriers in key areas and promoting growth and employment. as transport is a complex system dependent on many factors, it is important to take a regular stock of its implementation in the form of proposed initiatives and action priorities and to determine the future course of action.
in writing. ‒ transport accounts for 5% of gdp at european level, with the union remaining one of the world leaders in the field. i supported the report on the implementation of the 2011 white paper on transport which stresses the need to move towards a truly integrated transport system and a european transport area that aims to break the sector's dependence on oil. the report calls for the promotion of alternative fuels, while recalling the key role of the union in the cop21 conference. i also welcome the proposals that have been made on fair competition in the air transport sector and on the amendment of the regulation on air passenger rights.
in writing. i am in favour of a stronger harmonisation of the european transport system with economic growth, sustainability and fairer competition in transport. it is necessary to create a common european airspace and a faster and more efficient rail network through the fourth railway package.
in writing. the single market must also integrate without delay a network of dense, modern and efficient transport infrastructure, resource-efficient, serving free movement and trade, convenient for citizens and users, able to meet the challenge of sustainable mobility as well as urban mobility. the development of trans-european transport networks must be accelerated, in particular by implementing the mechanisms for interconnection in europe (emi). the fourth railway package to complete the creation of a single railway market was adopted by the european parliament on 26 february 2014. as parliamentarians we have taken care to protect the employment, status and working conditions of staff. if the technical part of the proposal to europeanise the rail network by transferring more powers to the european railway agency is not a problem for us, the political part is much more delicate. it would oblige transport contracts to be put up for competition by 2019. an integrated multimodal approach (rail, inland waterway and land) should be developed.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report on the implementation of the 2011 white paper on transport that i voted for yesterday calls on the european commission to adopt measures to help member states reduce their greenhouse gas emissions and calls for a comprehensive strategy for the decarbonisation of transport to achieve the objectives of the white paper. as part of the commission's mid-term review of european transport policy, the text calls for co-modality to be strengthened with a focus on the cleanest modes of transport in order to meet the 2030 targets (40% reduction in ghg emissions compared to 1990 levels) and 2050 (60% compared to 1990 levels). the text also calls on the commission to submit proposals to internalise the external costs of freight and passenger transport modes in order to ensure better application of the 'user pays' and 'polluter pays' principles. we also called for increased budgetary allocation, including through the european fund for strategic investments (efsi), the connecting europe facility (cef) to complete the trans-european transport network (ten-t) by 2030.
in writing. ‒ despite progress, too many inequalities still exist today in terms of equality between women and men. as this report points out, this is particularly true for science, technology, engineering and mathematics careers where women are vastly underrepresented. although almost 60% of university graduates are women, they represent less than 20% of full professors in these courses at the university level in the eu28. i can only support this initiative to promote equal access to scientific and academic careers.
in writing. – i voted in favor of this report as we need to do more to get more women in stem-related (sciences, technology, engineering and mathematics) educational fields and careers. here women are hugely under-represented accounting for just 24% of science and engineering professionals. it was also important for me to reaffirm that equality between men and women is one of the principles on which the european union was founded. unfortunately, women still experience unequal access to research positions, funding, publishing and academic awards. the report asks for the commission and member states to look at a number of positive measures such as to analyse legal provisions with the aim to enforce equal treatment of men and women. we also call for more flexible working conditions for both male and female researchers, allowing them to combine work with family life, and for elimination of the gender pay gap in the interests of gender equality. the commission is to propose a recommendation to member states containing common guidelines on institutional change to promote gender equality in universities and research institutions.
in writing. for too long, inequality between men and women has persisted. i support this report which encourages women to move more towards the scientific community, a community in which women are underrepresented. in general, too often, men are favoured for positions of responsibility, often because of outdated stereotypes and implicit discriminatory standards. it is essential to recognize the abilities of each person regardless of gender issues. even though some locks have been broken, the glass ceiling remains but on another level. we must remain vigilant and take the necessary steps to avoid undermining women's careers.
in writing. ‒ this report, which i voted for, analyses the barriers and 'bias' (whether conscious or not) faced by women in their academic and scientific careers. these barriers are numerous and complex, as they are based on various factors, such as discrimination due to stereotypes, but also due to obligations related to motherhood and family, preventing women from pursuing the professional careers they would like to pursue. in recent years, many campaigns have been launched to combat the problems mentioned above. they have put in place effective strategies to promote gender equality. however, the current situation is still largely unsatisfactory. the adopted text proposes that measures be taken by the commission and the member states within the framework of the european research area (era) and the specific programme horizon 2020 to strengthen equality between men and women in universities and in the scientific world.
in writing. ‒ the nva delegation advocates an inclusive society with equal rights and obligations for all, as well as a tailor-made equality policy that takes account of diverse target groups. we cannot accept any violation of this equality, whether at work or in private life. we recognise that people with stem (science, technology, engineering, mathematics) skills make a vital contribution to our labour market and economy. but the causes of the glass ceiling in women's scientific and academic careers are more social and deeper in nature. quotas are not the answer. we have chosen to abstain on this report because of the call for compulsory quotas for women.
in writing. ‒ although more and more women are obtaining higher education qualifications, they continue to face discrimination against men in terms of career opportunities and remuneration. i therefore support, in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity, the equal treatment and empowerment of girls through education. the attitude towards this must change in schools. the aim is to achieve equality between girls and boys at all levels of education, so as to break down unnecessary stereotypes and give girls equal opportunities.
in writing. ‒ given the potential of education in cultural change, investments at all levels of the education system to promote gender equality play a key role. similarly, the school must contribute to developing an intercultural approach to education in mutual respect and through intercultural and interreligious dialogue. i voted in favour of this initiative.
in writing. – i voted in favor of this report as i believe that every child has the right to the same non discriminative education. unfortunately this is not the case everywhere, especially for girls. here we need to improve measures to apply gender equality at all levels of the education system throughout the eu. we call for member states to ensure that their education authorities guarantee an equal right to education for women and men by actively incorporating the principle of equal treatment into educational goals and actions, thus preventing the emergence of inequalities between women and men as a result of sexist conduct and associated social stereotyping. the commission is urged to ensure that this recommendation be put to the national institutions responsible for implementing central, regional and local education policies, school management bodies and regional and local authorities.
in writing. gender stereotypes and stereotypes of women. they still exist. this still leaves very specific and limited roles for men and women. for example, the labour market is still divided into typically male and typically female occupations. parents, friends and the social environment in which one grows up, but also education and the media, play a crucial role in transmitting, disseminating or breaking these traditional role patterns. in this way, girls are still driven into typically female occupations and find it difficult to find their way into the so-called male occupations. education can play a crucial role in removing the barriers that impede young people's personal development and their empathic capacity for mutual respect. the school has an important role to play in the social, cultural and professional development of girls. to make progress, this process must begin at school at a very early age. in the classroom, the debate on study choice and career orientation should be stimulated. consistent investment in the development of information campaigns and learning programmes to combat gender segregation in the labour market is recommended to increase the number of female students and graduates in science and technology.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which considers that gender equality measures should be applied at all levels of the education system, including in curricula and teacher training, in order to put an end to gender stereotypes and help bridge the gap between women's education and their professional development. the text of this non-legislative resolution also calls for more investment to ensure quality public education for all.
in writing. ‒ the n-va delegation abstained from voting on this report. we believe that education is the foundation of responsible citizenship, is essential to ensuring gender equality and empowerment of girls, and is a fundamental human right that must be guaranteed for all children. we also advocate an inclusive society with equal rights and obligations for all, and a gender equality policy tailored to and focused on diverse target groups. we cannot accept any violation of this equality, whether at work or in private life. at the same time, subsidiarity is also important for the n-va. we are aware of the different levels of policy and the division of powers. in this respect, the present report is problematic, since education is not primarily an eu competence.
in writing. the agreement on the european economic area (eea agreement) is the most far-reaching and comprehensive instrument for extending the economic integration of the eu's internal market to third countries. a well-functioning and effective internal market based on a highly competitive social market economy is essential to foster growth and competitiveness, create jobs and give new impetus to the european economy, and internal market legislation is essential to ensure that it is properly implemented, applied and enforced. i welcome this report, since it again points out, among other things, the existing implementation deficits and the removal of obstacles to crossborder professional mobility in the countries concerned.
in writing. ‒ i supported this report which highlights the importance of the eea/efta and swiss trading partners, welcomes the large number of eu programmes in which eea/efta countries participate, while highlighting the transposition deficit in some countries such as liechtenstein, iceland and norway. the report also stresses the strong relationship between the eu and switzerland, but recalls the latter's obligations in terms of the free movement of persons, a pillar of the single market, which requires reciprocity and fairness in its use.
in writing. switzerland is an important partner for the european union. it is therefore essential that these relations be continuously strengthened. today, certain obstacles to this are still present. i am particularly concerned about the growing initiatives to challenge the free movement of people between the two areas. this would seriously impede relations. i am therefore glad that the european union has rejected switzerland's request to review the current provisions in order to introduce the idea of quotas. more than ever, we must remain vigilant and strengthen the dialogue to ensure that this fundamental principle is undeniably at the very heart of relations between switzerland and the european union.
in writing. ‒ switzerland's participation was called into question by a popular vote in 1992, and relations between switzerland and the european union today are based on more than 100 sectoral agreements which allow a high degree of integration of the country into the internal market. however, since the interruption of the negotiations for the participation of switzerland in the erasmus+ programme, the european parliament, through the vote on this report, expressed concern that these measures are likely to have consequences for the mobility of higher education between the eu and switzerland and called on switzerland and the eu to do everything possible to fulfil the necessary conditions for their participation in the erasmus+ programme in order to guarantee reciprocity of exchanges and not to penalise students.
in writing. ‒ europe is once again facing a test. countless numbers of refugees are pouring into eu countries every day. instead of insisting on compliance with the dublin procedure, it is essential to have a common european asylum system to deal with this problematic situation. i welcome the report because it calls for a permanent, binding system based on solidarity and responsibility, through which asylum seekers can be distributed to all european countries.
in writing. ‒ the joint resolution, which i endorsed, recalls the need for the union to base its immediate response to the current migration crisis on the principles of solidarity and fair sharing of responsibility and on a comprehensive strategy to promote safe and legal immigration in full respect of human rights and fundamental values. the resolution also calls for the eu to take action to ensure that the rights of asylum seekers are respected and that the eu's asylum system is updated. the commission also proposes to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the public authorities. it also reiterated its commitment to open borders within the schengen area while ensuring the efficient management of its external borders and stressed that the free movement of persons within the schengen area is one of the greatest achievements of the european construction.
in writing. ‒ i have given my unconditional support to the emergency measures proposed by the president of the commission to better distribute the reception of 160 000 refugees among the member states. i regret the lack of solidarity of governments towards asylum seekers. the migration crisis we are experiencing is the worst since the second world war. that's why i gave my support. i consider this to be a moral and human obligation. beyond emergency measures, i am also in favour of a permanent and binding relocation mechanism based on a fair distribution key between member states. i am also in favour of establishing a common list of third countries considered safe, which will speed up the processing of unfounded requests. finally, i regret that refugees have no other option than to resort to smugglers and dangerous routes to seek protection in europe. it is urgent that the eu has an effective and harmonised asylum system and that member states put in place safe and legal channels, including humanitarian corridors and humanitarian visas.
in writing. monitoring our borders and welcoming refugees concerns us all. we cannot therefore leave the bulk of the migration pressure, which is our common responsibility, to a few states. this is a practical application of solidarity between member states. in the current humanitarian context, it is imperative to distinguish between refugees and economic migrants. if we must work with urgency and show universal human solidarity, we must also work on the basis of strict conditions with a human face in the context of economic migration. but in no case should we be tempted to demonize immigration in a simplistic way. in the face of atrocities committed in certain parts of the world we must take part in global solidarity. this solidarity must be reflected both externally and internally. other countries, often neighbouring these conflict zones, are hosting the overwhelming majority of refugees. to fail to take our share of responsibility would be selfish and contrary to our humanistic values.
in writing. ‒ we are facing an unprecedented humanitarian crisis which europe and the member states must manage with humanism and realism, making a clear distinction between war refugees and economic migrants. this is the balance that is found in the resolution on migration and the situation of refugees in europe, which was adopted by the european parliament this afternoon and which i of course supported. the text follows on from jean-claude juncker's state of the union address yesterday, stressing the need for greater solidarity. in addition to the fair distribution of the 160,000 refugees, mainly syrians, across europe, we liberals want a radical reform of migration and asylum policy based on: - the creation of safe zones in and around conflict zones combined with safe and legal routes within the union; - the deepening of the schengen area by strengthening the external borders of the union. more generally, if europe is to be effective in economic migration this time around, and respond to the legitimate concerns of european citizens, it must do so without taboos and take the example of the countries of the new world: canada, the united states and australia, which have a chosen immigration policy.
in writing. ‒ i supported the joint resolution on migration and refugees, because the european union must go beyond the legitimate indignation to put in place a dignified and supportive migration policy. this is not the time to question schengen, this is not the time to judge each other's philosophical or religious convictions, this is the time to open up, to welcome those who are trying to save their lives, to flee war and bloody repression. i welcome the measures proposed by the commission concerning the distribution and resettlement of asylum seekers in need of international protection. it is now up to the states to prove that the union of which they are members is worthy of its name. the refugee status must be sanctified, but we must also act on the causes of the evil; these murderous conflicts at the gates of europe. the european union must contribute to their resolution by playing a more assertive role. the fight against mafia smugglers, who turn the world's misery into a shameful profit, must also be strengthened. the situation is complex and does not require a single response, but action is urgently needed. it is more than a european issue, it is a human issue.
in writing. ‒ for the n-va, the asylum crisis must be tackled with a balanced overall package of measures aimed at: the commission is therefore proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the following areas: the present resolution does not meet the conditions for such a structural approach. that is why the n-va delegation voted against. the n-va is in favour of a europe that is realistic. both the eu and the member states must take their responsibilities. the n-va cannot accept a right to buy-out the compulsory distribution of asylum seekers, which is now on the table. the european union has a responsibility to ensure that the rights of asylum seekers are respected. we need a system where all member states show solidarity in asylum. the same applies to the eastern european countries which receive and expect a great deal of european socioeconomic support but which have so far stubbornly refused to show solidarity in receiving asylum seekers. for us it is clear: for what, hear what.
in writing. ‒ the middle east peace process between israel and palestine has stalled. the eu calls for the immediate resumption of credible efforts for peace and reiterates its strong support for a two-state solution. i therefore welcome the resolution of parliament calling for a new multilateral approach by the eu which takes greater account of the interests of peace and security of both the israelis and the palestinians.
in writing. ‒ i have endorsed this joint resolution which calls firstly for the immediate resumption of credible peace efforts and welcomes the union's commitment to actively work towards a renewed multilateral approach to the peace process. parliament reaffirmed its firm support for the two-state solution, based on the 1967 borders, with a mutual agreement on the exchange of territories and jerusalem as the capital of the two entities, namely the state of israel, whose security would be guaranteed, and an independent, democratic, united and viable state of palestine, living side by side in peace and security, in mutual recognition, on the basis of the right to self-determination and in strict respect of international law. it stressed that non-violent means and respect for human rights and humanitarian law are the only way to achieve a just and lasting peace between israelis and palestinians.another important element of the resolution was to condemn the continued expansion of israeli settlements, which violates international humanitarian law, fuels palestinian resentment and undermines the viability of a two-state solution, and to call on the israeli authorities to immediately cease and desist from their settlement policy.
in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a resolution on the eu's role in the middle east peace process. this resolution should be the european commission's road map. as things stand, it is regrettable that there is no comprehensive and coherent vision of the eu's engagement in the peace process. the appointment of a special representative for the peace process at the mo therefore highlights the eu's commitment to the region, which can only be encouraged. europe must make the best possible use of its institutional and political expertise in the region to play a concrete political role in the resumption of a credible and lasting peace process. the aim must be to achieve, by non-violent means and with respect for human rights and humanitarian law, a bold initiative that serves the interests of peace and security of israelis and palestinians.
in writing. the palestinian and israeli peoples have a deep desire for peace. they both have the same right to live in their state, on land that belongs to them to develop their country and give a future to their children. this conflict has been going on for decades. feelings of despair, humiliation and rebellion have been engraved in many hearts and minds. but everyone knows that this situation cannot last, because if poverty breeds despair, injustice and humiliation breed violence. political courage is expected of all leaders. the european union must act to achieve a lasting solution in a fragile and changing geopolitical context. it is as john fitzgerald kennedy said, "in giving others the rights they have, we give ourselves rights".

in writing. ‒ i supported this joint resolution in which parliament reiterated its deep concern about the situation of human rights and fundamental freedoms in belarus, as well as the shortcomings identified in previous elections by independent international observers and the active persecution of opposition leaders after the elections; parliament welcomed the recent release of the last political prisoners and considered it a first step towards improving relations between the european union and belarus, but called on the country to move beyond symbolic gestures. it also called on belarus, the only country in europe still applying the death penalty, to join a global moratorium on the execution of the death penalty, which would be a first step towards its permanent abolition.
in writing. ‒ while remaining deeply concerned about the situation of human rights and fundamental freedoms in belarus, the european parliament, in voting this resolution, welcomed the release of the last political prisoners in the country at the end of august. the resolution calls on the belarusian government to rehabilitate released political prisoners and fully restore their civil and political rights, and recalls that belarus is the last european country to apply the death penalty and that 10 people have been executed since 2010. the non-binding resolution calls on belarus to hold the next presidential elections, due in october, "in accordance with internationally recognised standards" and to allow the opposition to participate in the elections on an equal footing. parliament also reiterated its call on the commission to support, with financial and political means, the efforts of civil society, independent media and non-governmental organisations to support the democratic aspirations of the belarusian people.
in writing. ‒ given the current high average unemployment rate, i welcome this report on promoting entrepreneurship, skills and competences among young people at all levels of education and training. relations between schools and enterprises must be encouraged so that pupils and students can acquire practical experience and models at an early stage. the main contribution to this would be the introduction of a dual training system throughout the eu, as is the case in the german-speaking community, among other countries.
in writing. ‒ the main objective of social and solidarity-based enterprises is to achieve their social objective and to give priority to the interests of employees over those of capital. in this sense, they are a key driver in advancing towards the europe 2020 targets on jobs, innovation and the reduction of poverty and social exclusion. the social and solidarity economy provides jobs for the categories of people most often excluded from the labour market. the introduction of national regulations on the social and solidarity economy in all the member states, as is already the case in countries such as belgium, would obviously be useful in this respect. i therefore approve this report.
in writing. europe has long advocated a more inclusive society, in particular through the creation of social enterprises aimed at the development of activities with social, societal or environmental objectives. it has also launched an initiative to promote the creation and development of social enterprises, in particular by facilitating their access to finance. one in four new businesses in europe and one in three in belgium are social enterprises. these companies, which reinvest part of their profits in their social or environmental mission, deserve our full support. they are distinguished by the strong commitment of their employees or partners. productive, supportive and competitive, they have a deep sense of the common good and provide jobs for more than 14 million europeans who have been weakened by the consequences of the financial crisis.
‒ today the european parliament was called upon to give its opinion on a report on social entrepreneurship and social innovation in the fight against unemployment. as a strong advocate of the social and solidarity-based economy, this report was particularly important to me. the social and solidarity economy in europe affects 14 million workers (or 6.5% of workers) and two million enterprises (or 10% of enterprises) in europe. the aim of these companies is to achieve their social objective. for example, creating jobs for vulnerable groups, providing services to their staff members or, more broadly, having positive social and environmental impacts. with this report, which i voted for, i congratulate the four member states, including belgium, which have national regulations on the social economy. however, i think it is important to increase the participation of social and solidarity-based economy enterprises in public procurement procedures. i would stress that the social economy could help to reduce youth unemployment considerably by setting up training courses for social entrepreneurs.
in writing. ‒ the eu has limited competence in social enterprise and social innovation and the commission tends to underestimate their importance. the lope fontagne report therefore stresses the importance of the social economy in combating (or avoiding) unemployment. social enterprises often do better in crisis situations. the report stresses the social objective and the more inclusive workplaces, but also the more democratic structures and the fact that the social economy is strongly linked to the general interest of society. the report calls for the eu to step up its efforts to deliver on the social entrepreneurship initiative and to recognise the non-profit sector and its economic actors. a strong link is established with the eu 2020 objectives. i therefore think it is important to support the alternative of the social economy and social innovation and hopefully to make it more mainstream and voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it proposes a number of reforms which are needed to help create a more competitive european labour market. in europe, unemployment remains one of our most important challenges. at the end of last year, 24 million europeans were unemployed. of these, 11.9 million were longterm unemployed and 5 million were under 25 years of age. the creation of jobs is a top priority. unfortunately, despite some signs of economic recovery, it is still too slow and laborious. the labour market needs to be reformed in several member states and structural reforms need to be pursued, as well as efforts in terms of training, strengthening synergies between education systems and enterprises and stimulating entrepreneurship.
in writing. after the financial and economic crisis of recent years, the economy is gradually recovering. we see this in the careful recovery of employment. nevertheless, the number of young people and those with low qualifications who are unemployed is still far too high. this alde report sets out concrete policy proposals to tackle the causes of these high unemployment rates. this requires structural reforms. the counselling of young unemployed people must be organised in such a way that young people can enter the labour market as soon as possible. in this fast-changing world of increasing globalisation, digitalisation and new technologies, new synergies between education and business can help to bridge the gap between the supply of skills among young people and the increasing demand for highly skilled labour. this will help to prepare young people for the labour market. small and medium-sized enterprises form the backbone of europe's economy. it is recommended that entrepreneurship classes be included in the curricula to encourage the entrepreneurial spirit among young people. by prioritising investment in innovation and new economic sectors and education, we can anticipate closely any developments in future skills needs in the labour market.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament gave its opinion today on the report on 'creating a competitive labour market in the 21st century union: adapting skills and qualifications to job demand and prospects, a way out of the crisis'. many eu member states are faced with a high level of unemployment (9.8% for the eu28). this is a situation which has been going on for too long now and for which europe and its member states must find solutions. unfortunately, it is clear that the current recipes do not work. it is therefore important to look at the revision of our labour market. in an increasingly mobile and flexible labour market, i stress the importance of putting in place a mechanism to secure the career path of european citizens. finally, the report encourages member states to introduce a minimum wage by law or by agreement, depending on national practice. i fully support this request, although i regret that the european parliament refuses to define a european reference level for this minimum wage.
in writing. ‒ in this report, skills are being put forward by the conservatives and neoliberals as the solution to mass unemployment. skills are the new trojan horse of the neoliberal market. but by focusing on skills one-sidedly, we are ignoring structural unemployment, wrong economic policies and the lack of good employment policies that should be producing more and better jobs. by claiming that 'the right skills' will keep you from becoming unemployed, you are simply blaming the victim (the jobseeker). in addition, the eu minimum wage was scrapped, 'entrepreneurship from kindergarten' was mentioned (can kindergarteners still be kindergarteners?) and 'incentives to work' (read: the unemployment benefit is paid to the unemployed person who has been unemployed for at least three years. we greens do not see it that way and voted against this resolution. moreover, we were able to present an alternative resolution which takes the debate away from supply and demand in the labour market and opens it up by denouncing the bad economic policies which fuel unemployment and inequality. our resolution was supported by the socialists and colleagues on the left, but unfortunately it did not pass.
in writing. ‒ these reports, which closely monitor the transposition of directives by the member states, show that the most problematic sectors are transport, health and consumer protection, environmental protection and the internal market. this monitoring is therefore important in the general interest of european citizens. the rapporteur points out two points which i think are relevant in this monitoring exercise. firstly, it is clear that austerity policies have led to clear cuts in the public administrations and the judicial apparatus of the member states. this can therefore have a significant impact on their ability to transpose european texts which are important for the daily lives of citizens. secondly, we must be extremely vigilant so that the refit programme, whose overall objective is to simplify european regulations, does not cause any setbacks in the protection of workers' health and safety or the protection of the environment. the charter of social rights itself calls on the union to ensure a high level of protection of the health of citizens and the safety of workers.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which notes in particular that the four areas in which member states have been subject to infringement procedures for failure to transpose in recent years were transport, health and consumer protection, environmental protection and internal market and services issues. the text of the report also calls on the commission and the member states to seek consensus at an earlier stage of the legislative process in order to ensure timely transposition and better implementation of legislation once enacted.

in writing. ‒ the convention on the abolition of forced labour is one of the eight core ilo conventions which define the basic international labour standards and is considered an instrument for the protection of human rights. however, 80 years after its adoption, the ilo estimates that at least 20.9 million people worldwide are victims of forced labor. the objective of this protocol is therefore to remedy shortcomings in the implementation of the legislation and to strengthen measures to prevent trafficking in human beings for the purpose of exploiting their labour and to protect and compensate victims of forced labour. the protocol calls in particular on ilo member states to develop a national policy and a national action plan for the effective and sustainable abolition of forced labour after consultation with workers' and employers' organisations. it also provides for measures to protect and assist victims of forced labour. the council decision will allow the member states to ratify those parts of the protocol which fall within the competence of the union. i can of course only support this report which the committee on civil liberties has unanimously approved.
in writing. ‒ forced labour is a violation of human rights and a violation of the dignity of millions of women, men, girls and boys. to date, it still affects 21 million people, victims of an exploitation that generates 150 billion dollars in revenue a year for those who organize and control it. all forms of trafficking and exploitation must be broken by law and determined action taken to enforce it. the forced labour convention is one of the eight core ilo conventions that define the basic international labour standards. it is seen as an instrument for the protection of human rights. i have supported this report because the objective of the protocol is to strengthen measures to prevent trafficking in human beings for the purpose of exploiting their labour, as well as the protection and compensation of victims of forced labour. the ratification of this protocol is an important step in the fight against trafficking and in guaranteeing the rights of victims of crime throughout europe. it will also help to combat traffickers.

in writing. ‒ the proposal authorises member states to ratify and take action, in the eu's interest, on those parts of the 2014 protocol that fall within eu competence by the end of 2016. the eu cannot do this on its own, as only states can ratify the forced labour convention. this convention is one of the eight fundamental conventions of the ilo (international labour organization) which together form the basic international labour standards and is considered an instrument of human rights. the 1930 convention calls on the member states to eliminate and criminalize the use of forced labour as soon as possible. more than 80 years later, the ilo estimates that at least 20.9 million people worldwide are victims of forced labor. the 2014 protocol aims to address implementation gaps and make progress in the prevention of trafficking for labour exploitation and in the protection and compensation of victims of forced labour. the ratification of this protocol is an important step in the fight against trafficking in human beings and in ensuring the rights of victims throughout europe and this report allows member states to do so. that's why i voted for it.

in writing. ‒ while agricultural products of a particular geographical origin which have certain qualities or are produced by traditional methods may be the subject of unitary protection of geographical indications at union level, the same cannot be said for non-agricultural products. the rapporteur, whose report i have approved, supports the introduction at european level of a single instrument for the protection of indications for non-agricultural products. this would lead to positive economic benefits for local or regional producers, create jobs in less favoured areas and provide consumers with clear information on the origin and manufacturing methods of products.
in writing. ‒ while agricultural products have been protected at european level since 1992, no common legislation has so far been adopted for industrial and craft products. it was therefore logical to extend the protection of geographical indications to these products, which symbolise traditional know-how and local culture and whose usurpation by competing companies cannot be tolerated. that is why i supported the proposal to extend the protection of geographical indications to non-agricultural products. i am convinced that this measure is likely to offer better guarantees to consumers, help producers and stimulate the local economy. the new rules could increase the attractiveness of the product for the consumer and enable the producer to increase the added value of his products. among the 800 products identified by the european commission as potentially affected are several belgian products such as antwerp diamonds, binche lace and mons earthenware.
in writing. i support this report which aims to strengthen trade at local and regional level. the extension of the protection of eu geographical indications to non-agricultural products is an essential step for local producers. it contributes to increasing the overall attractiveness of a territory, preserving local identities and promoting their particularities. it is in the union's interest to adopt such legislation in order to protect know-how and the jobs it generates, and to maximise the positive economic benefits. in addition, the geographical indication of products allows consumers to be fully informed of the origin of the product and thus to be better able to make an informed choice.
in writing. ‒ i voted this afternoon in favour of the resolution calling on the european commission to extend the protection of geographical indications (gi) to non-agricultural products. if the commission follows up this request, more than 800 listed products, in particular products from the belgian countryside, as varied as the blue stone of belgium, the carpets of tournai, the val saint lambert glass and crystal or the diamonds of antwerp, would benefit from the geographical indication. they would then share this quality label with such emblematic agricultural products as brussels chickens, gaumans pâté, ardennes ham and liège pequet. in europe, the regional products concerned would include porcelain, ceramics, ironwork, weaving and embroidery. all these activities are in the service of quality craftsmanship, which is subject to unfair and illegal competition from imitations and counterfeits. the 15 existing national laws on gi are not sufficient to protect this regional and local know-how. hence the need to create a uniform system at european level. the report also calls for the eu to take action to ensure that the eu's financial instruments are used to support the development of the eu's energy sector.
in writing. ‒ the text of the resolution voted today urges the european commission to present an initiative extending the protection of geographical indications at european level beyond what has already been done since 1992 for agricultural products, to include goods produced regionally and locally and craft products (such as the blue stone of belgium or the glass of the val saint-lambert). i welcome this, as it would support local economic development, boost tourism, increase consumer confidence and help to preserve cultural heritage and traditional craftsmanship. the european commission has already identified 800 products in europe that could benefit from such protection. the european parliament believes that this list could be revised upwards. moreover, the products concerned should be easily registered and included in a public register.

in writing. ‒ the aim of this report is to extend the protection of geographical indications. it is these geographical indications that make a particular region known and can boost the local and regional economy. local traders and producers are not excluded, and local customs and traditions are not easily lost. this protection will create additional jobs and help to preserve the craft. so i voted yes.

in writing. ‒ this regulation establishing a european small claims procedure aims to simplify and speed up the settlement of small claims in cross-border cases and to reduce the costs. it was specifically designed to help consumers and small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) to pursue their claims, thereby ensuring their access to justice. the aim of this report, which i supported, is to extend and improve the use of this instrument in the development and communication of this project.
in writing. the proposal voted on here facilitates the procedure for filing a small claim. individuals throughout the european union will be able to submit a claim without any further obligations. if it is not desired, the trial may be held without a hearing. if the hearing is necessary, it will also be possible to conduct it remotely, for example by videoconference. all these measures will make the judiciary more efficient and streamlined, which in turn will contribute to more transparent legislation. that is why i support this proposal.
in writing. ‒ the european small claims procedure has been in place since 2009. it is an optional simplified procedure based on standard forms and allows the recovery of funds held by a third party in another eu country. the system works well. it has reduced the costs of litigation for small crossborder claims by 40% and the length of the process has been reduced from two years to an average of five months. i supported this report because i felt that changes had to be made to this procedure to enable more citizens and small businesses to use it. in particular, i support raising the ceiling on debts that can be recovered through the procedure from eur 2 000 to eur 5 000, the proportionality of legal costs, the encouragement to use remote communication technologies for possible oral hearings and the provision of practical assistance by eu countries to fill in forms and give general information on the procedure and the jurisdiction of the court concerned.
in writing. i am pleased to see the culmination of this initiative taken by my group in 2011. with the development of cross-border trade, it was necessary to revise this regulation in order to improve access to justice for both european citizens and smes. the balanced compromise that has been reached is fully in line with the wider objective of better lawmaking. by increasing the small claims ceiling to eur 10 000, reducing the duration of the proceedings to 5 months and reducing the costs of the proceedings through pragmatic measures (e.g. payment by credit card, remote communication for hearings, capping of court fees, etc.); we are not only saving an estimated 40% but also, and above all, we are helping consumers and smes to bring actions to assert their rights. the european small claims procedure will need to be well communicated both at european level, via the e-justice portal, and at national level through awareness-raising campaigns, if it is to be successful.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on regulation (ec) no 861/2007 of 11 july 2007 establishing a european small claims procedure, which aims to simplify, speed up and reduce the costs of settling small crossborder disputes. this procedure has been specifically designed to help consumers and small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) to enforce their rights, thereby ensuring their access to justice. a review of the five years of application of the procedure shows that it has proved its worth. however, much remains to be done to expand and improve the use of this instrument. the european small claims procedure has reduced the costs of small claims cross-border proceedings by up to 40% and reduced their duration from a maximum of two years and five months to an average of five months. however, in some member states the use of small claims courts remains rare and therefore more needs to be done in terms of legal certainty, the use of modern technology and the transparency of proceedings.
in writing. ‒ the new european crossborder litigation procedure was voted on this afternoon. the european small claims procedure (escp) introduced in 2007 has reduced the cost of litigation by 40% and the length of litigation by more than 80%. the analysis of these latest figures shows that the contribution to consumers is therefore undeniable. but we wanted to improve the system further so that as many citizens as possible could benefit from it; this is not the case at the moment with only 86% of citizens and almost half of the courts saying they have never heard of this procedure
in writing. ‒ there are about 150 000 medium combustion plants in the eu which are a major source of sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides and dust emissions. while large combustion plants are covered by an ad hoc directive, air pollutant emissions from medium combustion plants are not. a proposal for a directive aims to regulate emissions from these medium-sized installations with the aim of reducing pollution for new and existing installations and of making effective application of the standards via a recording system. the report, which i have approved, supports the commission's proposal but provides clarifications on the application of the new directive in relation to the existing acquis, particularly in the area of industrial emissions.
in writing. the directive voted on here includes stricter limits for the emission of harmful substances from medium combustion plants (1-50 mw input), a category which has not been regulated so far. the directive also makes it possible to carry out more efficient controls on such installations. it can only improve air quality and at the same time encourage investment in better and cleaner installations.
in writing. ‒ there are about 143 000 'medium' combustion plants in europe (i.e. with a thermal output of between 1 and 50 mw). these installations are used for electricity generation, domestic or residential heating and cooling, and the production of heat or steam for industrial purposes. they are a major source of sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides and dust emissions. there are already eu regulations for small and large combustion plants, but until now, emissions of air pollutants from medium combustion plants were not regulated at eu level. that is why i supported this directive, especially since the text sets emission ceilings at an ambitious level to allow for a gradual improvement in air quality, while preserving the operation of existing installations, especially the smaller ones, operated by smes or local authorities, which are important, for example, for heating schools, hospitals or universities. of course, the directive does not prevent member states from enforcing standards that are stricter than those laid down by the directive.
europe has made serious efforts in recent years to clean up its air. despite measurable improvements, however, air quality in europe is still poor in many places. the air quality is still below the standards set by the eu and below the world health organisation's targets. the emission limit values for small and medium-sized combustion plants have now been set in addition to the emission standards for large combustion plants. today, there are some 143 000 small and medium-sized combustion plants in europe covered by this new directive. these are often local combustion plants that supply energy or heat to small village communities or large buildings or, for example, supply steam or hot water to public district heating networks. the directive, which has been tightened up by parliament, now sets maximum emission limits for nitrogen oxides, sulphur dioxide and fine dust. in order to comply with the directive and at the same time to guarantee the energy supply, the operators of these combustion plants have ample time to adapt to the stricter emission standards. the adoption of the directive by parliament is a major step forward in europe's ambition to achieve clean and healthy air.
in writing. ‒ amid the volkswagen scandal over the fraud in pollution tests of 11 million diesel vehicles worldwide, meps adopted important legislation on air quality this afternoon. the new legislation affects about 143 000 medium-sized combustion plants in the eu. these equipment, with a thermal output of between 1 and 50 mw, are used for various applications (electricity, domestic and industrial heating and cooling, etc.). unlike small and large combustion plants, they are not currently covered by eu legislation, although they cause an increase in particulate matter (pm) emissions. i supported this agreement at first reading with the council, as i did on 15 july in the committee on the environment. a compromise which allows the national authorities to introduce stricter limit values than those laid down by the directive. efforts will need to continue at all levels of government because, as the european environment agency points out, air pollution poses direct risks to people and the environment: concentrations of particulate matter are responsible for more than 400 000 premature deaths each year in the eu. this is an unacceptable figure!
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this european directive which will limit the emissions of certain air pollutants from medium-sized combustion plants, such as electricity generators and domestic or industrial heating or cooling systems. the vote confirms the agreement reached on 23 june by the negotiators of the european parliament, the european commission and the council of the eu on the first reading of this legislation, which for the first time will regulate the pollution of the 143 000 installations with a thermal output of 1 to 50 megawatts. the emission limit values for sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides and particulate matter from existing combustion plants of more than 5 mw will come into force in 2025 as proposed by the european commission. but smaller installations, with a thermal capacity of between 1 and 5 mw, generally used by smes, will only have to comply with the limit values from 2030. in areas where eu air quality standards are not being met, member states will be required to assess whether stricter limit values should be set. the text introduces rules for monitoring carbon monoxide.
in writing. ‒ the proposed changes improve the prospects for realistic implementation of the directive, so that it can become an important instrument for improving air quality in the european union, without imposing an unjustified burden on society and the economy. unfortunately, we had to compromise, but i voted for the text.
in writing. ‒ in march 2014, the commission published a proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to caseins and caseinates intended for human consumption. it repeals the previous directive on the subject and brings community legislation into line with international standards as regards caseins and caseinates. the proposal must be seen in the context of the general food law which aims at the free movement of safe and healthy food. in this respect, the new labelling requirements will allow consumers, especially those suffering from allergies, to make informed choices. i approved this report.
in writing. caseins and caseinates are substances obtained from milk by technological processes and are found in many products other than those of the dairy sector. the proposed directive harmonises european standards with international standards. this is an important step because it puts the european dairy industry on a level playing field globally. this will strengthen the internal market and update the standards for informing consumers about the presence of these substances in the products concerned. caseins and caseinates are allergens. the report recalls one of the eu's fundamental principles, which is to ensure that consumer protection is ensured by the establishment of strict and transparent regulations.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report by mr la via on casein and caseinates for human consumption. the aim of the technical adaptation is to repeal a 1983 directive and replace it with the present legislation in order to bring community provisions into line with international standards. the aim behind this technical jargon is to update the legal framework for casein, the protein material in milk. caseinates are products obtained by drying treated casein. a key point of this legislation concerns consumer information, since some citizens are allergic to casein as they are to lactose. this is why it is important to indicate their presence on food labels. this adaptation of european legislation to international standards will not end the debate on the good and bad sides of casein. on the positive side, casein is of great use in all situations where protein intake is limited over a long period of time. on the negative side, some animal proteins, such as casein, are thought to cause breast cancer and other forms of carcinoma. that's a great way to rehabilitate the baby.
in writing. ‒ in march 2014, the commission published its proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to caseins and caseinates intended for human consumption and repealing council directive 83/417/eec. in its proposal, the commission suggests replacing the directive with a new one, mainly for the following reasons: the need to adapt existing provisions to the development of legislation in the field of foodstuffs and to adjust the compositional requirements for food caseins to the corresponding international standard. these new provisions which i voted for will enable food business operators to enjoy a level playing field on the world market. the text also supports the labelling requirements for caseins and caseinates, which will allow consumers, especially those with food allergies or intolerances, to make informed choices.
in writing. ‒ casein and caseinates are milk proteins used as neutralising factors in food products. these proteins are often the cause of various allergies. this is why there is a call for stricter standards requiring the labelling of these caseins on the products in which they are used. this will no longer leave consumers in the dark about the nutrients and added values in their food and drink that can cause allergies. the european commission proposes to repeal and replace european directive 83/417/eec with a new directive. this will further develop the food law and will align the commission's implementing powers as set out in the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu). in addition, the maximum permitted casein content is adjusted to international standards. the commission proposal requires manufacturers to label added nutrients that could cause allergic reactions, something which is strongly supported by the greens. the european parliament does want the european commission's powers, as mentioned above, to be limited in time and to be limited. i support this proposal because it protects and safeguards the rights of consumers.

in writing. more and more shops offer products for sale on the internet. however, online payment systems have been less responsive to this trend. we need to make online payment systems more efficient. this will allow for more choice and make these systems more transparent. this is very important to increase confidence in e-commerce, which in turn will further grow e-commerce and the economy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because there is a need to update the eu rules on payment services in order to keep pace with innovation and make mobile and online payment methods safer, cheaper and more attractive for consumers and businesses alike. the proposal aims to improve consumer protection against fraud, abuse and payment incidents, for example in the event of a contentious transaction. under the proposed new rules, all payment service providers operating in the union will also be subject to appropriate rules, including on oversight. this new framework should create conditions for the emergence of new players and the development of innovative internet and mobile payment methods in europe. consumers and businesses will thus benefit from greater choice and better conditions.
in writing. the emergence of a digital market in europe, conditioned by the emergence of european champions of new technologies, is one of the european parliament's liberal priorities. we have just approved the updating of the rules on the currently fragmented and costly payment services market, which is estimated to cost €130 billion a year. european citizens are expected to spend €45 billion via mobile payments in 2015, an increase of almost 90% compared to 2014. figures that confirm the inevitable growth of digital in everyday life. this new regulatory framework will reduce costs, improve security and facilitate payments mainly via mobile and internet.
in writing. ‒ meps voted this afternoon on the tajani report on updating the rules on the payment services market. these services are growing rapidly but are currently characterised by their fragmented and costly nature, with an estimated total cost of €130 billion per year. a study predicts that european citizens will have spent €45 billion via mobile payments in 2015, an increase of almost 90% compared to 2014. figures that confirm the inevitable impact of digital technology on everyday life. i have of course supported the adaptation of the payment services legislation to the new technological media. this is the kind of legislation that can reconcile citizens with europe. this directive will certainly bring added value for the consumer, who will soon benefit from easier and cheaper payment solutions (online, mobile or tablet and card). this legislation makes it possible to take stock of and anticipate the main trends and the way in which consumers now purchase goods and services. the most visible of these is certainly the fact that trade via smartphones in europe will increase by an average of 42% each year.
in writing. the adoption of this report constitutes an update of the payment services directive. the text adopted aims to improve european rules on payment services in order to encourage innovation in this field in europe and to get rid of american systems such as paypal (the european parliament would like to see other european companies break through, as is already the case in germany with the sofort system...). the text adopted should therefore help to break the banking lock which still prevents the emergence of new payment services, but also to promote the development of innovative settlement methods in the european union. by stimulating the market for alternative online payment methods, the european parliament also hopes to bring down transaction costs. however, cheaper payment services cannot be less secure, so this directive will clearly oblige banks and other payment service providers to use technologies that ensure a secure user authentication procedure and reduce the risk of fraud for consumers. once formally approved by the council, the new legislative framework will enter into force in two years' time, but the technical specifications will have to be applied before then.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of mr tajani's proposal on the proposal for a european parliament and council directive on payment services in the internal market and amending directives 2002/65/ec, 2013/36/eu and 2009/110/ec and repealing directive 2007/64/ec, following the opinion of the experts in my political group. in particular, this regulation introduces rules on the charging of interchange fees for card-based payment transactions and aims to further accelerate the achievement of an efficient integrated market for card-based payment transactions.
in writing. ‒ according to studies, european citizens spent €45 billion via mobile devices in 2015. this represents an increase of about 90% over the previous year. these figures indicate an ever-increasing impact of online payments on our daily lives. it is estimated that trade via the so-called smartphones is increasing by about 42% annually. i voted for this report, of course, because it adapts european legislation to the ever more rapidly changing technological requirements. the european directive brings added value to the european citizen who will be able to benefit from simplified payment options at lower costs.

in writing. the need to abolish the death penalty is, for a humanist and a universalist like me, a matter of course. this extremely serious problem concerns the right to life, the right not to be subjected to cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment, the first of human rights and respect for human dignity. a man who kills another man is a disgrace to mankind. cruel and unacceptable, the death penalty is the denial of the humanity that lives in every human being. it is neither fair nor effective. it is neither moralising, intimidating nor deterrent. it carries all the social poisons, starting with racism and inequality. the abolition of the death penalty therefore meets an objective of universal justice. as european parliamentarians, we have a duty to campaign in all national and international forums for the universal abolition of the death penalty. we must keep this debate alive, weigh in on our governments and ensure that respect for life is mentioned in any trade agreement, bilateral or multilateral.

in writing. ‒ on 4 october 2010, the rupture of a waste reservoir in hungary led to the release of nearly one million cubic metres of highly alkaline red mud, which caused flooding in several villages, killed ten people, injured nearly 150 and polluted large areas of land, including 4 natura 2000 sites. the resolution is concerned that little or no lessons seem to have been learned in the last five years, as eu legislation and international conventions continue to be poorly applied, inspections remain weak and no or few shortcomings in eu legislation have been addressed during this period. the text adopted, which i supported, therefore calls in particular on the commission and the member states to intensify their efforts to ensure the full implementation and correct application of all relevant union legislation and all relevant international conventions, not only with regard to the manufacture of aluminium and the environmentally sound management of red sludge, but also, in general, the environmentally sound management of hazardous waste.

madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, as so often happens, the news catches up with the political momentum, and the commission has just demonstrated this to us, as it has just experienced by establishing that the tax breaks granted to fiat and starbucks by luxembourg and the netherlands were in fact disguised state subsidies. so now we know that it's not just immoral, it's illegal. and very clearly, if this text had been voted in 2011 or 2012, everything in the text we are about to vote on would not have allowed these tax evasion. and so, clearly, this case shows us that the european council has not yet grasped the importance of the issue. i really think that parliament's text is much more ambitious than the decision of 6 october last, and i would like to thank and congratulate our colleague markus ferber and all the fictitious rapporteurs. it is obviously a compromise text, and i would like to stress a few important points. the first, as has been said, is obviously the scope. all tax records of multinationals, without exception, must be analysed, whether national or international, and without time limit, otherwise what is the point? who else are we trying to protect? secondly, as we all know, rules are only effective if there are penalties. and that is what parliament is asking for, that there should be sanctions if the member states do not want to play along, or if they are slow in sending information or sending incorrect information. thirdly, we obviously want to strengthen the role of the commission in this process. we all know that we cannot be both judge and party. no system works when you are both judge and party, and yet that is what the council wants to achieve. fourthly, to combat these abuses, we must obviously call for greater transparency. but real transparency, not cosmetic transparency. you know that too much information kills information, and what we ask for and what is foreseen in this text is that there should be a publication that is clear, accessible and understandable to all, not just for specialists. finally, i would like to conclude with one final point: all companies operating in more than one country will receive a european identification number. i think this is essential to make it easier to monitor and to reduce the administrative burden. i hope, therefore, commissioner, that you will support this proposal, because apart from a few multinationals and a few member states, it is the whole of europe that is losing out, and it cannot continue to be this way.
the european parliament may not have a formal right to decide on this matter, but the unanimity with which we advocate a really effective exchange mechanism is a signal that the council cannot and must not ignore. only by giving the commission a central role in this exchange and giving it access to essential information on tax rulings can new tax scandals be avoided. the fear of the member states trying to shield these rulings from state aid investigations is, however, at times a painful spectacle. the founding countries themselves recognised that the common market could only flourish if a european authority was in place to ensure that individual member states did not grant aid that distorted competition. that is precisely why the commission was given the task of acting against unlawful state aid. why, then, this useful information on tax rulings granted should remain with the commission at this particular time remains a mystery to me. the perverse thing is that these cramped and misguided attempts to 'protect national sovereignty' end up playing member states against each other, playing the cards for multinationals and presenting the bill to citizens and smes.
in the package travel case, it was important to strike the right balance between protecting the rights of consumers and those of the tourism sector. i think we have succeeded in doing so, thanks to the good leadership of our rapporteur. consumers who book online will enjoy the same level of protection as those who book through a travel agency. they will also be protected against price increases, service provider bankruptcies and unforeseen and unavoidable situations such as natural disasters, such as we have seen with the eruption of the volcano in iceland. it also lays down clear rules on the termination of the contract and on the information to be provided by traders before, during and after the conclusion of the contract. on the other hand, we have also managed to ensure that we do not regulate the sectors concerned to the detriment of others by means of superfluous or bad regulation.
in writing. 67% of european citizens feel they are protected when buying online package holidays; it is not. the legislation on this subject dates from 1990 and does not take any account of this new type of online service, which now accounts for almost one in four journeys in europe. the vote this afternoon was therefore intended to protect the 138 million consumers who use these combined journeys better and to save them the inconvenience of, for example, an unjustified price increase, the bankruptcy of their operator, excessive changes in timetable or unforeseen events. almost 200 million european citizens visit an online travel site every month. it was time to dust off european legislation. we wanted to ensure that holidaymakers who combine their own holiday 'packages' from online travel services are better protected, as they do not benefit from the same coverage as those who go through traditional travel agencies. it is a step towards better protection of the rights of the european consumer.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which calls for an agreement between the eu and switzerland on the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts. this exchange of information is expected to be implemented in 2018. in the current context and in the wake of the swissleaks cases, it was essential to conclude an agreement to increase tax cooperation in order to combat tax evasion. the agreement contains certain provisions aimed at limiting the possibility for taxpayers to evade their reporting obligations to the tax authorities by transferring their assets or investing in financial products that do not fall within the scope of the agreement. the information to be exchanged covers not only income such as interest and dividends, but also account balances and proceeds from the sale of financial assets.
