in writing. - i voted in favour of the text. this agreement marks an important step in the current efforts to combat tax fraud and evasion, and reinforces the 2004 agreement which ensured that switzerland applies measures equivalent to those provided for in the union's savings tax directive. the agreement provides that the european union and switzerland will automatically exchange information on the financial accounts of their respective residents as of 2018. the aim is to deal with situations where a taxpayer seeks to conceal capital corresponding to income or assets on which tax has not been paid.
in writing. ‒ in its tax transparency package of march 2015, the commission proposed to repeal the 2003 savings tax directive while keeping the 2008 one, so that member states would not have to apply the provisions of both directives, thus avoiding the inconvenience caused by duplicate data collection and reporting systems. this report, which i voted for, calls for this to be done while highlighting the shortcomings of the savings directive: - bilateral agreements between the european union and third countries will continue to exist regardless of the repeal of the directive. - the commission has not been given a mandate to negotiate agreements on automatic exchange of information with the 12 overseas territories of the european union. - certain products, mostly low-risk deposit accounts recommended for savings purposes, will no longer be subject to notifications under the administrative cooperation directive. while the risks of tax fraud are low, it is considered important that the commission continue to monitor that the repeal of the directive does not create a loophole.

in writing. ‒ the fight against tax evasion and the need for fair taxation are major concerns at both european and global level. while there has been great progress internationally, it is important to exercise caution when repealing an existing directive that has been respected for several years. the scope of financial products covered by the savings tax directive and the administrative cooperation directive, although similar, are not exactly identical. some products, for most low-risk deposit accounts recommended for savings purposes, will no longer be subject to disclosure under the administrative cooperation directive. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. it proposed that the commission should report to the european parliament once all member states had drawn up their national lists of low-risk accounts.

in writing. ‒ i supported this report which helps to better protect european citizens who buy package holidays online. this will help them to avoid the inconvenience of unjustified price increases, the bankruptcy of their operator, excessive changes in working hours or unforeseen events.
in writing. ‒ the package travel agreement is a step in the right direction, but it is not yet perfect. we would actually like to see much better consumer protection for click-through bookings, where consumers book a night through the airline's website, for example. we must also be careful not to jeopardise the many smes in the sector. the new rules should therefore be evaluated quickly and thoroughly and, if necessary, updated by the european commission. but now we must look ahead. the agreement takes the protection of travellers to a higher level and also protects them when making online reservations. it is now up to the member states to transpose this agreement into national law as wisely as possible.
in writing. more and more holidaymakers are booking a combined package holiday online. in addition to a plane ticket, they book a rental car and a hotel overnight. the adoption of the directive will improve the protection of the 120 million european travellers who book online package holidays. the new duties will reduce the damage to travellers in the european union by eur 430 million annually. among other things, travellers will have more options to cancel their trip free of charge in the event of an unannounced higher cost or in the event of a natural disaster or terrorist attack.
in writing. ‒ on tuesday, the european parliament voted for a directive that will give the 120 million european citizens who book their package holidays online the same protection as those who book through a travel agency. the rules were written in a law from 1990, a long time ago when the internet was not even born! the new legislation now takes into account the new way in which travellers plan their combined trips with the help of new technological tools and erases this injustice in the treatment of consumers. the new rules will give travellers a range of rights in the event of problems: repatriation and reimbursement in the event of the tour operator's bankruptcy, and the organiser's coverage of three nights in the event of an unavoidable and unforeseeable event such as a natural disaster or terrorist attack that would prevent travellers from returning home on time. the traveller will also have the right to cancel his trip without incurring any additional costs if the price of the trip increases by more than 8% or if there are significant changes in the main characteristics of the trip such as the date of the trip, the flight schedule or the tourist category of accommodation.
in writing. ‒ consumers who buy air tickets or travel services online will now enjoy the same level of protection as those who use a travel agency. today we have finally approved the adaptation of the directive on package holidays and assisted travel. with this revised legislation, the rights of travellers in europe are strengthened overall. new booking models are now included in its scope and travellers are informed in detail of their rights. among other innovations, the legislation provides: - the right of the consumer to cancel a package tour whose price has increased by more than 8% without justification; - the right of the consumer to benefit from three nights of accommodation paid for by the organiser if the consumer is prevented, for some unforeseeable reason, from returning home; - consumer protection against the bankruptcy of package tour operators; - the possibility for the traveller to cancel a contract free of charge in exceptional circumstances. member states will have two years to transpose this directive into national law, which responds to the urgent need to modernise the old 1990 directive.
in writing. ‒ package holidays are holidays offered where various elements, such as transport, accommodation and activities, are included in the price. there is already a european directive on this subject, but it dates from 1990 and is out of date because certain market structures, such as the use of the internet, are not included in the text. the new directive should ensure a healthy balance between consumer protection and the need to protect retailers in this sector. the text, after a second reading by parliament, gives a clear description of these package holidays and of the differences with linked travel arrangements. this provides a clear demarcation of the different sectors, thereby providing consumers with information in a more transparent manner. it was important to me that consumer protection remained, while at the same time preventing retailers, who often offer better and more sustainable travel arrangements, from being overtaken by large companies that take over the market completely. i support this directive because it contains this balance. it is essential that all this be followed up properly so that these measures do not remain a blank canvas and are properly applied.
in writing. ‒ it was time to dust off european legislation. we wanted to ensure that holidaymakers who combine their own holiday 'packages' from online travel services are better protected as they do not benefit from the same coverage as those who go through traditional travel agencies. it is a step towards better protection of european consumer rights
in writing. ‒ european legislation has been in place for some time to protect citizens who book package holidays or travel arrangements. however, this protection did not yet exist for people who booked travel, transport, hotels, etc. separately, for example via the internet. that is why i voted in favour of this recommendation.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the new telecommunications package. the abolition of roaming charges was long awaited by all european citizens, but also by start-ups and smes. thanks to the vote on the telecoms package, this abolition will be effective from 15 june 2017 and european citizens will finally be able to move freely without incurring additional costs for mobile telephony and network access (calls, sms, data) throughout the european area. i welcome the vote, although i would have liked a more ambitious and clearer agreement on the other major issue in this legislation: net neutrality. of course, the text adopted provides the legal guarantee of an open internet in europe, which should avoid the risk of having a two-speed internet, but i consider that parliament's initial position on the principle of net neutrality was more ambitious, clearer and more precise.
in writing. ‒ on tuesday, the european parliament approved the text on the single european electronic communications market. it is the kind of legislation that has a real impact on the lives of european citizens. the text will eventually lead to a total ban on roaming charges for the use of mobile phones abroad in the union by june 2017. this means that calling abroad or surfing the internet via your smartphone in another member state will no longer incur additional costs. a first transitional ceiling will be effective from april 2016 and will reduce the current additional costs of €0.19 per minute for outgoing voice calls, €0.06 for sms and €0.20 per megabyte for mobile internet use. the initiative was introduced by former liberal commissioner neelie kroes in 2010. this is therefore an important step taken by parliament. the less ambitious "open internet" component requires internet service providers to ensure equal treatment of data flows on the net. on this important point, i regret that the negotiations have led to an ambiguous and equivocal agreement which does not live up to the expectations for the union's single telecommunications market.

in writing. ‒ i have of course supported the proposal as amended by the committee on international affairs to strengthen the legal framework on the prevention of torture, and more particularly to prevent the export of goods and substances which could be used for the execution of such acts. the existing union prohibition on trade in certain goods which could be used for capital punishment, torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment would therefore have an extended scope. the union maintains a firm opposition in principle to torture, the abolition of which is one of the main priorities of the union's human rights policy. torture is a cruel and inhuman act. thirty years after the adoption of the landmark convention against torture, and despite almost universal condemnation of the practice, torture remains a global scourge. it is therefore urgent to act to reverse this trend and to strengthen all the means available to achieve this.
in writing. ‒ europe has an important role to play in the fight against torture and the abolition of the death penalty. the 2005 anti-torture regulation already sets up an export control system for products that are or may be used in capital punishment or torture cases. the council also adopted a resolution on the situation in the former yugoslavia. the current regulation does, however, contain a number of shortcomings which it is high time to address. i therefore voted in favour of this proposal because the technical updates proposed by the commission are essential and aim at ensuring stricter controls. the idea is to expand the current eu ban to include services, finance, transport and insurance. the aim is also to prohibit the transit of goods prohibited by the eu and listed in the 2005 regulation. we have also revised the annex which lists safe countries to which exports of controlled medicinal substances do not require authorization.
in writing. ‒ following parliament's resolution of 17 june 2010, the commission published a proposal to amend the 'regulation against goods intended for torture' (regulation (ec) no 1236/2005 concerning trade in certain goods which could be used for capital punishment, torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment). i have of course supported this text in parliament which proposes, in addition to the current regime prohibiting the export and import of goods intended for torture and execution (annex ii) and the authorization regime for goods liable to be misappropriated for the purpose of torture (annex iii), to extend these restrictions to all goods liable to be used for capital punishment and torture. in particular, the provision of brokering services and technical assistance for any of the listed goods should be prohibited where the broker or the provider of technical assistance knows that the goods concerned are or may be intended for capital punishment, torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment, where controls are carried out to prevent such use.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the text. export controls, which are applicable throughout the union, are instruments of external trade policy which contribute to the achievement of a wider set of strategic objectives. regulation (ec) no 1236/2005 'against torture' is a prime means of strengthening the protection of human rights by subjecting to controls the assets and activities used, or which could be used, to inflict capital punishment, torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. it thus contributes to the european union's long-standing policy of abolishing the death penalty worldwide and combating torture. by combining prohibitions and authorisation requirements for trade in the goods listed in its annexes, it contributes to the achievement of these objectives. it establishes a regime prohibiting trade in goods specially intended for torture and execution and related technical assistance (annex ii) and an authorisation regime for 'multi-purpose' goods which could be diverted for use in torture and executions by lethal chemical injection.

in writing. ‒ after analysing the accounts, i note that the rate of implementation of payment appropriations after the budgetary correction at the end of the year was 69%. according to the joint undertaking, part of the explanation is the delays in the issuance of payment certificates by the national funding authorities. i would also like to recall the court of auditors' report which states that the annual accounts of the joint undertaking for the financial year 2013 present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the joint undertaking as at 31 december 2013. the same applies to its operating results and cash flows for the year ended on that date. for all these reasons, i have decided to vote in favour of the second czarnecki report and to give the executive director of the ecsel joint undertaking discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the artemis joint undertaking for the financial year 2013.

in writing. ‒ i have endorsed this resolution which stresses the need to deploy additional resources to help the countries most affected, particularly sierra leone, liberia and guinea. although the outbreak appears to be coming to an end, the events of recent months should serve as a reminder to the eu and its member states of the need to help develop social and medical services in these countries, which cannot cope with an ebola outbreak on their own.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that it is imperative to improve international governance in the management of health crises, especially as the likelihood of a food crisis arising from this epidemic (which has had devastating effects on smallholder farmers) is increasing. the crisis has served as a reminder to eu leaders of the need for them to stick to their goal of allocating at least 20% of public aid to the development of basic social services, with priority given to health care. it also shed light on the structural problems still present in a number of countries. one of the things i think is important is access to medicines because right now two billion people in the world don't have access to vaccines or the treatments they need to stay alive and healthy. i believe that access to medicines and research and development in this field must be geared primarily to the needs of patients, whether they live in our country or in developing countries.
in writing. ‒ since march 2014, sierra leone, liberia and guinea have been hit by the worst ebola outbreak ever recorded. the scale and complexity of the current outbreak has posed a real challenge to these three states, which have structural health and education gaps. however, the epidemic has also been a real test for the international community. the report therefore considers, inter alia, that the eu's long-term response beyond emergency aid will first have to be in the form of development aid, which will have to include investments in health to promote resilience, in particular in the organisation and management of health systems. the text also calls for the establishment of a permanent european rapid reaction team comprising experts, laboratory support teams, epidemiologists and a logistical infrastructure, including mobile laboratories, which can be deployed as soon as possible. i have of course supported all these measures.
in writing. ‒ since march 2014, sierra leone, liberia and guinea have been hit by the worst ebola outbreak ever known to mankind. the permeability of borders has facilitated the spread of the virus from one country to another. the three countries in question are among the lowest in the undp human development index. their average life expectancy is 60 years or less, they rarely have more than three years of schooling and about 80% of their citizens live in extreme poverty. the resolution was intended to recall that the current ebola crisis is both a sign of the structural weaknesses that persist in many countries and a reminder to eu officials to persevere in their commitment to devote at least 20% of public aid to the development of basic social sectors, with health as a priority.
in writing. ‒ following the recent revelations about volkswagen's cheating, it is imperative that european leaders seize this opportunity to strengthen controls in the automotive sector. it is imperative to strengthen the legislative framework and address gaps, in particular with regard to testing methods, in order to protect public health and consumers. the european environment agency estimated that as many as 430,000 premature deaths related to poor air quality occurred in 2011 alone. the impact of diesel vehicles on the achievement of the union's greenhouse gas emission targets, together with the importance of the automotive sector in general, demonstrates the need for action. that is why i support the motion for a resolution by parliament, which calls on the commission and the member states to work against the circumvention of emission requirements and to ensure that consumer rights are respected.
in writing. in the aftermath of the volkswagen scandal, it has become clear that the methods we currently use to measure car emissions are not accurate enough. that is why i voted for this resolution, because it calls, among other things, for the introduction of real driving emissions testing as soon as possible. this should give consumers a better idea of the real consumption and emissions of their cars.
in writing. ‒ every day new revelations emerge about the scandal of cheating on car emissions tests. i have supported this resolution because i condemn this organized fraud which has robbed millions of people and because i believe it is essential that a thorough investigation be carried out and that appropriate sanctions be imposed. we know the damage caused by air pollution. we have just set new limits for some key pollutants and next month we have the big climate conference. excess emissions of pollutants have many adverse effects on human health and are a cause of premature death. they also produce environmental damage. the vw scandal also has a significant impact on the reputation and competitiveness of the automotive sector. the sector is one of the main drivers of growth and innovation and contributes to employment in a significant number of member states. for these reasons, i believe that the whole european emission control system must be strengthened without further delay, that the commission must be involved in the investigations currently being carried out in several member states and that a monitoring authority should be set up at european level.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the opening of a committee of inquiry, supporting amendment no 17 to the joint motion for a resolution on emission measures in the automotive sector, and regret that this proposal was not adopted. i think it is necessary to shed light on the fraud of the volkswagen company, which manipulated its diesel-powered vehicles to deceive the american emissions inspections, and on any involvement of european authorities, whatever they may be. this case not only tarnishes the image of the automobile industry, but is also a sad symbol of non-europe in industry. i would urge that strict rules be put in place to govern practices and that exemplary penalties be imposed so that confidence can be restored. finally, the employment of workers in the sector, who deplore these malicious acts as much as i do, must be protected.
in writing. - i voted for this text. i have also formally asked the european authorities to impose sanctions and to urge the member states and regions to bring a complaint against the german company. to bring an action for damages would be only fair; the tax incentives granted by the public authorities to private individuals for the purchase of environmentally friendly vehicles are based on a lie by volkswagen. on the other hand, asking companies to control their behavior is like asking drivers to fine themselves!

the rapporteur. madam president, madam commissioner, mr president-in-office of the council, ladies and gentlemen, i have therefore, as you have just said, the responsibility of presenting our budgetary proposals for the so-called other institutions. among these other institutions, i would first start with those which, in our view, have presented the least problems between us in the committee on budgets and which, according to my information, will present the least problems with the other branch of the budgetary authority. i am referring to the court of auditors, the economic and social committee, the ombudsman, the european data protection supervisor and the european external action service, for which we have taken over the proposals originally put forward by the commission, because we have found them, after examination, to be fully justified. there are, however, some minor exceptions: one - very limited - in favour of the committee of the regions of a few tens of thousands of euros and the other, of a larger scale, in favour of the court of justice of the european union, whose ability to give judgment within a reasonable time would be, in our view, jeopardised by the blind application of cuts in support and translation staff. i now turn to the european parliament's budget itself. and although i know that a number of colleagues will find it difficult to believe me on this point, i consider that this is a budget of rigour and reform that we have the honour of putting before parliament. since the beginning of its work, the committee on budgets has accepted, on my proposal, to provide an exceptional envelope of eur 15 000. the sole purpose of this envelope is to finance urgent and necessary measures in the field of security: building security first, since it is true that access to buildings, mainly in brussels, has shown its deficiency; the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the future of the european union's information technology policy. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the budget and the implementation of the budgetary procedure. this limited increase is all the more significant because we have had to take account of the very recent creation of a new political group, which has led to requests for additional temporary posts and a significant increase in expenditure, which has been offset by other factors. to those who might be tempted to believe - and i know there are some - that this increase is still too high in the present context of budgetary restrictions, i would like to remind you of two realities: the first is that before presenting the european parliament's budget to the plenary, the committee on budgets must reach an agreement with the bureau of the european parliament, a body in which budgetary concerns are not necessarily a priority. the second reality is that despite this constraint, the committee on budgets has managed to reduce the requests initially approved by the bureau by more than eur 18 million. i should like to add, and this is not without significance, that at the instigation of the committee on budgets - and this is a point on which your rapporteur has worked very hard - the bureau agreed last night to a major reform of the personal assistants of members, which was known in budgetary terms as secretarial allowance - which is inadequately worded and which we propose to amend. under the old system, a member of parliament could spend all of this allowance on paying local assistants. some, in fact, had hired a large number of assistants and had not hired any accredited assistants. i thought - and i was not the only one - that in order to be able to carry out his job as legislator and monitor the executive, a member of parliament must have at least one, and preferably more, accredited assistants, that is to say, assistants who are working where parliament actually works. i thought i had six minutes. or is it only four minutes? (...) the bureau, in its decision yesterday, takes this concern into account to a large extent by allocating at least 25% of the sum made available to each member to the remuneration of accredited assistants. this means that the 25% will be frozen and not available if no accredited assistant is engaged. other provisions, which i do not have time to go into here, were approved; the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat fraud. for example, amendments to article 34 propose the application of reference thresholds to the salaries and fees of local assistants in order to limit the risk of remuneration that would be excessively different from the average of remuneration in the member state concerned. in addition, in order to better manage operating costs, proposals for amendments are under discussion in respect of parliamentary questions. this may seem marginal, but it is not marginal when we consider that since the beginning of the parliamentary term our colleagues have already asked more than 16 000 written questions and that each written question costs parliament and the commission a total of 780 euros. i am aware that certain provisions of this budget are the subject of considerable controversy. i am also aware that the negotiations which will shortly be opened with the council will be very close, particularly on the establishment plan. but i will defend with conviction and determination, together with the entire delegation of the european parliament, the choices you will make tomorrow when voting on the budgets of the other institutions.

in writing. ‒ i supported this report which provides, inter alia, for an additional €1.16 billion for migration management measures than the european commission originally proposed, in order to meet the needs of the member states which are handling the largest influxes of refugees and migrants, as well as those of non-eu countries which are hosting even more. on employment, parliament added €473 million for contracts for new programmes to help unemployed young people find work. farmers affected by the russian embargo on eu food imports and by low milk prices will also receive an additional €500 million. the european parliament also voted to allocate €1.3 billion to the european research programme horizon 2020 and the connecting europe facility (infrastructure) to repay funds borrowed from these to launch the juncker investment plan. i voted against any increase in fees and expenses for the activities of a member of the european parliament.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft eu budget for 2016, in full accordance with my group's political line, with the exception of the line on bullfighting where i rejected the amendment.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the 2016 draft budget proposed by parliament because, unlike the cuts made by the council, it provides for valuable resources to tackle the union's main challenges. economic recovery and job creation, of course - although this is primarily a matter of political choice and will - but also research and development, the migration crisis for which 800 million euros are planned, the framework for banking supervision and the development of cross-border infrastructure.
in writing. i voted for this report because it addresses some of the important problems we are facing as the eu today. the first is certainly the current migration crisis, for which more resources must be made available. the second is to support the competitiveness of our companies. it is important that we provide adequate funding for start-ups and companies that are growing. special attention should be paid to smes, as we are doing now by strengthening cosme.
in writing. ‒ with this resolution, the european parliament expresses its wish to increase the eu budget by more than eur 4 billion in 2016. the nva delegation does not share this view. it is not just the member states that must cut back, but the eu too. the n-va supports the additional expenditure in response to the migration crisis or to compensate for the efsi savings on horizon 2020 and the connecting europe facility, but considers that it should be initially placed within existing budgets before any increase in the budget can be envisaged. there are still very significant efficiency gains to be made within the current budget, for example in budget lines with a weak implementation rate or within budgets that do not provide eu added value. the nva delegation therefore voted against the joint resolution and instead supports the recommendations made in the alternative ecr resolution.
in writing. we have decided to be ambitious by providing additional funds (€4.1 billion more than the council's commitment position and €4.3 billion more than the council's payment/ordering position) in the 2016 eu budget to address the various crises facing europe. it is about meeting the needs arising from the unprecedented influx of refugees into and out of the eu, funding support for job creation for young people, improving the eu's competitiveness, etc. we therefore propose a budget of eur 157.4 billion for commitments and eur 146.4 billion for payments. the last word is not said. a conciliation procedure with the council is now under way and should lead to an agreement, which will be endorsed by the ecofin council on 23 november. we have also asked for all the flexibility instruments to be available to deal with unforeseen circumstances and therefore to have recourse to the contingency reserve if necessary.

in writing. this is a very important file. the aim is to ensure that the european court of justice can fully carry out its tasks and that it has the necessary judges. that is why we are talking about a substantial increase. i regret, however, the increase of 28 judges, whereas the ecj itself had asked for only 12 additional judges. this number is highly arbitrary and not based on a correct workload measurement as it should be.
in writing. ‒ at present, the court of justice of the european union is composed of 28 judges, one from each member state. however, the increase in the number of cases to be dealt with has resulted in an overload of work for the court and an inability to respond to cases within a reasonable time. an increase of 28 judges is therefore proposed for better functioning. i voted in favour of this doubling of the number of judges in 3 phases (12 judges in 2015, transfer of the 7 judges of the civil service tribunal in 2016, 9 additional judges in 2019) because following the quadrilogue (parliament, council, commission and court of justice) our group won on two essential elements in my opinion, namely: an analysis of the real needs of the court prior to the implementation of phases 2 and 3 of the reform as well as respect for gender parity in the appointment of new judges. it is, however, clear that this increase in the number of judges must be followed by an increase in the court's staff, in particular in the translation services, which are currently understaffed. these measures are necessary for the proper functioning of the judicial activities of the court.
in writing. between the euro crisis and the refugee crisis, this issue may seem secondary. it is actually symbolic. europe is not looking its best. the court of justice had proposed to create 12 new posts of judges. faced with the difficulty of reaching agreement between the member states, it decided to increase the number of additional judges to 28, even though judicial delays had meanwhile decreased and the court concerned did not require these judges. this major change was made without external consultation, without consultation of national parliaments, without impact assessment. the member states, who are always trying to reduce the european budget, have turned a blind eye to this unnecessary expenditure. this is the triumph of "particularist" technocracy over democracy. parliament should have refused this manifestly excessive expenditure. all over europe, public services, particularly the judiciary, are having to reduce their staff. the european parliament has already adopted a resolution on the situation in the former yugoslavia, which calls for the immediate release of all political prisoners. i regret the vote on this reform which not only abolishes the civil service tribunal but also plays into the hands of the eurosceptics.
in writing. ‒ the court of justice of the european union (cjeu) launched a legislative initiative in 2011 to amend its statute to allow the appointment of 12 additional judges to the tribunal. it relied on the need to reduce both the number of cases per judge and the duration of those cases before the court of first instance. in 2013, the court of justice reduced this request to 9 judges, a figure that was accepted by the council of the european union, the european commission and the european parliament. however, while during the previous parliamentary term, at the first reading by parliament, the number of 12 additional judges had been approved, the council did not appoint any of these 12 judges, as the member states had not reached agreement on the choice of judges. in october 2014, the court of justice therefore proposed to double the number of judges of the general court in three stages and to abolish the civil service tribunal. the council immediately accepted these new proposals, which are the subject of this report and were the subject of an overall compromise between the various political groups.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of returning to the previous proposal in the text and therefore disagree with the one presented today. it is a question of consistency between the two votes on his appointments. i have nevertheless voted in favour of the amendments in this text which advocate gender equality.
in writing. ‒ to address the backlog of judges, the european court of justice asked for 12 new judges to sit on its general court in 2011, a number it later reduced to nine. the council of justice ministers, however, failed to agree on which of the 28 eu member states should be allowed to provide an additional judge. the court of justice therefore decided to simply double the number of judges, despite the fact that the said backlog, mainly due to internal reorganisation, was largely eliminated to ± 10%. at a cost to the taxpayer of over 20 million euros a year, this is the quintessential european example of genuine waffle iron policy, and truly vindictive in times of rigid austerity. moreover, the planned abolition of the seven-judge civil service tribunal will only partially offset the costs. without a serious impact assessment, this proposal was quietly voted by the european parliament. the nva delegation therefore voted resolutely against.
in writing. ‒ the court of justice had asked for 12 additional judges because of its heavy workload. as the member states were unable to reach an agreement, the council decided to increase the number of judges by one per member state, i.e. 28. the backlog had already been reduced and the workload did not require 28 additional judges. i therefore voted for an increase of only 12 instead of 28 additional judges to reduce the workload but not to waste resources and staff. the increase to 56 judges is not a good thing for the european project and will only play into the hands of eurosceptics.
in writing. ‒ following the adoption of the european parliament (ep) position at first reading in plenary on 13 january 2015, informal negotiations have started with the latvian presidency with a view to reaching an early agreement at second reading. after two rounds of trilogue, the ep and the council reached an agreement on this dossier in march 2015. the text of the agreement was submitted to the ep's fisheries committee for a vote of approval in may 2015 and was approved by a very large majority. the european parliament's plenary session today definitively approved the council's position at first reading without any amendments.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the provisions on fisheries in the area covered by the gfcm (general fisheries commission for the mediterranean) agreement which provides an appropriate framework for multilateral cooperation to promote the development, conservation, rational management and optimum use of living marine resources in the mediterranean and the black sea at levels considered sustainable and with a low risk of depletion. we accept that derogations from the ban on trawl fishing in the black sea should be managed by the member states with the commission's oversight, but that they should not be a precedent in any future legal act.
in writing. ‒ i rejected the european commission's proposal to give member states the possibility of banning the use of imported gmos for human or animal feed. this would lead to a fragmentation of the internal market, and the absence of an impact assessment remains extremely worrying as regards the consequences of an a la carte authorisation/ban for our whole agriculture and food.
in writing. i fully support the report as presented in plenary. it rejects the commission's proposal to nationalize imports. that would be a serious infringement of the free movement of goods within the european union. it is also a measure which has no scientific basis whatsoever, but is purely a political response to the concerns about gmos in some member states. there is no difference at all (even at the cellular level) between a piece of meat from a cow that has been fed genetically modified food and a cow that has not been fed genetically modified food.
in writing. ‒ the n-va delegation voted against the european commission's proposal to allow member states to restrict or prohibit the use of genetically modified food and feed on their territory. the nva considers the new commission proposal problematic and incompatible with the better regulation agenda. it is unclear how the proposal can be implemented, monitored and enforced in practice. the proposal also threatens to fragment the european single market and may have serious consequences for international trade. the lack of an impact assessment is also problematic. the possible financial implications for the agricultural sector are not clear, but in any case the agricultural sector is likely to face considerable additional costs. for protein-rich animal feed (such as soya), europe is particularly dependent on imports from third countries where gm crops are widely grown. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of genetically modified organisms (gmos) in the food chain.
in writing. i welcome the rejection by the european parliament of the commission's proposal which provided for the possibility for member states to restrict or prohibit the use of genetically modified food and feed after they have been authorised. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work. the commission proposal would have risked fragmentation between member states and thus undermined the functioning of the internal market.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament sent a clear message to the commission on wednesday by opposing its proposal on gmos. the commission's text sought to allow any member state to restrict or prohibit the sale and use of food or feed containing eu-approved gmos on its territory. the idea may be interesting, but this text goes against the rules of free trade so dear to europe. this would be tantamount to member states taking back control of imported products at their frontiers, a practice contrary to the treaties. as rapporteur on the legislation on national bans on the cultivation of gmos negotiated earlier this year, i believe that it is nonsense to legislate the same on imports and on the cultivation of gmos. especially when you consider that europe is dependent on imported gm soybeans to feed its livestock, which cover more than 60% of european food needs. i welcome the decision by a large majority in parliament to ask the commission to come forward with another proposal which is more coherent, courageous and responsive to the needs of the european citizens.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of rejecting the commission's proposal (along with a large majority of meps: 577 votes against, 75 in favour and 38 abstentions) which is based on legislation in force since april and which would have given member states the choice of refusing to grow 8 gm seeds that have been approved by the eu or are in the process of being approved. parliament therefore opposed any nationalisation of decisions on gmos and considered the commission's proposal inapplicable in a single market without internal frontiers. for example, in the 'simple' case of belgium, flanders has traditionally tolerated gmos, unlike wallonia and brussels. the commission proposal makes it possible for a member state to decide on the use of gmos in part of its territory; the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the internal border controls in belgium are not disrupted. in fact, at present 19 member states have indicated their intention to ban genetically modified crops in part or in all of their territory. i personally regret that the commission does not dare to reject gmos on european territory, when a large majority of member states and citizens are against the exploitation of gmos.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament rejected the commission's proposal to give member states the possibility to ban the use of gmos on their territory, whether they have the option to accept it or not. this proposal, made without an impact assessment, goes against the single market, favours multinationals, but above all reflects the cowardice of the commission, which does not dare to refuse gmos on european territory when a large majority of member states and citizens are against the exploitation of genetically modified organisms. when will there be a simple majority to reject gmos, as 19 of the 28 member states and 60% of the population want?
in writing. ‒ whether one is for or against the authorisation of genetically modified organisms, i do not think that europe should have authorisation organised by member state. this would not only create unfair competition but would also require us to reintroduce controls at europe's internal borders to check whether or not certain foodstuffs or animal feeds contain gmos. i therefore voted against the european commission's proposal.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the revision of the authorisation procedure for novel foods because i believe that it does not present sufficient requirements in terms of the precautionary principle and food safety, given that the new regulation will cover, for example, nanomaterials or food derived from cloned animals.
in writing. this dossier contains a number of important elements. for example, it provides a centralised application procedure at eu level (and no longer at member state level) for so-called 'novel foods'. cloned food is now also being taken, whereas previously there was an unclear regulation on this subject which led to legal uncertainty. the processing of applications will also now be able to be handled in a shorter, more streamlined procedure.
in writing. ‒ the n-va delegation today gave the green light for the revision of legislation on novel foods. this review is important and urgent. the current legislation dates from 1997 and is no longer adapted to technological and scientific progress. a previous attempt to update the legislation failed in 2011. after almost 20 years of stagnation, it is really time for progress to benefit both our citizens and our businesses. the n-va strongly believes that the new legislation will encourage innovation. the approval procedure for new foodstuffs today takes an average of three years and is expensive. a uniform authorisation procedure that reduces administrative burdens should ensure that new foods can be brought to the market more quickly and at lower cost. this progress is important for flanders, where many companies (especially smes) are strong in the development of innovative foodstuffs. the new rules are of course without prejudice to consumer protection. the safety of the products remains paramount. the nva also welcomes the emphasis in the legislation on discouraging animal testing by applying the 3v principle (replacement, reduction, refinement).
in writing. after several years of deadlock, i am pleased that the european parliament has finally voted on the report on novel foods. it was essential that the 1997 eu legislation be updated to take account of the many new foods and changing dietary habits. i therefore welcome the fact that the authorization procedure for novel foods, now centralised at european level, is thus simplified in order to encourage innovation without compromising food safety. the introduction of traditional foods from third countries and considered safe on the european market should also be made easier. more transparency is also planned to reassure consumers. finally, animal testing in the food sector should also be reduced as duplication of testing will be avoided as soon as possible.
in writing. ‒ the proposal for a regulation on novel foods has been through a lot of bumps and bruises before it reached the plenary. after the failure of the negotiations in 2008, there was an urgent need to legislate to adapt the legal framework to the realities of today's food market. that is why i voted for the nicholson report without any additional amendments which might have ruined the fragile compromise reached with the council in june 2015. the european union is based on a comprehensive and strict regulatory framework for food safety. it must continue to promote its local products, but at the same time it must make room for new food trends and alternative sources of protein: mushrooms, algae, or even grilled insects, even if these still represent a niche market for human consumption. this variety of products is an undeniable plus for the european consumer. the new european legislation provides a framework for these new foods and provides safeguards in terms of food ethics, which i welcome. i am thinking of the inclusion of food derived from cloned animals in the legislative field and the necessary limitation of animal testing.
in writing. ‒ in this report i supported several amendments calling for the following information to be given to consumers when food from cloned animals and their offspring is placed on the market and marketed in the union, including imports, until the entry into force of specific legislation on food from cloned animals and their offspring: 'food from cloned animals'.
in writing. - i voted against the report on novel foods. it is not that i have anything against new food, far from it, but i cannot understand why in this text it is proposed that parliament no longer has a say or any power over the acceptance of the next products. it is in this sense that my decision is motivated and is expressed in a negative vote.
in writing. ‒ after a long road, a delicate balance/compromise has been reached with the council to adapt the legal framework to the realities of the current food market. the european union must continue to promote local products, to safeguard food safety and to provide opportunities for new food products to appear on the market. this balance is my approval.
in writing. ‒ knowing that 90% of europeans living in cities are exposed to pollution levels harmful to human health, i supported this resolution which favours strict and binding targets for the limitation of toxic emissions for 2025 and 2030. the proposals include the limitation of six toxic pollutants, the agricultural sector being also concerned.
in writing. i supported the agreement on this dossier. in view of the damage caused to the environment and to human health by the emission of pollutants, i believe it is important that this problem be tackled. we have taken an ambitious but realistic approach, including an exception for cows grazing outside.
in writing. ‒ air pollution remains a huge problem and requires a cross-border approach. the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat air pollution. the impact of air pollution on vulnerable groups, especially children, requires our absolute priority. the updating and extension of the nec directive is an opportunity to address this challenge. the nva delegation shares the analysis of the rapporteur and the european commission that we need to show ambition, mainly by tightening up the standards per member state for six of the most polluting substances by 2030, by setting binding interim targets by 2025 and by tackling pollution at source. the rapid introduction of real driving emissions tests in the automotive sector is also fundamental in this respect. we don't have time to waste. in order to make rapid and real progress possible, our proposals must also be realistic, based on figures and technologically feasible. after all, clean air is not achieved by riding aerial bicycles or by building aerial castles. the nva is pleased that a majority of parliament today is choosing responsible policies which offer the best guarantees in the interests of our health, well-being and prosperity.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european commission's proposals to set new emission ceilings for 6 key air pollutants, including nox, particulate matter and sulphur dioxide. i voted against an amendment to remove enteric methane from the list. i felt justified in not forcing the agricultural sector, which has already made considerable progress in this area and is going through a very difficult period, to respect objectives which, in the opinion of many experts, were neither realistic nor achievable. i have supported the vast majority of the other commission proposals because air pollution has enormous human and economic costs. in 2010, it caused more than 400 000 premature deaths in the european union. air pollution also damages the environment and knows no boundaries. the total costs are in the range of eur 330-940 billion per year, of which eur 4 billion in the healthcare sector.
in writing. i welcome the adoption by the european parliament of the report on emissions of certain air pollutants, which aims to revise the 2003 directive. the union intends to tackle the problem of air pollution. the text provides for emission ceilings for six major air pollutants, including sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, ammonia and methane. as regards enteric methane (produced by ruminants), i voted in favour of removing it from the scope of the text in order to avoid imposing an additional burden on farmers and to take account of the specificities and rules of the sector and the progress already made.
in writing. ‒ i voted this afternoon in favour of ambitious legislation on air quality. not because the paris climate summit is on the horizon, but because air pollution is responsible for 400 000 premature deaths in the eu every year. more specifically, i supported binding targets for six gases which are particularly harmful to the environment and/or human health: ammonia, fine particulate matter, nox, so2, vocs and methane. for the latter gas, which is bad for the ozone layer, i took account of the difficulty for the agricultural sector to comply with the most ambitious standards. that is why i strongly and convincingly supported amendment no 33, which provides for the exclusion of enteric methane from the scope of this directive. this will allow the herds to continue to graze in peace in the meadows. the opposite would have been harmful to cattle farming, which is adapting to the new rules laid down by the cap: the application of the third pillar, the so-called 'greening' pillar. but it is essential to do more about the invisible killer of air pollution, which kills ten times as many people each year as road accidents.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the vote on this report, which has led the european parliament to vote in favour of emission ceilings for pollutants which must be much stricter to combat air pollution. the report adopted reinforces the emission ceilings for certain pollutants that are hazardous to health for 2020-2030. air pollution causes some 400 000 premature deaths in the eu each year. the member states have committed themselves to tackling this situation, but they are not keeping their commitments. it is therefore a good thing that parliament has chosen to strengthen the european commission's proposal by tightening up the standards for six pollutants. basically, the ceilings must continue to be lowered by 2030 for sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxide, ammonia, methane, volatile organic compounds other than methane, fine particulate matter and ammonia. the european parliament has introduced binding interim targets to be met by 2025 and will have to negotiate with the member states to reach an agreement in the coming months.
in writing. ‒ europe must be at the forefront of the fight against climate change. we want a just transition to a sustainable, low-carbon economy. today we spend the equivalent of a planet and a half a year of resources. the future of our planet is in danger. the text voted today goes in that direction and sets limits for the emission of pollutants into the air for the member states of europe. this is thousands of tonnes of fine particulate matter, ammonia, nitrogen dioxide, sulphur and so on. i would remind you that poor air quality is responsible for more than 400 000 premature deaths each year and its economic cost to health is estimated at between €300 and €900 billion each year. 90% of europeans living in cities are exposed to pollution levels considered to be dangerous. a real change of course is needed! i have also made a very important point, namely that i voted in favour of excluding enteric methane. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's agricultural policy is not disrupted by the introduction of new technologies.
in writing. ‒ we must not forget that our own farmers produce food of the highest quality in a highly regulated environment. if we were to tighten the emission standards for methane and ammonia without scientific research into how this could be possible, we would force our agriculture to operate from outside the eu or go bankrupt. i voted for the survival of european agriculture and for cleaner air.
in writing. ‒ even if the european citizens' initiative were to function perfectly, it cannot be expected to solve the democratic deficit that is characteristic of this european union. i support the principle of the european citizens' initiative, not because of the so-called idea of european integration, but because it can be a means of drawing the attention of the european commission and the elected representatives of the european parliament to certain themes and major or minor social problems. the schöpflin report states that the success of the european citizens' initiative is being undermined by all kinds of practical obstacles. this involves placing the finger on the wound. our group therefore calls not only for the removal of these obstacles or for the user-friendliness of the initiative instrument, but also for an obligation on the commission to follow up a successful european citizens' initiative with an appropriate legislative proposal. we have therefore amended the report, but at the same time we support it.
in writing. ‒ the s&d group played a leading role in launching the european citizens' initiative, which allows european citizens to directly influence the democratic process. this initiative is a step forward for direct democracy, public participation and involvement in the european debate. three years after the entry into force of this new instrument, it seems appropriate to evaluate its implementation in order to identify any shortcomings. i supported the own-initiative report of the committee on constitutional affairs calling on the european commission and the member states to improve the eci in order to ensure its effectiveness and attractiveness for citizens.
in writing. the citizens' initiative is a good tool to involve citizens more in european policy-making. this resolution recognises this and proposes a number of adjustments to improve this instrument. this will make it easier to collect signatures, give the initiative more visibility and improve the provision of information to the organisers.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which underlines that the european citizens' initiative (eci) is the first transnational participatory democracy instrument which gives citizens the opportunity to engage directly with the european institutions and to actively participate in the development of european policies. the resolution also stresses that a dedicated office for ecis could also raise public awareness of these initiatives. indeed, since 2012, only three of the 31 registered ecis have reached the final stage. the report also calls for the establishment of a european network of national authorities responsible for the protection of the environment.
in writing. ‒ this report strengthens the european citizens' initiative (eci) as an instrument for political participation by citizens. since the lisbon treaty, there has been a legal framework for the european citizens' initiative, but various reactions from citizens' movements point to its ineffectiveness. the aim of this report is therefore to improve the ebi mechanism to make it more user-friendly and to remove certain obstacles for organisers and initiators. we greens would like to see the european commission and the european parliament give more effect to successful citizens' initiatives. that is why we tabled three amendments to ensure that. firstly, there is no clear obligation for the commission to respond to a successful citizens' initiative with a legislative proposal. the first amendment therefore proposes that the commission should respond within 12 months. secondly, parliament must be able to come up with a legislative initiative report if the commission fails in the above proposal. thirdly, citizens' initiatives which challenge primary legislation of the european union must also be allowed, which has been difficult so far. unfortunately, all these amendments were rejected, hence our abstention in the final vote.
in writing. ‒ the european citizens' initiative (eci) has its origins in the convention and was designed to give the european citizen the opportunity to participate in the launching of legislative initiatives. the original idea was therefore that once in place, this instrument would make it possible to mobilise civil society more and to strengthen european citizenship, particularly at transnational level. the commission has also been asked to provide information on the implementation of the eic in the member states and to provide information on the implementation of the eic in the union. the commission report lists 51 initiatives (com (2015) 145). this report seeks to improve the functioning of the eic to make it more user-friendly and to remove some of the obstacles that have proved to be a source of difficulty for eic organisers. the commission should undertake a thorough review of the eic in 2016 and parliament's opinion on this instrument will have weight because it will reflect, first and foremost, the view of the grassroots, that of the citizens who have tried to use the eic.
in writing. ‒ the resolution i have approved supports the development of a macro-regional strategy for the adriatic and ionian region, as this new model of multi-level governance, in which the regions are increasingly interested, offers considerable benefits. in this report, parliament takes stock of the benefits that the region could derive, in particular the protection of its marine, coastal and terrestrial ecosystems and blue growth, highlighting the immense potential of the region in terms of blue jobs and sustainable and innovative economic development and growth, due to its exceptional geographical position and specific coastal structure. it also noted the positive impact of the strategy on the development of sustainable and competitive tourism, which is of crucial importance for the european economy and the development of social cohesion within the union.
the events following the break-up of yugoslavia have placed a devastating and long-term mortgage on the economic development and cooperation between the countries of the adriatic and ionian region. in recent years, the region has also been hit hard by the economic crisis. the eu's third macro-regional strategy has chosen a plan of action to ensure that these countries can finally put their political and economic problems behind them through targeted cooperation. as the area plays an important role in strengthening the geographical continuity in europe, strategic and smart investments are needed for the whole region. at the same time, this region has enormous potential, which can only be exploited if all the countries in the region work together. the strategic investment funds that the eu has are providing the necessary investment in energy networks between countries, the elimination of 'missing links' in infrastructure, innovations in shipping and fisheries and the development of the region's tourist assets. eusair also enables the non-eu countries of the western balkans to cooperate with eu member states.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the jakovcic report on an eu strategy for the adriatic and ionian region. this vote is a welcome to the commission communication on the european union strategy for the region. first, it is important that this region focuses on blue growth. it has a remarkable geographical position and a very rich marine biodiversity. these two factors represent a huge potential for the creation of blue jobs. secondly, it is necessary to improve transport networks and the distribution of energy between the countries participating in this macro-regional strategy and also between them and their other neighbours. finally, it is also important to preserve the quality of the environment in this region, as the adriatic sea is home to almost half of all marine species recorded in the mediterranean.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the text. the strategy is timely for two reasons, both linked to the political changes in the union. firstly, the juncker commission decided to focus its policy on investment, through the investment plan and the resulting european fund for strategic investments. the countries of the adriatic and ionian region therefore have a good opportunity to make up for the investment shortfall they have experienced in recent years. the strategy offers opportunities to target these investments in a way that delivers results for the benefit of the whole region. secondly, the commission has repeatedly stated that there will be no further enlargement in the near future. while this is bad news for the western balkan countries, the strategy will bring them closer to the union by aligning their policies and working closely with the member states.
in writing. ‒ i have endorsed this resolution which underlines the importance of cohesion policy for many member states, particularly in terms of investment in times of crisis, in the implementation of the europe 2020 strategy. it is a comprehensive strategy for sustainable growth and jobs, centred on the key objectives of employment, innovation, climate change and energy sustainability, education and the fight against poverty and social exclusion. at the same time, the resolution also stresses that these objectives can be furthered by progress in gender equality.
in writing. ‒ this report dealt with an important policy pursued by the european union, namely cohesion policy. this policy, a key instrument for implementing the europe 2020 strategy, aims to reduce regional disparities and promote convergence. it has a budget of €351.8 billion for 2020. by voting for this report, i support the definition of thematic objectives that will make it possible to maximise the effectiveness of this policy. this report also covered the europe 2020 strategy for which the commission launched the review process in 2014. the report makes a number of recommendations for the mid-term review of the strategy. in the future, the future cohesion policy and the future long-term strategy of the union must be drawn up before the end of the current commission's mandate. the european parliament elections will take place in 2019, which imposes timetable constraints. in line with all these remarks, i have decided to vote in favour of this report.

on behalf of the alde group.– mr president, this debate tonight may not be the fiercest that we will see here in this parliament today, but i think that with this file we are creating more financial stability in a very important market for our european economy. securities financing transactions (sfts) play an important role in financial markets and the financing of our economy. i would like to congratulate the negotiating team for its very balanced approach. by a balanced approach i mean that the result has considered all sft stakeholders, whilst achieving financial stability. at the end of the day, we wanted to ensure that the reporting is actually being used and is useful for its intended purpose. the proposed regulation delivers binding transparency and reporting requirements in three key areas. first, all securities financing transactions have to be reported to trade repositories, and here the burden for non-financial parties, such as smes, was reduced by allowing their financial counterparties to do the reporting for them. second, we have ensured transparency towards investors. funds have to inform investors of their sft activities in the prospectus, and this will enable them to assess the risk as part of their investment decisions. third, the report addresses transparency around re-use of assets. parties have a responsibility to communicate the risks and consequences in the event of a default. assets can only be reused within certain parameters and with prior consent, except for title transfer collateral arrangements (ttcas) where the legal title has already been transferred. another important point is that we came up with a realistic implementation timeframe. we wanted to avoid the mistakes that we have seen with the implementation of emir and we rectified some of the shortcomings. all parties should now have sufficient time to implement the necessary requirements. to conclude, i believe that we have come up with a very balanced approach. we have created transparency in a difficult and technical market, both towards supervisors and investors with a minimal burden for all the stakeholders. therefore, i hope that members can join me in voting in favour tomorrow.

in writing. ‒ due to the economic crisis, long-term unemployment has doubled since 2007 and now accounts for half of total unemployment, or more than 12 million people. in 2014, more than 60% of the long-term unemployed had been out of work for at least two consecutive years. these figures are highly worrying as longterm unemployment is driving people away from the labour market due to the erosion of their skills and professional networks. i therefore fully support the resolution of the employment committee on the council recommendation on the integration of the longterm unemployed into the labour market. the resolution is based on three main objectives: to significantly improve the registration of the longterm unemployed with an employment service so that they are all taken into account; assess the individual potential, needs and preferences of the longterm unemployed before they reach 18 months of unemployment; propose a comprehensible, balanced and adapted vocational integration agreement between the long-term unemployed and the services concerned at the latest when the person concerned has been unemployed for 18 months.
in writing. as the economic climate is gradually improving, it is time to look at how we can reactivate the longterm unemployed in the european union. some of the focuses are on increasing training and the use of targeted activation policies. the longterm unemployed must also be able to find employment elsewhere, and so retraining becomes very important in order to continue to use this human capital. this will benefit society as a whole.
since the economic crisis of 2007, longterm unemployment in europe has doubled. 60% of the unemployed have to go more than two years without earning an income from a job. as the period of unemployment continues, not only are work-related skills and competences lost, but the risk of social exclusion and poverty also increases. the recovery in the economy has not yet had a positive effect on structural unemployment. the commission has also proposed that the member states should take measures to ensure that the longterm unemployed are not displaced from their jobs. firstly, employment services and all the labour market partners involved should not wait for people to be longterm unemployed to prepare them for re-entry into the labour market. the earlier the return to the labour market is started, the greater the chances of finding a new job. in addition, the basis for a successful counselling project for the unemployed will always be to provide the unemployed with new skills and competences adapted to the rapidly changing requirements of the labour market. the better the preparation of the unemployed, and in particular the longterm unemployed, for the modern labour market, the greater the chances of finding a permanent job.
in writing. ‒ i supported the text and the three main measures in the proposal: i) significantly improve the registration of longterm unemployed with an employment service so that they are all taken into account; ii) assess the individual potential, needs and preferences of longterm unemployed before they reach 18 months of unemployment; (iii) to propose a comprehensible, balanced and adapted vocational integration agreement between the longterm unemployed and the services concerned at the latest when the person concerned has been unemployed for 18 months; the individual assessment should take place before the person reaches 12 months of unemployment so that the vocational integration agreement can be put in place before the person reaches 18 months of unemployment; the three-step approach should include non-governmental actors, such as social ngos working with the longterm unemployed, in the overall process, where appropriate.
in writing. ‒ i have approved this resolution in which the european parliament votes in favour of legislation setting the guidelines for the use of civil drones. this should include training of users with information on privacy and personal data protection. aircraft should be equipped with detection and avoidance technology in order not to jeopardise the safety of manned aircraft and to take into account densely populated areas and no-fly zones such as airports. similarly, the use of drone systems by law enforcement and intelligence services should obviously respect the fundamental rights to privacy, data protection, free movement and freedom of expression. finally, the competent data protection authorities in the member states should share the specific data protection guidelines for drones used for commercial purposes.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the safe use of drones in civil aviation. commercial use is increasing and recreational use is becoming more popular. the resolution stresses that drones have the potential to stimulate economic growth and job creation but calls for all guarantees relating to privacy and data protection, including mandatory registration of drones and their equipment with identification chips. this is to facilitate accident investigations and the arrest of criminals who use them illegally. the commission should support research into 'detection and avoidance' technologies to enable drones to avoid collisions with other airspace users. it is also necessary to develop and use 'geotargeting' technologies to prevent drones from flying over no-fly zones, such as airports and nuclear power stations. the resolution also supports the rules proposed by the commission to help national authorities and other qualified bodies manage validation and surveillance activities in cross-border sales of drones and the provision of services.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament adopted a report calling for the adoption of a european framework legislation on the safe use of remotely piloted aircraft systems, more commonly known as drones. these small flying machines, which are becoming increasingly popular, are currently outside the scope of harmonised legislation at european level. in view of the increasing use of drones by individuals, whether for recreational purposes or for misuse, there is a growing need to ensure that drones do not pose a threat to public safety or privacy. the aim is to integrate drones into european airspace by using technological means: installing an identification chip that would help trace the wrongful owner, incorporating detection and avoidance software to avoid accidents or adding a geo-location program that would prevent drones from flying over no-fly zones. this would allow the safe and secure development of this booming sector, whose cross-border trade is hampered by the lack of mutual recognition of national authorisations for drones and their operators. the commission said it was preparing a legislative proposal which should be adopted by the end of 2015.
in writing. ‒ rpas are now becoming a reality and will soon be available on the european market. the rpas market, which represents an opportunity to foster new job creation, is a source of innovation and economic growth for the years to come. but it also raises new challenges in terms of safety, security and respect for citizens' rights, which must be addressed before rpas can be used on a reasonable scale in a civilian context. the absence of harmonised regulations in europe and of validated technologies is the main obstacle to the opening of the rpas market today. regulation at european level covering all relevant issues, including safety, security, privacy and data protection requirements, is therefore necessary. in addition, r&d efforts are also required to ensure the gradual integration of rpas into civil aviation from 2016. in this respect, it should be noted that the european commission will use the horizon 2020 programme to support meaningful r & d actions.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament voted this afternoon in favour of european legislation on the use of drones. with 2 500 operators, europe dominates the world market for civil use. this technology, originally used mainly for military purposes, is now open to all, pushing the limits of existing legislation. to ensure the safety of citizens, respect for privacy and coherence between member states, while encouraging innovative technologies, european legislation is indispensable!
