in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the provisions proposed by my distinguished colleague, mrs de monte. tourism is a key sector of the european economy with growth potential and generates more than 10% of the union's gdp if tourism-related sectors are included. tourism is also an important driver of employment, directly employing 13 million workers, representing at least 12% of employment in the union.
in writing. ‒ the n-va voted against this resolution today because of the far-reaching measures. the tourism sector is in danger of being saddled with many new rules. in addition, the principle of subsidiarity is not respected. tourism policy is largely a matter for the member states and the regions. this is barely mentioned in the resolution. the tourism sector is one of the most important economic sectors in the european union. the sector is often dominated by small family businesses or smes. we must give these companies every opportunity and not bury them under administrative obligations. unfortunately, the resolution does not strike the right balance between support for an important sector and all sorts of unnecessary things. the sector does not need a new tourism agency, the sector does not need a new european budget line, the sector does not need another label. the n-va wants to give the tourism sector all the support it can get, but we do not believe that this can be done by additional european regulatory pressure. it is a missed opportunity for this resolution to fall into the old habit of centralized european bureaucracy.
in writing. ‒ the tragedies of malaysia airlines flight 370 and air france flight 447 have shown the limitations of current air navigation systems, which have not been able to identify and locate aircraft in distress in a timely manner. as a result, search, rescue and recovery operations have been seriously hampered. flight tracking systems can only cover 30% of the airspace at present. the public's confidence in air transport must be maintained through the use of advanced technologies. the satellite tracking system is one of them. it would enable public authorities, air navigation service providers and airlines in europe and the rest of the world to strengthen and increase the efficiency of air traffic management and to significantly improve aviation safety.
in writing. i welcome the adoption by the european parliament of a resolution on the development of technology for the creation of a global airplane tracking system. this technology, which uses satellites, is designed to allow aircraft to be located at any time and in any place on the globe. in view of the recent tragedies of missing aircraft, the development of such technology is essential to facilitate search and rescue operations. it should also make it possible to provide rapid answers to the families of those on board missing or crashed aircraft. the european parliament therefore favours the development of such technology and asks the commission to fix the frequencies to be used, in order to avoid any interference. i am pleased that the development of this technology may eventually make it possible to locate public transport aircraft even when they are flying over remote or desert areas. in view of the current situation, it is more important than ever to make aviation safety a priority. i therefore welcome and support the union's action to ensure ever greater safety for travellers.
in writing. ‒ the tragedies of air france flight af447 in june 2009 and malaysia airlines flight mh370 in march 2014 have highlighted the need for new systems to locate aircraft at all times. such global air traffic management surveillance systems would make it easier to locate an aircraft in the event of abnormal behaviour, an emergency or an accident. the european commission, in cooperation with the european aviation safety agency (easa) and the international civil aviation organization (icao), has started to examine the various technical options based on their performance, and has proposed rules on aircraft tracking. the text of the resolution i voted on today supports the commission's efforts to rapidly develop a global, results-based flight tracking system that allows air navigation service providers to locate aircraft and calls on the commission to take the necessary steps ahead of the world radiocommunication conference in geneva in november 2015 to support the future development of a global satellite flight tracking system.
in writing. ‒ the tragedies of air france flight af447 (1 june 2009) and malaysia airlines flight mh370 (8 march 2014) have highlighted the need for new systems to locate public transport aircraft at all times, even in remote locations. such surveillance systems in the field of global air traffic management would facilitate the tracking of an aircraft in the event of abnormal behaviour, an emergency or an accident.

for the greens/efa group mr president, welcome to the house, mr vice-president dombrovskis, i have listened to you very attentively. i don't hear much new in your speech, but if i listen to the faint signals, i hear the adjective or the noun "social" repeatedly. and i'm curious to know what's in the fall package. since you are talking about this and your boss wants the european union to be awarded a triple a rating for its social policy - and we are far from that - i would like to make a few suggestions. the results of the fight against poverty - as you have noted - are not very encouraging. but when it comes to fighting inequality, you have tools available to you in the semester. today, you say that we must continue to deregulate the labour markets, because we are finally allowing those who are excluded from the labour market to enter it more easily. but the result is that those who have jobs see their working conditions, both paid and unpaid, deteriorating simply because of greater competition between workers. what you could do instead is decide to focus your recommendations on tax instruments, because the tax instrument is the first redistributive instrument. if you really want to fight poverty effectively, perhaps this is the direction to take. do not tell me that tax policy is not a competence of the european union, because i have already seen in many country-specific recommendations recommendations on the tax system. so instead of focusing on competition in the labour market, you could say: 'i do encourage member states to introduce a tax shift from labour income to other forms of income', but you have to be careful because if you say 'from labour income to vat', it is again the weaker classes in society who suffer. so perhaps you could emphasize the issue of progressive taxation. we have been seeing a reduction in the progressivity of income tax in europe for decades. perhaps there is something to be done on this side which would at least enable you to recommend to the member states greater social justice. the same is true of competitiveness, which is not a bad word! i heard you talking about reviving the investment. the two areas where investment is absolutely necessary if we are to be competitive are energy efficiency and resource efficiency - in other words, for the same unit of gross domestic product, we should consume both less energy and fewer resources than our competitors. it is a question of greater independence for europe, which is known to be poor in resources and energy, but also a condition for competitiveness. it would be good to have this in your recommendations, since the european commission talks a lot about the circular economy, but i haven't seen much action yet. i would like to end with two specific countries, i have one minute left. firstly, germany: the barroso ii commission had once again protected germany by preventing excessive surpluses from being really targeted by the macroeconomic imbalance procedure. where are we today? the ifo forecast of 8.4% in terms of germany's trade surpluses. i hope that the macroeconomic imbalance procedure will point to the inadequacy of german domestic demand and ask germany to balance its balance of payments once and for all. a surplus of 8.4% is completely nonsensical from a macroeconomic point of view. secondly, i would like to say a few words about greece, first of all to our colleagues. i think it is important, in terms of democratic legitimacy, that our parliament closely follows what is happening in the implementation of the assistance programme for greece. and i think we need to stop procrastinating. we have an economic and monetary committee, an employment committee and a regi committee. let us gather them together and convene - i have no other word - not only the european commission, but also the eurogroup, the european stability mechanism and greece so that we can judge for ourselves the current challenges in the implementation of the plan.

in writing. ‒ i supported this report which is in favour of enhancing interoperability for public administrations, businesses and individuals in europe in the continuation of the efforts made by the commission since 1995 to promote the exchange of data between administrations. interoperability can enhance the quality of public services, the competitiveness of businesses and the service to individuals.
in writing. this report reinforces efforts to improve interoperability between administrations. in the digital age and in an increasingly united europe, it is essential for administrations to make the interaction between administrations, businesses and individuals efficient, both at national and european level. in addition to lowering costs, interoperability will improve the quality of service and thus boost our society. the isa 2 programme proposes a series of measures which will enable us to better meet a major challenge facing all our member states.
in writing. ‒ with the isa programme coming to an end on 31 december 2015, a new eu programme for interoperability solutions for public administrations, businesses and individuals in europe was needed. the decision, which i supported, proposes here to establish, for the period 2016-2020, a programme on interoperability solutions for public administrations, businesses and individuals in europe (the 'isa2 programme'). the specific objectives are to: improve, exploit and reuse existing cross-border or cross-sector interoperability solutions; developing, exploiting and reusing new cross-border or cross-sectoral interoperability solutions; assess the ict implications of proposed or adopted union legislation and identify areas where new legislation could promote interoperability; to create a european interoperability reference architecture (eir) as a tool for developing and evaluating interoperability solutions; create an instrument to facilitate the re-use of existing interoperability solutions and identify areas where such solutions are still lacking; evaluate and promote existing and develop new common specifications and standards and establish a mechanism to measure and quantify the benefits of interoperability solutions.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council establishing a programme on interoperability solutions for public administrations, businesses and individuals in europe (isa 2) because it is part of the continuation of the efforts in this field, in particular the isa (interoperability solutions for european public administrations) programme still in force, but at the same time opens a new cycle which cannot fail to take into account technological developments, the new needs of administrations and civil society and the new possibilities offered by cloud computing. the isa 2 will complete the digital single market and contribute to the implementation of an ambitious european digital strategy by acting as a global driver.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal because the new programme allows for crossborder and cross-sectoral interaction between european public services. the new isa2 programme will eventually lead to a harmonised interoperability landscape within europe, which will save costs and time in the long term. the proposal will also contribute to the creation of a digital single market within the european union. i also welcome the fact that the new isa2 programme is now also aimed at businesses and citizens and not just at public services. this will require the commission to respond more to the needs of civil society when drawing up this programme, or, in other words, to take account of the demand side as well as the supply side.
in writing. ‒ i supported this resolution of the parliament which aims, in general, to make the european elections more attractive. it proposes, in particular, to improve the visibility of european political parties by displaying their names and logos on ballot papers, on electoral material and in election programmes. it also proposes setting a common deadline of 12 weeks before the european elections for the nomination of leading candidates by european political parties so as to allow them to present their electoral programmes and organise the political debates between the candidates. the resolution also stresses the need for better representation of women in european elections and for the vote of european citizens residing in another eu country to be encouraged.
in writing. the organisation of european elections still varies widely between member states. although the principles for this have been laid down in european legislation, the procedure and practical organisation are largely determined by the member states. the european parliament therefore adopted a legislative initiative with recommendations to harmonise the european elections, to make them less national and to involve citizens more closely in the process. in order to enhance the visibility of the european project, it is recommended that a federal european electoral district be introduced alongside the european 'national' lists. this will enable all citizens, wherever they live, to vote for their candidate for president of the european commission. i also support the idea of harmonizing the distribution of seats and the voting age, of launching the campaign in all countries at the same time and of ensuring that the european elections take place on the same day everywhere. equal representation of men and women on the electoral roll or the right to vote for citizens living abroad, principles which i introduced in belgium as minister for institutional reform, are now incorporated in the european electoral law.

mr president, the question of china's market economy status is being debated, as we have seen tonight. it would have a major impact on employment in our economy, particularly because china has a clearly aggressive trade policy. these fears are particularly acute in the steel sector, where employers and unions share the same view. china is not a market economy, it is flooding our market with steel products at prices that do not respect the principles of fair competition. recognising it as such would therefore be detrimental to hundreds of thousands of direct and indirect jobs and, more generally, to our economy as a whole. in order to be recognised as a market economy in the european union, china must comply with five technical criteria, but these are far from being met. we must defend the values of our socially regulated market economy and not grant that status to china. it is a question of the vitality and future of our economy, but above all of our industry and its jobs.
the energy union is a particularly good initiative for me to finally start working on a single european energy market. we all know that the 28 small national networks, the 28 separate national regulators and the different forms of energy policy adopted in 28 countries are no longer sustainable. a real european energy strategy presupposes that we at least try to work together and not make decisions which affect others without discussing the consequences with each other. i am therefore very pleased and can only applaud the fact that you are also ensuring systematic follow-up with this state of the energy union. it is particularly important to me that we work quickly towards clearly measurable objectives. a european regulator to follow that, an open and transparent market in which free competition can play and the stronger interconnection of our networks to make that market possible. investment security is crucial, because we must act quickly to improve this connectivity and certainly projects of common interest, such as the nemo project between belgium and the united kingdom, must be given priority. it is clear that, as with migration policy or economic policy, we really need a european approach. we have to stop the shredding. this is the only way for consumers and businesses to benefit from affordable, secure and sustainable energy in the long term.
do we want to meet the climate targets? do we want green energy? do we want to be energy independent? i think the answer is: loud and clear three times yes. but we must also be realistic. so let us not use this mid-term review to beat ourselves up. we need an ambitious but above all a realistic policy. my region, flanders, is doing well, but there are also limits to our small and densely populated region. our potential is at sea. but offshore wind energy is very expensive. who's gonna pay for that? are we going to pass the bill back to the consumer? eurorealism also means knowing how to choose the right priorities. first things first. the commission will also continue to monitor the implementation of the union's energy policy in the light of the new energy market developments.

in writing. ‒ as a member of the european parliament's committee on the internal market and consumer protection (imco), i welcome the new directive on insurance mediation adopted by the plenary, which is due to enter into force at the end of 2017, particularly as it will better protect against misrepresentation in this partly very complex area, make the insurance business more transparent and raise the level of consumer protection overall. the aim is to provide european consumers with better information, advice and the ability to compare different insurance products more easily. the latter is to be achieved, inter alia, by means of standardised information sheets. however, in order to avoid unnecessary confusion for consumers and for reasons of equal treatment, the new rules will apply not only to insurance companies and insurance brokers but to all companies selling insurance, including, for example, travel agencies and car rental companies.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament has just voted on an updated legislation in the field of insurance. from now on, when people buy insurance, they will be better informed, better protected. measures are also provided for insurance distributors and sales staff to respond more effectively to customer needs. insurance distributors will be required to register with a competent authority in their home member state. in addition, regular training and updating of sales staff will be required. continuing vocational training of at least 200 hours over five years should also be provided for. this amendment is a real step forward in this area and i fully support it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of strengthening european provisions on information and advice offered by insurance salesmen. it seems to me that it is essential to simplify and also make insurance contracts more secure by introducing new information and consumer protection requirements which are the same for all insurance distribution channels. i am particularly in favour of the requirement to provide purchasers of insurance contracts with all information concerning the nature of the distributor's remuneration and, for certain complex life insurance products, the total cost of the insurance contract, including the costs of advice and services. it seems to me essential that, before signing a non-life insurance contract, policyholders receive, in clear and plain language, a product information document containing standard information on the type of insurance, the obligations attached to the contracts, the insured and excluded risks, and the means of payment and premiums.
in writing. i am pleased that the european parliament has adopted this directive which aims to ensure fair competition in insurance products and to strengthen consumer rights. in this sensitive sector, it was important to require insurance distributors to register with a competent authority in their home member state. moreover, given the complexity of certain insurance products, it was essential that consumers have clear information on the total costs of insurance contracts. in the same vein, they should also receive a clear and simple document informing them about the product before they sign a contract.
in writing. ‒ at this plenary session of the european parliament, i was asked to give my opinion on the supplementary report on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on insurance intermediation. the aim was to update the legislation on insurance to better regulate these professions and to better protect customers. among these changes, there is a simple, standardised and free pre-contractual information on the types of insurance contracts, which should be provided to customers in order to enable them to understand the nature and risks of the insurance-based investment product offered to them; an obligation for insurance and reinsurance intermediaries and intermediaries carrying on insurance intermediation on an ancillary basis to register with a competent authority in their home member state; an obligation for such intermediaries to be covered by professional indemnity insurance covering liability resulting from professional misconduct. many other regulatory obligations are imposed on these professions and protect the clients. in agreement with this reinforcement of the rules, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament has just voted on an updated legislation in the field of insurance. from now on, when people buy insurance, they will be better informed, better protected. measures are also provided for insurance distributors and sales staff to respond more effectively to customer needs. insurance distributors will be required to register; such registration shall be carried out with a competent authority in their member state of origin. in addition, regular and up-to-date training should be provided for sales staff. continuing vocational training of at least 200 hours over 5 years should also be provided for. as regards the benefits to the customer, citizens who subscribe to an insurance product will have to be informed of the total costs of the contract. they will also receive, before the conclusion of the agreement, standard, clear, comprehensible and free information on the type of insurance, the obligations linked to the contracts, the insured and excluded risks, as well as the means of payment and premiums.

in writing. the eu solidarity fund is, as its name suggests, not just a technical tool but an act of solidarity towards disaster-stricken regions in the member states and developing countries. it is a strong political signal that europe is much more than an international organisation with distant institutions, it is a project of living together. our world is translating the interdependence of all into a necessary solidarity. our main challenge in a globalised world is that of unity, of humanity, that is to say, being able to live in solidarity with all peoples. i welcome the fact that the proposal for a decision of the parliament and the council mobilises a maximum annual ceiling of eur 500 million for the period 2014-2020 and that the fund can be mobilised up to eur 50 million in payment and commitment appropriations for the purpose of the rapid and efficient disbursement of disaster advances in the following year.
in writing. ‒ the european union solidarity fund (eusf) is intended to enable the union to respond to emergency situations caused by large-scale natural disasters and to express europe's solidarity with the european regions affected. the fund thus has the capacity to provide financial assistance to member states and accession countries in the event of a 'major natural disaster', i.e. if the total amount of direct damage caused by the disaster exceeds eur 3 billion or 0.6% of the country's gross national income. it can also be mobilised in the event of a regional disaster. the conditions governing the mobilisation of the eusf are set out in the relevant basic act (council regulation (ec) no 2012/2002) as amended in 2014 (regulation (eu) no 661/2014). the present proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council, which i voted for today, is not linked to any particular disaster. it is intended instead to enter in the general budget of the union for 2016 an amount of eur 50 million in commitment and payment appropriations for the purpose of the rapid and efficient payment of advances in the event of a disaster occurring in the following year.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the text by mr christoforou on the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on the mobilisation of the european union solidarity fund, in accordance with point 11 of the interinstitutional agreement of 2 december 2013 between the european parliament, the council and the commission on budgetary discipline, on cooperation in budgetary matters and on sound financial management, for the purpose of paying advances under the 2016 budget.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal because it will strengthen the effectiveness of the european solidarity fund. i am convinced that this measure will speed up the disbursement of aid by means of an advance payment before a final decision is taken.
in writing. ‒ i supported this report approving the 2016 budget. compared with the council's initial proposals, this budget provides for increased funding to deal with the refugee crisis, and it increases expenditure in important areas such as research and development and support for smes. parliament thus secured an additional €800 million for the distribution of refugees across the european union and additional funding to support neighbouring countries. this work will be supported by increased funding for agencies dealing with migration-related issues. frontex will be able to hire an additional 60 people, while bea and europol will be able to create an additional 30 posts. in addition, we secured an additional €18 million for financial assistance to the united nations relief and works agency for palestine refugees (unrwa). however, vigilance and combativeness will be needed to ensure that budgetary levers are properly used to boost quality employment and strengthen the fight against poverty.
in writing. ‒ this is a rigorous budget, which increases by only 1.6%, while we have to invest 15 million in building security and it security. it is also a reform budget, marked by strict controls on the hiring of local assistants, so that deviations, or even real abuses, are quickly detected and do not happen again. finally, it is an interinstitutional budget of loyalty in which parliament confirms its objective of reducing its staff by 5% according to a precise timetable until 2019. it should be stressed, however, that this 2016 budget of the european union is a transitional budget before the necessary revision of the financial perspective next year.
in writing. ‒ as indicated in the 2016 budget, additional resources should be allocated to tackle the asylum crisis. the n-va needs to invest mainly in sensitively strengthening europe's external borders, promoting reception in the region so that refugees can stay safely close to their region, and improving cooperation between european intelligence services. these measures should help us to prevent new asylum dramas. it is also positive that the 2016 budget remains within the expenditure limits of the multiannual financial framework and that the eu is using this budget to focus on the competitiveness of our economies. the nva delegation in the european parliament approves the 2016 budget for these reasons, but warns of unjustified euphoria. it is unacceptable that the european parliament, for example, needs two more years to reduce its civil service by 5%. the eu, like national governments, must do more and better with less.
in writing. ‒ addressing the root causes of migration in africa, helping refugees in the member states, improving competitiveness by helping businesses, protecting farmers and supporting youth employment and learning mobility are some of the key priorities in the 2016 budget approved by parliament this afternoon. in addition to the eur 143.9 billion needed to cover its expenditure, the union has committed eur 155 billion for various projects. balancing the many legitimate needs of the union, it represents only about 1% of the gross national income of the 28 member states and only 6% is spent on administrative costs, which is a complete misunderstanding of the costly 'european bureaucracy'. it is a europe that is now in a position to act in a wide range of sectors that directly affect the daily lives of europeans, even if adjustments are already to be expected, particularly in view of the refugee crisis and the funds that will soon be allocated to turkey to deal with it.
in writing. ‒ in the 2016 budget, which i voted for, the overall amount of commitment appropriations is €155 billion, with a margin under the ceilings of the 2016 multiannual financial framework of €2.3 billion in commitment appropriations. the overall amount of payment appropriations for 2016 amounts to eur 143,9 billion, an increase of 1,8% compared to the 2015 budget. the flexibility instrument shall be mobilised to provide the sum of eur 1,5 billion in commitment appropriations for heading 3 (security and citizenship) and eur 24,0 million in commitment appropriations for heading 4 (europe in the world) as part of the measures to respond to the refugee crisis. compared to the commission's initial proposal, there are increases of eur 31.8 million for commitment appropriations for horizon 2020, eur 14.2 million for the cosme programme (improving access to finance for smes) and eur 6.6 million for erasmus+, which i welcome. for heading 3 'security', the level of commitments is set at eur 4.052 billion, with no margin below the expenditure ceiling for the heading and with eur 1.5 billion being mobilised under the flexibility instrument.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of mr deprez on the joint draft general budget of the european union for the financial year 2016, approved by the conciliation committee in the context of the budgetary procedure. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this joint text because it is clear that the european union needs to have sufficient resources to deal with the refugee crisis. there must be more resources to protect europe's external borders. the external borders of greece, italy, etc. are also the external borders of all individual member states, and so i voted for this text which, among other things, gives more money to frontex. it is a necessary step forward to bring the present crisis under control and to safeguard schengen.
in writing. ‒ diethylhexylphthalate (dehp) is in the category of so-called endocrine disruptors. these are chemicals that can have a harmful effect on the human hormonal system. they can lead to breast cancer, infertility, diabetes, and even alzheimer's disease, among other things. dehp is mainly used as a plasticizer in the recycling process of plastic items. it is found in all the consumer goods we use every day, such as textiles, furniture and building materials. scientific tests have shown that dehp affects the mammalian hormonal system and may even lead to irreversible consequences for human reproduction. in this context, and because there are already less harmful, viable and cheaper alternatives available today, i fully support the present resolution which opposes the authorization of recycled soft pvc containing dehp.
in writing. ‒ i have approved this report which rejects the commission's decision on the authorisation of the use of recycled flexible pvc containing dehp. studies have shown that this component is harmful to living organisms.
in writing. ‒ i supported this resolution because i believe that the european commission should not allow the recycling of plastics containing the dehp flexibilising additive for the production of new products. dehp is known to be toxic. it disrupts the endocrine system and can affect the rate of development and reproductive abilities of the individual. recycling needs to be further developed and encouraged, but this argument cannot justify the use of substances whose waste can be hazardous. i am also concerned that the operators who applied for authorisation to recycle dehp have not demonstrated that workers would be adequately protected from health risks.
in writing. i welcome the rejection by the european parliament of the commission's draft decision on the recycling of dehp-containing plastics. i join the majority of my colleagues who expressed in their vote their concern about this phthalate, which is known to have the capacity to disrupt the endocrine system. since this chemical is considered to be of 'high concern' under the reach regulation and since the effects of endocrine disruptors on human health must be fully considered, the shortcomings in the authorisation application convinced parliament to oppose the commission's proposal.
in writing. ‒ in 1999, when i first came to the european parliament, the european union banned the use of six phthalates in children's toys, the most common of which is dehp. this chemical, derived from phthalic acid, is used as a plasticizer and has been evaluated as an endocrine disruptor, thus posing a risk to human health. this characteristic justifies that in 2005 the ban was extended to all soft pvc childcare articles containing phthalates. the european parliament sounded the alarm this afternoon about the massive use of dehp in everyday objects by adopting a resolution opposing the authorisation of the recycling of plastics containing the dehp plasticizer for the production of pvc. this is in contrast to the opinion of the european commission, which would be in favour of it. the reasons given are not convincing: the recycling technique would justify the continued use of substances whose waste could be hazardous and a marketing authorization would enable manufacturers to reduce their production costs. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'customs' in the definition of the term 'commercial'.
in writing. ‒ as early as 2000, the european commission's communication (com ((1999) 0706) to the council and the european parliament on a community strategy on endocrine disruptors included dehp in annex 1 which lists 553 candidate substances with an apparent endocrine disrupting effect. dehp is a reproductive toxicant. the european executive must protect european citizens and their environment from dangerous chemicals, so i voted for the european commission to withdraw its draft request for implementation.
in writing. ‒ pvc containing dehp is widely present in everyday consumer products such as textiles, furniture and construction materials. since dehp is not chemically bound to plastic, it is readily dispersed into the environment. an application for authorisation should focus on the use of the substance and the presence of the substance in recycled materials is not to be taken into account for the granting of an authorisation.
in writing. ‒ given the danger of dehp due to its negative impact on the environment and human health, i voted in favour of this objection, so that the european commission would not allow plastics containing this substance to be recycled.
in writing. ‒ i abstained on this taxe report for the following reason. yes, multinationals have to pay taxes. it is not possible for small and mediumsized enterprises and workers to bear all the burdens. yes to transparency to combat tax evasion and to hold all member states accountable. however, i also say 'no' to a supranational tax union. this taxe report, with its ccctb (common consolidated charge base), is in any case a first step towards such a unified european taxation system. that's when i hang up. the solution to the problem of harmful tax practices lies with the heads of state or government meeting, not with the commission.
in writing. ‒ in response to the public debate on procedures for compulsory tax information in the member states and the luxleaks case on tax advantages for companies in luxembourg, the european parliament set up a special committee of inquiry (taxe). the report, adopted by the plenary, calls for a stronger approach and a tougher crackdown on tax avoidance. the effective tax rate of some multinational companies on profits made in european territories is close to zero percent. the fact that this is unfair to small and mediumsized enterprises is self-explanatory and damaging. i therefore welcome the call for a common corporate tax base and for more transparency in the hitherto secret agreements between eu countries and multinational companies. this is accompanied by the requirement that multinational enterprises in all sectors must disclose in their annual accounts a series of aggregated information broken down by member state and third country in which they have an establishment. however, since this country-specific reporting would be unreasonable for smes, i am pleased that parliament has adopted an epp amendment which provides for an exemption for smes from this obligation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which is crucial in the fight against tax evasion by multinationals. the text sets out three measures which are essential to ensure that the fight against tax evasion by multinationals is effective. 1. the all transnational corporations, without exception, must be able to be analysed and verified. the finance ministers propose not to check the rescripts older than 5 years, it makes no sense. the european parliament also proposes to control national and international records. the european council is forgetting the international agreements. 2. the rules are only effective if there are penalties. the european parliament proposes to impose sanctions. the council does not provide for any sanctions. 3. the you can't be a judge and then leave. the council of finance ministers wishes to be the reference body responsible for auditing and regulating tax returns. it is up to the commission to play this role to ensure greater fairness. parliament, in voting on this report, has made strong commitments in favour of the fight against tax evasion. it is now essential that the council and the commission do the same.
in writing. ‒ the vote on the report of the special committee on tax rulings, which i supported, was highly anticipated, as public opinion was very sensitive to the subject. the luxleaks scandal, which came to light on 5 november 2014, has raised awareness of the scale of secret deals aimed at obtaining drastic tax cuts for companies. however, it is thanks to these taxes that a state can pursue an inclusive social policy, support the investments necessary for our society, enable young people to benefit from the best possible education system, etc. it therefore seemed important at the time to set up a special committee in the european parliament to shed light on these questionable tax practices and, above all, to propose recommendations, in particular with a view to putting an end to harmful tax competition between member states. i would like to reiterate my wish that a proposal for a common consolidated corporate tax base should be tabled in parliament as soon as possible. this would be a first step towards more fiscal union in a europe that is suffering from its incomplete federalism.
in writing. - i want the whole luxleaks thing shed light on. the luxleaks scandal, which broke on 5 november 2014 with the publication by the international consortium of investigative journalists of nearly 28 000 pages of confidential documents establishing more than 500 private tax arrangements between the luxembourg tax authorities and more than 300 multinational companies between 2002 and 2010, revealed the extent of the use of secret agreements involving complex financial structures to obtain drastic tax reductions. in many cases, the luxembourg subsidiaries, with a turnover of several hundred million euros, have only a small presence and a limited economic activity in luxembourg.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which contains some recommendations made by the commission and the special committee of the european parliament in the wake of the luxleaks scandal. the report calls for a balanced, fair and transparent tax policy.
in writing. ‒ in stark contrast to her own television appearances, defending christmas carols and the christian history of europe and criticizing the dubious role of the oil states, colleague rachida dati sent this report off in a politically correct smurf. certainly, there are some concrete and good measures to prevent radicalisation, such as the separation of prisoners and the specialised training of prison staff. but anyone who believes that islamic jihadism can be countered by manipulating search engines and by telling attractive narratives and preventative messages on the net is naive. if there is an appeal for a comprehensive strategy, then for me this also means, and perhaps above all, that lessons must be drawn from the eu's failing border policy rather than from the rosy-eyed story. the powers and resources transferred to the eu in this area should be transferred back to the member states so that they can once again effectively control their borders and implement a return policy (such as the expulsion of criminal aliens, returned syrian fighters, hate-imam, etc.). it's the best form of prevention. i could not therefore approve this report.
in writing. ‒ in response to the problem of so-called 'foreign fighters', this own-initiative report proposes all the measures that can be taken to prevent radicalisation and the recruitment of eu citizens by terrorist organisations. the report focuses on prevention, particularly online, in prisons and through education. i welcome the fact that this resolution calls for both the speedy completion of an eu directive on passenger name records (pnr) and the establishment of a blacklist of european jihadists and jihadist terror suspects. the terrible attacks in paris have once again demonstrated beyond doubt that terror knows no bounds. for this reason, coordinated action and increased cooperation between member states are essential. i therefore support this resolution and expressly support full european intelligence cooperation.
in writing. ‒ the tragic events in paris require a multi-pronged response, both security and prevention. this report addresses several important aspects in this respect. in terms of prevention, he stresses the need for internet service providers to collaborate with the authorities, but also the role of education, social policies and actions in neighbourhoods. it also stressed the absolute need to increase cooperation between member states in the collection and exchange of information, both in preventative and law enforcement matters, particularly through tools such as sis ii, vis and ecris. the member states must supply these data banks in order to maximise the effectiveness of the fight against these barbaric acts. i also supported the amendment calling for the urgent reinforcement of checks at the external borders of the schengen area in the current situation. this reinforcement and the exchange of information are essential if we are to maintain the schengen area and ensure the security of our citizens.
in writing. ‒ the report by rachida dati on the prevention of radicalisation adopted this afternoon has enabled meps to send a clear message: yes we are at war against daesh and terrorism. and the dramatic attacks in paris 13 days ago, and the foiled attacks in brussels this weekend, show that no one is immune to religious fanaticism. i voted for all the amendments which tighten the measures and sanctions against the various actors of terrorism: recruiters and preachers of hatred, jihadist fighters and sponsors, whether they are on european territory or are about to enter it. europe must regain control of its borders. this requires a firm stance towards foreign fighters, who must be confined in institutions adapted to their return to european soil. and by expelling the hate preachers who prey on salafi mosques. other more technical aspects of counter-terrorism need to be strengthened: the criminal liability of website providers and the need to defeat the encryption of communications by terrorist organisations. because the security of european citizens is not negotiable!
in writing. ‒ the paris attacks have once again underlined the urgent need for coordinated action by member states and the european union to prevent radicalisation and to better combat terrorism. the resolution i supported contains concrete proposals: the establishment of a european blacklist of jihadists and suspected jihadist terrorists (member states are asked to bring any foreign fighter under judicial control); the need for mandatory and systematic checks at the external borders of the union; the strengthening of the exchange of information between national authorities and europol in order to identify and monitor suspected terrorists, as well as the confiscation of their passports and the freezing of their financial assets; the need to strengthen intercultural dialogue in order to prevent marginalization and encourage integration. finally, in order to prevent the dissemination of hate speech and terrorist propaganda on the internet, the adopted text also provides for the immediate removal of illegal content promoting violent extremism and calls on the member states to consider legal action, including criminal prosecution, against social networks and service providers that refuse to comply with an administrative or judicial request to remove illegal or terrorist content.
in writing. ‒ terrorism and violent extremism should not be linked to any religion, country or population alone. they are often a reflection of a socioeconomic context in which low education and unequal distribution of wealth and opportunity are a breeding ground. the fight against terrorism and radicalisation must tackle the root causes of the evil. we must also dare to question our trade relations (including arms trade!) with certain countries (saudi arabia). collecting more data on all people is not the answer. we're just making the haystack bigger than it is. the screening of internet data can only be done in a clear legal context. it still doesn't exist. the report rightly calls for good cooperation between governments and internet providers to remove illegal content. we need to share best practices, provide support to families so that they can more quickly identify and address radicalization. strengthening instruments such as europol, eurojust and sis can lead to more efficient cooperation. you can't fight fear with more security alone, especially if it comes at the expense of privacy. we must ensure that human rights are respected, and we must not confuse refugees with terrorists. our basic values of democracy, freedom, equality and solidarity must above all be respected.
in writing. ‒ this is a text which has no legislative or binding force. however, we had to address the issue of radicalisation. indeed, 5 000 european citizens have joined terrorist organisations and other military formations, including the ranks of the islamic state group, the nusra front and other organisations outside the european union, particularly in the middle east and north africa regions. this phenomenon is accelerating to a considerable extent. it's time to act!
in writing. ‒ i support this proposal which makes some recommendations to prevent radicalisation among our own european citizens. on november 13, 2015, horrific terrorist attacks were committed in paris by some of our own citizens. a more european coordinated approach is needed to counter the radicalisation that leads to such terror. we need to move with the times and realize that radicalization often happens through the internet or social media. i have therefore chosen to monitor internet companies more closely so that such attacks can be prevented in the future and that such terrorist organisations are not provided with a digital platform to recruit people.
in writing. ‒ health and safety at work is a major concern for society. i believe that every worker, without exception, has the right to the highest level of health protection at work. in particular, the european commission and the member states should set indicative targets for the reduction of occupational diseases and accidents at work. that is why i support the report on the eu strategic framework for health and safety at work 2014-2020.
in writing. ‒ every year, more than 4 000 workers die in the union as a result of accidents at work and more than 150 000 die as a result of work-related diseases. in this report, which i supported, the european parliament calls on the commission to take decisive action to protect workers from the new risks of cancer and psychological disorders such as burnout and stress. this includes the review of exposure limit values in the light of new scientific knowledge, the systematic monitoring and follow-up of workers exposed to psychological risks, in particular stress or burnout, and the fight against asbestos.
in writing. despite a large number of guidelines to achieve a healthy working environment for workers, we still have 4,000 fatal accidents at work every year and the number of fatal work-related diseases continues to peak at 150,000 per year. continuous evaluation and adjustment of risk prevention measures and the inducement of behavioural changes for all actors involved in the work process therefore remain a priority. at the same time, the labour market in europe is undergoing major changes. people will work longer in the future, change jobs more often, and build more flexibility into their careers. ensuring well-being and health at work adds value to society as a whole and contributes to people's active and healthy ageing. in this context, we must continue to take concrete preventive measures to eliminate as far as possible the risk of accidents and illnesses among workers. in addition to continuing to address chronic work-related diseases, new challenges such as psychological and social risks in the workplace must be carefully identified and preventive action taken to achieve safe and healthy working environments for all european workers, both physically and mentally. after all, good health is a fundamental right in europe and prevention remains the best approach.
in writing. ‒ every year, more than 4 000 workers in the union die as a result of accidents at work and the number of fatal work-related diseases is over 150 000 every year. the european parliament has therefore enthusiastically supported the commission's proposal on the european union's strategic framework for health and safety at work. the text concerns the 217 million european workers, and the question is whether labour regulations are an essential part of the legislative activity of the european institutions. this strategy is timely and will be able to respond to the important challenges that are arising: better enforcement of existing rules, improvement of the prevention of work-related diseases, and this while taking into account the ageing of the european workforce. in concrete terms, this will include further consolidating national strategies, helping small and micro enterprises to comply with the rules with assessments, simplifying legislation, providing better statistics to assess the issues at stake and finally strengthening coordination with international organisations. an effective strategy, in the long term, for the benefit of the worker.
in writing. ‒ every year, more than 4 000 workers in the eu lose their lives in the course of their work. more than 150,000 people die from work-related diseases. every effort must be made to prevent such human tragedies from happening again and to adapt legislation to the realities on the ground in order to ensure its proper application. if there is one issue on which the 'triple a social' targeted by the president of the european commission, jean-claude juncker, depends, it is the health and safety of european workers. in my view, the simplification of our regulations, which aims to make european union legislation simpler and more effective (the refit programme drawn up by the european commission), cannot in any way weaken the rules governing health and safety at work. i am also convinced that it is with the help of the actors on the ground that we must define the best policies to be implemented. better working conditions, and therefore a reduction in accidents and illnesses, benefit not only workers, whose physical integrity is preserved, but also social security systems, which are thus strengthened, and the competitiveness of enterprises.
in writing. ‒ after months of delay, the european commission presented its new strategy for health and safety at work 2014-2020. it outlines three major challenges: implementing existing health and safety rules, preventing work-related diseases and ageing our eu workforce. the report is the ep's official response to this and was reinforced by several green amendments focusing on 'better prevention than cure'. we call on the commission to come up with a comprehensive strategy on occupational exposure to endocrine disruptors. we're asking for recognition of the risks associated with stress at work, including burnout. the existing directives on health and safety at work should not be undermined by the european commission's refit programme to simplify legislation, which could also have negative consequences for the health and safety of workers. to help smes reduce their administrative burden without compromising the health and safety of their workers, new tools are being developed to facilitate risk assessment to comply with legislation. i support this report because it puts the health and safety of workers first. that's the key.
in writing. ‒ the n-va delegation abstained from voting on this report. n-va fully endorses the importance of a high level of protection of human health. in doing so, union action may support and complement national policies, but should respect the policy autonomy of the member states. the present report does not, unfortunately, sufficiently respect this division of powers. the nva delegation, on the other hand, fully welcomes the encouragement of the exchange of good practice, the call for consistent and transparent rules that should make it easier for companies to comply with them, and the special attention paid to smes.
in writing. - i voted for the text. health and safety at work is a fundamental interest of society and an investment that has a positive impact on the productivity and competitiveness of enterprises, improves the sustainability of social security systems and allows people to work in good health until the legal retirement age. as a reminder, occupational accidents and diseases represent a considerable burden on society and improving occupational health and safety in europe can contribute to economic recovery and the achievement of the europe 2020 strategy, for which little progress has been made so far towards the 75% employment rate for 20-64 year olds.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this plan because better well-being and health at work contribute to a better society as a whole. we all have to work longer in europe because of ageing. this strategic plan can, through prevention, ensure that we nevertheless age in a more active and healthier way.

in writing. ‒ i have endorsed this report, which highlights the positive aspects of the action taken so far at european level in organising sustainable urban mobility. in this respect, it stresses the importance of spatial planning for the creation of well-organised, efficient and sustainable transport networks, as well as the information and involvement of all stakeholders (citizens, traders, transport operators, etc.) in order to ensure transparency and efficiency in urban mobility projects.
due to increasing urbanisation, 82% of eu citizens will soon live in an urban environment. together, these people account for almost 85% of european gdp. cities are important engines of innovation and economic growth, and it is in them that we still find the best opportunities for employment, education, cultural activities and catering. but the increasing pressure of mobility and the finding that urban transport is responsible for 25 percent of co2 emissions threatens to undermine the vitality of the city. new and sustainable models of urban mobility are needed to maintain and sustain the dynamism of cities. new urban transport plans will therefore primarily use low-carbon modes of transport that connect to an urban grid of smart traffic hubs that allow for quick and easy transition from one mode of transport to another. the development of sustainable transport plans must always seek to strike a balance between the ecological and social impact of a mobility plan and the needs of the city's residents and visitors, all without undermining the city's economic engine.
in writing. ‒ congestion and pollution in large cities are painful realities of our daily lives that need to be improved urgently for good health and a better environment. this was also emphasized by the european parliament this evening when it adopted the delli report on sustainable urban mobility. some of the ways are known to reduce the presence of cars in cities: better public transport networks, easy train-metro bus connections, the development of car-sharing or teleworking. i did not, however, support amendment no 1 to remove all subsidies for fossil fuels. the idea is relevant and partly in line with the conclusions of the oecd in its september report, which identified no less than 800 measures to support fossil fuels worldwide. however, it seems impractical in reality, since many subsidies for polluting energy directly benefit the most vulnerable people. the priority is therefore to reverse the current practice and to shift public support towards renewable energy. one idea to be explored, put forward by the oecd experts, would be to subsidize household incomes directly by means of a cheque, leaving them free to spend it as they see fit.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which encourages in particular member states to review their strategies to promote non-motorised transport in order to serve the converging interests of improving mobility and the urban environment. the adopted text also encourages member states to promote the use of bicycles, including by setting ambitious targets for bicycle use rates by 2030 and to improve conditions for walking and cycling.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the initiative of my colleague karima delli. mobility is not an end in itself, but should be a right for all citizens. 80% of europeans will soon live in cities; mobility should therefore promote access for all, including persons with reduced mobility, to education, work, culture, leisure and health. yet urban mobility is often seen as a constraint, which has its origin in the overuse of the private car running on traditional fuels. in fact, the shift to more sustainable modes of transport is very slow: the car remains the main mode of our mobility, accounting for 43% of the kilometres travelled worldwide and three quarters of journeys in europe. the dependence on cars and its corollary, road congestion, which is estimated to cost 80 billion euros for all european cities, makes city dwellers prisoners of a mobility that is suffered, if not chosen.
in writing. ‒ a sharp increase in mobility pressures and the associated pollution in our cities is a growing problem for our society. it is clear that we need to look for new co2-neutral transport options that improve urban mobility in a sustainable way. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. i therefore voted in favour of this report because better and more sustainable mobility can also be a major boost for our economy.
i have four reservations about the files we are discussing today. without a doubt, we should invest in renewable energy. but the more renewable energy we produce, the more we strain the existing grids with peaks and troughs in supply. to counteract this we need better links between the member states. second point of order: if we want to give renewable energy a fair chance, we need to let the market do its job as quickly as possible. and we must not allow these to be falsified, for example, by allowing member states to grant subsidies for a particular technology. a third point: the commission considers that the aid is compatible with the internal market if it is granted to the beneficiary in accordance with the conditions laid down in article 107 (3) (c) of the treaty. fourth and final point: if we are to achieve the 2020 and 2030 targets and the subsequent targets, we need energy storage. conclusion the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's energy policy is not undermined by the fact that the community is not able to meet its energy needs.

what do we see? yes, growth is returning to spain, but at what cost? when employment increases, it is unskilled employment, it is part-time employment. this is what creates this new category of working poor. in spain, a leading country in the eurozone, one in three children is facing poverty. so if you call that success, let me have a few questions. your revenue is actually falling. they are countercyclical: they compress public demand and private demand. the result: no growth. so if you're so hung up on it, it's not the right solution. as cop 21 comes to a close, we should actually put the whole package on investment in the energy transition. this is obviously a climate requirement, but it's also a geostrategic requirement if we want to stop defending people like putin or saudi arabia. it's a macroeconomic requirement if we're going to stop spending hundreds of billions of dollars a year on fossil fuels. this is a requirement in terms of jobs, since everyone knows that renewable energy is much more job-intensive than traditional energy. secondly, 150 years after unification, 25 years after reunification, germany, which is a monetary union and a customs union, is still not homogeneous. it is not tomorrow that the european union and the euro zone will be homogeneous, and so there is no euro that holds without powerful rebalancing mechanisms within the euro zone. these mechanisms must be implemented by the private sector, namely the banking union, which is known to be incomplete - it is known that it will be difficult to bring about the emergence of the third pillar, the common deposit guarantee - but also by the public sector. this includes a common taxation system, a euro-zone budget and a common social security embryo. the five presidents' report makes only very vague reference to all this, and it is well known that there is no political will to do so at present. if we do not go through these rebalancing mechanisms, the euro area is doomed. i do not want it to disappear, and therefore these rebalancing mechanisms will have to be put in place. answer is "blue cardboard". dear mr pirinski, i think competitiveness is a real issue. it is not just a question of foreign trade, since every day our compatriots buy goods and services and see what they get for their money. i am not opposed in principle to having advice on this subject, but under certain conditions. first, they must deal with competitiveness in all its aspects, i.e. values and not just costs. secondly, when we talk about costs, it is not just labour costs, but also energy costs, resource costs, return on capital, in other words all costs. finally, these councils must not be limited to bringing together experts, whose origins are generally well known, but must deliberately include the social partners, whether trade unions, employers or political representatives. in these circumstances, i would like to consider the idea of setting up these councils devoted to competitiveness, but as a real subject.
i would like to welcome you to this parliament of the european union. you come here as the president of the part of the european union where the euro is the currency, in a european parliament that is completely divided. it has become impossible to agree in this parliament even on the broad outlines of this euro-policy and this monetary union. a large group here is in favour of more euros and of the euro. the commission is therefore proposing a unification of socioeconomic policy and further cuts in southern europe, even if this causes a social bloodbath there. there is also a large group of people who are in favour of your euro zone and of the continuation of the euro. that group should know much less about austerity, does not expect much from it, nothing structural, nothing fundamental and also wants a continuation of your loose ecb policy, with more or less preserving the derailed budgetary situations. and then there is a third group who believe that holding on to the single euro for all our countries is a fantasy that we should let go of slowly and sooner rather than later. this group will continue to grow and in the coming year will bring more and more truth to the fore, which will hurt, because the euro crisis will continue, as will the asylum crisis. for these reasons, i wish you much reflection and also much relief during your christmas holidays.
thank you, mr president, and thank you to all the chairmen who are here today. unfortunately, i don't have a pleasant message for you either, because i think your report is based on a piece of outdated philosophy: the commission has already made a number of proposals. this is not what europeans are waiting for. on the contrary, i think they've had enough. in britain, there is a debate about brexit. in denmark, they vote against the justice policy. in france, the national front has never won so many votes. in eastern europe something is brewing against europe, against this unique idea. it is always either more europe or total destruction. my dear colleagues, that will not work and how do i know that? because we tried it in belgium. we have had a federal union with transfers, with a lack of democratic support, and that is not working. what does work is more responsibility, responsibility both for the european institutions and for all the european member states and so we have to look at that 'no bailout' rule as we had it in the maastricht treaty; we need to see if and how we can repair it, reinforce it. because that is the way to perfectly secure the euro, and that is what we must do. that way we can do it without all these new institutions, without all these new powers and also without all these new taxes. responsibility, unity and diversity, doing what europe is really strong at and not opting for a suffocating european superstate. that is the way we must go with this european union.
the european union is a political union, a political union of the people, a political union of the people, a political union of the people. i am frankly pained to see that even a mere reference to completing the banking union is too sensitive for some member states. i would like to hear from those ministers how they think they can avoid a repeat of the 2008-2009 debacle, in which bank and government debt reinforced each other, without a fully-fledged banking union, including a genuine european deposit guarantee mechanism. for me, strengthening or deepening emu is a matter of pure pragmatism. my inspiration is the simple need to give the emu the necessary instruments to function better and thus also to increase its legitimacy and support among the citizens. i therefore welcome the fact that the commission does not allow itself to be paralysed by these short-sighted national reflexes and puts forward realistic concrete proposals. the commission is also proposing to increase the number of national experts in the field of the environment. the adjusted timing of the semester also allows for greater involvement of national parliaments and the social partners. but the closer involvement of the national level should not be interpreted as a signal that it is there that the real legitimacy lies. no, the european construction is characterized by a multi-layered legitimacy in which the european parliament plays a crucial role. the european interest is much more than the sum of the interests of the individual member states. the founding fathers realized that they had to protect themselves against their own national reflexes, because they undermine the surplus of european cooperation. the european union is supranational in nature, and that is why it needs strong institutions and a strong european parliament, in order to guarantee the legitimacy of this structure. so no, i am not a young dreamer who is stubbornly clinging to an outdated idea of a european superstate. i simply want to help in a purely pragmatic way and do what is necessary to make this european and monetary union work better in the future. thank you, sir.
i think that the commission should be able to take the initiative in this matter. of course they are through the internal market. the european parliament has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. we must take responsibility together as the european union, the commission, parliament and the member states. firstly, by ensuring that the credibility of the stability pact is restored. secondly, by completing the banking union in order to guarantee financial stability to citizens and businesses. and thirdly, by completing that capital markets union to ensure that we are less dependent on bank financing and we can finally make real investments in our real economy. but countries must also take responsibility for this story. it is not possible for them to agree on structural reforms and then implement only 10 or 15% of them in their own country. how can we have a common economic policy if that is the credibility and lack of ownership of different countries? so you will have to put more pressure on them to ensure that these structural reforms are also implemented in those countries. the last point is democratic responsibility. i think we must also start a debate on this, to ensure that this parliament can play its part more than ever with national parliaments in ensuring these reforms and stability. the european central bank has given us as politicians time, has given politicians time to take responsibility. it is time for the european central bank to do its job as an independent monetary institution and for us politicians at european and national level to work together to solve this problem once and for all.

in writing. the functioning of the eu is based on a balanced budget financed from own resources, i.e. traditional own resources, vat-based resources (maximum 50% of each member state's gni) and resources based on gross national income. the amount of this budget is capped at 1.23% of the total gross national income of the member states. when a country becomes a member of the eu, it commits to pay its annual contribution in proportion to its wealth. in the event of disproportionate payment, the member state may benefit from a correction, as is currently the case for germany, the netherlands, the united kingdom, austria and sweden. the report which has been voted on is purely technical and does not deal with the calculation of the amounts of the member states' contributions in terms of own resources. in particular, it proposes a number of clarifications and improvements, mainly of a technical nature, reflecting the experience gained, in particular with regard to the accounting of own resources, the management of the commission's cash resources, the evaluation of gni data by the commission (eurostat), the impact of criminal investigations on the identification and provision of traditional own resources and the reporting of amounts of uncollectable traditional own resources.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which stresses the need for effective rules governing the timely payment of member states' contributions to the union budget in order to enable the commission to manage its cash efficiently. the report also supports the possibility for the commission to ask member states to pay one-third of vat and gni-based resources in the first half of the year, in order to enable the commission to further reduce the payment delays of the previous year linked to the european agricultural guarantee fund and the european structural and investment funds, as well as interest on late payments. the text also stresses the importance of timely payment of amounts due to beneficiaries of the union budget.
in writing. - i voted for the deprez proposal. we stress the need for effective rules governing the timely payment of member states' contributions to the union budget in order to enable the commission to manage its cash efficiently. parliament supported the possibility for the commission to ask member states to pay one-third of vat and gni-based resources in the first half of the year, in order to enable the commission to further reduce the payment delays of the previous year linked to the european agricultural guarantee fund and the european structural and investment funds and the interest on late payments.
in writing. ‒ this report covers the allocation of traditional own resources, vat and gni resources and measures to meet cash requirements. the european commission is using this to avoid any problems due to technical recalculations. i therefore voted in favour of this report because it is designed to avoid internal frictions.

in writing. ‒ nokia's difficulties and competition from third countries have had a significant impact on employment in the ict sector in finland. from 2008 to 2014, the number of workers in the sector increased from 326,000 to 276,000. the oulu region was particularly affected and in spring 2015 there were still 1 500 jobseekers in the ict sector looking for work. i therefore supported the intervention of the egf to support the efforts of the finnish authorities to facilitate their integration into the labour market.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) aims to help reintegrate workers who have lost their jobs as a result of the global trade crisis and the victims of the financial crisis. the request in question, submitted by finland, concerns redundancies in the information technology sector. indeed, in recent years, the distribution of ict employment between the eu and other economies has been to the detriment of the eu. while volume in this sector is increasing globally, it has decreased in europe as companies and services are relocated to china, india, taiwan and other non-european destinations. in 2014 alone, the number of employees in ict companies in finland decreased by 3% (i.e. 1 500 people). the aim is to help 1 603 redundant employees in 69 enterprises in different regions of finland. the aid will amount to eur 2 623 200 and will help to co-finance active labour market measures focusing on job search assistance, training, vocational reorientation, etc. this request has my support and that of the european parliament.
in writing. ‒ globalisation is inevitable and goes hand in hand with the opening up of new markets, international competition, economic growth and job creation. the downside of this is job losses in less competitive sectors. the nva delegation in the european parliament understands the objectives of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf), but also has an eye on the taxpayer who pays the bill. moreover, social policy should be a competence of the member states in the first instance. a european transfer union is not a panacea for tackling unemployment. in particular, structural reforms are needed to restore economic growth. the n-va meps therefore abstained from voting on this dossier.
in writing. ict employment in finland fell by 3% (around 10 000 workers) between 2008 and 2014, mainly due to microsoft's €5.4 billion takeover of former phone leader nokia and the outsourcing of ict companies specialising in programming, consulting and other it activities to china, india and other non-european countries. it is our duty to respond to finnish demand by mobilising eur 2.636 million to help reintegrate the 1,200 workers made redundant in this sector. solidarity is one of the union's values. i welcome the initiative of finland, which did not wait for the mobilisation of this fund to help its workers by launching the implementation of personalised services on 1 august 2014.
