in writing. ‒ with reference to the commission's package on the european energy union, parliament's position on this issue is set out in this resolution. in principle, i share the view that the eu should aim to reduce its dependence on individual energy suppliers (security of supply) and that energy efficiency should be fundamentally reconsidered and treated as an independent source of energy. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the nuclear industry is not left behind. i regret, however, that the text does not take account of an amendment which is important to me and which deals with the negative consequences of fracking on the climate, the environment and public health. that is why i abstained in the final vote. since i believe that fracking is not a promising technology and that, apart from the environmental and health risks, the investment and development costs are too high, member states should refrain from exploring and extracting shale gas.
in writing. ‒ at a time when cop 21 has delivered ambitious and necessary targets, i supported this resolution in which parliament reaffirms its commitment to the 2030 climate and energy targets of reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 40%, increasing the share of renewable energy in the european energy mix to 27% and increasing energy efficiency by 30%. parliament also stressed that the energy union should be a comprehensive approach focusing on various aspects such as the achievement of a fully integrated internal energy market, security of supply, the best use of the union's energy resources, limiting energy demand, reducing greenhouse gas emissions mainly through renewable energy sources and an eu-wide carbon market, and research and innovation in the energy sector. it also stressed the obvious fact that citizens should be at the heart of the energy union and benefit from safe, sustainable and affordable energy and called for their involvement in all the work of the energy union.
in writing. ‒ the energy union is without doubt the most important policy package of this legislature. all vital policy areas come together here: the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a common position on the following issues: we need to make big legislative strides in the coming year to increase the share of renewable energy, reduce energy consumption through greater energy efficiency, and guarantee the continuity of gas supply. in 2016, we also need to take important steps to develop a balanced ets system that ensures that we can further reduce co2 emissions, but also that adequate attention is paid to the competitiveness of our energy-intensive businesses.
in writing. ‒ europe imports 53% of the energy it consumes. this costs him over a billion euros a day. i have supported this report recommending a number of measures which will help to reduce the cost of energy bills, decarbonise the european economy and reduce europe's dependence on imported fossil fuels. this is a major project for the european union. the energy union must provide eu citizens with safe, sustainable and affordable energy. building it will require concerted efforts by member states to reduce their dependence on energy imports by integrating their energy markets, improving security of supply, making the best use of existing and renewable sources and moderating demand, but it is essential to go beyond this framework of 28 regulations and so many energy bundles to be more efficient and secure the eu's energy future. my group has played an important role in ensuring energy efficiency and renewable energy in the future european energy package. we have laid the foundations for a much more comprehensive and ambitious approach to the integration of energy systems and solutions.
the paris agreement on the environment is the most ambitious, most compelling and most hopeful agreement ever to mitigate global warming. with this agreement, almost 200 countries have taken a definitive step towards a low-carbon economy. the same ambition is reflected in the report: towards a european energy union in recent years, the vulnerability of europe to disruptions in energy supply has been explicitly addressed on a number of occasions. the eu today depends on the goodwill of foreign partners for half of its energy needs. this dependence makes energy the achilles' heel of our society and economy. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's energy supply is not affected by the crisis. in addition, our dependence on conventional fossil fuels is far too great. developing european energy security that ensures sovereignty and environmental objectives is a priority for a strong economic and political position. i therefore support the ambitions of this report, which explicitly favours energy efficiency, renewable energy and the development of innovative, environmentally friendly energy sources, because a common greening of the european energy market will also have a positive impact on new employment.
in writing. ‒ the vote on this report today in plenary allowed me to express my unconditional support for the amendments which consider that the use of hydraulic fracturing (i.e. shale gas) in the european union entails risks and adverse effects for the climate, the environment and public health, and jeopardises the achievement of the union's long-term decarbonisation target. i believe that, given the limited capacity of unconventional fuels to meet the energy demand of the union in the future and the high investment and costs involved in their exploitation, hydraulic fracturing is not a technology of the future and i have therefore, together with others, urged member states not to engage in any exploration or exploitation of shale gas.
in writing. ‒ the report makes it clear that we need a european and regional approach to linking energy networks between member states. this is necessary to accommodate the fluctuations in renewable energy. our delegation is also committed to energy efficiency. the best and cheapest kilowatt hour is the one that is not used. the resolution is on this line. the transition to a genuine energy market system is necessary. this requires the rapid elimination of market-distorting subsidies and taxes. parliament approved higher targets for renewable energy, efficiency and greenhouse gases. the delegation voted against this in order to honour the agreement between the member states. although some of the elements do not agree with our views, the overall package is a clear signal on how the energy union should be shaped.
in writing. ‒ i see the added value of a european energy union. this can only benefit the citizens of europe. that is why i voted in favour of this report. but as far as the nuclear aspect is concerned, i think it is necessary that nuclear research can still be subsidised.
in writing. ‒ without the free flow of energy across borders, there can be no real internal energy market in the eu. in this context, the restructuring of the electricity market which this resolution is concerned with is a correct and important step in this direction. the creation of electricity grids is essential to this, as it both promotes the spread of renewable energy and lowers electricity prices in europe.
in writing. ‒ i have endorsed this resolution which welcomes the commission's communication and strategy, which represent positive progress towards achieving the 10% interconnection target in the electricity sector and towards improving the functioning of the internal electricity market in the union. parliament stated that renewable energy, improved energy efficiency, a sustainable energy mix that generates energy savings and an internal energy market that allows the free movement of energy are important means of ensuring a stable, secure, independent, inclusive, transparent and competitive energy system across the union, which promotes the creation of quality jobs and wealth in a sustainable, future-oriented economy. the resolution also stresses that electricity interconnection is one of the prerequisites for the completion of an integrated internal electricity market which, if well designed, will enable us to achieve our climate objectives, including the union's objective of becoming a leader in renewable energy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which proposes a number of measures, including better interconnection of electricity grids, in order to gradually build a genuine european electricity network. investing in the integration of the european electricity market could reduce prices by at least eur 2 per mwh and thus save almost eur 40 billion per year by 2030. this interconnection is crucial, both to achieve our climate goals and to make europe more competitive with cheaper electricity. the 10% interconnection target by 2020 is a very valuable contribution to the implementation of the energy union, but it can only be achieved if all member states achieve it at the same time. it will therefore be necessary to work with the 12 member states which remain below the 10% electricity interconnection target and are therefore largely isolated from the internal electricity market. i also believe it is essential that the eu sets ambitious, evidence-based and regionally agreed complementary interconnection targets for 2030.
in writing. europe can strengthen its independence from foreign energy suppliers by developing a finely-meshed integrated network of electricity highways across europe. this strategy of interconnectivity ensures the security of energy supply. it is also a way of making the best use of existing european energy resources and of developing a more coordinated internal energy market. we are thus better able to resist all kinds of disturbances and an internal energy market will ensure better pricing, which in turn will be beneficial to the strength of european companies. the development of energy hubs and energy highways will ensure that the growing share of energy from renewable energy sources is used in a more efficient way. with the increasing number of energy prosumers generating energy locally and in remote areas from environmentally friendly energy sources, it is essential to ensure that the energy generated is not wasted. north sea wind turbines will generate more than 8% of total electricity demand by 2030. then there is the need to make that energy available throughout europe. that is why i endorse in this report the commitment to systematically synchronise and extend the electricity connection with the 'external regions' of the european union, so that in the long term all countries will have access to an internal electricity market.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament was invited to give its opinion on a report on the european electricity grid for 2020. in this report, parliament acknowledges in particular that the 10% electricity interconnection target is one of the preconditions for the completion of the integrated internal electricity market. the benefits of this market could be many, including increased security and reduced price volatility. the figure of at least eur 2/mwh is also mentioned in the report. while this 10% target by 2020 is a major objective, ambitious, evidence-based and regionally agreed complementary interconnection targets should be set for the medium term and certainly by 2030. it is now important that the commission and the member states give strong political support and approval to the energy network project in the north sea region.
in writing. ‒ better connections to the electricity networks between member states are needed not only to improve the eu's geopolitical energy position, but also to achieve the climate and energy objectives. the objective of connecting at least 10% of electricity production to the networks in other member states is therefore a step in the right direction. the greens want to set targets in advance for specific regions on the basis of scientific research. additional qualitative parameters are also needed, such as increased transparency and involvement of local actors and civil society organisations in 'projects of general interest'. the best available technologies should also be used to minimise the impact on the environment. belgium is one of the best-interconnected eu countries with 17% interconnectivity. four projects are in the pipeline, including the stevin plan to ensure that offshore wind farms can be connected to the fixed grid. but 12 member states have not yet reached the 10% target. i voted in favour of this report and the recommendations contained in it. the eu needs to achieve better, tailor-made and smart interconnection of electricity networks between countries. only then will it be possible to make the switch to renewable energy.
in writing. ‒ the strategic advantage of interconnectivity should lead to a more resilient and independent european network. moreover, greater interconnectivity will enable us to distribute renewable energy more effectively throughout the european union.
in writing. ‒ in 2010, the eu launched the progress microfinance facility with a total volume of eur 205 million to ensure that socially and financially disadvantaged people have a chance to build a livelihood. progress is designed to make it easier for these people to set up micro-enterprises and to provide targeted support for these micro-enterprises. the present mid-term review report is positive. progress can help to achieve the employment objectives of the europe 2020 strategy, even in the context of an economic crisis. i think this instrument is very useful because it helps, among other things, unemployed people, the socially vulnerable and young people who otherwise have little chance of obtaining credit to set up businesses and thus create employment themselves. progress supports micro-enterprises, which represent a large proportion of european employers. it's about helping yourself. progress thus fills a significant social and employment gap.
in writing. ‒ the eu set up the progress european microfinance facility in 2010 with a total budget of €205 million to provide socially and financially disadvantaged people in europe with the opportunity to build a decent life. the instrument is currently available in only 22 of the 28 member states, due to the diversity of levels of development of national economies within the union, the varying level of market interest and the regulatory conditions in place. the commission has drawn up an interim report on the instrument, which is still valid until 2016. in its resolution on the report, parliament noted that the impact in terms of job creation was less than expected, although it must be acknowledged that many beneficiaries would have been completely excluded from the credit market in the absence of microcredit. the commission also proposes to reduce the number of rejected applications, to promote social enterprises and to cooperate with microfinance intermediaries. it also called on the member states to increase awareness of the activities linked to the programme.
in writing. the economic situation is prompting us to strengthen the financial instruments, in particular those for setting up new businesses. access to microfinance can play a significant role in this regard. even if the results in terms of job creation are lower than we expected, this mechanism still represents significant benefits because many people would not have been able to access credit in the absence of microcredit. the mechanism must therefore be improved. to this end, it is necessary, in particular, to ensure greater publicity for this instrument and to extend its geographical and sectoral scope so that it can cover all activities in the union.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on the implementation of the european progress microfinance facility. microfinance is an important issue in that it contributes to the achievement of the europe 2020 objectives, in particular in terms of social inclusion and reducing social inequalities. the european progress microfinance facility is therefore important in that it increases access to this type of microfinance. this instrument can thus be a real breath of fresh air for people who have lost or are in danger of losing their jobs, for those who are having difficulties entering or returning to the labour market, etc. this support will enable them to try to start or develop their own micro-enterprises. while this instrument has already proved its worth, i remain convinced that it is the duty of the member states to create contact points to make it better known to potential beneficiaries and citizens in general. i also regret that this instrument does not finance a large number of social enterprises. as this instrument will end in 2016, i can only hope that easi (the eu programme for employment and social innovation) will take over to support microfinance and social entrepreneurship in europe.
in writing. ‒ the n-va delegation abstained from voting on this report. it believes that a european microfinance facility can be very useful in the fight against social exclusion and welcomes a european policy supporting activation strategies. the n-va delegation fully supports initiatives that give oxygen to smes and facilitate their establishment and development. however, the obstacle in this report is that 'refugees, asylum seekers and migrants' are identified as a special target group of the financial facility, on which the commission should focus its efforts in particular. this could mean that the above groups - whose (long-term) residence is very uncertain - have access to social assistance from day one. the n-va delegation is concerned that this could set a precedent for further, immediate claims for all kinds of social benefits.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the implementation of the european progress microfinance facility, because its objective is to help the less privileged people to find work. this facility will help people in europe to start businesses, learn new skills and find a job.
in writing. ‒ the complexity and diversity of the technical measures of the common fisheries policy, as well as the fact that they are spread over many different regulations, have contributed to making their application difficult for fishermen. similarly, the effectiveness of the multiannual plans adopted between 2002 and 2009 has been uneven. the present report, which i supported, therefore considers that to ensure the implementation of the objectives of this common policy, future technical measures should be simplified, contained in a clearly structured legal framework and developed on the basis of sound scientific advice reviewed by peers.
in writing. technical measures and multiannual plans are essential tools in the sustainable management of our marine resources. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of the euro against counterfeiting and pirated goods, which was adopted by the council on 27 june, was based on the principle of the free movement of goods. it is crucial to make them as easy to read as possible in order to make them easier for fishermen to apply. parliament called for the adoption of a directive on the protection of the environment against the adverse effects of ionising radiation. parliament also recalls the objectives and principles of the new common fisheries policy reformed in 2013, such as environmental sustainability and the ecosystem approach. the union plays a crucial role in the sustainable management of fish stocks and the preservation of the marine environment. the necessary corollary to achieving sustainable fisheries is consistent and readable technical measures and multiannual plans.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which considers it urgent to establish a coherent set of technical measures for the main basins, taking into account their respective specificities. in particular, given the landing obligation in force since 1 january 2015 which will be applied progressively to all fish stocks by 2019, the european parliament called for the provisions on technical measures to be sufficiently flexible to take into account real-time developments in fisheries and to further enable the fishing industry to put innovations in gear selectivity into practice.
in writing. ‒ the new cfp promotes sustainable fisheries, namely through the conservation of fish stocks and long-term productivity. a new structure for technical measures and multiannual plans will ensure the long-term sustainability of the fisheries sector and, moreover, contribute to achieving the most important objectives of the reformed cfp. that is why i voted in favour of this report.

member of the commission. – madam president, honourable members of parliament, let me start by expressing my thanks for your contribution to this debate today, for your support and also for your concerns and worries that we have shared together here. i can tell you that i took note of what was said, but let me first say this: what we have presented here today is not about entirely closing or opening borders, because neither is realistic. so on the points you have made, the question of not going far enough, today you must all admit that it is a very important step forward. this is a gradual process as europe moves forward. some of you referred to the fact that rules need to be better enforced. i fully agree with you – be it the schengen border code or asylum legislation, this commission, i can tell you, does its job in fully enforcing eu law. we are launching infringement proceedings wherever it is necessary, but sometimes rules also need to be adapted to a new reality. that does not mean, as i said during my introductory remarks, that we substitute member states’ responsibilities. i want to be clear on that. we do not touch member states’ sovereignty. what we have presented today has a strong preventive and supportive role to all member states with external borders. the next pressure might be in a totally different part of europe’s borders, so we must be well prepared. i think that you share with me the point of view that when the very first migratory refugee flows approached the european borders we were all caught by surprise – member states and the european union. the european union did not have a migration policy, it was something fragmented, scattered around within the commission, but now thanks to your support we have adopted the european agenda on migration and have taken many other decisions together: the relocation and resettlement scheme and the action plan against smugglers. so we have made a step forward, but today we are moving ahead in a bold way. let us be realistic and honest. the current crisis shows one thing, which is that no member state can manage this complex situation alone and our solidarity measures have not brought the necessary support either. this is why this agency’s staffing capacities and budget will be considerably reinforced. let me also be clear about protection – some of you raised the point, including ms keller – and say that we are not creating a fortress europe. the rights of people seeking international protection will never be put into question. we have a responsibility to offer protection to those in need and we will continue to do so. that is why it is so crucial to see this proposal as part of a comprehensive strategy which started, as i said before, with the adoption of the european agenda on migration, continued with many other initiatives – the implementation measures such as relocation mechanisms and the hotspots – and will be continued with measures allowing resettlement and legal migration. that implementation and relocation mechanism remains a priority for us although it has not worked properly so far, for reasons you know as well as i do. all member states must be part of the relocation scheme, and i would ask you to put pressure on your countries to do more, because if they all respond you will see spectacularly altered results on this. that is also why we have presented a recommendation for humanitarian admission for turkey, to offer legal and safe ways for people seeking protection to come to europe. je voudrais m'adresser à m. deprez. je in writing. with the proposal for a european border and coast guard, europe is finally stepping up its response to the refugee crisis. it is not too early, because there are currently major gaps in external border control. greece in particular is dropping too many flags, which is causing member states to threaten to temporarily close their internal borders. frontex must now be developed into an effective common border and coast guard with more manpower, more resources and a permanent corps of 1500 border guards. the new border agency is to intervene when external border controls fail in a member state. the agency should also play a much more active role in the return policy. we cannot leave the burden and responsibility to the border member states alone: we must control our common external borders together. the ministers of the interior must now move quickly to implement this proposal. we must finally understand that europe is not the problem, but part of the solution. we have wasted more than a decade of delay in building a european border guard and the problems have only grown. a strong eu must tackle the refugee crisis together and not fail to provide the necessary resources.

in writing. the coal and steel sectors are the backbone of the european construction. the steel industry is fundamental to our economy. the sector is facing major difficulties within the european union. since 2008, 40 million tonnes of steel production capacity have been closed. dependence on imports from third countries is a challenge for our manufacturing industries. in addition, the international market is currently experiencing global overcapacity mainly from china. in view of the economic and ecological challenges facing the steel sector, i welcome this report, which has the merit of formulating a series of proposals to strengthen the competitiveness and sustainability of the european steel sector.
in writing. ‒ respect for the rules of competition is essential to ensure economic recovery, safeguard employment and ensure that the european steel industry remains competitive on a global scale. the carbon border adjustment scheme, which i voted for today, would allow the european union to develop a quality climate policy while preserving its competitiveness, putting it on an equal footing with countries that do not respect social and environmental standards. while the recent cop21 climate conference produced an ambitious agreement to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in the future, the time needed to implement these measures must also be taken into account. in the meantime, the conditions for equal competition are not met and the risk of carbon leakage from the european union remains and weighs on our industry. it is therefore necessary to place european industries on an equal footing with their external competitors. i also want the money that would be obtained through the border adjustment system to be used, at least in part, for environmental initiatives and the fight against climate change.
in writing. - i voted for the text. the commission also found that the union industry had a significant market share in the union market, which was much higher than the union industry's market share. this capacity adjustment has been so large that any recovery in european demand will result in a historic trade deficit in europe, generating dependency and loss of industrial know-how, which would inevitably affect downstream sectors such as automotive, construction and low-carbon technologies. the closures in european aluminium, on the other hand, take place against a background of growth in european aluminium demand in recent years; this has resulted in increased imports. steel and aluminium are two significant examples of the difficulties encountered in these professions, which must simultaneously pursue their energy and environmental modernization, which would require an investment policy that few of them can afford today.

in writing. ‒ by voting in favour of this resolution, i would like to make a call on the european parliament's behalf to the authorities of bosnia and herzegovina to use this 20th anniversary of the dayton peace agreement as an additional incentive to carry out the necessary reforms with a view to future accession to the european union.
in writing. ‒ in the light of the growing threat of terrorism and the recent terrorist attacks that have shaken europe, i welcome this resolution calling for stricter rules on arms exports. in view of the changed security environment in the eu's neighbouring countries and the increase in arms smuggling and illicit trade, stricter application of the eight criteria for conventional arms exports and better coordination at eu level are necessary. the aim is to increase transparency and public scrutiny of the export control framework to provide a better overview of the end-use and use of weapons.
in writing. ‒ the news shows how vital it is to combat arms trafficking. however, it is clear that this needs to be organised at european level, especially when we know that member states are major arms exporters to third countries, to which exports amounted to almost eur 26 billion in 2013. i therefore supported this report which calls for a european approach to exports, in particular by ensuring that the member states comply with the eight criteria set out in common position 2008/944/cfsp. the report also calls on member states to address the concept of risk in authorisation procedures for arms transfers, to support the creation of an independent european arms control authority or to put in place an effective control system to combat possible export diversion.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which calls on member states to apply the european arms export code more strictly and to support the creation of an independent european arms control authority. the authority would be responsible for ensuring that everyone respects the minimum standards, but countries would be free to apply stricter standards if they so wish. for many years we have been selling arms to countries that were once considered stable but are now in conflict and sometimes use these weapons against us. i therefore felt that a good risk assessment and a harmonised and coherent european policy on this matter were necessary.
in writing. following the multiple and dramatic attacks that have taken place in europe and beyond, the security situation of all european citizens requires stricter application of the european code on arms exports. we need transparency and tools that can properly assess the risks of conflict in the world. that is why i voted in favour of the creation of an independent european arms control authority under the auspices of the high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. the aim is to go beyond the simple exchange of information and to allow the high representative to give an opinion to ensure that the member states comply with the minimum rules in this area.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report and in particular the provision calling on member states to support the creation of an independent european arms control authority (eaca) under the auspices of the high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. such an authority should be empowered to give an opinion to member states which intend to grant an authorisation refused by at least one other member state. this opinion should consist of an independent assessment of the applicability of the eight common criteria (including the recipient's compliance with international commitments, respect for human rights, the internal situation in the country of final destination, the preservation of peace, regional security and stability, the national security of member states and allied or friendly states, etc.) and could also be requested by states to assess the applicability of the eight common criteria to any european export authorisation.
in writing. ‒ after years of silence, a progress report on the implementation of the common position on arms exports is finally on the table. not a day too soon, considering that belgium has been singled out for a number of recent attacks as a source of used weapons. the reputation of our country and the safety of everyone benefit from more focused efforts in the fight against illegal weapons. and that is exactly what this report by my green colleague is calling for. for example, more stringent but coordinated action is needed at european level, where member states can implement their own, even more stringent, programmes, but where efforts must also be made to collect, analyse and exchange data with an anti-abuse clause in end-user certificates and on-site investigations of end-users. the commission has also been asked to provide a report on the implementation of the new arms embargo, which is to be adopted by the council on 1 january. the eu accounts for 25,4% of the arms market, member states exported eur 36,7 billion in 2013, of which eur 26,7 billion was exported outside the union. the report also focuses on private security firms, private gun ownership, the growing importance of dual-use technology, with a clear need to better regulate drones and spy technology. more transparency, cooperation with civil society and greater parliamentary involvement are crucial.
in writing. - we voted in favour of the text. the s&d group reiterates that adherence to the common position is essential for the application of the union's principles and values, particularly in the field of international human rights law and international humanitarian law, and for the exercise of its responsibilities in the field of regional and global security.
in writing. ‒ we must at all times prevent our european weapons from falling into the hands of terrorists. the recent terrorist threat makes a well-controlled european arms export policy more necessary than ever. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ to avoid any appropriation of nature, two texts provide a framework for the protection of biotechnological inventions in europe (a 1998 directive and the 1973 patent convention). these texts exclude from the scope of patents 'processes for the production of plants which are essentially biological'. the european patent office has decided that plants derived from these methods may be protected provided they meet three criteria: novelty, innovation and industrial application. i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that products obtained by essentially biological processes such as plants, seeds, traits and native genes should not be patentable. crop breeding is an innovative process that has been practiced by farmers and farming communities since the birth of agriculture. this process is important for genetic diversity; the availability of non-proprietary varieties and breeding methods is essential. i therefore call on the commission to clarify as a matter of urgency the scope and interpretation of directive 98/44/ec in order to establish legal certainty regarding the prohibition of the patentability of products obtained by essentially biological processes.
in writing. ‒ meps voted overwhelmingly by 413 votes to 86 to adopt a resolution to clarify eu rules on patents for plant varieties. this is a very important initiative and follows the worrying decision taken in march 2015 by the european patent office that traits of plant origin could now be patentable. this decision concerned tomatoes and broccoli obtained by conventional breeding techniques. the direct consequence is that small farmers and gardeners will now have to pay to continue to have free access to plant seeds. i have of course voted in favour of this resolution which is based on the strong principles of fairness and the fight against monopolies in the food chain. the trend is worrying with 10 companies sharing 60% of the global seed market. it is therefore essential to do everything possible to preserve the right of farmers to use seed extracted from their own crops. the commission, which has been too silent so far, must act quickly to defend in europe an agricultural model which rejects all patents on plants and plant material.
in writing. ‒ yesterday i opposed the establishment of a european list of 36 priority invasive alien species, because in my opinion this list is incomplete and not based on scientific criteria. in these circumstances, the fight against this scourge will not be effective. for this reason, the european parliament objected, by a large majority, to the draft decision establishing this priority list in the framework of the european regulation aimed at preventing and managing the introduction and spread of this pest in the union through coordinated action plans. in doing so, parliament followed the recommendation of the parliamentary committee on the environment, as formulated on 2 december last.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the resolution because farmers are only partially protected and the industry's greed to patent all the seed has not been stopped. neither the european commission nor the european patent office will use this weak text to give a different interpretation to the march 2015 ruling (according to which certain characteristics of tomatoes and broccoli can be patented as long as they are not related to a single variety). the breeder's right itself provides the possibility - even within the framework of the biotechnology directive 98/44 - to breed in the context of research and innovation, even if a patent is attached to it. but after active lobbying by europe bio (agrochemicals), supported by the social democrats and the christian democrats, farmers' protection has been only partially regulated. although in practice they are mainly engaged in seed propagation and breeding (via farm-specific or locally adapted varieties), it is the concentration of power in the seed sector that threatens this right of the farmer. with the pressure to keep new plant breeding techniques out of gmo legislation, it was even more important to curb industry greed so that not all seed is patented. the resolution does not go far enough for me.
in writing. ‒ i am very concerned that the recent decision of the epo's enlarged board of appeal in cases g2/12 (tomatoes) and g2/13 (broccoli) could lead to an increase in the number of patents granted by the epo for natural traits introduced into new varieties through essentially biological processes such as crossing and selection. the commission should urgently clarify the scope and interpretation of directive 98/44/ec, in particular article 4 thereof, as well as articles 12 (3) (b) and 13 (3) (b) thereof, in order to establish legal certainty regarding the prohibition of the patentability of products obtained from essentially biological processes and to clarify that the production from patented biological material is allowed.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i am convinced that it will stimulate innovation and the development of new varieties that can guarantee global food security, further tackle climate change and prevent monopolies within the plant breeders' sector.
in writing. ‒ i supported this joint resolution which strongly condemns violence and all human rights violations, particularly by the army and police in burundi. parliament urged all parties to establish the conditions for rebuilding confidence and promoting national unity and called for the immediate resumption of an open and transparent national dialogue between the government, opposition parties and civil society representatives. i believe that the international community must spare no effort to put an end to the violence in that country and to restore the rule of law and respect for fundamental rights.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i am very concerned about the climate of civil war and the seriousness of the political situation, as well as the rapidly deteriorating humanitarian situation in burundi. i strongly condemn the killings, extrajudicial executions, physical harm to persons, acts of torture and other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment, arbitrary arrests and unlawful detentions, including detention of children, and violations of freedom of the press and freedom of expression. the restoration of security, stability and the restoration of democracy and the rule of law are urgently needed in the interests of the burundian people. to this end, it is necessary that a thorough and independent investigation be carried out into the current killings and abuses, that the perpetrators of these acts be brought to justice and that the immediate disarmament of all armed groups allied to political parties be carried out, in strict compliance with international law and human rights.
in writing. burundi is on the brink of civil war following the events of the last few days and the dangerous, ambiguous, ethnically-tinged rhetoric of the ruling power. this political crisis, the most serious since 2005, is forcing the international community to take a stand. i welcome the proposal of the african union peace and security council to send a force of 5,000 men to burundi. we are facing crimes against humanity, crimes under international law that cannot go unpunished. we can no longer tolerate disproportionate violence, arbitrary arrests, extrajudicial abuses, kidnappings, destroyed media, a muzzled opposition, a dismantled civil society, closed ngos, and so on. the east african rapid reaction force will be responsible for protecting the population and, beyond that, helping to maintain stability in the subregion. i believe that we must move towards a transition which will eventually lead to new elections.
in writing. ‒ i co-signed the resolution which was voted on today and which expresses the european parliament's deep concern at the high level of insecurity and the serious political situation in burundi, as well as the rapid deterioration of the humanitarian situation and the consequences this could have for security and stability in the whole subregion. the text adopted condemns the recent violent attacks and the increase in human rights violations, including murders, extrajudicial executions, attacks on the physical integrity of persons, acts of torture, arbitrary arrests and unlawful detentions, as well as violations of freedom of the press and freedom of expression, and general impunity. the resolution also calls for an immediate end to violence, human rights violations and intimidation against opponents, and for the immediate disarmament of all armed groups allied to political parties. the resolution also reminds the burundian authorities of their obligation to ensure security in their territory and to guarantee fundamental civil and political rights and freedoms, as provided for in the burundian constitution and the african charter of human rights.
in writing. ‒ in recent months, we have witnessed a growing violence in burundi. in musical terms, a crescendo often heralds a climax. the one we are seeing materialize in your country is far from lyrical. on the contrary, it is a chronicle of a predicted chaos. the slaughter continues and is becoming more and more frightening. dozens of your citizens were killed last weekend in numerous arbitrary executions. burundi has taken another step towards its decline. the confrontations with the opposition, which became increasingly violent and targeted, ended in a bloodbath in the streets of bujumbura. have we learned nothing from rwanda? do we not see the same calls for hatred and the same search for a scapegoat? my colleague arena was outraged again recently!
in writing. – the resolution invites all parties concerned to talk, and we are ready to fully support it. but haven’t we gone beyond the moment where talks can be held as if nothing has happened? blood is in the streets. armed forces are arbitrarily killing their own fellow citizens. it is clear burundi has reached a stage of deep chaos, where fundamental rights are of no importance. as a liberal, i cannot accept this. the eu and its member states must freeze all assistance to the burundian government, while continuing to support the civil population in these dire days of political and humanitarian turmoil. we must also stand ready to support an african-led peace-keeping operation, to bring stability again. otherwise burundi, because of the unreasonable power struggle by its president nkurunziza, will sink away into violent trouble and risk infecting the entire central african region.
in writing. ‒ virunga national park in north kivu is a unesco world heritage site for its habitats and rich biodiversity, which is unmatched in africa. the resolution, which i supported, stresses that the park is subject to several dangers. it has been the scene of violent conflict for over 20 years and has been the subject of poaching and illegal exploitation of mineral and natural resources. moreover, since 2007, oil concessions covering more than 85% of the park have been granted to total and soco, the latter being to date the only company to have prospected the park. parliament therefore called for every effort to be made to avoid irreversible damage to the park. it called on the commission and the member states to work towards preserving the integrity of the park by strengthening their commitment to funding the conservation, economic development and sustainable diversification of the surrounding region, and asked the eeas to engage in diplomatic action to help the congolese government to abandon oil exploration and exploitation in the park.
in writing. ‒ i supported this resolution, stressing the absolute need to avoid irreversible damage to the virunga national park, which is a unesco world heritage site. unfortunately, it has become one of the most dangerous places in the world for wildlife conservation. the park is the scene of intensive poaching, illegal logging, illegal mining, corruption, rape, murder. in the last ten years alone, more than 150 forest rangers have been killed in the line of duty. not to mention the death threats, intimidation, arbitrary arrests against anyone who denounces the impotence of the state or the greed of the oil companies. i also express my deep concern at the irreversible damage that could be caused to virunga national park as a result of oil exploration and exploitation and call for measures to help protect the park as one of the last remaining gorilla reserves, to address the root causes of armed conflict and corruption, and to support sustainable development and peacebuilding strategies in the democratic republic of congo.
in writing. i would like to commend the courage and unwavering determination of the park director, emmanuel de mérode, who has been fighting tirelessly to bring the attention of the international community to this remote region, far from the spotlight and the international stage. these magnificent landscapes are the scene of poaching, illegal logging, illegal mining, corruption, rape, murder; that's over 150 rangers, rangers who have been killed in the line of duty in the last decade. there are numerous death threats, intimidation, arbitrary arrests against anyone who denounces the impotence of the state, the greed of the oil companies. i call on the drc authorities to investigate the threats and violence against guards, to ensure justice is done and to prevent irreversible damage to virunga national park. although the british company soco international has decided to withdraw from the virunga national park, the congolese government should not give the license to another operator or decide to exploit the oil itself in the name of economic development, which would only fuel greed, violence and conflict.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution which stresses the need to prevent irreversible damage to the virunga national park, which was declared a world heritage site in 1979 and inscribed on the list of world heritage in danger by unesco in 1994, and which is home to many endangered species, such as the iconic mountain gorilla and the okapi, in particular from oil exploration and exploitation and other illegal activities. it is unacceptable that oil concessions were granted to the french company total and the british company soco international in 2007, in violation of the paris convention for the protection of the world cultural and natural heritage, the 1992 convention on biological diversity, the ramsar convention and congolese legislation. the european parliament is therefore deeply concerned at the illegal exploitation of the natural resources of the park by armed groups who use mining activities to finance their military operations and enrich themselves.
in writing. ‒ virunga national park (vnp) in the democratic republic of congo is africa's first national park, a unesco world heritage site and has been supported by the european commission and several member states for 25 years. the illegal trade in raw materials and the exploitation and exploration of oil in virunga park are not only causing environmental damage and the destruction of the park, but also more violence and violation of human rights. the oil concessions granted by total and soco are also in breach of a number of (international) laws. the eu once again stresses the absolute need to prevent irreversible damage to virunga national park. the resolution calls for the european external action service to coordinate a diplomatic response and make it clear that what is happening in this park is unacceptable. by focusing on sustainable forest management, economic development of the region, alternative energy and the fight against illegal logging, the integrity of the park can be maintained. the resolution also calls for active companies (such as soco) to respect international human rights law and for binding agreements to be reached on how multinationals make money. for all these reasons, i am voting in favour of this resolution.
in writing. - i voted without hesitation for the resolution. it is essential to prevent irreversible damage to the virunga national park, which was declared a world heritage site in 1979 and inscribed on the list of world heritage in danger by unesco in 1994.
in writing. ‒ virunga national park is not only africa's oldest national park, it is also one of the most biodiverse and unique national parks in the world. the future of this beautiful park and its resources are under severe pressure. armed conflict, corruption, and unbridled economic interests are major threats to the park and its endangered species. over the past ten years, more than 150 rangers have been killed in the line of duty. those who denounce the culpable negligence of the government are threatened, intimidated or imprisoned without cause. i call on the congolese authorities to investigate and prosecute the threats and violence against the rangers. i believe that the congolese government must do everything possible to stop and prevent irreparable damage to the virunga national park from oil exploration and exploitation or other illegal activities.
